docs.text:
Files: - Modify: flake.nix, flake.lock, test/go.mod, test/go.sum, test/smoke_test.go, Makefile - Create: test/identity_helpers_test.go, test/identity_test.go

Interfaces: - Consumes: everything above. - Produces: - ensureCredentials(t, name) credentials - (*totpClock).code(t, account, credentials) string - browserAuthorize(t, account, credentials) (code string, ok bool) - exchangeCode(t, code, secret) map[string]any - hasGroup(claims, group) bool - tests TestIdentityLogin and TestIdentityDenied, plus unit tests TestIdentityTOTPWaitsForNextStep and TestIdentityHasGroup

  • Step 1: Add chromium and the Go modules

In flake.nix, add chromium to packages (alphabetically, after bmake). Then:

nix develop -c true
cd test && go get github.com/chromedp/chromedp@v0.21.0 github.com/pquerna/otp@v1.5.0 github.com/stretchr/testify@latest && cd ..
  • Step 2: Write the unit tests first, in test/identity_test.go
package test

import (
    "os"
    "testing"
    "time"

    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestIdentityTOTPWaitsForNextStep(t *testing.T) {
    c := credentials{TOTPSecret: "JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP", Algorithm: "sha256", Digits: 6, Period: 30}
    t0 := time.Unix(1_800_000_000, 0) // start of a 30 s step
    now := t0
    var slept time.Duration
    clock := &totpClock{
        now:   func() time.Time { return now },
        sleep: func(d time.Duration) { slept += d; now = now.Add(d) },
        last:  map[string]uint64{},
    }

    first := clock.code(t, "dev-admin", c)
    second := clock.code(t, "dev-admin", c)

    assert.Equal(t, 30*time.Second, slept, "second code must wait for the next step")
    assert.NotEqual(t, first, second)
    assert.Equal(t, totpCode(t, c, t0.Add(30*time.Second)), second)
}

func TestIdentityHasGroup(t *testing.T) {
    assert.True(t, hasGroup(map[string]any{"groups": []any{"homelab-admins"}}, "homelab-admins"))
    assert.True(t, hasGroup(map[string]any{"groups": []any{"homelab-admins@auth.127-0-0-1.nip.io"}}, "homelab-admins"))
    assert.False(t, hasGroup(map[string]any{"groups": []any{"homelab-admins-old"}}, "homelab-admins"))
    assert.False(t, hasGroup(map[string]any{}, "homelab-admins"))
}

func TestIdentityLogin(t *testing.T) {
    if os.Getenv("ENV") != "dev" {
        t.Skip("identity tests run against the sandbox only")
    }
    secret := smokeClientSecret(t)

    for _, account := range testAccounts {
        if account.group == "" {
            continue
        }
        t.Run(account.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            c := ensureCredentials(t, account.name)

            code, ok := browserAuthorize(t, account.name, c)
            require.True(t, ok, "no authorization code for %s", account.name)

            claims := exchangeCode(t, code, secret)
            t.Logf("groups claim for %s: %v", account.name, claims["groups"])
            assert.Equal(t, account.name+"@example.com", claims["email"])
            assert.True(t, hasGroup(claims, account.group), "groups %v lack %s", claims["groups"], account.group)
        })
    }
}

func TestIdentityDenied(t *testing.T) {
    if os.Getenv("ENV") != "dev" {
        t.Skip("identity tests run against the sandbox only")
    }
    c := ensureCredentials(t, "dev-outsider")

    _, ok := browserAuthorize(t, "dev-outsider", c)

    assert.False(t, ok, "an account in no homelab group must not get an authorization code")
}
  • Step 3: Run the unit tests and watch them fail

Run: cd test && go test -run 'TestIdentity(TOTPWaitsForNextStep|HasGroup)' ./... Expected: FAIL to build with undefined: credentials, undefined: totpClock, undefined: hasGroup, and the other helpers.

  • Step 4: Create test/identity_helpers_test.go
package test

import (
    "bytes"
    "context"
    "crypto/rand"
    "crypto/tls"
    "encoding/base32"
    "encoding/base64"
    "encoding/json"
    "io"
    "math/big"
    "net/http"
    "net/url"
    "regexp"
    "strconv"
    "strings"
    "testing"
    "time"

    "github.com/chromedp/cdproto/network"
    "github.com/chromedp/chromedp"
    "github.com/gruntwork-io/terratest/modules/k8s"
    "github.com/pquerna/otp"
    "github.com/pquerna/otp/totp"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

const (
    kanidmURL         = "https://auth.127-0-0-1.nip.io"
    dexURL            = "https://dex.127-0-0-1.nip.io"
    smokeRedirect     = "https://smoke.127-0-0-1.nip.io/callback"
    credentialsSecret = "identity-test-credentials"
)

type testAccount struct {
    name  string
    group string // empty: the account is in no homelab group
}

var testAccounts = []testAccount{
    {"dev-admin", "homelab-admins"},
    {"dev-editor", "homelab-editors"},
    {"dev-viewer", "homelab-users"},
    {"dev-outsider", ""},
}

// credentials of a sandbox test account, stored in a Secret so reruns can log in again
type credentials struct {
    Password   string `json:"password"`
    TOTPSecret string `json:"totpSecret"` // base32 without padding
    Algorithm  string `json:"algorithm"`  // sha1, sha256 or sha512
    Digits     int    `json:"digits"`
    Period     uint   `json:"period"`
}

// The sandbox uses a local CA; these tests only ever run against it.
var insecureClient = &http.Client{
    Timeout:       30 * time.Second,
    Transport:     &http.Transport{TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true}},
    CheckRedirect: func(*http.Request, []*http.Request) error { return http.ErrUseLastResponse },
}

func kanidmNamespace() *k8s.KubectlOptions { return k8s.NewKubectlOptions("", "", "kanidm") }

func randomPassword(t *testing.T) string {
    const alphabet = "abcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789"
    var b strings.Builder
    for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
        n, err := rand.Int(rand.Reader, big.NewInt(int64(len(alphabet))))
        require.NoError(t, err)
        b.WriteByte(alphabet[n.Int64()])
    }
    return b.String()
}

// ensureCredentials returns stored credentials, or enrols new ones with the reset token kaniop published.
func ensureCredentials(t *testing.T, account string) credentials {
    stored, err := k8s.RunKubectlAndGetOutputE(t, kanidmNamespace(),
        "get", "secret", credentialsSecret, "-o", "jsonpath={.data."+account+"}")
    if err == nil && stored != "" {
        raw, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(stored)
        require.NoError(t, err)
        var c credentials
        require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(raw, &c))
        return c
    }

    c := enrol(t, account, resetToken(t, account))

    encoded, err := json.Marshal(c)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    if _, err := k8s.RunKubectlAndGetOutputE(t, kanidmNamespace(), "get", "secret", credentialsSecret); err != nil {
        k8s.RunKubectl(t, kanidmNamespace(), "create", "secret", "generic", credentialsSecret)
    }
    patch, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"stringData": map[string]string{account: string(encoded)}})
    require.NoError(t, err)
    k8s.RunKubectl(t, kanidmNamespace(), "patch", "secret", credentialsSecret, "--type", "merge", "-p", string(patch))
    return c
}

var resetTokenPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`/ui/reset\?token=([^\s"&]+)`)

// resetToken reads the newest credential reset link kaniop published for the account.
func resetToken(t *testing.T, account string) string {
    var token string
    require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        out, err := k8s.RunKubectlAndGetOutputE(t, kanidmNamespace(), "get", "events",
            "--field-selector", "involvedObject.name="+account+",reason=TokenCreated",
            "--sort-by", ".lastTimestamp", "-o", "jsonpath={range .items[*]}{.message}{\"\\n\"}{end}")
        if err != nil {
            return false
        }
        matches := resetTokenPattern.FindAllStringSubmatch(out, -1)
        if len(matches) == 0 {
            return false
        }
        token = matches[len(matches)-1][1]
        return true
    }, 5*time.Minute, 10*time.Second, "no TokenCreated event for %s", account)
    return token
}

func kanidmPost(t *testing.T, path string, body any, out any) {
    payload, err := json.Marshal(body)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    resp, err := insecureClient.Post(kanidmURL+path, "application/json", bytes.NewReader(payload))
    require.NoError(t, err)
    defer resp.Body.Close()
    raw, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, resp.StatusCode, "POST %s: %s", path, raw)
    if out != nil {
        require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(raw, out), "POST %s: %s", path, raw)
    }
}

type cuSession struct {
    Token string `json:"token"`
}

type cuStatus struct {
    MfaRegState json.RawMessage `json:"mfaregstate"`
}

func (s cuStatus) state() string {
    var name string
    if json.Unmarshal(s.MfaRegState, &name) == nil {
        return name
    }
    var tagged map[string]json.RawMessage
    if json.Unmarshal(s.MfaRegState, &tagged) == nil {
        for k := range tagged {
            return k
        }
    }
    return ""
}

// enrol sets a password and a TOTP through Kanidm's credential update API (Kanidm requires MFA for persons).
func enrol(t *testing.T, account, token string) credentials {
    var exchanged []json.RawMessage
    kanidmPost(t, "/v1/credential/_exchange_intent", token, &exchanged)
    require.Len(t, exchanged, 2)
    var session cuSession
    require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(exchanged[0], &session))

    update := func(request any) cuStatus {
        var status cuStatus
        kanidmPost(t, "/v1/credential/_update", []any{request, session}, &status)
        return status
    }

    c := credentials{Password: randomPassword(t)}
    update(map[string]string{"password": c.Password})

    generated := update("totpgenerate")
    var reg struct {
        TotpCheck struct {
            Secret []int  `json:"secret"`
            Algo   string `json:"algo"`
            Step   uint   `json:"step"`
            Digits int    `json:"digits"`
        } `json:"TotpCheck"`
    }
    require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(generated.MfaRegState, &reg), "mfaregstate: %s", generated.MfaRegState)
    secret := make([]byte, len(reg.TotpCheck.Secret))
    for i, b := range reg.TotpCheck.Secret {
        secret[i] = byte(b)
    }
    c.TOTPSecret = base32.StdEncoding.WithPadding(base32.NoPadding).EncodeToString(secret)
    c.Algorithm, c.Period, c.Digits = reg.TotpCheck.Algo, reg.TotpCheck.Step, reg.TotpCheck.Digits

    code, err := strconv.Atoi(clock.code(t, account, c))
    require.NoError(t, err)
    verified := update(map[string][]any{"totpverify": {code, "smoke-test"}})
    if verified.state() == "TotpInvalidSha1" {
        verified = update("totpacceptsha1")
    }
    require.Equal(t, "None", verified.state(), "TOTP not accepted: %s", verified.MfaRegState)

    kanidmPost(t, "/v1/credential/_commit", session, nil)
    return c
}

func totpCode(t *testing.T, c credentials, at time.Time) string {
    algorithms := map[string]otp.Algorithm{"sha1": otp.AlgorithmSHA1, "sha256": otp.AlgorithmSHA256, "sha512": otp.AlgorithmSHA512}
    algorithm, ok := algorithms[c.Algorithm]
    require.True(t, ok, "unknown TOTP algorithm %q", c.Algorithm)
    digits := otp.DigitsSix
    if c.Digits == 8 {
        digits = otp.DigitsEight
    }
    code, err := totp.GenerateCodeCustom(c.TOTPSecret, at, totp.ValidateOpts{Period: c.Period, Digits: digits, Algorithm: algorithm})
    require.NoError(t, err)
    return code
}

// totpClock hands out codes from a step not used before, because Kanidm rejects a reused step.
type totpClock struct {
    now   func() time.Time
    sleep func(time.Duration)
    last  map[string]uint64
}

var clock = &totpClock{now: time.Now, sleep: time.Sleep, last: map[string]uint64{}}

func (k *totpClock) code(t *testing.T, account string, c credentials) string {
    for {
        now := k.now()
        step := uint64(now.Unix()) / uint64(c.Period)
        if step > k.last[account] {
            k.last[account] = step
            return totpCode(t, c, now)
        }
        k.sleep(time.Duration(uint64(c.Period)-uint64(now.Unix())%uint64(c.Period)) * time.Second)
    }
}

// browserAuthorize logs in through Dex and Kanidm and returns the code sent to the smoke client.
func browserAuthorize(t *testing.T, account string, c credentials) (string, bool) {
    opts := append(chromedp.DefaultExecAllocatorOptions[:], chromedp.Flag("ignore-certificate-errors", true))
    allocCtx, cancelAlloc := chromedp.NewExecAllocator(context.Background(), opts...)
    defer cancelAlloc()
    ctx, cancelBrowser := chromedp.NewContext(allocCtx)
    defer cancelBrowser()
    ctx, cancelTimeout := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 3*time.Minute)
    defer cancelTimeout()

    codes := make(chan string, 1)
    chromedp.ListenTarget(ctx, func(ev any) {
        if e, ok := ev.(*network.EventRequestWillBeSent); ok && strings.HasPrefix(e.Request.URL, smokeRedirect) {
            if u, err := url.Parse(e.Request.URL); err == nil && u.Query().Get("code") != "" {
                select {
                case codes <- u.Query().Get("code"):
                default:
                }
            }
        }
    })

    authURL := dexURL + "/auth?" + url.Values{
        "client_id":     {"smoke"},
        "redirect_uri":  {smokeRedirect},
        "response_type": {"code"},
        "scope":         {"openid email profile groups"},
        "state":         {"identity-test"},
    }.Encode()

    require.NoError(t, chromedp.Run(ctx,
        network.Enable(),
        chromedp.Navigate(authURL),
        chromedp.WaitVisible(`input#username`),
        chromedp.SendKeys(`input#username`, account+"\n"),
        chromedp.WaitVisible(`input#password`),
        chromedp.SendKeys(`input#password`, c.Password+"\n"),
        chromedp.WaitVisible(`input#totp`),
    ), "login form for %s", account)
    require.NoError(t, chromedp.Run(ctx, chromedp.SendKeys(`input#totp`, clock.code(t, account, c)+"\n")))

    select {
    case code := <-codes:
        return code, true
    case <-time.After(30 * time.Second):
        return "", false
    }
}

func smokeClientSecret(t *testing.T) string {
    secret := k8s.GetSecret(t, k8s.NewKubectlOptions("", "", "global-secrets"), "dex.smoke")
    return string(secret.Data["client_secret"])
}

// exchangeCode trades the code for tokens at Dex and returns the ID token claims.
func exchangeCode(t *testing.T, code, secret string) map[string]any {
    form := url.Values{"grant_type": {"authorization_code"}, "code": {code}, "redirect_uri": {smokeRedirect}}
    req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, dexURL+"/token", strings.NewReader(form.Encode()))
    require.NoError(t, err)
    req.SetBasicAuth("smoke", secret)
    req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
    resp, err := insecureClient.Do(req)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    defer resp.Body.Close()
    raw, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, resp.StatusCode, "token exchange: %s", raw)

    var tokens struct {
        IDToken string `json:"id_token"`
    }
    require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(raw, &tokens))
    parts := strings.Split(tokens.IDToken, ".")
    require.Len(t, parts, 3)
    payload, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(parts[1])
    require.NoError(t, err)
    var claims map[string]any
    require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(payload, &claims))
    return claims
}

// hasGroup accepts Kanidm's short group names and SPNs (name@domain).
func hasGroup(claims map[string]any, group string) bool {
    groups, _ := claims["groups"].([]any)
    for _, g := range groups {
        if s, ok := g.(string); ok && (s == group || strings.HasPrefix(s, group+"@")) {
            return true
        }
    }
    return false
}

- [ ] **Step 2: `docs/concepts/secrets-management.md`**

Replace the description of the secret generator Job with this section (keep the rest of the page):

```markdown
## Generated secrets

Random secrets (admin passwords, OAuth2 client secrets) are listed in `platform/global-secrets/values.yaml`. For each one, an external-secrets `Password` generator creates a Secret in namespace `global-secrets` once, and the `global-secrets` ClusterSecretStore shares it with the apps that reference it.

They are never rotated automatically: both sides of a client secret would have to restart together, and admin passwords are stored in the app's database on first start.

To rotate one by hand:

1. `kubectl -n global-secrets delete secret <name>`. external-secrets generates a new value.
2. Restart every app that uses it (for example `kubectl -n dex rollout restart deploy/dex` and the client app).
3. For an admin password, also change it inside the app to the new value.

Kanidm OAuth2 client secrets are generated by the kaniop operator instead, as `<client>-kanidm-oauth2-credentials` in the client's namespace.

The script prints the idm_admin password for the login prompt and ends with a credential reset link to send to the person. Kanidm requires a password plus TOTP or a passkey.

docs.title: Gateway API (sub-project 2) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Replace ingress-nginx and every Ingress with two Cilium Gateway API Gateways (homelab for the LAN, homelab-public for the Cloudflare Tunnel) sharing one wildcard certificate, and prove it in the sandbox with five more apps.

Architecture: - Gateways. metal/ installs the Gateway API CRDs before Cilium and enables Cilium's Gateway controller. A new ArgoCD component system/gateway holds both Gateways, the wildcard Certificate and an HTTP→HTTPS redirect route. - Routes. Every app attaches an HTTPRoute (gitea also a TCPRoute) to one Gateway, mostly through its chart's own route support after upgrading the chart to its latest version. - Sandbox CA. trust-manager copies the dev CA into a ConfigMap homelab-dev-ca in every namespace. It replaces the ingress certificate secrets that Go apps used for ca.crt, and it is the CA for Kanidm's BackendTLSPolicy.

Tech Stack: Cilium 1.20.2, Gateway API CRDs v1.6.3 (standard channel), cert-manager v1.21.2, trust-manager v0.25.0, Helm wrapper charts synced by ArgoCD, Ansible (metal/), Go tests with terratest and chromedp.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-gateway-api-design.md

  • Gateways (namespace gateway):
  • homelab: listeners http (80, routes from namespace gateway only), https (443, hostname *.<domain>, routes from all namespaces), ssh (22, TCP, TCPRoutes from namespace gitea only). Sandbox address 172.30.255.200.
  • homelab-public: listener https only; annotation external-dns.kubernetes.io/target: homelab-tunnel.<domain>; address from the pool.
  • Wildcard secret homelab-wildcard-tls (Certificate homelab-wildcard, issuer letsencrypt-prod).
  • Services created by Cilium: cilium-gateway-homelab, cilium-gateway-homelab-public.
  • parentRefs: {name: homelab, namespace: gateway, sectionName: https}, or homelab-public for excalidraw, blog and matrix's Element. In the sandbox, excalidraw uses homelab.
  • Annotations: external-dns prefix external-dns.kubernetes.io/ (never external-dns.alpha.). Public routes carry external-dns.kubernetes.io/cloudflare-proxied: "true"; the target is set only on homelab-public.
  • Dev CA: ConfigMap homelab-dev-ca, key ca.crt, in every namespace; mounts use optional: true. Paths stay /etc/homelab-dev-ca/ca.crt (Dex: /etc/dex/dev-ca/ca.crt).
  • Helm values: Helm replaces lists and cannot delete keys across values files; dev overrides restate whole lists. Use "" (not null) to blank an annotation in values-dev.yaml.
  • Gateway API kinds render as gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1. Charts choose the API version from .Capabilities; scripts/render-chart passes the same API versions ArgoCD sees (Task 1).
  • Hosts (sandbox): <app>.127-0-0-1.nip.io; prod keeps khuedoan.com until sub-project 3.
  • Offline unit tests: cd test && go vet ./... && go test -run 'TestSmokeAppsForEnv|TestIdentity(HasGroup|TOTPWaitsForNextStep)|TestGatewayRouteReady' ./....

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. Running sandbox upgrade: the ApplicationSet does not delete an Application's resources, so the old ingress-nginx Service keeps holding 172.30.255.200 and the homelab Gateway gets no address. → Task 15 deletes ingress-nginx's leftovers before make dev, and TestGatewayProgrammed asserts the address.
  2. Cilium on an existing cluster: its operator enables the Gateway controller only if the CRDs exist when it starts, and a Helm values change does not restart it. → Task 3 restarts the operator and agents whenever the Cilium release changes; Task 15 checks GatewayClass cilium is Accepted.
  3. Renames from major chart upgrades: app-template 5 renames PVCs (<app>-data → <app>), ConfigMaps (homepage-config → homepage) and the main Service of multi-controller apps (ollama → ollama-main); gitea 12 renders TCPRoute v1alpha2, which v1.6 CRDs no longer serve. → Tasks 8, 9, 10 and 12 assert the rendered names; Task 10 writes its own TCPRoute.
  4. Wrong Gateway means wrong exposure: a LAN app on homelab-public is published on the internet; a public app on homelab silently loses its DNS record. → Task 13's pre-PR check lists every route's parent in both environments and compares it with the allowed set.
  5. Large uploads and long requests through Envoy: nginx had proxy-body-size: 0 for zot and 50m for speedtest; Envoy differs. → zot's route sets timeouts.request: 0s, and TestGatewayZotLargePush pushes 200 MiB.

        "accepted with resolved backends": {`{"spec":{"hostnames":["a.example"]},"status":{"parents":[{"conditions":[` + both + `]}]}}`, true},
        "not reconciled yet":              {`{"spec":{"hostnames":["a.example"]}}`, false},
        "backend missing":                 {`{"spec":{"hostnames":["a.example"]},"status":{"parents":[{"conditions":[{"type":"Accepted","status":"True"},{"type":"ResolvedRefs","status":"False"}]}]}}`, false},
        "one parent refused":              {`{"spec":{"hostnames":["a.example"]},"status":{"parents":[{"conditions":[` + both + `]},{"conditions":[{"type":"Accepted","status":"False"},{"type":"ResolvedRefs","status":"True"}]}]}}`, false},
        "no hostname":                     {`{"status":{"parents":[{"conditions":[` + both + `]}]}}`, false},
    }
    for name, c := range cases {
        t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
            var r httpRoute
            require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(c.route), &r))
            assert.Equal(t, c.want, r.ready())
        })
    }
}

  • Step 3: Implement the helpers. Create test/gateway_helpers_test.go:
package test

import (
    "encoding/json"
    "os/exec"
    "testing"
    "time"

    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// condition is the part of a Kubernetes status condition the tests read.
type condition struct {
    Type   string `json:"type"`
    Status string `json:"status"`
}

// conditionsMet reports whether every wanted condition type has status True.
func conditionsMet(conditions []condition, types ...string) bool {
    status := map[string]string{}
    for _, c := range conditions {
        status[c.Type] = c.Status
    }
    for _, t := range types {
        if status[t] != "True" {
            return false
        }
    }
    return true
}

// httpRoute is the part of a Gateway API HTTPRoute the tests read.
type httpRoute struct {
    Spec struct {
        Hostnames []string `json:"hostnames"`
    } `json:"spec"`
    Status struct {
        Parents []struct {
            Conditions []condition `json:"conditions"`
        } `json:"parents"`
    } `json:"status"`
}

// ready reports whether the route has a hostname and every parent Gateway accepted it with resolved backends.
func (r httpRoute) ready() bool {
    if len(r.Spec.Hostnames) == 0 || len(r.Status.Parents) == 0 {
        return false
    }
    for _, p := range r.Status.Parents {
        if !conditionsMet(p.Conditions, "Accepted", "ResolvedRefs") {
            return false
        }
    }
    return true
}

// getResource decodes `kubectl get <args> --output json` into out and reports whether the command succeeded.
// It reads stdout only, so kubectl warnings cannot break the JSON.
func getResource(t *testing.T, namespace string, out any, args ...string) bool {
    args = append(append([]string{"--namespace", namespace, "get"}, args...), "--output", "json")
    raw, err := exec.Command("kubectl", args...).Output()
    if err != nil {
        return false
    }
    require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(raw, out))
    return true
}

// routeHost waits until the HTTPRoute is ready and returns its first hostname.
func routeHost(t *testing.T, namespace, name string) string {
    var route httpRoute
    require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        route = httpRoute{}
        return getResource(t, namespace, &route, "httproute", name) && route.ready()
    }, 30*time.Minute, 30*time.Second, "HTTPRoute %s/%s is not accepted with resolved backends", namespace, name)
    return route.Spec.Hostnames[0]
}
  • Step 4: Add the sandbox Gateway tests. Append to test/gateway_test.go:
func gatewaySandboxOnly(t *testing.T) {
    if os.Getenv("ENV") != "dev" {
        t.Skip("Gateway tests run against the sandbox only")
    }
}

// gateway is the part of a Gateway API Gateway the tests read.
type gateway struct {
    Status struct {
        Addresses []struct {
            Value string `json:"value"`
        } `json:"addresses"`
        Conditions []condition `json:"conditions"`
    } `json:"status"`
}

func TestGatewayProgrammed(t *testing.T) {
    gatewaySandboxOnly(t)
    for _, name := range []string{"homelab", "homelab-public"} {
        t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
            var gw gateway
            require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
                gw = gateway{}
                return getResource(t, "gateway", &gw, "gateway", name) && conditionsMet(gw.Status.Conditions, "Accepted", "Programmed")
            }, 20*time.Minute, 15*time.Second, "Gateway %s is not programmed", name)
            if name == "homelab" {
                require.NotEmpty(t, gw.Status.Addresses)
                assert.Equal(t, sandboxIngress, gw.Status.Addresses[0].Value, "the localhost proxy forwards to this address")
            }
        })
    }
}

func TestGatewayHTTPSRedirect(t *testing.T) {
    gatewaySandboxOnly(t)
    host := routeHost(t, "excalidraw", "excalidraw")
    resp, err := insecureClient.Get("http://" + host + "/some/path?x=1")
    require.NoError(t, err)
    resp.Body.Close()
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusMovedPermanently, resp.StatusCode)
    assert.Equal(t, "https://"+host+"/some/path?x=1", resp.Header.Get("Location"))
}

func TestGatewayNoIngress(t *testing.T) {
    gatewaySandboxOnly(t)
    var ingresses struct {
        Items []any `json:"items"`
    }
    require.True(t, getResource(t, "default", &ingresses, "ingress", "--all-namespaces"))
    assert.Empty(t, ingresses.Items, "every component uses Gateway API routes")
    var namespace struct{}
    assert.False(t, getResource(t, "default", &namespace, "namespace", "ingress-nginx"), "ingress-nginx must be gone")
}

func TestGatewayGiteaSSH(t *testing.T) {
    gatewaySandboxOnly(t)
    require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        conn, err := net.DialTimeout("tcp", net.JoinHostPort(sandboxIngress, "22"), 10*time.Second)
        if err != nil {
            return false
        }
        defer conn.Close()
        _ = conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second))
        banner, err := bufio.NewReader(conn).ReadString('\n')
        return err == nil && strings.HasPrefix(banner, "SSH-2.0-")
    }, 20*time.Minute, 15*time.Second, "no SSH banner from gitea on %s:22", sandboxIngress)
}

// TestGatewayZotLargePush uploads one 200 MiB blob through the Gateway, as an image push would.
func TestGatewayZotLargePush(t *testing.T) {
    gatewaySandboxOnly(t)
    base := "https://" + registryHost
    waitForApp(t, base+"/livez")
    password := secretValue(t, "global-secrets", "registry.ci", "password")

    // Same content every run, so zot stores a single copy
    blob := make([]byte, 200<<20)
    rand.New(rand.NewSource(1)).Read(blob)
    digest := fmt.Sprintf("sha256:%x", sha256.Sum256(blob))

    client := *insecureClient
    client.Timeout = 5 * time.Minute

    req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", base+"/v2/gateway-test/blobs/uploads/", nil)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    req.SetBasicAuth("ci", password)
    resp, err := client.Do(req)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    resp.Body.Close()
    require.Equal(t, http.StatusAccepted, resp.StatusCode)
    location, err := resp.Location()
    require.NoError(t, err)
    query := location.Query()
    query.Set("digest", digest)
    location.RawQuery = query.Encode()

    req, err = http.NewRequest("PUT", location.String(), bytes.NewReader(blob))
    require.NoError(t, err)
    req.SetBasicAuth("ci", password)
    req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")
    start := time.Now()
    resp, err = client.Do(req)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    body, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
    resp.Body.Close()
    require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, resp.StatusCode, "%s", body)
    t.Logf("pushed 200 MiB through the Gateway in %s", time.Since(start).Round(time.Millisecond))
}

docs.title: Task 3: Gateway API CRDs and Cilium's Gateway controller
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: metal/roles/cilium/defaults/main.yml, metal/roles/cilium/tasks/main.yml, metal/roles/coredns_rewrite/tasks/main.yml, metal/inventories/dev.yml, metal/Makefile

Interfaces: - Produces: GatewayClass cilium (created by Cilium); CoreDNS sends *.127-0-0-1.nip.io to cilium-gateway-homelab.gateway.svc.cluster.local in the sandbox.

  • Step 1: Variables. In metal/roles/cilium/defaults/main.yml, after cilium_namespace: kube-system add:
# Gateway API CRDs (standard channel). Cilium enables its Gateway controller only when they exist at start.
gateway_api_version: v1.6.3

and add to cilium_values (after l2announcements):

  gatewayAPI:
    enabled: true
  • Step 2: Install the CRDs first, restart Cilium after a change. In metal/roles/cilium/tasks/main.yml:
  • Insert as the first task:
- name: Install the Gateway API CRDs
  kubernetes.core.k8s:
    definition: "{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.url', 'https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/' ~ gateway_api_version ~ '/standard-install.yaml', split_lines=false) | from_yaml_all | list }}"
    apply: true
    server_side_apply:
      field_manager: ansible
  • Add register: cilium_release to the Install Cilium task.
  • Insert after Install Cilium:
# Neither a values change nor new CRDs restart Cilium; the operator reads both only at start
- name: Restart Cilium after a change
  when: cilium_release is changed
  kubernetes.core.k8s:
    state: patched
    kind: "{{ item.kind }}"
    namespace: "{{ cilium_namespace }}"
    name: "{{ item.name }}"
    definition:
      spec:
        template:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              homelab/cilium-restarted: "{{ now(utc=true).isoformat() }}"
    wait: true
    wait_timeout: 600
  loop:
    - { kind: Deployment, name: cilium-operator }
    - { kind: DaemonSet, name: cilium }
  • Step 3: The CoreDNS rule targets the Gateway and replaces an older one.
  • In metal/inventories/dev.yml, change the rule to:
    coredns_rewrite_rule: 'rewrite name regex (.*)\.127-0-0-1\.nip\.io cilium-gateway-homelab.gateway.svc.cluster.local answer auto'
  • In metal/roles/coredns_rewrite/tasks/main.yml, change the Corefile: expression of Add the rewrite rule to drop any existing rewrite name regex line first (the old rule pointed at ingress-nginx and would win, being first):
        Corefile: "{{ corefile.split('\n') | reject('search', '^\\s*rewrite name regex ') | join('\n') | replace('    ready\n', '    ready\n    ' ~ coredns_rewrite_rule ~ '\n') }}"

  • Rename the task to Add the rewrite rule, replacing an older one.

  • Step 4: Name the socat target after the Gateway. In metal/Makefile, rename ingress_ip to gateway_ip (definition and both uses) and put # The homelab Gateway (system/gateway/values-dev.yaml) above its definition.

  • Step 5: Verify.

Run: 

ansible-playbook --syntax-check -i metal/inventories/dev.yml metal/cluster.yml
grep -rn ingress metal --include=*.yml --include=Makefile
Expected: syntax check passes; grep prints nothing.

Then check the Jinja on a sample Corefile (throwaway, outside the repo):

cat > /tmp/corefile-test.yml <<'EOF'
- hosts: localhost
  gather_facts: false
  vars:
    corefile: ".:53 {\n    errors\n    ready\n    rewrite name regex (.*)\\.127-0-0-1\\.nip\\.io ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx.svc.cluster.local answer auto\n    kubernetes cluster.local\n}\n"
    coredns_rewrite_rule: 'rewrite name regex (.*)\.127-0-0-1\.nip\.io cilium-gateway-homelab.gateway.svc.cluster.local answer auto'
  tasks:
    - ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "{{ corefile.split('\n') | reject('search', '^\\s*rewrite name regex ') | join('\n') | replace('    ready\n', '    ready\n    ' ~ coredns_rewrite_rule ~ '\n') }}"
EOF
ansible-playbook /tmp/corefile-test.yml | grep msg && rm /tmp/corefile-test.yml
Expected: exactly one rewrite line, pointing at cilium-gateway-homelab.

docs.title: Task 5: The Gateways replace ingress-nginx
docs.text:
Files: - Create: system/gateway/Chart.yaml, system/gateway/values.yaml, system/gateway/values-dev.yaml, system/gateway/templates/certificate.yaml, system/gateway/templates/gateway.yaml, system/gateway/templates/https-redirect.yaml - Delete: system/ingress-nginx/ - Modify: system/argocd/values-dev.yaml (allowlist)

Interfaces: - Consumes: ClusterIssuer letsencrypt-prod, GatewayClass cilium. - Produces: Gateways gateway/homelab (listeners http, https, ssh) and gateway/homelab-public (listener https); secret gateway/homelab-wildcard-tls.

  • Step 1: Chart and values. Create system/gateway/Chart.yaml:
apiVersion: v2
name: gateway
version: 0.0.0

system/gateway/values.yaml:

domain: khuedoan.com
# Fixed LB IPs for the Gateways; empty takes the next free address from the Cilium pool
addresses:
  homelab: ""
  homelab-public: ""

system/gateway/values-dev.yaml:

domain: 127-0-0-1.nip.io
addresses:
  # The localhost proxy (metal/Makefile) forwards 127.0.0.1:80/443 here
  homelab: 172.30.255.200
  • Step 2: Certificate. system/gateway/templates/certificate.yaml:
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: homelab-wildcard
spec:
  secretName: homelab-wildcard-tls
  dnsNames:
    - "*.{{ .Values.domain }}"
  issuerRef:
    group: cert-manager.io
    kind: ClusterIssuer
    name: letsencrypt-prod
  • Step 3: Gateways. system/gateway/templates/gateway.yaml:
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: homelab
spec:
  gatewayClassName: cilium
  {{- with .Values.addresses.homelab }}
  addresses:
    - type: IPAddress
      value: {{ . }}
  {{- end }}
  listeners:
    # Only the HTTPS redirect (templates/https-redirect.yaml)
    - name: http
      protocol: HTTP
      port: 80
      allowedRoutes:
        namespaces:
          from: Same
    - name: https
      protocol: HTTPS
      port: 443
      hostname: "*.{{ .Values.domain }}"
      tls:
        mode: Terminate
        certificateRefs:
          - name: homelab-wildcard-tls
      allowedRoutes:
        namespaces:
          from: All
    # Gitea SSH
    - name: ssh
      protocol: TCP
      port: 22
      allowedRoutes:
        namespaces:
          from: Selector
          selector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: gitea
        kinds:
          - kind: TCPRoute
---
# Published through the Cloudflare Tunnel: external-dns points public hosts at the tunnel,
# and cloudflared forwards to this Gateway only
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: homelab-public
  annotations:
    external-dns.kubernetes.io/target: homelab-tunnel.{{ .Values.domain }}
spec:
  gatewayClassName: cilium
  {{- with index .Values.addresses "homelab-public" }}
  addresses:
    - type: IPAddress
      value: {{ . }}
  {{- end }}
  listeners:
    - name: https
      protocol: HTTPS
      port: 443
      hostname: "*.{{ .Values.domain }}"
      tls:
        mode: Terminate
        certificateRefs:
          - name: homelab-wildcard-tls
      allowedRoutes:
        namespaces:
          from: All
  • Step 4: Redirect. system/gateway/templates/https-redirect.yaml:
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: https-redirect
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - name: homelab
      sectionName: http
  rules:
    - filters:
        - type: RequestRedirect
          requestRedirect:
            scheme: https
            statusCode: 301
  • Step 5: Remove ingress-nginx and switch the allowlist.
git rm -r system/ingress-nginx

In system/argocd/values-dev.yaml, replace - path: system/ingress-nginx with - path: system/gateway.

  • Step 6: Verify.

Run: 

scripts/render-chart system/gateway | yq 'select(.kind != null) | .kind + "/" + .metadata.name + " " + ((.spec.addresses // []) | map(.value) | join(","))' | grep -v -- ---
scripts/render-chart system/gateway dev | yq 'select(.kind=="Gateway") | .metadata.name + " " + ((.spec.addresses // []) | map(.value) | join(",")) + " " + (.spec.listeners | map(select(.name=="https")) | .[0].hostname)' | grep -v -- ---
grep -rn ingress-nginx system/argocd
Expected: - prod: Certificate/homelab-wildcard, Gateway/homelab, Gateway/homelab-public (no addresses), HTTPRoute/https-redirect - dev: homelab 172.30.255.200, homelab-public with no address; hostnames *.127-0-0-1.nip.io - grep prints nothing.

      readOnly: true
      optional: true
  • Step 4: zot. In platform/zot/values.yaml, replace the ingress block (including proxy-body-size) with:
  httproute:
    enabled: true
    parentRefs:
      - name: homelab
        namespace: gateway
        sectionName: https
    hostnames:
      - registry.khuedoan.com
    # Image pushes upload large blobs: no request timeout
    rules:
      - matches:
          - path:
              type: PathPrefix
              value: /
        timeouts:
          request: 0s

In platform/zot/values-dev.yaml, replace the ingress block with:

  httproute:
    hostnames:
      - registry.127-0-0-1.nip.io

and the dev-ca volume's secret: block with:

      configMap:
        name: homelab-dev-ca
        optional: true
  • Step 5: Verify.

Run: 

for c in system/argocd platform/dex platform/grafana platform/zot; do for e in prod dev; do
  echo "== $c $e"
  scripts/render-chart $c $e | yq 'select(.kind=="HTTPRoute" or .kind=="Ingress") | [.kind, .apiVersion, .metadata.name, .spec.hostnames[0], .spec.parentRefs[0].namespace + "/" + .spec.parentRefs[0].name + "/" + .spec.parentRefs[0].sectionName] | join(" ")' | grep -v -- ---
done; done
for c in system/argocd platform/dex platform/grafana platform/zot; do scripts/render-chart $c dev | grep -c 'name: homelab-dev-ca'; done
scripts/render-chart platform/zot | yq 'select(.kind=="HTTPRoute") | .spec.rules[0].timeouts.request'
Expected: one HTTPRoute gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1 <name> <host> gateway/homelab/https per render with names argocd-server, dex, grafana, zot, prod hosts on khuedoan.com and dev hosts on 127-0-0-1.nip.io; no Ingress; each dev render mentions homelab-dev-ca at least once; zot timeout 0s.

  • Step 6: Commit.
git add system/argocd platform/dex platform/grafana platform/zot
git commit -m "feat: Argo CD, Dex, Grafana and zot use HTTPRoutes and the dev CA ConfigMap"

docs.title: Task 7: Kanidm behind the Gateway with backend TLS
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: platform/kanidm/Chart.yaml, platform/kanidm/templates/kanidm.yaml, platform/kanidm/values.yaml, platform/kanidm/values-dev.yaml - Create: platform/kanidm/templates/certificate.yaml

Interfaces: - Consumes: Gateway gateway/homelab; ConfigMap homelab-dev-ca (sandbox). - Produces: HTTPRoute and BackendTLSPolicy kanidm/kanidm (created by kaniop); secret kanidm/kanidm-tls.

  • Step 1: kaniop 0.19.0. In platform/kanidm/Chart.yaml, set the kaniop dependency version: 0.19.0.

  • Step 2: Gateway in the Kanidm CR. In platform/kanidm/templates/kanidm.yaml, replace:

  # cert-manager issues the ingress certificate; Kanidm serves the same secret (kanidm-tls)
  ingress:
    ingressClassName: nginx
    annotations:
      cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-prod
      nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/backend-protocol: HTTPS

with:

  # Kanidm serves TLS itself (templates/certificate.yaml); the Gateway re-encrypts to it
  tlsSecretName: kanidm-tls
  gateway:
    parentRefs:
      - name: homelab
        namespace: gateway
        sectionName: https
    backendTlsPolicy:
      validation:
        hostname: {{ .Values.kanidm.domain }}
        {{- with .Values.kanidm.backendCA }}
        caCertificateRefs:
          - group: ""
            kind: ConfigMap
            name: {{ . }}
        {{- else }}
        wellKnownCaCertificates: System
        {{- end }}
  • Step 3: Certificate. Create platform/kanidm/templates/certificate.yaml:
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: kanidm
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
spec:
  secretName: kanidm-tls
  dnsNames:
    - {{ .Values.kanidm.domain }}
  issuerRef:
    group: cert-manager.io
    kind: ClusterIssuer
    name: letsencrypt-prod
  • Step 4: Values. In platform/kanidm/values.yaml, under kanidm, after storage: 1Gi add:
  # ConfigMap (key ca.crt) that signs Kanidm's certificate; empty trusts the system CAs (Let's Encrypt)
  backendCA: ""

In platform/kanidm/values-dev.yaml, under kanidm, after domain: auth.127-0-0-1.nip.io add:

  # The sandbox CA, distributed by trust-manager; Cilium accepts only a ConfigMap here
  backendCA: homelab-dev-ca
  • Step 5: Verify.

Run: 

for e in prod dev; do scripts/render-chart platform/kanidm $e | yq 'select(.kind=="Kanidm") | .spec.tlsSecretName, .spec.gateway' | grep -v -- ---; done
scripts/render-chart platform/kanidm | yq 'select(.kind=="Certificate") | .spec.dnsNames[0]'
scripts/render-chart platform/kanidm dev | grep -c ingress
Expected: kanidm-tls in both; prod validation hostname: auth.khuedoan.com with wellKnownCaCertificates: System; dev hostname: auth.127-0-0-1.nip.io with caCertificateRefs ConfigMap homelab-dev-ca; certificate auth.khuedoan.com; ingress count 0.

  • Step 6: Commit.
git add platform/kanidm
git commit -m "feat(kanidm): HTTPRoute with BackendTLSPolicy, own certificate, kaniop 0.19.0"

docs.title: Task 8: app-template 5 routes for the sandbox apps
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: apps/excalidraw/values.yaml, apps/excalidraw/values-dev.yaml; apps/{actualbudget,homepage,pairdrop,speedtest}/{Chart.yaml,values.yaml}; system/argocd/values-dev.yaml (allowlist) - Create: apps/{actualbudget,homepage,pairdrop,speedtest}/values-dev.yaml

Interfaces: - Produces: HTTPRoutes excalidraw/excalidraw, actualbudget/actualbudget, homepage/homepage, pairdrop/pairdrop, speedtest/speedtest.

  • Step 1: excalidraw (public in production). In apps/excalidraw/values.yaml, replace the whole ingress block with:
  route:
    main:
      annotations:
        external-dns.kubernetes.io/cloudflare-proxied: "true"
      hostnames:
        - draw.khuedoan.com
      parentRefs:
        - name: homelab-public
          namespace: gateway
          sectionName: https

Replace the whole apps/excalidraw/values-dev.yaml with:

app-template:
  route:
    main:
      # No Cloudflare Tunnel in the sandbox: attach to the LAN Gateway behind the localhost proxy.
      # Helm cannot delete the annotation across values files; an empty value is inert without external-dns.
      annotations:
        external-dns.kubernetes.io/cloudflare-proxied: ""
      hostnames:
        - draw.127-0-0-1.nip.io
      parentRefs:
        - name: homelab
          namespace: gateway
          sectionName: https

  • Step 2: Upgrade the four apps to app-template 5.3.0. In apps/{actualbudget,homepage,pairdrop,speedtest}/Chart.yaml, set version: 5.3.0.

  • Step 3: Routes. In each of the four values.yaml, replace the whole app-template.ingress block (including the proxy-body-size annotation in speedtest) with a route on homelab:

App hostname actualbudget budget.khuedoan.com homepage home.khuedoan.com pairdrop drop.khuedoan.com speedtest speedtest.khuedoan.com 
  route:
    main:
      hostnames:
        - budget.khuedoan.com
      parentRefs:
        - name: homelab
          namespace: gateway
          sectionName: https

(with each app's hostname). The route's default rule targets the main Service's primary port.

  • Step 4: Keep names that app-template 5 would change.
  • apps/actualbudget/values.yaml: under app-template.persistence.data add suffix: data (keeps PVC actualbudget-data, which make backup uses).

  • apps/homepage/values.yaml: under app-template.persistence.config, replace name: homepage-config with identifier: config (the ConfigMap is now named homepage).

  • Step 5: Sandbox hosts. Create apps/<app>/values-dev.yaml for each of the four, e.g. apps/actualbudget/values-dev.yaml:

app-template:
  route:
    main:
      hostnames:
        - budget.127-0-0-1.nip.io

(home, drop, speedtest for the others.)

  • Step 6: Allowlist. In system/argocd/values-dev.yaml, after - path: apps/excalidraw add:
              - path: apps/actualbudget
              - path: apps/homepage
              - path: apps/pairdrop
              - path: apps/speedtest
  • Step 7: Verify.

Run: 

for a in excalidraw actualbudget homepage pairdrop speedtest; do for e in prod dev; do
  scripts/render-chart apps/$a $e | yq 'select(.kind=="HTTPRoute") | [.apiVersion, .metadata.name, .spec.hostnames[0], .spec.parentRefs[0].name, .spec.rules[0].backendRefs[0].name + ":" + (.spec.rules[0].backendRefs[0].port|tostring), (.metadata.annotations // {} | tostring)] | join(" ")' | grep -v -- ---
done; done
scripts/render-chart apps/actualbudget | yq 'select(.kind=="PersistentVolumeClaim") | .metadata.name'
scripts/render-chart apps/homepage | yq 'select(.kind=="ConfigMap") | .metadata.name'
scripts/render-chart apps/homepage | yq 'select(.kind=="Deployment") | .spec.template.spec.volumes[] | select(.configMap) | .configMap.name'
Expected: - every route gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1, named after the app, backend <app>:<port> (excalidraw 80, actualbudget 5006, homepage 3000, pairdrop 3000, speedtest 3000) - excalidraw prod on homelab-public with cloudflare-proxied: "true"; excalidraw dev and all others on homelab - PVC actualbudget-data; homepage ConfigMap homepage and the Deployment mounts ConfigMap homepage.

  • Step 8: Commit.
git add apps/excalidraw apps/actualbudget apps/homepage apps/pairdrop apps/speedtest system/argocd/values-dev.yaml
git commit -m "feat(apps): HTTPRoutes with app-template 5.3.0, four more apps in the sandbox"

docs.title: Task 9: app-template 5 routes for the production-only apps
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: apps/{blog,jellyfin,ollama,paperless}/{Chart.yaml,values.yaml}

Interfaces: - Produces: HTTPRoutes blog/blog (public), jellyfin/jellyfin-{main,transmission,prowlarr,radarr,sonarr,jellyseerr}, ollama/ollama-{main,ai}, paperless/paperless.

  • Step 1: Upgrade. Set version: 5.3.0 in the four Chart.yaml.

  • Step 2: blog (public). Replace the ingress block with:

  route:
    main:
      annotations:
        external-dns.kubernetes.io/cloudflare-proxied: "true"
      hostnames:
        - www.khuedoan.com
      parentRefs:
        - name: homelab-public
          namespace: gateway
          sectionName: https

  • Step 3: paperless. Replace the ingress block with a route.main on homelab for paperless.khuedoan.com (same shape as Task 8 Step 3), and add suffix: data under persistence.data.

  • Step 4: jellyfin (one route per host; a route's hostnames apply to all its rules). Replace the ingress block with:

  route:
    main:
      hostnames:
        - jellyfin.khuedoan.com
      parentRefs: &parentRefs
        - name: homelab
          namespace: gateway
          sectionName: https
      rules:
        - backendRefs:
            - identifier: main
              port: http
    transmission:
      hostnames:
        - transmission.khuedoan.com
      parentRefs: *parentRefs
      rules:
        - backendRefs:
            - identifier: main
              port: transmission
    prowlarr:
      hostnames:
        - prowlarr.khuedoan.com
      parentRefs: *parentRefs
      rules:
        - backendRefs:
            - identifier: main
              port: prowlarr
    radarr:
      hostnames:
        - radarr.khuedoan.com
      parentRefs: *parentRefs
      rules:
        - backendRefs:
            - identifier: main
              port: radarr
    sonarr:
      hostnames:
        - sonarr.khuedoan.com
      parentRefs: *parentRefs
      rules:
        - backendRefs:
            - identifier: main
              port: sonarr
    jellyseerr:
      hostnames:
        - jellyseerr.khuedoan.com
      parentRefs: *parentRefs
      rules:
        - backendRefs:
            - identifier: main
              port: jellyseerr

and add suffix: data under persistence.data.

  • Step 5: ollama. Replace the ingress block with:
  route:
    main:
      hostnames:
        - ollama.khuedoan.com
      parentRefs: &parentRefs
        - name: homelab
          namespace: gateway
          sectionName: https
      rules:
        - backendRefs:
            - identifier: main
              port: http
    ai:
      hostnames:
        - ai.khuedoan.com
      parentRefs: *parentRefs
      rules:
        - backendRefs:
            - identifier: ui
              port: http

Under service.main add controller: main (required with two controllers) and forceRename: ollama (the UI calls http://ollama:11434). Add suffix: data under persistence.data.

  • Step 6: Verify.

Run: 

for a in blog jellyfin ollama paperless; do
  scripts/render-chart apps/$a | yq 'select(.kind=="HTTPRoute") | [.apiVersion, .metadata.name, .spec.hostnames[0], .spec.parentRefs[0].name, .spec.rules[0].backendRefs[0].name + ":" + (.spec.rules[0].backendRefs[0].port|tostring)] | join(" ")' | grep -v -- ---
  scripts/render-chart apps/$a | yq 'select(.kind=="PersistentVolumeClaim" or .kind=="Service") | .kind + "/" + .metadata.name' | grep -v -- ---
done
Expected: - blog on homelab-public, everything else on homelab, all v1 - jellyfin: 6 routes to jellyfin:8096/9091/9696/7878/8989/5055; ollama: ollama-main → ollama:11434, ollama-ai → ollama-ui:8080 - PVCs jellyfin-data, ollama-data, paperless-data; Services ollama and ollama-ui.

git add apps/blog apps/jellyfin apps/ollama apps/paperless

docs.title: Task 10: gitea 12.7.0 with HTTP and SSH routes, in the sandbox
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: platform/gitea/Chart.yaml, platform/gitea/values.yaml, platform/gitea/templates/config-job.yaml, platform/gitea/templates/config-source.yaml, system/argocd/values-dev.yaml - Create: platform/gitea/templates/tcproute.yaml, platform/gitea/values-dev.yaml

Interfaces: - Consumes: Gateway listeners homelab/https and homelab/ssh. - Produces: HTTPRoute gitea/gitea (smoke), TCPRoute gitea/gitea-ssh to Service gitea-ssh:22.

  • Step 1: Upgrade. In platform/gitea/Chart.yaml, set version: 12.7.0.

  • Step 2: HTTP route. In platform/gitea/values.yaml, replace the gitea.ingress block with:

  gatewayAPI:
    enabled: true
    core:
      httpRoute:
        enabled: true
        # The Gateway terminates TLS, so ROOT_URL uses https
        tls: true
        parentRefs:
          - name: homelab
            namespace: gateway
            sectionName: https
        hostnames:
          - git.khuedoan.com
  • Step 3: SSH route. The chart's own tcpRoute renders v1alpha2, which the v1.6 CRDs do not serve. Create platform/gitea/templates/tcproute.yaml:
# The chart's tcpRoute is still v1alpha2
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: TCPRoute
metadata:
  name: gitea-ssh
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - name: homelab
      namespace: gateway
      sectionName: ssh
  rules:
    - backendRefs:
        - name: gitea-ssh
          port: 22
  • Step 4: Optional config job. Wrap templates/config-job.yaml and templates/config-source.yaml each in:
{{- if .Values.configJob.enabled }}
...existing content...
{{- end }}

and append to platform/gitea/values.yaml:

# Creates organizations and migrates repositories (files/config/config.yaml)
configJob:
  enabled: true
  • Step 5: Sandbox values. Create platform/gitea/values-dev.yaml:
gitea:
  gatewayAPI:
    core:
      httpRoute:
        hostnames:
          - git.127-0-0-1.nip.io
  gitea:
    config:
      server:
        ROOT_URL: https://git.127-0-0-1.nip.io
      # Small single-pod setup: SQLite and in-memory cache, session and queue
      database:
        DB_TYPE: sqlite3
      cache:
        ADAPTER: memory
      session:
        PROVIDER: memory
      queue:
        TYPE: level
  postgresql-ha:
    enabled: false
  valkey-cluster:
    enabled: false
# The config job migrates upstream's repositories from GitHub, including mirrors owned by a user
# the sandbox does not have
configJob:
  enabled: false

  • Step 6: Allowlist. In system/argocd/values-dev.yaml, after - path: platform/zot add - path: platform/gitea.

  • Step 7: Verify.

Run: 

for e in prod dev; do echo "== $e"
  scripts/render-chart platform/gitea $e | yq 'select(.kind=="HTTPRoute" or .kind=="TCPRoute" or .kind=="Job" or .kind=="StatefulSet" or .kind=="Ingress") | [.kind, .apiVersion, .metadata.name, (.spec.hostnames // [""])[0], (.spec.parentRefs[0].sectionName // "")] | join(" ")' | grep -v -- ---
done
scripts/render-chart platform/gitea dev | yq 'select(.metadata.name=="gitea-inline-config") | .stringData.database'
Expected: - prod: HTTPRoute v1 gitea git.khuedoan.com https, TCPRoute v1 gitea-ssh ssh, the config Job, StatefulSets for postgresql-ha and valkey-cluster - dev: the two routes (host git.127-0-0-1.nip.io), no Job, no StatefulSet - database DB_TYPE=sqlite3.

  • Step 8: Commit.
git add platform/gitea system/argocd/values-dev.yaml
git commit -m "feat(gitea): 12.7.0 with HTTP and SSH routes, SQLite in the sandbox"

docs.title: Task 11: woodpecker and matrix routes
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: platform/woodpecker/Chart.yaml, platform/woodpecker/values.yaml, apps/matrix/Chart.yaml, apps/matrix/values.yaml - Create: platform/woodpecker/templates/httproute.yaml, apps/matrix/templates/httproute.yaml

Interfaces: - Produces: HTTPRoutes woodpecker/woodpecker-server, matrix/elementweb (public), matrix/dendrite.

  • Step 1: woodpecker 3.7.5. Set version: 3.7.5 in platform/woodpecker/Chart.yaml. In values.yaml, delete woodpecker.server.ingress and append:
route:
  hostname: ci.khuedoan.com

Create platform/woodpecker/templates/httproute.yaml:

# The woodpecker chart has no Gateway API support
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: woodpecker-server
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}

  parentRefs:
    - name: homelab

route:
  # Published through the Cloudflare Tunnel
  elementHostname: chat.khuedoan.com
  # LAN only, as before
  dendriteHostname: matrix.khuedoan.com

Create apps/matrix/templates/httproute.yaml:

    external-dns.kubernetes.io/cloudflare-proxied: "true"

  parentRefs:
    - name: homelab-public

    - {{ .Values.route.elementHostname }}

---

  parentRefs:
    - name: homelab

  hostnames:
    - {{ .Values.route.dendriteHostname }}

    - backendRefs:
        - name: {{ .Release.Name }}-dendrite

  • Step 3: Verify.

Run: 

for c in platform/woodpecker apps/matrix; do
  scripts/render-chart $c | yq 'select(.kind=="HTTPRoute" or .kind=="Ingress") | [.kind, .metadata.name, .spec.hostnames[0], .spec.parentRefs[0].name, .spec.rules[0].backendRefs[0].name + ":" + (.spec.rules[0].backendRefs[0].port|tostring)] | join(" ")' | grep -v -- ---
  scripts/render-chart $c | yq 'select(.kind=="Service") | .metadata.name' | grep -v -- ---
done
Expected: woodpecker-server ci.khuedoan.com homelab woodpecker-server:80, elementweb chat.khuedoan.com homelab-public matrix-elementweb:80, dendrite matrix.khuedoan.com homelab matrix-dendrite:8008; the backend Services exist in the same render; no Ingress.

git add platform/woodpecker apps/matrix

docs.title: Task 12: cloudflared and external-dns for the public Gateway
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: system/cloudflared/Chart.yaml, system/cloudflared/values.yaml, system/external-dns/Chart.yaml, system/external-dns/values.yaml

Interfaces: - Consumes: Service gateway/cilium-gateway-homelab-public; Gateway annotation external-dns.kubernetes.io/target.

  • Step 1: cloudflared on app-template 5.3.0. Set version: 5.3.0 in system/cloudflared/Chart.yaml. In values.yaml:
  • replace the tunnel ingress rule:
            - hostname: '*.khuedoan.com'
              service: https://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx
              originRequest:
                noTLSVerify: true

with:

            # Only the public Gateway: apps on the LAN Gateway stay off the internet
            - hostname: '*.khuedoan.com'
              service: https://cilium-gateway-homelab-public.gateway
              originRequest:
                noTLSVerify: true
                # The Gateway's listener needs the requested host as SNI
                matchSNItoHost: true

  • under persistence.config, replace name: cloudflared-config with identifier: config (app-template 5 names the ConfigMap cloudflared).

  • Step 2: external-dns 1.23.0. Set version: 1.23.0 in system/external-dns/Chart.yaml. Replace system/external-dns/values.yaml with:

external-dns:
  provider:
    name: cloudflare
  # Routes attached to a Gateway; the DNS target comes from the Gateway (homelab: its LB IP,
  # homelab-public: the Cloudflare Tunnel)
  sources:
    - gateway-httproute
  # Never delete records (the previous chart default; the chart now requires it)
  policy: upsert-only
  txtOwnerId: homelab
  env:
    - name: CF_API_TOKEN
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: cloudflare-api-token
          key: value
  extraArgs:
    - --annotation-filter=external-dns.kubernetes.io/exclude notin (true)
  interval: 5m
  triggerLoopOnEvent: true
  metrics:
    enabled: true
    serviceMonitor:
      enabled: true
  • Step 3: Verify.

Run: 

scripts/render-chart system/cloudflared | yq 'select(.kind=="ConfigMap") | .metadata.name, .data."config.yaml"'
scripts/render-chart system/cloudflared | yq 'select(.kind=="Deployment") | .spec.template.spec.volumes[] | select(.configMap) | .configMap.name'
scripts/render-chart system/external-dns | yq 'select(.kind=="Deployment") | .spec.template.spec.containers[0].args'
scripts/render-chart system/external-dns | yq 'select(.kind=="ClusterRole") | .rules[] | select(.apiGroups[0]=="gateway.networking.k8s.io") | .resources[0]'
Expected: ConfigMap cloudflared with service https://cilium-gateway-homelab-public.gateway and matchSNItoHost: true, mounted by the Deployment; external-dns args include --source=gateway-httproute, --policy=upsert-only, --provider=cloudflare and the new annotation filter; RBAC for gateways and httproutes.

  • Step 4: Commit.
git add system/cloudflared system/external-dns
git commit -m "feat: cloudflared and external-dns use the public Gateway"

docs.title: Task 13: Scripts, docs and the pre-PR checks
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: scripts/get-status, scripts/get-dns-config, docs/installation/sandbox.md, docs/reference/architecture/networking.md, docs/reference/architecture/overview.md, docs/concepts/certificate-management.md, docs/how-to-guides/expose-services-to-the-internet.md, README.md, CLAUDE.md

  • Step 1: Scripts. In scripts/get-status, replace kubectl get ingress --all-namespaces with:
kubectl get gateways --namespace gateway
kubectl get httproutes,tcproutes --all-namespaces

Replace the kubectl line of scripts/get-dns-config with:

# One line per route hostname: the address of the Gateway the route is attached to
kubectl get gateways,httproutes --all-namespaces --output json | jq -r '
  (.items | map(select(.kind == "Gateway")) | map({key: (.metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name), value: (.status.addresses[0].value // "pending")}) | from_entries) as $addr
  | .items[] | select(.kind == "HTTPRoute") | . as $r
  | ($r.spec.parentRefs[0] | (.namespace // $r.metadata.namespace) + "/" + .name) as $gw
  | ($r.spec.hostnames // [])[] | "\($addr[$gw] // "pending") \(.)"'

docs.title: Sandbox SSO (1c) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Grafana, ArgoCD and zot log people in through Dex → Kanidm, grant permissions from the homelab-* groups, keep a local break-glass account each, and the sandbox tests prove every role.

Architecture: - Groups. Kanidm emits a custom homelab_groups claim with short group names. Dex maps it to groups, so every app sees ["homelab-<x>"] in both sandbox and production. The Kanidm client also prefers short usernames. - Generated secrets. New client and admin secrets come from the 1b global-secrets generator. - Dev CA trust. In the sandbox, each Go app trusts the dev CA through SSL_CERT_DIR plus its own ingress certificate's ca.crt. - Tests. A shared chromedp login helper drives each app's SSO entry point; the tests then call the app's API with the session cookies.

Tech Stack: Grafana chart 13.5.0 (Grafana 13.2.3, repo https://grafana-community.github.io/helm-charts), argo-cd chart 10.10.3 (Argo CD 3.5.5), zot chart 0.1.128 (zot v2.1.22), kaniop 0.18.0, Dex 2.46.0, ESO 2.12.0, Go + chromedp v0.16.0.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-sandbox-sso-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Workflow:
  • Work on branch dev, and push to origin dev when a task says so (the sandbox syncs from it).
  • One concern per commit. Commits end with Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>.
  • Run everything inside the dev shell. For kubectl, export KUBECONFIG=$PWD/metal/kubeconfig.yaml.
  • Chart.lock is gitignored.
  • Versions: current stable, pinned exactly (verified 2026-10-13): Grafana chart 13.5.0 from https://grafana-community.github.io/helm-charts, zot chart 0.1.128, argo-cd chart 10.10.3 (unchanged).
  • Helm values: Helm replaces lists and cannot delete keys across values files; dev overrides restate whole lists. A null only removes a chart default.
  • Groups:
  • Names: homelab-admins, homelab-editors, homelab-users.
  • Claim: the groups claim from Dex must be exactly ["homelab-<x>"].
  • Username: Kanidm short name, e.g. dev-admin, via preferShortUsername: true.
  • Dev hosts: grafana.127-0-0-1.nip.io, argocd.127-0-0-1.nip.io, registry.127-0-0-1.nip.io, dex.127-0-0-1.nip.io, auth.127-0-0-1.nip.io. Production keeps the domains already in values.yaml.
  • Dex static clients:
  • grafana-sso, argocd, zot, plus smoke (dev only)
  • secrets dex.grafana, dex.argocd, dex.zot, dex.smoke (key client_secret)
  • env vars GRAFANA_SSO_CLIENT_SECRET, ARGOCD_CLIENT_SECRET, ZOT_CLIENT_SECRET, SMOKE_CLIENT_SECRET
  • Local accounts:
  • Grafana admin, password from grafana.admin (key password)
  • ArgoCD admin (initial admin secret)
  • zot htpasswd ci, password from registry.ci (key password)
  • Dev CA trust (dev values only): mount the app's ingress TLS secret key ca.crt at /etc/homelab-dev-ca/ca.crt, and set SSL_CERT_DIR=/etc/ssl/certs:/etc/homelab-dev-ca.
  • Test conventions:
  • Identity and SSO tests connect to sandboxIngress (172.30.255.200) directly.
  • Credentials and tokens never go to test logs (quietKanidmNamespace or similar).
  • Every TestSSO* calls waitForIdentityStack first.
  • Make: make dev runs the smoke filter Smoke|Identity|SSO.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. Fresh-cluster bootstrap. The ArgoCD chart now contains an ExternalSecret, but ESO's CRDs do not exist when system/bootstrap.yml applies ArgoCD. → Task 4 guards the template with .Capabilities.APIVersions.Has and checks an offline render has no ExternalSecret; Task 7 rebuilds from scratch.
  2. zot pods with auth enabled. Probes must stay green (they use /livez//readyz), and anonymous registry calls must get 401 rather than 200 from a lingering anonymous policy. → Task 5 waits for rollout and asserts anonymous 401.
  3. Rerun make dev. zot API-key creation runs every time, so labels must not collide; Grafana and ArgoCD logins must work with stored credentials. → Task 5 uses a timestamped key label; Task 7 reruns.
  4. Production RBAC defaults. A typo in policy.csv or a non-empty policy.default would silently give every SSO user access. → Task 4 asserts the prod render has policy.default: '' and the exact g, lines.
  5. Dex static client lists. Dev must restate grafana-sso, argocd, zot and smoke; forgetting one breaks that app only in the sandbox. → Task 2 asserts the client ids in both renders.

docs.text:
Files: - Modify: platform/dex/templates/kanidm-client.yaml, platform/dex/values.yaml, platform/dex/values-dev.yaml - Modify: test/identity_test.go

Interfaces: - Produces: the Dex ID token for a dev-* account has groups == ["homelab-<x>"] and preferred_username == "<account>".

  • Step 1: Write the failing assertion

In test/identity_test.go, inside TestIdentityLogin's subtest, replace

            assert.True(t, hasGroup(claims, account.group), "groups %v lack %s", claims["groups"], account.group)

with

            assert.Equal(t, []any{account.group}, claims["groups"])
            assert.Equal(t, account.name, claims["preferred_username"])
  • Step 2: Run it against the sandbox and watch it fail

Run: cd test && ENV=dev go test -run 'TestIdentityLogin/dev-admin' -count=1 ./... Expected: FAIL. groups holds SPNs, UUIDs and idm_* entries, and preferred_username is dev-admin@auth.127-0-0-1.nip.io.

  • Step 3: Kanidm client: claim map and short usernames

In platform/dex/templates/kanidm-client.yaml, add under spec: (after disableConsentPrompt: true):

  # Short usernames (dev-admin rather than dev-admin@<domain>)
  preferShortUsername: true
  # Short, domain-free group names for every app, mapped to `groups` by Dex
  claimMap:
    - name: homelab_groups
      joinStrategy: array
      valuesMap:
        {{- range list "homelab-admins" "homelab-editors" "homelab-users" }}
        - group: {{ . }}
          values:
            - {{ . }}
        {{- end }}

          overrideClaimMapping: true

docs.text:
Files: - Create: test/sso_test.go - Modify: test/identity_helpers_test.go (shared browser login) - Modify: platform/grafana/Chart.yaml, platform/grafana/values.yaml - Create: platform/grafana/values-dev.yaml, platform/grafana/templates/admin-secret.yaml - Modify: system/argocd/values-dev.yaml (allowlist)

Interfaces: - Consumes: Task 1 groups, Task 2 grafana.admin; 1b helpers (ensureCredentials, clock, insecureClient, sandboxIngress, waitForIdentityStack, quietKanidmNamespace, testAccounts). - Produces: - newBrowser(t) (context.Context, func()) - kanidmLogin(t, ctx, account string, c credentials, password string) - appLogin(t, account string, c credentials, startURL, appHost string) []*http.Cookie - getJSON(t, method, target string, cookies []*http.Cookie, user, pass string, body, out any) int - TestSSOGrafana

  • Step 1: Refactor the browser plumbing in test/identity_helpers_test.go

Replace the whole browserAuthorize function with these four functions (behaviour of browserAuthorize is unchanged):

// newBrowser starts headless chromium that resolves sandbox hosts to the ingress LB IP.
func newBrowser(t *testing.T) (context.Context, func()) {
    opts := append(chromedp.DefaultExecAllocatorOptions[:],
        chromedp.Flag("ignore-certificate-errors", true),
        chromedp.Flag("host-resolver-rules", "MAP *.127-0-0-1.nip.io "+sandboxIngress),
        // NixOS-WSL exports an LD_LIBRARY_PATH built for a newer glibc than the dev shell's chromium
        chromedp.Env("LD_LIBRARY_PATH="),
    )
    allocCtx, cancelAlloc := chromedp.NewExecAllocator(context.Background(), opts...)
    ctx, cancelBrowser := chromedp.NewContext(allocCtx)
    ctx, cancelTimeout := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 3*time.Minute)
    // Start the browser on the long-lived context; the first Run owns the browser's lifetime
    require.NoError(t, chromedp.Run(ctx, network.Enable()))
    return ctx, func() { cancelTimeout(); cancelBrowser(); cancelAlloc() }
}

// browserStep runs actions with a 30 s timeout and reports the page on failure.
func browserStep(t *testing.T, ctx context.Context, name, account string, actions ...chromedp.Action) {
    stepCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 30*time.Second)
    defer cancel()
    if err := chromedp.Run(stepCtx, actions...); err != nil {
        var location, text string
        _ = chromedp.Run(ctx, chromedp.Location(&location), chromedp.Evaluate(`document.body ? document.body.innerText.slice(0, 500) : ""`, &text))
        require.NoError(t, err, "login step %q for %s at %s:\n%s", name, account, location, text)
    }
}

// kanidmLogin completes Kanidm's login form, which the browser must already show.
// Kanidm asks for the TOTP code before the password.
func kanidmLogin(t *testing.T, ctx context.Context, account string, c credentials, password string) {
    browserStep(t, ctx, "username", account, chromedp.SendKeys(`input#username`, account+"\n"), chromedp.WaitVisible(`input#totp`))
    browserStep(t, ctx, "totp", account, chromedp.SendKeys(`input#totp`, clock.code(t, account, c)+"\n"), chromedp.WaitVisible(`input#password`))
    browserStep(t, ctx, "password", account, chromedp.SendKeys(`input#password`, password+"\n"))
}

// browserAuthorize logs in through Dex and Kanidm with the given password. It returns the code sent to
// the smoke client, or an empty code and the text of the page the browser ended on.
func browserAuthorize(t *testing.T, account string, c credentials, password string) (string, string) {
    ctx, cancel := newBrowser(t)
    defer cancel()

    codes := make(chan string, 1)
    chromedp.ListenTarget(ctx, func(ev any) {
        if e, ok := ev.(*network.EventRequestWillBeSent); ok && strings.HasPrefix(e.Request.URL, smokeRedirect) {
            if u, err := url.Parse(e.Request.URL); err == nil && u.Query().Get("code") != "" {
                select {
                case codes <- u.Query().Get("code"):
                default:
                }
            }
        }
    })

    authURL := dexURL + "/auth?" + url.Values{
        "client_id":     {"smoke"},
        "redirect_uri":  {smokeRedirect},
        "response_type": {"code"},
        "scope":         {"openid email profile groups"},
        "state":         {"identity-test"},
    }.Encode()
    browserStep(t, ctx, "open", account, chromedp.Navigate(authURL), chromedp.WaitVisible(`input#username`))
    kanidmLogin(t, ctx, account, c, password)

    select {
    case code := <-codes:
        return code, ""
    case <-time.After(30 * time.Second):
        var text string
        require.NoError(t, chromedp.Run(ctx, chromedp.Evaluate(`document.body ? document.body.innerText : ""`, &text)))
        return "", text
    }
}

// appLogin opens an app's SSO entry point, logs in through Dex and Kanidm, waits until the browser is back
// on appHost (outside any callback or login path) and returns the cookies the app set.
func appLogin(t *testing.T, account string, c credentials, startURL, appHost string) []*http.Cookie {
    ctx, cancel := newBrowser(t)
    defer cancel()

    browserStep(t, ctx, "open", account, chromedp.Navigate(startURL), chromedp.WaitVisible(`input#username`))
    kanidmLogin(t, ctx, account, c, c.Password)

    require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        var location string
        if chromedp.Run(ctx, chromedp.Location(&location)) != nil {
            return false
        }
        u, err := url.Parse(location)
        return err == nil && u.Host == appHost && !strings.Contains(u.Path, "callback") && !strings.Contains(u.Path, "/login")
    }, 30*time.Second, 500*time.Millisecond, "%s did not return to %s", account, appHost)

    var cookies []*http.Cookie
    require.NoError(t, chromedp.Run(ctx, chromedp.ActionFunc(func(ctx context.Context) error {
        got, err := network.GetCookies().WithURLs([]string{"https://" + appHost + "/"}).Do(ctx)
        for _, c := range got {
            cookies = append(cookies, &http.Cookie{Name: c.Name, Value: c.Value})
        }
        return err
    })))
    require.NotEmpty(t, cookies, "no session cookies from %s", appHost)
    return cookies
}

// getJSON sends a request with cookies or basic auth, decodes a JSON body into out (if not nil) and returns the status.
func getJSON(t *testing.T, method, target string, cookies []*http.Cookie, user, pass string, body any, out any) int {
    var reader io.Reader
    if body != nil {
        payload, err := json.Marshal(body)
        require.NoError(t, err)
        reader = bytes.NewReader(payload)
    }
    req, err := http.NewRequest(method, target, reader)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    if body != nil {
        req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
    }
    for _, c := range cookies {
        req.AddCookie(c)
    }
    if user != "" {
        req.SetBasicAuth(user, pass)
    }
    resp, err := insecureClient.Do(req)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    defer resp.Body.Close()
    raw, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    if out != nil && resp.StatusCode < 300 {
        require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(raw, out), "%s %s: %s", method, target, raw)
    }
    return resp.StatusCode
}

    argocdHost   = "argocd.127-0-0-1.nip.io"
    registryHost = "registry.127-0-0-1.nip.io"

func skipUnlessSandbox(t *testing.T) {
    if os.Getenv("ENV") != "dev" {
        t.Skip("SSO tests run against the sandbox only")
    }
    waitForIdentityStack(t)
}

// waitForApp blocks until the app answers on its sandbox host.
func waitForApp(t *testing.T, target string) {
    require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        resp, err := insecureClient.Get(target)
        if err != nil {
            return false
        }
        resp.Body.Close()
        return resp.StatusCode < 500
    }, 20*time.Minute, 15*time.Second, "%s is not ready", target)
}

// secretValue reads one key of a Secret without logging it.
func secretValue(t *testing.T, namespace, name, key string) string {
    options := k8s.NewKubectlOptions("", "", namespace)
    options.Logger = logger.Discard
    return string(k8s.GetSecret(t, options, name).Data[key])
}

func TestSSOGrafana(t *testing.T) {
    skipUnlessSandbox(t)
    base := "https://" + grafanaHost
    waitForApp(t, base+"/api/health")

    expected := map[string]struct {
        role         string
        grafanaAdmin bool
    }{
        "dev-admin":  {"Admin", true},
        "dev-editor": {"Editor", false},
        "dev-viewer": {"Viewer", false},
    }
    for account, want := range expected {
        t.Run(account, func(t *testing.T) {
            cookies := appLogin(t, account, ensureCredentials(t, account), base+"/login/generic_oauth", grafanaHost)

            var user struct {
                Login          string `json:"login"`
                IsGrafanaAdmin bool   `json:"isGrafanaAdmin"`
            }
            require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, getJSON(t, "GET", base+"/api/user", cookies, "", "", nil, &user))
            assert.Equal(t, account, user.Login)
            assert.Equal(t, want.grafanaAdmin, user.IsGrafanaAdmin)

            var orgs []struct {
                Role string `json:"role"`
            }
            require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, getJSON(t, "GET", base+"/api/user/orgs", cookies, "", "", nil, &orgs))
            require.Len(t, orgs, 1)
            assert.Equal(t, want.role, orgs[0].Role)
        })
    }

    t.Run("local-admin", func(t *testing.T) {
        password := secretValue(t, "grafana", "grafana-admin", "admin-password")
        assert.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, getJSON(t, "GET", base+"/api/user", nil, "admin", password, nil, nil))
    })
}

func TestSSOArgoCD(t *testing.T) {
    skipUnlessSandbox(t)
    base := "https://" + argocdHost
    waitForApp(t, base+"/api/version")

    type check struct{ resource, action, object string }
    sync := check{"applications", "sync", "default/excalidraw"}
    del := check{"applications", "delete", "default/excalidraw"}
    exec := check{"exec", "create", "default/excalidraw"}
    expected := map[string]map[check]string{
        "dev-admin":  {sync: "yes", del: "yes", exec: "yes"},
        "dev-editor": {sync: "yes", del: "no", exec: "yes"},
        "dev-viewer": {sync: "no", del: "no", exec: "no"},
    }
    for account, checks := range expected {
        t.Run(account, func(t *testing.T) {
            cookies := appLogin(t, account, ensureCredentials(t, account), base+"/auth/login", argocdHost)
            for c, want := range checks {
                var answer struct {
                    Value string `json:"value"`
                }
                require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, getJSON(t, "GET", base+"/api/v1/account/can-i/"+c.resource+"/"+c.action+"/"+c.object, cookies, "", "", nil, &answer))
                assert.Equal(t, want, answer.Value, "%s %s %s", c.resource, c.action, c.object)
            }
        })
    }

    t.Run("local-admin", func(t *testing.T) {
        password := secretValue(t, "argocd", "argocd-initial-admin-secret", "password")
        var session struct {
            Token string `json:"token"`
        }
        require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, getJSON(t, "POST", base+"/api/v1/session", nil, "", "", map[string]string{"username": "admin", "password": password}, &session))
        assert.NotEmpty(t, session.Token)
    })
}

func TestSSOZot(t *testing.T) {
    skipUnlessSandbox(t)
    base := "https://" + registryHost
    waitForApp(t, base+"/livez")
    upload := base + "/v2/sso-test/blobs/uploads/"

    expectedUpload := map[string]int{
        "dev-admin":  http.StatusAccepted,
        "dev-editor": http.StatusAccepted,
        "dev-viewer": http.StatusForbidden,
    }
    for account, want := range expectedUpload {
        t.Run(account, func(t *testing.T) {
            cookies := appLogin(t, account, ensureCredentials(t, account), base+"/zot/auth/login?provider=oidc", registryHost)

            var key struct {
                APIKey string `json:"apiKey"`
            }
            label := fmt.Sprintf("sso-test-%d", time.Now().UnixNano())
            require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, getJSON(t, "POST", base+"/zot/auth/apikey", cookies, "", "", map[string]any{"label": label, "scopes": []string{}}, &key))
            require.NotEmpty(t, key.APIKey)

            assert.Equal(t, want, getJSON(t, "POST", upload, nil, account, key.APIKey, nil, nil))
            assert.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, getJSON(t, "GET", base+"/v2/_catalog", nil, account, key.APIKey, nil, nil))
        })
    }

    t.Run("ci", func(t *testing.T) {
        password := secretValue(t, "global-secrets", "registry.ci", "password")
        assert.Equal(t, http.StatusAccepted, getJSON(t, "POST", upload, nil, "ci", password, nil, nil))
    })

    t.Run("anonymous", func(t *testing.T) {
        assert.Equal(t, http.StatusUnauthorized, getJSON(t, "GET", base+"/v2/_catalog", nil, "", "", nil, nil))
    })
}
