docs.title: Compact apps layout (step 4) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Turn the 11 app-template wrapper charts under apps/ into apps/<name>.yaml values files deployed by an ApplicationSet apps that pins app-template once and passes global.domain and global.publicGateway, without changing what gets deployed.

Architecture: A second ApplicationSet in system/argocd (git files generator, multi-source: app-template chart + $values ref) creates one Application per file. scripts/render-chart renders an app file the same way, reading the chart and parameters from the ApplicationSet values. Every converted app is checked against a baseline render of its old wrapper chart.

Tech Stack: Argo CD ApplicationSet (argocd-apps chart 2.0.6, goTemplate), app-template 5.3.0, Helm, yq, Python (comparison script, not committed).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-apps-layout-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Branch feat/apps-layout (spec committed there). PR into dev; merge only with the user's go-ahead. Commits end with: 
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01GZDRNK1oUcGXXSC3R6dhN2
  • Run inside the dev shell. Never rm with variables or inside sh -c (the harness blocks it); use literal paths.
  • app-template 5.3.0, pinned only in the ApplicationSet apps (prod and dev sources).
  • Parameters: prod global.domain=khuedoan.com, global.publicGateway=homelab-public; sandbox global.domain=127-0-0-1.nip.io, global.publicGateway=homelab.
  • Application name = Helm release = namespace = file name without .yaml.
  • Domain templating: <host>.khuedoan.com → <host>.{{ .Values.global.domain }} for this homelab's own hosts (routes, env, homepage links). Keep literal: the blog image registry.khuedoan.com/blog, homelab.khuedoan.com (upstream's docs site), horus.khuedoan.com (a WireGuard peer), github.com/khuedoan/..., peer comments.
  • Public apps use parentRefs[].name: '{{ .Values.global.publicGateway }}' (excalidraw, blog). matrix stays apps/matrix/ (chart, synced by root).
  • ExternalSecrets through app-template set target.deletionPolicy: Retain (the ESO default the old templates had; app-template defaults to Delete).
  • Workspace for baselines and the comparison script: .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-14-apps-layout/ (git-ignored).

docs.text:
1. Fields app-template does not template: a literal {{ .Values.global.domain }} or {{ .Values.global.publicGateway }} in a rendered object. → every task's comparison shows the substituted value; Task 7 greps renders for {{ .Values.
  2. Silent defaults of app-template 5 for apps moving from 3.x: tailscale and wireguard get automountServiceAccountToken: false and a ServiceAccount. tailscale needs the token (TS_KUBE_SECRET). → Task 6 sets it at pod level and checks the render.
  3. ESO templates inside externalSecrets: app-template does not template externalSecrets.*.target, so wireguard's backtick escape must go. → Task 6 compares wg0.conf with the baseline.
  4. ApplicationSet handover on the running sandbox: root deletes the five apps' resources, then apps recreates them. → Task 9 checks Applications and reruns make dev.
  5. Production-only apps (blog, jellyfin, ollama, paperless, tailscale, wireguard) are covered only by render comparison. → expected differences are listed per task; anything else is a bug.

import sys, yaml
docs = [d for d in yaml.safe_load_all(open(sys.argv[1])) if d]

docs.title: Task 2: scripts/render-chart renders app files
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: scripts/render-chart

Interfaces: - Consumes: .argocd-apps.applicationsets.apps.template.spec.sources[0] in system/argocd/values.yaml / values-dev.yaml (Task 3). - Produces: scripts/render-chart apps/<name>.yaml [env].

  • Step 1: Show it fails today: scripts/render-chart apps/excalidraw/values.yaml → Expected: an error (it expects a chart directory).

  • Step 2: Implement. Replace scripts/render-chart with:

#!/bin/sh
# Render a component the same way ArgoCD does.
# Usage: scripts/render-chart <chart-dir> [env]   wrapper chart: values.yaml, then values-<env>.yaml if it exists
#        scripts/render-chart apps/<name>.yaml [env]   app file: app-template with the ApplicationSet "apps" parameters
set -eu
target="$1"
env="${2:-prod}"
argocd=system/argocd
set --
# ArgoCD passes the cluster's API versions; charts pick Gateway API versions from them
set -- "$@" --api-versions gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
for kind in Gateway HTTPRoute TCPRoute BackendTLSPolicy ReferenceGrant; do
  set -- "$@" --api-versions "gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1/$kind"
done

if [ -f "$target" ]; then
  name="$(basename "$target" .yaml)"
  # The sandbox restates the ApplicationSet source in values-dev.yaml
  source_of() {
    query=".argocd-apps.applicationsets.apps.template.spec.sources[0]$1"
    if [ "$env" != prod ] && [ "$(yq "$query" "$argocd/values-$env.yaml" 2>/dev/null)" != null ]; then
      yq "$query" "$argocd/values-$env.yaml"
    else
      yq "$query" "$argocd/values.yaml"
    fi
  }
  for parameter in $(source_of '.helm.parameters[] | .name + "=" + .value'); do
    set -- "$@" --set-string "$parameter"
  done
  exec helm template "$name" "$(source_of .chart)" --repo "$(source_of .repoURL)" \
    --version "$(source_of .targetRevision)" --namespace "$name" --include-crds -f "$target" "$@"
fi

name="$(basename "$target")"
[ -f "$target/values.yaml" ] && set -- "$@" -f "$target/values.yaml"
[ "$env" != prod ] && [ -f "$target/values-$env.yaml" ] && set -- "$@" -f "$target/values-$env.yaml"
helm dependency update "$target" >/dev/null
helm template "$name" "$target" --namespace "$name" --include-crds "$@"

  • Step 3: Verify the chart path still works: scripts/render-chart system/gateway dev | yq 'select(.kind=="Gateway") | .metadata.name' → homelab, homelab-public; shellcheck scripts/render-chart clean. (The file path is verified after Task 3.)

  • Step 4: Commit: git commit -m "build: render-chart renders app-template app files".

docs.title: Task 3: ApplicationSet apps
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: system/argocd/values.yaml, system/argocd/values-dev.yaml, system/argocd/values-seed.yaml

Interfaces: - Produces: ApplicationSet apps (goTemplate) generating Applications named after apps/*.yaml.

  • Step 1: Prod. In system/argocd/values.yaml, change root's syncPolicy: to syncPolicy: &syncPolicy, and append under argocd-apps.applicationsets:
    # One Application per app-template values file apps/<name>.yaml (apps/matrix/ is a chart, synced by root)
    apps:
      namespace: argocd
      goTemplate: true
      goTemplateOptions:
        - missingkey=error
      generators:
        - git:
            repoURL: *repoURL
            revision: *revision
            files:
              - path: apps/*.yaml
      template:
        metadata:
          name: '{{ .path.filename | trimSuffix ".yaml" }}'
        spec:
          destination:
            name: in-cluster
            namespace: '{{ .path.filename | trimSuffix ".yaml" }}'
          project: default  # TODO
          sources:
            - repoURL: https://bjw-s-labs.github.io/helm-charts
              chart: app-template
              targetRevision: 5.3.0
              helm:
                releaseName: '{{ .path.filename | trimSuffix ".yaml" }}'
                valueFiles:
                  - '$values/apps/{{ .path.filename }}'
                # App files template hosts as <app>.{{ .Values.global.domain }}; public apps attach to
                # the Gateway named by global.publicGateway
                parameters:
                  - name: global.domain
                    value: khuedoan.com
                  - name: global.publicGateway
                    value: homelab-public
            - repoURL: *repoURL
              targetRevision: *revision
              ref: values
          syncPolicy: *syncPolicy

              - path: apps/pairdrop.yaml

docs.title: Task 6: Convert paperless, tailscale, wireguard
docs.text:
Files: - Create: apps/{paperless,tailscale,wireguard}.yaml; Delete: apps/{paperless,tailscale,wireguard}/

  • Step 1: paperless. Extract; template paperless. in the route and PAPERLESS_URL: 'https://paperless.{{ .Values.global.domain }}'; append (replaces templates/secret.yaml):
externalSecrets:
  secret:
    forceRename: paperless-secret
    secretStoreRef:
      kind: ClusterSecretStore
      name: global-secrets
    dataFrom:
      - extract:
          key: paperless.admin
    target:
      deletionPolicy: Retain
  • Step 2: tailscale (app-template 3.1 → 5.3). Extract; replace the top-level serviceAccount: {name: tailscale} and the four templates with:
serviceAccount:
  tailscale: {}
rbac:
  # https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/blob/main/docs/k8s/role.yaml
  roles:
    tailscale:
      type: Role
      rules:
        - apiGroups: [""]
          resources: ["secrets"]
          verbs: ["create"]
        - apiGroups: [""]
          resourceNames: ["tailscale"]
          resources: ["secrets"]
          verbs: ["get", "update", "patch"]
  bindings:
    tailscale:
      type: RoleBinding
      roleRef:
        identifier: tailscale
      subjects:
        - identifier: tailscale
externalSecrets:
  auth:
    forceRename: tailscale-auth
    secretStoreRef:
      kind: ClusterSecretStore
      name: global-secrets
    data:
      - secretKey: TS_AUTHKEY
        remoteRef:
          key: external
          property: tailscale-auth-key
    target:
      deletionPolicy: Retain

and under controllers.tailscale add:

    # tailscale stores its state in the Secret tailscale (TS_KUBE_SECRET); app-template 5 disables the token by default
    pod:
      automountServiceAccountToken: true
    serviceAccount:
      identifier: tailscale

  • Step 3: wireguard (app-template 3.5 → 5.3). Extract; replace rawResources.secret with externalSecrets.secret: forceRename: wireguard-secret, the same secretStoreRef, data and target moved up from rawResources.secret.spec.spec (dedented), plus target.deletionPolicy: Retain. app-template does not template externalSecrets, so write the ESO template directly: PrivateKey = {{ .WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY }} (drop the backtick escape). Keep horus.khuedoan.com and the peer comments literal. The persistence.config.name: "{{ .Release.Name }}-secret" stays.

  • Step 4: Remove the three directories.

  • Step 5: Compare (loop over paperless tailscale wireguard) and read every diff line. Allowed differences:

  • all three: ExternalSecret gains app-template labels and target.deletionPolicy: Retain
  • paperless dev: the sandbox domain
  • tailscale, wireguard (3 → 5): selector and pod labels app.kubernetes.io/component → app.kubernetes.io/controller, labels and namespace on objects; wireguard gets a ServiceAccount wireguard with automountServiceAccountToken: false

  • must hold: tailscale pod automountServiceAccountToken: true, serviceAccountName: tailscale; wireguard wg0.conf identical to the baseline (yq 'select(.kind=="ExternalSecret") | .spec.target.template.data."wg0.conf"' on both)

  • Step 6: Commit: git commit -m "refactor(apps): paperless, tailscale and wireguard as app-template values files".

docs.title: Task 7: Docs, CLAUDE.md and pre-PR checks
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: docs/installation/sandbox.md, docs/getting-started/vpn-setup.md, CLAUDE.md

  • Step 1: Docs.
  • vpn-setup.md: ./apps/wireguard/values.yaml → ./apps/wireguard.yaml (two places).
  • sandbox.md: "Make changes" — apps are apps/<name>.yaml, rendered with scripts/render-chart apps/<name>.yaml [dev]; to add an app to the sandbox, list its file in the apps generator of system/argocd/values-dev.yaml; hosts use {{ .Values.global.domain }}.

  • CLAUDE.md Sandbox section: replace "Components synced in the sandbox are listed in system/argocd/values-dev.yaml" and the values-dev.yaml bullet with: apps are app-template values files apps/<name>.yaml (ApplicationSet apps, app-template pinned there; environment through global.domain and global.publicGateway; apps/matrix/ is the only chart); other components are wrapper charts with optional values-dev.yaml; both sandbox allowlists live in system/argocd/values-dev.yaml.

  • Step 2: Pre-PR checks.

ls apps
grep -rn 'targetRevision: 5.3.0' system/argocd apps | wc -l   # prod + dev (+ seed) sources only
for f in apps/*.yaml; do for e in prod dev; do scripts/render-chart $f $e > /tmp/r.yaml || echo "FAIL $f $e"; grep -n '{{ .Values' /tmp/r.yaml | sed "s|^|$f $e |"; done; done
for c in system/argocd apps/matrix; do for e in prod dev; do scripts/render-chart $c $e > /dev/null || echo "FAIL $c $e"; done; done
(cd test && go vet ./... && go test -run 'TestSmokeAppsForEnv|TestIdentity(HasGroup|TOTPWaitsForNextStep)|TestGatewayRouteReady' ./...)
mkdocs build --strict && rm -r site
Expected: apps lists 11 *.yaml files and matrix; app-template 5.3.0 only in the ApplicationSet sources (system/argocd/values*.yaml); no FAIL, no unrendered {{ .Values in any render; tests ok; docs build.

  • Step 3: Commit: git commit -m "docs: apps/<name>.yaml layout".

docs.title: Task 8: Pull request
docs.text: • Push feat/apps-layout, open a PR into dev (summary, the comparison results per app, the expected differences, the sandbox handover note; end with 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)). Ask the user before merging.

docs.title: Task 9: Sandbox after the merge
docs.text:
• Step 1: git switch dev && git pull --ff-only; export KUBECONFIG=$PWD/metal/kubeconfig.yaml.
  • Step 2: Handover. Wait until kubectl -n argocd get applications shows the five apps again, generated by apps (kubectl -n argocd get application excalidraw -o jsonpath='{.metadata.ownerReferences[0].name}' → apps). If an Application stays missing after 10 minutes, check kubectl -n argocd get applicationset apps -o yaml conditions.
  • Step 3: make dev → 50/50.
  • Step 4: make dev-clean && make dev → 50/50.
  • Step 5: Mark roadmap step 4 done in CLAUDE.md on a new branch, PR into dev.

docs.title: Step 5b: Forgejo replaces Gitea — Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Replace Gitea with Forgejo (Kanidm SSO, SSH, seeded GitOps repo that production Argo CD syncs from), production on CloudNativePG, sandbox on SQLite.

Architecture: A wrapper chart platform/forgejo around the official Forgejo chart, with our own templates for the Kanidm client, SSH TCPRoute, admin secret, CloudNativePG Cluster and a seed Job. A wrapper chart platform/cloudnative-pg for the operator (production only). Argo CD switches to ops/homelab on Forgejo with a repository credential from global-secrets.

Tech Stack: Helm wrapper charts, Argo CD ApplicationSets, kaniop KanidmOAuth2Client, external-secrets, Gateway API, Go tests (terratest, chromedp).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-forgejo-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Forgejo chart forgejo 17.3.0 from oci://code.forgejo.org/forgejo-helm; image tag 16.0.6 (rootless, the chart appends -rootless).
  • CloudNativePG chart cloudnative-pg 0.29.1 from https://cloudnative-pg.github.io/charts; PostgreSQL image ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:18.6-standard-trixie.
  • Every name this repo controls is forgejo; gitea remains only where the chart or image imposes it (values key gitea:, init container configure-gitea, GITEA_*/GITEA__* env, /data/gitea, /var/lib/gitea, /etc/gitea) and in history (past specs and plans, docs/reference/changelog.md, docs/reference/architecture/decision-records.md, docs/reference/roadmap.md, the external tutorial title in README.md).
  • Feature branch feat/forgejo (already created from dev), PR into dev; never commit to dev or master.
  • Basic checks on the branch: scripts/render-chart <dir> and scripts/render-chart <dir> dev for every changed chart or app file; cd test && go vet ./... && go test -run 'TestSmokeAppsForEnv|TestIdentity(HasGroup|TOTPWaitsForNextStep|PKCE)|TestGatewayRouteReady' ./...; mkdocs build --strict (then rm -r site).
  • make dev runs only after the PR is merged into dev; ask the user before merging.
  • Helm replaces lists: a list overridden in values-dev.yaml is restated in full.
  • No personal data in the repo; production KanidmGroups never set members.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. Kaniop secret not ready when Forgejo starts — the pod must wait (CreateContainerConfigError) and then start normally, never run with an empty client secret: the CLIENT_SECRET env uses secretKeyRef without optional. Covered by TestSSOForgejo on a fresh sandbox.
  2. A second login of the same person must reuse the account (no duplicate, no link-account page) and keep the admin flag in sync: TestSSOForgejo logs every account in twice (Task 2).
  3. Seed Job re-run (Argo CD re-sync, script change) must not touch an existing repository: the script only creates on 404; TestForgejoSeed runs the script a second time against the live repository (Task 3).
  4. An account in no role group must not get a Forgejo account: TestSSOForgejo checks dev-outsider gets "Access Denied".
  5. Sandbox-only overrides leaking into production (SQLite, CA mounts, seed source): the production render must show DB_TYPE=postgres, no homelab-dev-ca, and the upstream seed repository (render checks in Tasks 2 and 3).

docs.title: Task 1: CloudNativePG operator (platform/cloudnative-pg)
docs.text:
Files: - Create: platform/cloudnative-pg/Chart.yaml, platform/cloudnative-pg/values.yaml

docs.title: Task 2: Forgejo with Kanidm SSO and SSH, Gitea removed
docs.text:
Files: - Create: platform/forgejo/Chart.yaml, values.yaml, values-dev.yaml, templates/admin-secret.yaml, templates/kanidm-client.yaml, templates/tcproute.yaml, templates/database.yaml - Delete: platform/gitea/ (whole directory) - Modify: platform/global-secrets/values.yaml, platform/kanidm/values.yaml, platform/kanidm/values-dev.yaml, system/gateway/templates/gateway.yaml, system/argocd/values-dev.yaml, Makefile - Test: test/apps_test.go, test/smoke_test.go, test/gateway_test.go, test/sso_test.go

Interfaces: - Consumes: Cluster CRD (Task 1) in production only. - Produces: Services forgejo-http (port 3000) and forgejo-ssh (port 22) in namespace forgejo; Secret forgejo-admin (username, password); values keys host, database.cnpg.*, forgejo.image.* used by Task 3; global-secrets key forgejo.admin (property password) used by Task 3.

  • Step 1: Write the failing unit test

In test/apps_test.go, replace {"gitea", "gitea"}, in the dev list with {"forgejo", "forgejo"},.

  • Step 2: Run it

Run: cd test && go test -run TestSmokeAppsForEnv ./... Expected: FAIL, smokeApps(dev) = [... {gitea gitea}] , want [... {forgejo forgejo}].

  • Step 3: Update the smoke list

In test/smoke_test.go, replace {"gitea", "gitea"}, with {"forgejo", "forgejo"}, in both lists (the dev list and the production list; keep the production list in its current order, Forgejo where Gitea was).

Run: cd test && go test -run TestSmokeAppsForEnv ./... Expected: PASS.

  • Step 4: Write the cluster tests (they run in make dev)

In test/gateway_test.go, rename TestGatewayGiteaSSH to TestGatewayForgejoSSH and change its failure message to "no SSH banner from forgejo on %s:22".

In test/sso_test.go, add forgejoHost = "git.127-0-0-1.nip.io" to the host constants (align the = like the others) and append:

func TestSSOForgejo(t *testing.T) {
    skipUnlessSandbox(t)
    base := "https://" + forgejoHost
    waitForApp(t, base+"/api/healthz")
    start := base + "/user/oauth2/Kanidm"

    for _, c := range []struct {
        account string
        allowed bool
        admin   bool
    }{{"dev-admin", true, true}, {"dev-editor", true, false}, {"dev-viewer", true, false}, {"dev-outsider", false, false}} {
        t.Run(c.account, func(t *testing.T) {
            if !c.allowed {
                assert.Contains(t, browserDenied(t, c.account, ensureCredentials(t, c.account), start), "Access Denied")
                return
            }
            // Twice: the second login must reuse the account and keep the admin flag
            for range 2 {
                cookies := appLogin(t, c.account, ensureCredentials(t, c.account), start, forgejoHost)
                var user struct {
                    Login   string `json:"login"`
                    IsAdmin bool   `json:"is_admin"`
                }
                require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, getJSON(t, "GET", base+"/api/v1/user", cookies, "", "", nil, &user))
                assert.Equal(t, c.account, user.Login)
                assert.Equal(t, c.admin, user.IsAdmin)
            }
        })
    }
}

If /api/v1/user rejects the session cookie (401) when this runs in make dev, that is a test-design defect, not a Forgejo one: switch the assertions to GET base+"/user/settings" (200 and the page contains the username) and GET base+"/-/admin" (200 for admins, 404 otherwise) and ledger the ruling.

In the root Makefile, change smoke_filter='Smoke|Identity|SSO|Gateway' to smoke_filter='Smoke|Identity|SSO|Gateway|Forgejo'.

Run: cd test && go vet ./... Expected: no output.

  • Step 5: Show the render is missing

Run: scripts/render-chart platform/forgejo dev 2>&1 | head -3 Expected: an error (no such chart).

  • Step 6: Create platform/forgejo

platform/forgejo/Chart.yaml:

apiVersion: v2
name: forgejo
version: 0.0.0
dependencies:
  - name: forgejo
    version: 17.3.0
    repository: oci://code.forgejo.org/forgejo-helm

platform/forgejo/values.yaml:

host: git.khuedoan.com
database:
  # CloudNativePG cluster forgejo-db (templates/database.yaml); the sandbox uses SQLite
  cnpg:
    enabled: true
    instances: 3
    image: ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:18.6-standard-trixie
    size: 10Gi
forgejo:
  fullnameOverride: forgejo
  image:
    # Chart defaults, restated for templates/seed-job.yaml
    registry: code.forgejo.org
    repository: forgejo/forgejo
    # The chart defaults to the LTS release; the rootless image gets the -rootless suffix
    tag: 16.0.6
  # The chart's test pod uses an unpinned busybox
  test:
    enabled: false
  # One pod: SQLite (sandbox), the repositories volume and the in-memory session cannot be shared
  strategy:
    type: Recreate
    # null removes the chart default; Kubernetes rejects rollingUpdate with Recreate
    rollingUpdate: null
  persistence:
    claimName: forgejo-data
    size: 10Gi
  httpRoute:
    enabled: true
    parentRefs:
      - name: homelab
        namespace: gateway
        sectionName: https
    hostnames:
      - git.khuedoan.com
  deployment:
    # Also set in the init container that registers the login source (gitea.oauth below)
    env:
      - name: CLIENT_SECRET
        valueFrom:
          secretKeyRef:
            name: forgejo-kanidm-oauth2-credentials
            key: CLIENT_SECRET
  # `gitea:` is the Forgejo chart's own key for the app's settings
  gitea:
    admin:
      existingSecret: forgejo-admin
      email: forgejo@local.domain
    oauth:
      - name: Kanidm
        provider: openidConnect
        key: forgejo
        # Expanded by the init script's shell from deployment.env
        secret: ${CLIENT_SECRET}
        autoDiscoverUrl: https://auth.khuedoan.com/oauth2/openid/forgejo/.well-known/openid-configuration
        scopes: openid,profile,email,groups
        # Short group names from the client's claimMap (templates/kanidm-client.yaml)
        groupClaimName: homelab_groups
        adminGroup: homelab-admins
    config:
      server:
        DOMAIN: git.khuedoan.com
        ROOT_URL: https://git.khuedoan.com
        SSH_DOMAIN: git.khuedoan.com
        LANDING_PAGE: explore
        OFFLINE_MODE: true
      service:
        # Accounts come only from Kanidm
        ALLOW_ONLY_EXTERNAL_REGISTRATION: true
        SHOW_REGISTRATION_BUTTON: false
      oauth2_client:
        ENABLE_AUTO_REGISTRATION: true
        USERNAME: preferred_username
        ACCOUNT_LINKING: disabled
      repository:
        DISABLED_REPO_UNITS: repo.wiki,repo.projects,repo.packages
        DISABLE_STARS: true
        DEFAULT_BRANCH: master
      service.explore:
        DISABLE_USERS_PAGE: true
      actions:
        ENABLED: false
      webhook:
        ALLOWED_HOST_LIST: private
      database:
        DB_TYPE: postgres
        HOST: forgejo-db-rw:5432
        NAME: forgejo
        USER: forgejo
      cache:
        ADAPTER: memory
      session:
        PROVIDER: memory
      queue:
        TYPE: level
    # GITEA__<section>__<key> is the chart's naming for app.ini settings from env variables
    additionalConfigFromEnvs:
      - name: GITEA__DATABASE__PASSWD
        valueFrom:
          secretKeyRef:
            name: forgejo-db-app
            key: password

platform/forgejo/values-dev.yaml:

host: git.127-0-0-1.nip.io
database:
  cnpg:
    enabled: false
forgejo:
  persistence:
    size: 1Gi
  httpRoute:
    hostnames:
      - git.127-0-0-1.nip.io
  deployment:
    # Restated (lists are replaced), plus the sandbox CA for calls to Kanidm
    env:
      - name: CLIENT_SECRET
        valueFrom:
          secretKeyRef:
            name: forgejo-kanidm-oauth2-credentials
            key: CLIENT_SECRET
      - name: SSL_CERT_DIR
        value: /etc/ssl/certs:/etc/homelab-dev-ca
  extraVolumes:
    - name: dev-ca
      # Not optional: the pod waits until trust-manager has copied the CA here
      configMap:
        name: homelab-dev-ca
  extraContainerVolumeMounts: &devCAMounts
    - name: dev-ca
      mountPath: /etc/homelab-dev-ca
      readOnly: true
  extraInitVolumeMounts: *devCAMounts
  gitea:
    # Restated (lists are replaced) with the sandbox Kanidm
    oauth:
      - name: Kanidm
        provider: openidConnect
        key: forgejo
        secret: ${CLIENT_SECRET}
        autoDiscoverUrl: https://auth.127-0-0-1.nip.io/oauth2/openid/forgejo/.well-known/openid-configuration
        scopes: openid,profile,email,groups
        groupClaimName: homelab_groups
        adminGroup: homelab-admins
    config:
      server:
        DOMAIN: git.127-0-0-1.nip.io
        ROOT_URL: https://git.127-0-0-1.nip.io
        SSH_DOMAIN: git.127-0-0-1.nip.io
      # SQLite; HOST, NAME and USER from values.yaml stay but SQLite ignores them
      database:
        DB_TYPE: sqlite3
    # No PostgreSQL password in the sandbox
    additionalConfigFromEnvs: []

platform/forgejo/templates/admin-secret.yaml:

apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: {{ .Values.forgejo.gitea.admin.existingSecret }}
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
spec:
  secretStoreRef:
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
    name: global-secrets
  target:
    template:
      engineVersion: v2
      data:
        username: forgejo_admin
        password: {{` "{{ .password }}" `}}
  data:
    - secretKey: password
      remoteRef:
        key: forgejo.admin
        property: password

platform/forgejo/templates/kanidm-client.yaml:

apiVersion: kaniop.rs/v1beta1
kind: KanidmOAuth2Client
metadata:
  name: forgejo
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
spec:
  kanidmRef:
    name: kanidm
    namespace: kanidm
  displayname: Forgejo
  # Confidential client; Forgejo also sends PKCE (S256), which Kanidm requires
  origin: https://{{ .Values.host }}
  redirectUrl:
    - https://{{ .Values.host }}/user/oauth2/Kanidm/callback
  disableConsentPrompt: true
  preferShortUsername: true
  strictRedirectUrl: true
  # Short, domain-free group names: homelab-admins become site admins (adminGroup in values.yaml)
  claimMap:
    - name: homelab_groups
      joinStrategy: array
      valuesMap:
        {{- range list "homelab-admins" "homelab-editors" "homelab-users" }}
        - group: {{ . }}
          values:
            - {{ . }}
        {{- end }}
  scopeMap:
    {{- range list "homelab-admins" "homelab-editors" "homelab-users" }}
    - group: {{ . }}
      scopes: [openid, profile, email, groups]
    {{- end }}

platform/forgejo/templates/tcproute.yaml:

# The chart's tcpRoute is still v1alpha2
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: TCPRoute
metadata:
  name: forgejo-ssh
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - name: homelab
      namespace: gateway
      sectionName: ssh
  rules:
    - backendRefs:
        - name: forgejo-ssh
          port: 22

platform/forgejo/templates/database.yaml:

{{- with .Values.database.cnpg }}
{{- if .enabled }}
# CloudNativePG generates the Secret forgejo-db-app (password for the owner forgejo)
apiVersion: postgresql.cnpg.io/v1
kind: Cluster
metadata:
  name: forgejo-db
  namespace: {{ $.Release.Namespace }}
spec:
  instances: {{ .instances }}
  imageName: {{ .image }}
  bootstrap:
    initdb:
      database: forgejo
      owner: forgejo
  storage:
    size: {{ .size }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}

  • Step 7: Rewire the rest of the cluster to Forgejo and delete Gitea

  • git rm -r platform/gitea

  • platform/global-secrets/values.yaml: rename - name: gitea.admin to - name: forgejo.admin.
  • platform/kanidm/values.yaml: oauth2ClientNamespaces: [argocd, grafana, zot, actualbudget, paperless, forgejo].
  • platform/kanidm/values-dev.yaml: oauth2ClientNamespaces: [argocd, grafana, zot, actualbudget, paperless, forgejo, kanidm].
  • system/gateway/templates/gateway.yaml: the comment above the ssh listener becomes # Forgejo SSH, and kubernetes.io/metadata.name: gitea becomes kubernetes.io/metadata.name: forgejo.

  • system/argocd/values-dev.yaml: - path: platform/gitea becomes - path: platform/forgejo.

  • Step 8: Render checks

Run each and compare:

  1. scripts/render-chart platform/forgejo dev > /tmp/claude-1000/-home-nixos-homelab/44339b87-568a-46fd-9484-aed834c50ef8/scratchpad/forgejo-dev.yaml && grep -E '^kind:' /tmp/claude-1000/-home-nixos-homelab/44339b87-568a-46fd-9484-aed834c50ef8/scratchpad/forgejo-dev.yaml | sort | uniq -c Expected: Deployment, ExternalSecret, HTTPRoute, KanidmOAuth2Client, PersistentVolumeClaim, two Service, Secrets, TCPRoute; no Cluster, no Pod (chart test disabled).
  2. In that file: grep -E 'image: code.forgejo.org/forgejo/forgejo:16.0.6-rootless' -c ≥ 2 (init + main); grep -c 'homelab-dev-ca' ≥ 1; grep 'DB_TYPE' shows sqlite3; grep -c 'GITEA__DATABASE__PASSWD' is 0; the init script contains --auto-discover-url "https://auth.127-0-0-1.nip.io/oauth2/openid/forgejo/.well-known/openid-configuration", --admin-group "homelab-admins", --group-claim-name "homelab_groups", --secret "${CLIENT_SECRET}" (the init script is base64 in a Secret: decode with yq 'select(.kind=="Secret" and .metadata.name=="forgejo-init") | .stringData // .data' and base64 -d if needed).
  3. scripts/render-chart platform/forgejo > …/forgejo-prod.yaml: one Cluster (forgejo-db, 3 instances, image ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:18.6-standard-trixie); DB_TYPE is postgres; GITEA__DATABASE__PASSWD present; homelab-dev-ca absent; --auto-discover-url "https://auth.khuedoan.com/....
  4. scripts/render-chart platform/kanidm dev | grep -A8 oauth2ClientNamespace lists forgejo; same without dev.

test/forgejo_test.go:

package test

import (
    "net/http"
    "os"
    "testing"
    "time"

    "github.com/gruntwork-io/terratest/modules/k8s"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// TestForgejoSeed checks the seed Job copied the GitOps repository and that Argo CD's repository
// credential reads it, as production Argo CD will.
func TestForgejoSeed(t *testing.T) {
    if os.Getenv("ENV") != "dev" {
        t.Skip("Forgejo tests run against the sandbox only")
    }
    base := "https://" + forgejoHost
    waitForApp(t, base+"/api/healthz")
    admin := secretValue(t, "forgejo", "forgejo-admin", "username")
    password := secretValue(t, "forgejo", "forgejo-admin", "password")

    var repo struct {
        Private bool `json:"private"`
        Empty   bool `json:"empty"`
    }
    require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        return getJSON(t, "GET", base+"/api/v1/repos/ops/homelab", nil, admin, password, nil, &repo) == http.StatusOK
    }, 20*time.Minute, 15*time.Second, "ops/homelab was not seeded")
    assert.True(t, repo.Private)
    assert.False(t, repo.Empty)

    user := secretValue(t, "argocd", "argocd-repo-forgejo", "username")
    pass := secretValue(t, "argocd", "argocd-repo-forgejo", "password")
    assert.Equal(t, "http://forgejo-http.forgejo:3000/ops/homelab", secretValue(t, "argocd", "argocd-repo-forgejo", "url"))
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, getJSON(t, "GET", base+"/api/v1/repos/ops/homelab/branches/master", nil, user, pass, nil, nil))
}

// TestForgejoSeedIsIdempotent runs the seed script again against the seeded repository: it must succeed
// without touching it.
func TestForgejoSeedIsIdempotent(t *testing.T) {
    if os.Getenv("ENV") != "dev" {
        t.Skip("Forgejo tests run against the sandbox only")
    }
    options := k8s.NewKubectlOptions("", "", "forgejo")
    job, err := k8s.RunKubectlAndGetOutputE(t, options, "get", "jobs", "-o", "jsonpath={.items[0].metadata.name}")
    require.NoError(t, err)
    require.NotEmpty(t, job)
    rerun := job + "-rerun"
    _, err = k8s.RunKubectlAndGetOutputE(t, options, "create", "job", "--from=job/"+job, rerun)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    defer k8s.RunKubectlE(t, options, "delete", "job", rerun)
    _, err = k8s.RunKubectlAndGetOutputE(t, options, "wait", "--for=condition=complete", "--timeout=5m", "job/"+rerun)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    logs, err := k8s.RunKubectlAndGetOutputE(t, options, "logs", "job/"+rerun)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    assert.Contains(t, logs, "ops/homelab exists")
}

#!/bin/sh
# Seeds the GitOps repository once: creates the org ops and copies SEED_REPOSITORY into ops/homelab.
# Never changes an existing org or repository: after the seed, Forgejo is the source of truth.
set -eu

base=http://forgejo-http:3000
api="${base}/api/v1"

# status <curl args...>: prints the HTTP status, authenticated as the local admin
status() {
    curl --silent --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' --max-time 600 \
        --user "${FORGEJO_ADMIN_USERNAME}:${FORGEJO_ADMIN_PASSWORD}" "$@"
}

until curl --silent --fail --output /dev/null "${base}/api/healthz"; do
    echo "waiting for Forgejo"
    sleep 5
done

case "$(status "${api}/orgs/ops")" in
    200) echo "org ops exists" ;;
    404)
        code="$(status --request POST --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
            --data '{"username": "ops", "visibility": "private"}' "${api}/orgs")"
        [ "${code}" = 201 ] || { echo "creating org ops: HTTP ${code}" >&2; exit 1; }
        echo "created org ops"
        ;;
    *) echo "checking org ops: unexpected status" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

case "$(status "${api}/repos/ops/homelab")" in
    200) echo "ops/homelab exists" ;;
    404)
        code="$(status --request POST --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
            --data "{\"clone_addr\": \"${SEED_REPOSITORY}\", \"repo_owner\": \"ops\", \"repo_name\": \"homelab\", \"service\": \"git\", \"mirror\": false, \"private\": true}" \
            "${api}/repos/migrate")"
        [ "${code}" = 201 ] || { echo "copying ${SEED_REPOSITORY}: HTTP ${code}" >&2; exit 1; }
        echo "copied ${SEED_REPOSITORY} into ops/homelab"
        ;;
    *) echo "checking ops/homelab: unexpected status" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

platform/forgejo/templates/seed-job.yaml:

{{- $script := .Files.Get "files/seed.sh" }}
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: forgejo-seed
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
data:
  seed.sh: {{ $script | quote }}
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  # A new name when the script or the source changes, so Argo CD runs it again
  name: forgejo-seed-{{ print $script .Values.seed.repository | sha256sum | trunc 7 }}
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
  annotations:
    # After the Deployment is healthy
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "1"
spec:
  backoffLimit: 10
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
        - name: seed
          # The Forgejo image (already on the node) has curl
          image: {{ with .Values.forgejo.image }}{{ .registry }}/{{ .repository }}:{{ .tag }}-rootless{{ end }}
          command: [sh, /seed/seed.sh]
          env:
            - name: SEED_REPOSITORY
              value: {{ .Values.seed.repository | quote }}
            - name: FORGEJO_ADMIN_USERNAME
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: forgejo-admin
                  key: username
            - name: FORGEJO_ADMIN_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: forgejo-admin
                  key: password
          volumeMounts:
            - name: seed
              mountPath: /seed
              readOnly: true
      volumes:
        - name: seed
          configMap:
            name: forgejo-seed

docs.title: k3d Sandbox and Istio Gateway Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: The sandbox runs on k3d and production on k3s defaults, Cilium leaves the repo, and Istio serves the Gateways istio-system/gateway and istio-system/public; make dev passes 72/72 from scratch.

Architecture: metal/ creates a one-server k3d cluster (k3s v1.37.1, traefik off) with the Gateway API CRDs in k3s's auto-deploy manifests, plus a host-network socat container that forwards 127.0.0.1:80/443/22 to the k3d node (where ServiceLB serves the Gateway); production's Ansible k3s role drops its Cilium-specific flags and gets kube-vip v1.2.4 with a service load balancer for one class. A new wrapper chart system/istio-system (Istio base + istiod 1.31.1, two Gateways, the wildcard certificate, the redirect route, a sandbox-only CoreDNS rewrite) replaces system/gateway, and every route moves to the new Gateway names.

Tech Stack: k3d 5.9.0, k3s v1.37.1+k3s1, Istio 1.31.1, Gateway API v1.6.3 (standard channel), kube-vip v1.2.4, Ansible, Helm wrapper charts, Argo CD, Go tests.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-k3d-istio-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Versions, pinned exactly: k3d 5.9.0 (nixpkgs-unstable), rancher/k3s:v1.37.1-k3s1 / v1.37.1+k3s1, Istio charts base and istiod 1.31.1 from https://blob.istio.io/istio-release/charts, Gateway API v1.6.3 standard-install.yaml, ghcr.io/kube-vip/kube-vip:v1.2.4.
  • Gateway names: istio-system/gateway (LAN, listeners http 80, https 443, ssh 22) and istio-system/public (Tunnel, https only, Service ClusterIP); certificate secret wildcard-tls; generated Services gateway-istio and public-istio.
  • global.publicGateway: public in production, gateway in the sandbox.
  • Production kube-vip: API VIP 192.168.1.100 as before; service load balancer only for loadBalancerClass: kube-vip.io/kube-vip-class; Gateway gateway on 192.168.1.224, wireguard on 192.168.1.225.
  • The sandbox has no kube-vip: the Gateway Service has no class there and ServiceLB publishes it.
  • No cilium, homelab-public, cilium-gateway-* or namespace: gateway reference may remain outside docs/superpowers/ (history).
  • Spec deviations already ruled while planning (recorded in Task 3's commit message and the spec): Gateway API standard channel (v1.6.3 ships TCPRoute there, and Istio 1.31 serves TCPRoute and BackendTLSPolicy without PILOT_ENABLE_ALPHA_GATEWAY_API), so the alpha flag is not set; the Gateway's production IP is the kube-vip annotation kube-vip.io/loadbalancerIPs on its Service (through the parametersRef ConfigMap) instead of spec.addresses.
  • Istio's chart repository is https://blob.istio.io/istio-release/charts (the old istio-release.storage.googleapis.com index stops at 1.30.5 and 1.31 release candidates); a scratch render of base + istiod 1.31.1 from it gave docker.io/istio/pilot:1.31.1, pilot.resources applied, and the webhooks istiod-default-validator and istio-validator-istio-system.
  • Spike done while planning (2026-10-14), so the spec's fallback applies: a port published by k3d (Docker) answered 200 from WSL but timed out from Windows (curl.exe and PowerShell through WSL interop; mirrored networking: Docker DNATs the loopback traffic and the kernel drops it). A host-network socat bound to 127.0.0.1 and forwarding to the k3d node IP answered 200 from Windows, and WSL reached the node IP directly. kubectl reached k3d's API on 0.0.0.0:<port> from WSL, so the kubeconfig needs no rewrite. Hence: no k3d port mapping; socat 127.0.0.1:{80,443,22} → node IP (browser, SSH); tests dial the node IP directly (no socat stalls, as today).
  • Branch feat/k3d-istio from dev, PR into dev; ask before merging. KUBECONFIG=$PWD/metal/kubeconfig.yaml for kubectl.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. Argo CD drift on Istio's webhooks: istiod patches caBundle and failurePolicy into its ValidatingWebhookConfigurations, which would keep istio-system OutOfSync or flap. Expected: Synced and stable. Pinned in Task 3 (ignore rule in argocd-cm plus RespectIgnoreDifferences=true) and checked in Task 7 (the Argo CD sync check).
  2. First sync ordering on a fresh cluster: Gateways need the istio GatewayClass, which istiod creates after it starts. Expected: Argo CD retries until the Gateways are accepted; no manual step. Checked in Task 7 (fresh make dev).
  3. CoreDNS rewrite: coredns-custom must be picked up by k3s's CoreDNS without editing the Corefile, or every pod-to-Kanidm call fails. Pinned in Task 3 (render check of the ConfigMap key nip-io.override) and checked in Task 7 (identity and SSO tests).
  4. Host ports 80/443/22 on 127.0.0.1, and a node IP that changes when the cluster is recreated: the proxy must point at the current node and refuse with a clear message when another process holds a port. Pinned in Task 1 (the proxy is recreated on every make dev and the port guard is tested).
  5. Production render: no Cilium flag left in the k3s config, kube-vip serves only its class, the Gateway Service gets the class and IP annotation in production and neither in the sandbox. Pinned by the render checks in Tasks 2 and 3.

docs.title: Task 1: k3d sandbox cluster and localhost proxy (metal/, flake.nix)
docs.text:
This task removes the current kind sandbox (it is rebuilt on k3d) because the proxy needs host ports 80 and 443.

Files: - Create: metal/k3d-dev.yaml - Modify: metal/Makefile - Modify: flake.nix (packages: unstable.k3d replaces unstable.kind and unstable.cilium-cli) - Modify: .gitignore (add metal/gateway-api-*.yaml) - Delete: metal/kind-dev.yaml, metal/inventories/dev.yml

Interfaces: - Produces: make -C metal env=dev creates k3d cluster homelab-dev (node container k3d-homelab-dev-server-0), writes metal/kubeconfig.yaml, and (re)creates the container homelab-dev-proxy forwarding 127.0.0.1:80/443/22 to the node IP; Gateway API v1.6.3 CRDs present; make -C metal env=dev clean deletes both. The variable gateway_api_version = v1.6.3 in metal/Makefile. Node container name k3d-homelab-dev-server-0 (Task 5 reads its IP).

  • Step 1: Remove the kind sandbox (old Makefile, on this branch before editing)

Run: make dev-clean && kind get clusters Expected: No kind clusters found.; docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -c homelab-dev-proxy prints 0.

  • Step 2: Write the check that fails before the change

Create .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-14-k3d-istio/check-task1.sh (workspace, not committed):

#!/bin/sh
# k3d sandbox: node Ready, CRDs from the auto-deploy manifests, traefik off, proxy pointing at the node
set -e
export KUBECONFIG="$PWD/metal/kubeconfig.yaml"
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node --all --timeout=180s >/dev/null
kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.nodeInfo.kubeletVersion}{"\n"}'
for crd in gateways httproutes tcproutes backendtlspolicies; do
  kubectl wait --for=condition=Established "crd/$crd.gateway.networking.k8s.io" --timeout=180s >/dev/null
done
test "$(kubectl get crd gateways.gateway.networking.k8s.io -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.gateway\.networking\.k8s\.io/bundle-version}')" = v1.6.3
# traefik off; CoreDNS is k3s's own (kube-proxy and ServiceLB's controller run inside the k3s process)
! kubectl -n kube-system get deployment traefik >/dev/null 2>&1
kubectl -n kube-system get deployment coredns >/dev/null
node=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' k3d-homelab-dev-server-0)
docker inspect -f '{{join .Args " "}}' homelab-dev-proxy | grep -q "TCP:$node:443"
echo "k3d sandbox checks: pass (node $node)"

Run: chmod +x .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-14-k3d-istio/check-task1.sh && .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-14-k3d-istio/check-task1.sh Expected: FAIL (no cluster).

  • Step 3: Create metal/k3d-dev.yaml
# Sandbox cluster: one k3s server with k3s's own networking (Flannel, kube-proxy, ServiceLB, network policy),
# like production; Istio serves the Gateways (system/istio-system). No host port mapping: under WSL mirrored
# networking Windows cannot reach ports Docker publishes, so metal/Makefile runs a localhost proxy instead.
apiVersion: k3d.io/v1alpha5
kind: Simple
metadata:
  name: homelab-dev
servers: 1
agents: 0
image: rancher/k3s:v1.37.1-k3s1
options:
  k3s:
    extraArgs:
      - arg: --disable=traefik
        nodeFilters: [server:*]
      # Embedded etcd, like production
      - arg: --cluster-init
        nodeFilters: [server:*]
      # Control plane metrics for kube-prometheus-stack
      - arg: --etcd-expose-metrics
        nodeFilters: [server:*]
      - arg: --kube-controller-manager-arg=bind-address=0.0.0.0
        nodeFilters: [server:*]
      - arg: --kube-scheduler-arg=bind-address=0.0.0.0
        nodeFilters: [server:*]
  kubeconfig:
    updateDefaultKubeconfig: false
    switchCurrentContext: false
  • Step 4: Rewrite metal/Makefile

Replace the line dev: kind cluster proxy with dev: k3d proxy, and everything from kind_cluster = homelab-dev to the end of the file with:

k3d_cluster = homelab-dev
k3d_node = k3d-$(k3d_cluster)-server-0
gateway_api_version = v1.6.3
gateway_api_manifest = gateway-api-$(gateway_api_version).yaml

# Gateway API CRDs for k3s's auto-deploy manifests (production: roles/k3s)
$(gateway_api_manifest):
    curl -fsSL -o "$@" https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/$(gateway_api_version)/standard-install.yaml

k3d: $(gateway_api_manifest)
    k3d cluster list $(k3d_cluster) >/dev/null 2>&1 \
        || k3d cluster create --config k3d-dev.yaml \
            --volume "$(CURDIR)/$(gateway_api_manifest):/var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/manifests/gateway-api.yaml@server:*"
    k3d kubeconfig get $(k3d_cluster) > kubeconfig.yaml

proxy_name = homelab-dev-proxy
proxy_bind = 127.0.0.1

# ServiceLB publishes the Gateway (system/istio-system) on the node; Windows reaches WSL's 127.0.0.1 only
# through a host process, so forward 80, 443 and 22 there. Recreated each time: the node IP can change.
proxy:
    @docker rm -f $(proxy_name) >/dev/null 2>&1; \
    if ss -ltnH '( sport = :80 or sport = :443 or sport = :22 )' | grep -q .; then \
        echo "ports 80/443/22 are already in use on this host:"; ss -ltnp '( sport = :80 or sport = :443 or sport = :22 )'; exit 1; \
    fi; \
    node="$$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' $(k3d_node))"; \
    docker run -d --name $(proxy_name) --network host --restart unless-stopped \
        --entrypoint sh alpine/socat:1.8.1.3 -c "\
            socat TCP-LISTEN:80,bind=$(proxy_bind),fork,reuseaddr TCP:$$node:80 & \
            socat TCP-LISTEN:22,bind=$(proxy_bind),fork,reuseaddr TCP:$$node:22 & \
            exec socat TCP-LISTEN:443,bind=$(proxy_bind),fork,reuseaddr TCP:$$node:443" >/dev/null

clean:
    docker rm -f $(proxy_name) >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    k3d cluster delete $(k3d_cluster)
    rm -f kubeconfig.yaml

Then delete the kind files:

git rm -q metal/kind-dev.yaml metal/inventories/dev.yml
  • Step 5: flake.nix and .gitignore

In flake.nix, replace the two lines

            unstable.cilium-cli
            unstable.kind

with

            unstable.k3d

Append to .gitignore:

metal/gateway-api-*.yaml

Reload the shell so k3d is on PATH (direnv reload or nix develop); k3d version prints v5.9.0.

  • Step 6: Create the cluster and run the checks

Run: make -C metal env=dev && .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-14-k3d-istio/check-task1.sh Expected: v1.37.1+k3s1 and k3d sandbox checks: pass (node 172.x.y.z).

Windows reaches the proxy (WSL interop runs the Windows curl): (cd /mnt/c && /mnt/c/Windows/System32/curl.exe -s -m 10 -o NUL -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1/) Expected: 404 (ServiceLB has no Gateway yet, so the node answers nothing on 80 — any HTTP status or a fast 000 connection refused from the node is acceptable here; the full check is Task 7 Step 3). Record what it printed.

Port guard: docker rm -f homelab-dev-proxy && docker run -d --name port-guard-check --network host --entrypoint socat alpine/socat:1.8.1.3 TCP-LISTEN:80,bind=127.0.0.1,fork,reuseaddr - >/dev/null && sleep 1 && make -C metal env=dev proxy; echo "exit=$?"; docker rm -f port-guard-check >/dev/null && make -C metal env=dev proxy && echo "proxy back" Expected: ports 80/443/22 are already in use on this host:, a non-zero exit, then proxy back.

  • Step 7: Commit
git add metal/k3d-dev.yaml metal/Makefile flake.nix flake.lock .gitignore
git commit -m "feat(metal): sandbox on k3d with k3s defaults, localhost proxy to the node"

docs.title: Task 2: Production k3s defaults and kube-vip service load balancer (metal/)
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: metal/roles/k3s/defaults/main.yml - Modify: metal/roles/k3s/tasks/main.yml (Gateway API manifest) - Modify: metal/roles/k3s/templates/kube-vip.yaml.j2 - Modify: metal/cluster.yml - Modify: metal/inventories/prod.yml, metal/inventories/stag.yml - Delete: metal/roles/cilium/, metal/roles/coredns_rewrite/

Interfaces: - Consumes: gateway_api_version value v1.6.3 (same as metal/Makefile). - Produces: production k3s config without Cilium flags; kube-vip serving class kube-vip.io/kube-vip-class; inventory vars gateway_ip: 192.168.1.224, wireguard_ip: 192.168.1.225 (documentation of the addresses used in system/istio-system and apps/wireguard.yaml).

  • Step 1: Write the check (fails before the change)

Create .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-14-k3d-istio/check-task2.sh:

#!/bin/sh
# Production metal/: k3s defaults, kube-vip service LB for one class, no Cilium
set -e
cd metal
out=$(mktemp -d)
ansible localhost -i inventories/prod.yml -m ansible.builtin.template \
  -a "src=roles/k3s/templates/kube-vip.yaml.j2 dest=$out/kube-vip.yaml" \
  -e @roles/k3s/defaults/main.yml -e control_plane_endpoint=192.168.1.100 >/dev/null
ansible localhost -i inventories/prod.yml -m ansible.builtin.copy \
  -a "content={{ k3s_server_config | to_nice_yaml }} dest=$out/k3s.yaml" \
  -e @roles/k3s/defaults/main.yml -e control_plane_endpoint=192.168.1.100 >/dev/null
cat "$out/k3s.yaml"
grep -q 'ghcr.io/kube-vip/kube-vip:v1.2.4' "$out/kube-vip.yaml"
for env in svc_enable lb_class_only cp_enable; do grep -A1 "name: $env" "$out/kube-vip.yaml" | grep -q '"true"'; done
grep -A1 'name: lb_class_name' "$out/kube-vip.yaml" | grep -q 'kube-vip.io/kube-vip-class'
! grep -q 'flannel-backend\|disable-kube-proxy\|disable-network-policy\|servicelb' "$out/k3s.yaml"
grep -q 'traefik' "$out/k3s.yaml" && grep -q 'local-storage' "$out/k3s.yaml"
grep -q 'v1.37.1+k3s1' roles/k3s/defaults/main.yml
grep -q 'gateway-api/releases/download/{{ gateway_api_version }}/standard-install.yaml' roles/k3s/tasks/main.yml
! grep -rqi cilium cluster.yml inventories roles
ansible-playbook -i inventories/prod.yml cluster.yml --syntax-check >/dev/null
echo "production metal checks: pass"

Run: chmod +x .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-14-k3d-istio/check-task2.sh && .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-14-k3d-istio/check-task2.sh Expected: FAIL (kube-vip v0.6.4).

  • Step 2: metal/roles/k3s/defaults/main.yml

Replace the whole file with:

k3s_version: v1.37.1+k3s1
k3s_config_file: /etc/rancher/k3s/config.yaml
k3s_token_file: /etc/rancher/node/password
k3s_service_file: /etc/systemd/system/k3s.service
k3s_data_dir: /var/lib/rancher/k3s
k3s_kubeconfig_file: /etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml
# Keep in sync with metal/Makefile (sandbox)
gateway_api_version: v1.6.3
# k3s's own networking (Flannel, kube-proxy, ServiceLB, network policy), like upstream nixos;
# Istio serves the Gateways, Rook Ceph the storage
k3s_server_config:
  tls-san:
    - "{{ control_plane_endpoint }}"
  disable:
    - local-storage
    - traefik
  disable-helm-controller: true
  secrets-encryption: true
  # Control plane metrics for kube-prometheus-stack
  etcd-expose-metrics: true
  kube-controller-manager-arg:
    - bind-address=0.0.0.0
  kube-scheduler-arg:
    - bind-address=0.0.0.0
  • Step 3: Gateway API CRDs in metal/roles/k3s/tasks/main.yml

In "Ensure config directories exist", add - "{{ k3s_data_dir }}/server/manifests" to the loop. After the task "Copy kube-vip manifests", add:

- name: Install the Gateway API CRDs through k3s's auto-deploy manifests
  when: "'masters' in group_names"
  ansible.builtin.get_url:
    url: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/{{ gateway_api_version }}/standard-install.yaml
    dest: "{{ k3s_data_dir }}/server/manifests/gateway-api.yaml"
    mode: 0644
  • Step 4: metal/roles/k3s/templates/kube-vip.yaml.j2

Change the image to ghcr.io/kube-vip/kube-vip:v1.2.4 and replace the env: list with:

      env:
        - name: address
          value: {{ control_plane_endpoint }}
        - name: vip_arp
          value: "true"
        - name: vip_leaderelection
          value: "true"
        # The API server VIP
        - name: cp_enable
          value: "true"
        - name: lb_enable
          value: "true"
        # LoadBalancer Services that ask for kube-vip (the LAN Gateway, wireguard); ServiceLB serves the rest
        - name: svc_enable
          value: "true"
        - name: lb_class_only
          value: "true"
        - name: lb_class_name
          value: kube-vip.io/kube-vip-class
  • Step 5: Remove Cilium and the CoreDNS role

metal/cluster.yml becomes:

- name: Create Kubernetes cluster
  hosts: metal
  roles:
    - prerequisites
    - k3s
    - automatic_upgrade

metal/inventories/prod.yml all.vars becomes:

  vars:
    control_plane_endpoint: 192.168.1.100
    # kube-vip LoadBalancer addresses (set on the Services: system/istio-system, apps/wireguard.yaml)
    gateway_ip: 192.168.1.224
    wireguard_ip: 192.168.1.225

metal/inventories/stag.yml: delete the whole all: block (its only vars were cilium_*). Then:

git rm -rq metal/roles/cilium metal/roles/coredns_rewrite
grep -rn "load_balancer_ip_pool" metal || echo "no pool references"

Expected: no pool references (if a template still uses it, replace it with the two *_ip vars and record a ruling).

  • Step 6: Run the check

Run: .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-14-k3d-istio/check-task2.sh Expected: the rendered k3s config (no flannel-backend, disable-kube-proxy, disable-network-policy, servicelb) and production metal checks: pass.

  • Step 7: Commit
git add metal
git commit -m "feat(metal): k3s defaults in production, kube-vip v1.2.4 serves one LoadBalancer class, no Cilium"

docs.title: Task 3: system/istio-system replaces system/gateway
docs.text:
Files: - Create: system/istio-system/Chart.yaml, values.yaml, values-dev.yaml - Create: system/istio-system/templates/gateway.yaml, certificate.yaml, https-redirect.yaml, coredns-custom.yaml - Delete: system/gateway/ - Modify: system/argocd/values.yaml (argocd-cm ignore rule, RespectIgnoreDifferences=true in the shared sync policy), system/argocd/values-dev.yaml (allowlist) - Modify: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-k3d-istio-design.md (record the two planning rulings)

Interfaces: - Consumes: Gateway API CRDs (Task 1/2). - Produces: Gateways istio-system/gateway (sections http, https, ssh) and istio-system/public (section https); Services gateway-istio, public-istio; secret wildcard-tls; sandbox ConfigMap kube-system/coredns-custom key nip-io.override. Values: domain, gateway.loadBalancer ({class, ip} or null), corednsRewrite (bool).

  • Step 1: Write the render check (fails before the chart exists)

Create .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-14-k3d-istio/check-task3.sh:

#!/bin/sh
# system/istio-system renders: Istio, two Gateways, kube-vip only in prod, CoreDNS rewrite only in dev
set -e
dev=$(scripts/render-chart system/istio-system dev 2>/dev/null)
prod=$(scripts/render-chart system/istio-system 2>/dev/null)
n=0
check() { echo "$3: $1"; test "$1" = "$2"; n=$((n+1)); }
check "$(echo "$dev" | yq ea '[select(.kind == "Gateway") | .metadata.name + ":" + ([.spec.listeners[].name] | join(","))] | join(" ")')" "gateway:http,https,ssh public:https" "gateways"
check "$(echo "$dev" | yq ea '[select(.kind == "Gateway") | .spec.gatewayClassName] | unique | join(",")')" "istio" "class"
check "$(echo "$dev" | yq 'select(.kind == "Deployment" and .metadata.name == "istiod") | .spec.template.spec.containers[0].image' | sed 's/.*://')" "1.31.1" "istiod image"
check "$(echo "$dev" | yq 'select(.kind == "ConfigMap" and .metadata.name == "coredns-custom") | .metadata.namespace + " " + (.data["nip-io.override"] | test("gateway-istio.istio-system.svc.cluster.local") | tostring)')" "kube-system true" "coredns rewrite"
check "$(echo "$prod" | yq ea '[select(.kind == "ConfigMap" and .metadata.name == "coredns-custom")] | length')" "0" "no coredns rewrite in prod"
check "$(echo "$prod" | yq 'select(.kind == "ConfigMap" and .metadata.name == "gateway-options") | .data.service' | yq '.spec.loadBalancerClass + " " + .metadata.annotations["kube-vip.io/loadbalancerIPs"]')" "kube-vip.io/kube-vip-class 192.168.1.224" "prod gateway LB"
check "$(echo "$dev" | yq ea '[select(.kind == "ConfigMap" and .metadata.name == "gateway-options")] | length')" "0" "no kube-vip options in dev"
check "$(echo "$dev" | yq 'select(.kind == "ConfigMap" and .metadata.name == "public-options") | .data.service' | yq '.spec.type')" "ClusterIP" "public ClusterIP"
check "$(echo "$dev" | yq 'select(.kind == "Certificate") | .spec.secretName + " " + .spec.dnsNames[0]')" "wildcard-tls *.127-0-0-1.nip.io" "certificate"
check "$(echo "$prod" | yq 'select(.kind == "Gateway" and .metadata.name == "public") | .metadata.annotations["external-dns.kubernetes.io/target"]')" "homelab-tunnel.khuedoan.com" "public dns target"
check "$(scripts/render-chart system/argocd dev 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'path: system/istio-system')" "1" "allowlist"
check "$(scripts/render-chart system/argocd 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'admissionregistration.k8s.io_ValidatingWebhookConfiguration')" "1" "webhook ignore rule"
test ! -d system/gateway && n=$((n+1)) && echo "system/gateway removed"
echo "istio-system render checks: $n/13 pass"

Run: chmod +x .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-14-k3d-istio/check-task3.sh && .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-14-k3d-istio/check-task3.sh Expected: FAIL (system/istio-system does not exist).

  • Step 2: Chart and values

system/istio-system/Chart.yaml:

apiVersion: v2
name: istio-system
version: 0.0.0
dependencies:
  - name: base
    version: 1.31.1
    repository: https://blob.istio.io/istio-release/charts
  - name: istiod
    version: 1.31.1
    repository: https://blob.istio.io/istio-release/charts

system/istio-system/values.yaml:

domain: khuedoan.com
gateway:
  # kube-vip serves the LAN Gateway's Service on its own VIP (metal/roles/k3s): Forgejo SSH keeps port 22
  # (node sshd owns it on the node IPs) and the address moves to another node when one fails
  loadBalancer:
    class: kube-vip.io/kube-vip-class
    ip: 192.168.1.224
# Sandbox only: pods resolve sandbox hostnames to the Gateway instead of their own loopback
corednsRewrite: false
istiod:
  pilot:
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 128Mi

system/istio-system/values-dev.yaml:

domain: 127-0-0-1.nip.io
gateway:
  # No kube-vip in the sandbox: ServiceLB publishes the Gateway on the k3d node (host ports 80/443/22)
  loadBalancer: null
corednsRewrite: true
  • Step 3: Templates (moved from system/gateway, renamed)

system/istio-system/templates/gateway.yaml:

{{- with .Values.gateway.loadBalancer }}
# Merged into the Service Istio generates for the Gateway (spec.infrastructure.parametersRef)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: gateway-options
data:
  service: |
    metadata:
      annotations:
        kube-vip.io/loadbalancerIPs: {{ .ip }}
    spec:
      loadBalancerClass: {{ .class }}
---
{{- end }}
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: gateway
spec:
  gatewayClassName: istio
  {{- if .Values.gateway.loadBalancer }}
  infrastructure:
    parametersRef:
      group: ""
      kind: ConfigMap
      name: gateway-options
  {{- end }}
  listeners:
    # Only the HTTPS redirect (templates/https-redirect.yaml)
    - name: http
      protocol: HTTP
      port: 80
      allowedRoutes:
        namespaces:
          from: Same
    - name: https
      protocol: HTTPS
      port: 443
      hostname: "*.{{ .Values.domain }}"
      tls:
        mode: Terminate
        certificateRefs:
          - name: wildcard-tls
      allowedRoutes:
        namespaces:
          from: All
    # Forgejo SSH
    - name: ssh
      protocol: TCP
      port: 22
      allowedRoutes:
        namespaces:
          from: Selector
          selector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: forgejo
        kinds:
          - kind: TCPRoute
---
# cloudflared forwards to it in the cluster, so it needs no external address
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: public-options
data:
  service: |
    spec:
      type: ClusterIP
---
# Published through the Cloudflare Tunnel: external-dns points public hosts at the tunnel,
# and cloudflared forwards to this Gateway only
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: public
  annotations:
    external-dns.kubernetes.io/target: homelab-tunnel.{{ .Values.domain }}
spec:
  gatewayClassName: istio
  infrastructure:
    parametersRef:
      group: ""
      kind: ConfigMap
      name: public-options
  listeners:
    - name: https
      protocol: HTTPS
      port: 443
      hostname: "*.{{ .Values.domain }}"
      tls:
        mode: Terminate
        certificateRefs:
          - name: wildcard-tls
      allowedRoutes:
        namespaces:
          from: All

system/istio-system/templates/certificate.yaml:

apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: wildcard
spec:
  secretName: wildcard-tls
  dnsNames:
    - "*.{{ .Values.domain }}"
  issuerRef:
    group: cert-manager.io
    kind: ClusterIssuer
    name: letsencrypt-prod

system/istio-system/templates/https-redirect.yaml:

apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: https-redirect
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - name: gateway
      sectionName: http
  rules:
    - filters:
        - type: RequestRedirect
          requestRedirect:
            scheme: https
            statusCode: 301

system/istio-system/templates/coredns-custom.yaml:

{{- if .Values.corednsRewrite }}
# k3s's CoreDNS imports *.override keys from this ConfigMap into its server block (the Corefile itself is
# managed by k3s); pods would otherwise resolve *.127-0-0-1.nip.io to their own loopback
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: coredns-custom
  namespace: kube-system

python3 - <<'EOF'
import pathlib, re, subprocess
files = subprocess.run(["grep", "-rlE", "namespace: gateway$", "apps", "platform", "system", "--include=*.yaml", "--include=*.tpl"],
                       capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()
pattern = re.compile(r"^(\s*-?\s*)name: (homelab-public|homelab|'\{\{ \.Values\.global\.publicGateway \}\}')\n(\s*)namespace: gateway$", re.M)

func nodeAddressFromInspect(out string) (string, error) {

docs.title: SSO directly with Kanidm (step 5a) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Remove Dex: Grafana, Argo CD and zot log in with their own Kanidm OAuth2 clients (roles unchanged), and Actual Budget and paperless get Kanidm SSO limited to homelab-budget and homelab-documents.

Architecture: Each app declares a kaniop KanidmOAuth2Client in its own namespace (wrapper chart template, or rawResources in an app file). The admin tools keep the homelab_groups claim map; the personal-data apps are gated by a scopeMap on their access group. kaniop's generated Secret <client>-kanidm-oauth2-credentials replaces the dex.* global secrets. Tests talk to Kanidm directly with the sandbox client smoke and PKCE.

Tech Stack: Kanidm 1.11.2, kaniop 0.19.0, Grafana 13.5.1, Argo CD (argo-cd 10.10.3), zot 0.1.128, Actual Budget 26.10.0, paperless-ngx 3.3.1, Go tests (chromedp v0.16.0, terratest).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-kanidm-sso-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Branch feat/kanidm-sso (spec committed). PR into dev; merge only with the user's go-ahead. Commits end with: 
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01GZDRNK1oUcGXXSC3R6dhN2
  • Dev shell; no rm with variables or in sh -c.
  • Kanidm endpoints (domain D = khuedoan.com prod, 127-0-0-1.nip.io sandbox): authorize https://auth.D/ui/oauth2, token https://auth.D/oauth2/token, issuer and discovery https://auth.D/oauth2/openid/<client> (/.well-known/openid-configuration), userinfo https://auth.D/oauth2/openid/<client>/userinfo. Kanidm puts claim-map claims in both the ID token and userinfo.
  • Every client: kanidmRef: {name: kanidm, namespace: kanidm}, disableConsentPrompt: true, preferShortUsername: true, strictRedirectUrl: true. PKCE is mandatory for every client.
  • Role groups homelab-admins, homelab-editors, homelab-users; access groups homelab-budget, homelab-documents. Claim homelab_groups (array of short names), as in today's Dex client.
  • Secret of a confidential client: <metadata.name>-kanidm-oauth2-credentials, keys CLIENT_ID, CLIENT_SECRET.
  • Client namespaces allowed by the Kanidm CR: argocd, grafana, zot, actualbudget, paperless, and kanidm (sandbox client smoke).
  • Sandbox members: homelab-budget = dev-admin, dev-viewer; homelab-documents = dev-admin, dev-editor. Production groups set no members.
  • App files (apps/*.yaml) get the sandbox CA through global.devCA ("true" in system/argocd/values-dev.yaml, "" in prod and seed) and an optional custom volume of ConfigMap homelab-dev-ca (app-template rejects optional on configMap volumes).
  • Offline test pattern: TestSmokeAppsForEnv|TestIdentity(HasGroup|TOTPWaitsForNextStep|PKCE)|TestGatewayRouteReady.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. kaniop ignores clients outside its namespace selector (no error on the client, just never reconciled, no Secret). → Task 2 renders the selector; the SSO tests (Task 11) fail fast through waitForSecret.
  2. Bootstrap renders system/argocd offline before kaniop's CRDs exist. → Task 4 guards the Argo CD client with .Capabilities.APIVersions.Has, and checks the offline render has no KanidmOAuth2Client.
  3. Actual Budget makes the first OpenID user the server owner. → sandbox test order logs in dev-admin first; CLAUDE.md production note.
  4. Group claim name drift: apps that still read groups would see SPNs/UUIDs and deny everyone. → each app task greps its render for groups vs homelab_groups; SSO tests check every role.
  5. Kanidm refuses non-PKCE token requests: the smoke client and every app must send PKCE. → TestIdentityPKCE (offline) checks the S256 challenge; app settings enable PKCE explicitly where it is optional (Grafana, Argo CD, paperless).

    assert.Regexp(t, `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43,128}$`, verifier)
    sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(verifier))

// pkcePair returns a random PKCE verifier and its S256 challenge; Kanidm requires PKCE for every client.
func pkcePair() (string, string) {
    raw := make([]byte, 32)
    if _, err := rand.Read(raw); err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    verifier := base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(raw)
    sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(verifier))
    return verifier, base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(sum[:])
}
(crypto/rand is already imported; add crypto/sha256). Rerun → PASS.

  • Add:

// waitForSecret waits for a Secret that an operator creates (kaniop client credentials) and returns its data.
func waitForSecret(t *testing.T, namespace, name string) map[string][]byte {
    options := k8s.NewKubectlOptions("", "", namespace)
    options.Logger = logger.Discard
    var data map[string][]byte
    require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        secret, err := k8s.GetSecretE(t, options, name)
        if err != nil {
            return false
        }
        data = secret.Data
        return true
    }, 20*time.Minute, 15*time.Second, "Secret %s/%s does not exist", namespace, name)
    return data
}

In test/sso_test.go add hosts budgetHost = "budget.127-0-0-1.nip.io", paperlessHost = "paperless.127-0-0-1.nip.io" and:

func TestSSOActualBudget(t *testing.T) {
    skipUnlessSandbox(t)
    base := "https://" + budgetHost
    waitForApp(t, base+"/account/login-methods")

    // dev-admin first: the first OpenID user becomes the server owner
    for _, c := range []struct {
        account string
        allowed bool
    }{{"dev-admin", true}, {"dev-viewer", true}, {"dev-editor", false}} {
        t.Run(c.account, func(t *testing.T) {
            var start struct {
                Data struct {
                    ReturnURL string `json:"returnUrl"`
                } `json:"data"`
            }
            require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, getJSON(t, "POST", base+"/account/login", nil, "", "",
                map[string]any{"loginMethod": "openid", "returnUrl": base}, &start))
            token, page := actualOpenIDLogin(t, c.account, ensureCredentials(t, c.account), start.Data.ReturnURL, base)
            if !c.allowed {
                assert.Empty(t, token)
                assert.Contains(t, page, "Access Denied")
                return
            }
            require.NotEmpty(t, token, "no Actual token for %s; page:\n%s", c.account, page)
            var me struct {
                Data struct {
                    UserName string `json:"userName"`
                } `json:"data"`
            }
            assert.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, getJSON(t, "GET", base+"/account/validate", nil, "", "", nil, &me, "X-ACTUAL-TOKEN", token))
            assert.Equal(t, c.account, me.Data.UserName)
        })
    }
}

func TestSSOPaperless(t *testing.T) {
    skipUnlessSandbox(t)
    base := "https://" + paperlessHost
    waitForApp(t, base+"/accounts/login/")
    for _, c := range []struct {
        account          string
        allowed, superus bool
    }{{"dev-admin", true, true}, {"dev-editor", true, false}, {"dev-viewer", false, false}} {
        t.Run(c.account, func(t *testing.T) {
            start := base + "/accounts/oidc/kanidm/login/?process=login"
            if !c.allowed {
                _, page := browserDenied(t, c.account, ensureCredentials(t, c.account), start)
                assert.Contains(t, page, "Access Denied")
                return
            }
            cookies := appLogin(t, c.account, ensureCredentials(t, c.account), start, paperlessHost)
            var me struct {
                Username    string `json:"username"`
                IsSuperuser bool   `json:"is_superuser"`
            }
            require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, getJSON(t, "GET", base+"/api/profile/", cookies, "", "", nil, &me))
            assert.Equal(t, c.account, me.Username)
            assert.Equal(t, c.superus, me.IsSuperuser)
        })
    }
}

with helpers in test/identity_helpers_test.go: - actualOpenIDLogin(t, account, c, idpURL, appBase string) (token, page string): new browser, navigate to idpURL, wait input#username, kanidmLogin, then wait (30 s, like browserAuthorize) for a request to appBase + "/openid-cb" (listen to network.EventRequestWillBeSent) and return its token query parameter, or the page text when Kanidm shows "Access Denied". - browserDenied(t, account, c, startURL string) (string, string): navigate to startURL, wait input#username, kanidmLogin, poll the page text for "Access Denied" (30 s) and return it. - If paperless shows allauth's confirmation page before redirecting (a form with a submit button on /accounts/oidc/kanidm/login/), appLogin and browserDenied click button[type=submit] first when input#username is not visible within 5 s. Implement this as an optional step in a shared openLogin(ctx, startURL) helper used by both. - Superuser check: if /api/profile/ does not return is_superuser, read it from /api/ui_settings/ (user.is_superuser) instead; the assertion stays the same. - [ ] Step 6: Smoke lists. smokeApps("dev"): drop {"dex", "dex"}, add {"paperless", "paperless"}; same in TestSmokeAppsForEnv. - [ ] Step 7: Verify offline: cd test && gofmt -l . && go vet ./... && go test -run 'TestSmokeAppsForEnv|TestIdentity(HasGroup|TOTPWaitsForNextStep|PKCE)|TestGatewayRouteReady' ./... → ok. - [ ] Step 8: Commit: test: identity and SSO tests talk to Kanidm directly; Actual Budget and paperless SSO tests.

docs.title: OpenCloud with Kanidm OIDC Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: OpenCloud runs as apps/opencloud.yaml at drive.<domain>, logs in with a public Kanidm client, admits only homelab-files (homelab-admins → Admin, others → User), and the sandbox tests prove login, roles, refusal and file storage.

Architecture: One app-template values file adapted from upstream nixos (52c32ab), with a ConfigMap that adds OpenCloud's proxy.yaml role mapping and a KanidmOAuth2Client in rawResources. Kanidm gets the access group homelab-files. A Go/chromedp test logs in through the web UI, captures the bearer token the UI sends to /graph, and checks the role and a WebDAV round trip.

Tech Stack: app-template 5.3.0, OpenCloud 8.1.0 (opencloud-rolling), kaniop KanidmOAuth2Client, Go + chromedp + terratest, mkdocs.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-opencloud-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Image docker.io/opencloudeu/opencloud-rolling:8.1.0, pinned exactly; app-template stays 5.3.0 (pinned by the apps ApplicationSet).
  • Host drive.{{ .Values.global.domain }} on gateway/homelab, section https.
  • Kanidm client opencloud, public: true, redirects /, /oidc-callback.html, /oidc-silent-redirect.html; scopeMap only homelab-files; claim homelab_groups with homelab-admins and homelab-files.
  • Role mapping order: admin ← homelab-admins, then user ← homelab-files.
  • Sandbox members: homelab-files: [dev-admin, dev-editor]; production KanidmGroups never set members.
  • PVCs opencloud-config (1Gi) and opencloud-data (20Gi).
  • Branch feat/opencloud from dev, PR into dev; ask before merging.
  • Basic checks before the PR: scripts/render-chart (prod and dev) for apps/opencloud.yaml, apps/homepage.yaml, platform/kanidm, system/argocd; cd test && go vet ./... && go test -run 'TestSmokeAppsForEnv|TestIdentity(HasGroup|TOTPWaitsForNextStep|PKCE)|TestGatewayRouteReady' ./...; mkdocs build --strict.
  • Shell: export KUBECONFIG=$PWD/metal/kubeconfig.yaml for anything that talks to the sandbox.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. dev-editor (role User) listing /graph/v1.0/applications: the test resolves role names through it; if OpenCloud restricts it to admins, the editor case fails for a test reason, not a product one. Expected: readable by every user (no requireAdmin on the route in 8.1.0). Pinned by the editor case in Task 3.
  2. Second login of the same person: must reuse the account (same Graph id, since the username is Kanidm's sub) and keep the role. Pinned in Task 3 (two logins per allowed account).
  3. The personal drive does not exist yet right after the first login: /graph/v1.0/me/drive may answer 404 for a moment. Expected: the test waits for it instead of failing. Pinned in Task 3 (require.Eventually).
  4. The config PVC's opencloud.yaml from opencloud init must survive restarts and never be regenerated (regenerating changes the internal secrets). Expected: the init container only runs init when the file is missing or empty. Pinned by the render check in Task 2 (the -s guard is in the rendered init args).
  5. Production render: SSL_CERT_DIR must be empty and the dev-ca volume optional, so production pods start without the sandbox ConfigMap. Pinned by the prod render check in Task 2.

Interfaces: - Consumes: Task 1's group homelab-files and namespace opencloud in oauth2ClientNamespaces. - Produces: Deployment opencloud (namespace opencloud), Service opencloud:9200, HTTPRoute host drive.<domain>, KanidmOAuth2Client opencloud, PVCs opencloud-config and opencloud-data.
