docs.title: Sandbox Branch Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: make dev force-pushes the current commit to GitHub branch sandbox, which the sandbox's Argo CD syncs, so feature branches pass the sandbox tests before their merge.

Architecture: system/argocd/values-dev.yaml points both ApplicationSets at revision sandbox. The root Makefile gains sandbox-push (refuses uncommitted changes, then git push --force origin HEAD:sandbox) before the cluster steps and sandbox-refresh (asks Argo CD to re-read git) before the tests.

Tech Stack: GNU/POSIX make, git, kubectl, Argo CD annotations.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-sandbox-branch-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Branch name sandbox on origin (github.com/duongle-steven/homelab); overwritten by every make dev.
  • Production and staging values (values.yaml, values-seed.yaml) do not change.
  • Uncommitted changes to tracked files stop make dev before anything is pushed or created; untracked files (.direnv/, site/) are ignored.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A refresh on a fresh cluster (no Argo CD yet) must not fail make dev. Pinned in Task 1 (the refresh ignores errors) and proven by Task 3's fresh build.
  2. New apps added on a branch appear only after the ApplicationSet controller re-reads git. Expected: the refresh also annotates the ApplicationSets. Pinned in Task 1.
  3. Running make dev on dev after a merge pushes dev's commit to sandbox (no special case). Covered by the workflow docs (Task 2).
  4. A push failure (offline, auth) stops before the cluster steps. Pinned by the target order in Task 1.
  5. Forgejo's seed copies GitHub's default branch, not sandbox; the seed tests only need master to exist. Unchanged; noted in Task 2's docs.

docs.title: Task 1: sandbox branch in Argo CD and make dev
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: system/argocd/values-dev.yaml:42 (revision: &revision dev) - Modify: Makefile (dev target)

  • Step 1: Write the check (fails before the change)

Create .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-15-sandbox-branch/check-task1.sh:

#!/bin/sh
# The sandbox's ApplicationSets read branch sandbox; make dev refuses uncommitted changes before pushing
set -e
f=$(mktemp); trap 'rm -f "$f"; git checkout -q -- README.md' EXIT
scripts/render-chart system/argocd dev > "$f" 2>/dev/null
r=$(yq ea '[select(.kind == "ApplicationSet") | (.spec.generators[].git.revision, .spec.template.spec.source.targetRevision, .spec.template.spec.sources[].targetRevision) | select(. != null)] | unique | join(",")' "$f")
echo "sandbox revisions: $r"
test "$r" = "5.3.0,sandbox"
echo " " >> README.md
out=$(make sandbox-push 2>&1 || true)
echo "$out" | grep -q "commit your changes first"
echo "make dev refuses uncommitted changes"

Run: chmod +x .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-15-sandbox-branch/check-task1.sh && .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-15-sandbox-branch/check-task1.sh Expected: FAIL with sandbox revisions: 5.3.0,dev.

  • Step 2: values-dev.yaml

Replace revision: &revision dev with:

            # make dev force-pushes the current commit here, so a branch is tested before its merge
            revision: &revision sandbox
  • Step 3: Makefile

Replace the dev: target with:

# The sandbox syncs GitHub branch sandbox (system/argocd/values-dev.yaml): test the commit you are on
dev: sandbox-push
    $(MAKE) env=dev ENV=dev INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY=1 smoke_filter='Smoke|Identity|SSO|Gateway|Forgejo|Mesh' metal system sandbox-refresh smoke-test

sandbox-push:
    @if [ -n "$$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ]; then \
        echo "commit your changes first: make dev tests the commit at HEAD"; \
        git status --short --untracked-files=no; exit 1; \
    fi
    git push --force origin HEAD:sandbox

# An existing sandbox picks up the new commit now instead of at the next poll; on a fresh one there is nothing yet
sandbox-refresh:
    -@kubectl -n argocd annotate applicationsets --all argocd.argoproj.io/application-set-refresh=true --overwrite >/dev/null 2>&1
    -@kubectl -n argocd annotate applications --all argocd.argoproj.io/refresh=normal --overwrite >/dev/null 2>&1
  • Step 4: Run the check

Run: .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-15-sandbox-branch/check-task1.sh Expected: sandbox revisions: 5.3.0,sandbox and make dev refuses uncommitted changes.

docs.title: Environment Settings (Step 7b) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Domain, time zone and seed repository come from infra/<env>/cluster/config.json; no chart or app file names a domain; scripts/configure is gone.

Architecture: config.json gains domain, timezone, seed_repository; both ApplicationSets pass global.baseDomain, global.timezone, global.seedRepository (next to global.addresses). Each component uses them by one of three routes found in the spike: its own templates read the global; a subchart that runs tpl gets {{ .Values.global.baseDomain }} in its values; a subchart that does not gets the piece from a wrapper-rendered object through its existing-object input. scripts/check-network-config becomes scripts/check-env-config and guards all of it.

Tech Stack: Helm (wrapper charts, tpl), Argo CD ApplicationSets, Python check script, Terragrunt bootstrap module, Go tests.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-16-env-settings-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Global names: global.baseDomain, global.timezone, global.seedRepository (never global.domain: argo-cd owns it).
  • Production config.json: domain khuedoan.com (placeholder), timezone Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh, seed_repository https://github.com/duongle-steven/homelab. Sandbox: 127-0-0-1.nip.io, Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh, https://github.com/duongle-steven/homelab.
  • Host names are <label>.<baseDomain>; labels unchanged (argocd, grafana, git, registry, auth, ci, chat, matrix, home, …).
  • values-dev.yaml keeps only sandbox differences; a file left empty is deleted.
  • Every changed component renders in production and the sandbox (scripts/render-chart <dir> [dev]).

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A subchart value that looks templated in one place but is copied raw elsewhere (e.g. argo-cd's global.domain also feeding a URL) — the guard's literal-{{ check must catch it. Pinned in Task 1's check (no rendered {{ .Values.global).
  2. A wrapper object that replaces a subchart's (argocd-cm, zot config, Forgejo app.ini section) must keep every setting the subchart rendered before, not only the domain ones. Pinned in Tasks 4 (render diff before/after shows only the intended differences).
  3. Argo CD self-management: replacing argocd-cm by a wrapper template must not drop the chart's own keys (url, admin.enabled, exec.enabled, ignoreDifferences customizations). Pinned in Task 4 (diff) and Task 7 (SSO tests).
  4. The seed placeholder in values-seed.yaml must never reach a cluster unreplaced. Pinned in Task 6 (bootstrap render check).
  5. Production-only components (woodpecker, renovate, matrix, cloudflared) are only rendered. Pinned in Task 5 (renders) and the production checklist.

docs.title: Task 1: Config, globals and the guard
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: infra/production/cluster/config.json, infra/sandbox/cluster/config.json, system/argocd/values.yaml, system/argocd/values-dev.yaml, system/argocd/values-seed.yaml (the valuesObject blocks), scripts/check-network-config → scripts/check-env-config (git mv), CLAUDE.md/docs references to the script name

Interfaces: - Produces: .Values.global.{baseDomain,timezone,seedRepository} in every component and app; scripts/check-env-config.

  • Step 1: Rename and extend the check (RED)

git mv scripts/check-network-config scripts/check-env-config; update its docstring's first line to "No chart or app file holds an environment setting (address, domain)." and every reference (grep -rln check-network-config --exclude-dir=site --exclude-dir=docs/superpowers .; replace in CLAUDE.md, docs, Makefiles).

Add near the top:

# Domains that belong in infra/<env>/cluster/config.json, never in a chart or app file
DOMAINS = {"prod": "khuedoan.com", "dev": "127-0-0-1.nip.io"}
# Globals we pass to every chart (system/argocd ApplicationSets): no subchart may define them in its own global
OUR_GLOBALS = {"addresses", "baseDomain", "timezone", "seedRepository"}

and in main(), before printing failures:

    # No domain literal in charts and app files (comments excepted)
    grep = subprocess.run(["git", "grep", "-n", "-E", r"khuedoan\.com|127-0-0-1\.nip\.io", "--", "system", "platform", "apps"],
                          capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    for line in grep.splitlines():
        path, _, text = line.split(":", 2)
        if not text.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            failures.append(f"{path}: names a domain: {text.strip()[:80]}")
    # A render never carries the other environment's domain, nor an unrendered global
    for env, other in (("prod", DOMAINS["dev"]), ("dev", DOMAINS["prod"])):
        for target in targets():
            text = "".join(yaml.safe_dump(d) for d in render(target, env) if d.get("kind") != "CustomResourceDefinition")
            if other in text:
                failures.append(f"{target} ({env}): renders {other}")
            if "Values.global." in text:
                failures.append(f"{target} ({env}): renders an untemplated .Values.global reference")
    # Our globals must not collide with a subchart's own global values (argo-cd has global.domain, Istio global.network)
    for chart in sorted(glob.glob("system/*/charts/*.tgz") + glob.glob("platform/*/charts/*.tgz") + glob.glob("apps/*/charts/*.tgz")):
        out = subprocess.run(["helm", "show", "values", chart], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
        own = set(((yaml.load(out, Loader=Loader) or {}).get("global") or {}).keys())
        for key in sorted(own & OUR_GLOBALS):
            failures.append(f"{chart}: its global.{key} collides with ours")

(The render loop reuses render(); merge it into the existing per-target loop if that avoids rendering twice — renders are the slow part.) targets() must render after helm dependency update so charts/*.tgz exist; render-chart already runs it.

Run: scripts/check-env-config > .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-16-env-settings/check-red.log; tail -1 .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-16-env-settings/check-red.log; grep -c 'names a domain' .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-16-env-settings/check-red.log Expected: failures, about 50 names a domain lines (the inventory in the spec), no collision lines.

  • Step 2: Config and globals

Add to both config.json files (values per Global Constraints):

  "domain": "khuedoan.com",
  "timezone": "Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh",
  "seed_repository": "https://github.com/duongle-steven/homelab",

In every valuesObject.global block of system/argocd/values.yaml (&values and the apps' *addresses neighbour), values-dev.yaml and values-seed.yaml, add beside addresses:

                    baseDomain: '{{ .domain }}'
                    timezone: '{{ .timezone }}'
                    seedRepository: '{{ .seed_repository }}'

(In values.yaml the apps source reuses *values's map if it is an anchor; otherwise restate. Keep the apps' global.domain parameter for now: Task 3 moves the app files.)

Run: scripts/env-values prod root | sort; scripts/env-values dev apps | sort Expected: the three new keys with the environment's values (plus the five addresses keys).

  • Step 3: Commit
git add -A scripts infra system/argocd CLAUDE.md docs
git commit -m "feat: domain, time zone and seed repository in infra/<env>/cluster/config.json; check-env-config"

docs.title: Task 2: Components whose own templates use the domain
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: system/istio-system/{values.yaml,values-dev.yaml,templates/gateway.yaml,templates/certificate.yaml,templates/coredns-custom.yaml}, platform/kanidm/{values.yaml,values-dev.yaml,templates/kanidm.yaml}, platform/{grafana,forgejo,zot}/templates/kanidm-client.yaml and their values.yaml/values-dev.yaml host: keys

  • Step 1: istio-system: every .Values.domain → .Values.global.baseDomain; delete domain: from values.yaml and values-dev.yaml; coredns-custom.yaml's rewrite uses .Values.global.baseDomain (its comment may keep the example name).
  • Step 2: kanidm: kanidm.domain: auth.khuedoan.com → the template builds auth.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }} (replace the value with host: auth and use {{ .Values.host }}.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }} wherever .Values.kanidm.domain is read; grep -rn 'kanidm.domain' platform/kanidm).
  • Step 3: grafana, forgejo, zot: host: <name>.khuedoan.com → host: grafana / git / registry; their kanidm-client.yaml uses https://{{ .Values.host }}.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }}; delete host: from their values-dev.yaml.
  • Step 4: Verify

Run: for c in system/istio-system platform/kanidm platform/grafana platform/forgejo platform/zot; do for e in prod dev; do scripts/render-chart $c $e >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "render FAIL $c $e"; done; done; scripts/render-chart system/istio-system dev | grep -c '127-0-0-1.nip.io'; scripts/render-chart platform/grafana | yq 'select(.kind=="KanidmOAuth2Client") | .spec.origin' Expected: no render FAIL; a non-zero count; https://grafana.khuedoan.com.

  • Step 5: Commit — git commit -am "feat: istio-system, kanidm and Kanidm clients build host names from global.baseDomain"

docs.title: Task 3: Subcharts with tpl, and the app files
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: platform/grafana/{values.yaml,values-dev.yaml}, system/cloudflared/values.yaml, platform/forgejo/values.yaml (route only), apps/*.yaml, system/argocd/{values.yaml,values-dev.yaml,values-seed.yaml} (apps parameter)

  • Step 1: grafana: grafana.ini URLs and route hostnames → grafana.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }}, https://auth.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }}/…; delete those keys from values-dev.yaml (keep its sandbox-only settings).
  • Step 2: cloudflared: '*.khuedoan.com' → '*.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }}'. forgejo: route hostname git.khuedoan.com → git.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }} (delete from values-dev.yaml).
  • Step 3: apps: sed -i 's/\.Values\.global\.domain/.Values.global.baseDomain/g' apps/*.yaml; apps/blog.yaml image registry.khuedoan.com/blog → registry.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }}/blog (if app-template does not template image.repository, move the image to a field it does or ledger the limitation and leave blog for 7c's domain); apps/homepage.yaml https://homelab.khuedoan.com (upstream's docs site) → https://github.com/duongle-steven/homelab. Remove the global.domain parameter from the apps ApplicationSet in values.yaml, values-dev.yaml, values-seed.yaml (baseDomain now comes from valuesObject).
  • Step 4: Verify

Run: scripts/render-chart platform/grafana dev | grep -E 'root_url|auth_url'; scripts/render-chart apps/homepage.yaml dev | grep -c 'home.127-0-0-1.nip.io'; scripts/render-chart system/cloudflared | grep hostname Expected: sandbox URLs for grafana; non-zero; '*.khuedoan.com'.

  • Step 5: Commit — git commit -am "feat: grafana, cloudflared, Forgejo's route and the apps read global.baseDomain"

docs.title: Task 4: Subcharts without tpl (sandbox components)
docs.text:
Files: - Modify/Create: system/argocd/{values.yaml,values-dev.yaml,templates/argocd-cm.yaml,templates/httproute.yaml}, platform/forgejo/{values.yaml,values-dev.yaml,templates/app-ini.yaml}, platform/zot/{values.yaml,values-dev.yaml,templates/config.yaml}

For each component, before editing save the current render (scripts/render-chart <dir> > before.yaml, also dev) in the workspace; after, diff the renders: only the domain-carrying objects may differ, and only by moving into the wrapper object.

  • Step 1: argocd
  • argo-cd.global.domain: 'argocd.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }}' (the chart templates it; check the render's url:).
  • argo-cd.configs.cm.create: false; new templates/argocd-cm.yaml renders ConfigMap argocd-cm (labels app.kubernetes.io/name: argocd-cm, app.kubernetes.io/part-of: argocd) with data: {{ tpl (toYaml .Values.cm) . | nindent 2 }}; move the content of argo-cd.configs.cm into a top-level cm: map, adding the keys the chart set itself (copy them from before.yaml's argocd-cm: url, admin.enabled, application.instanceLabelKey, exec.enabled, … whatever it rendered); oidc.config's issuer → https://auth.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }}/oauth2/openid/argocd; delete the sandbox's oidc.config override from values-dev.yaml.
  • argo-cd.server.httproute.enabled: false; new templates/httproute.yaml with the same spec the chart rendered (from before.yaml), hostname argocd.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }}.
  • Diff: argocd-cm keys identical except the issuer's host; the HTTPRoute identical except owner labels.
  • Step 2: forgejo
  • [server] (DOMAIN, ROOT_URL, SSH_DOMAIN): remove from gitea.config.server and render a ConfigMap forgejo-app-ini-server in templates/app-ini.yaml with key server and value DOMAIN=git.<baseDomain>\nROOT_URL=https://git.<baseDomain>\nSSH_DOMAIN=git.<baseDomain> (keep the other server keys in gitea.config.server); add gitea.additionalConfigSources: [{configMap: {name: forgejo-app-ini-server}}].
  • OAuth autoDiscoverUrl: the chart writes it into its configure-gitea script inside double quotes. Probe: set autoDiscoverUrl: https://auth.${HOMELAB_DOMAIN}/oauth2/openid/forgejo/.well-known/openid-configuration and deployment.env: [{name: HOMELAB_DOMAIN, valueFrom: {configMapKeyRef: {name: forgejo-app-ini-server, key: domain}}}] (add domain: <baseDomain> to that ConfigMap), then check the render: the init container configure-gitea gets the env (if deployment.env reaches only the main container, look for the chart's init-container env input in helm show values platform/forgejo/charts/forgejo-*.tgz; if none, ledger and use the chart's gitea.oauth with an explicit sandbox override kept in values-dev.yaml as the only remaining domain there).
  • Delete the moved keys from values-dev.yaml.
  • Step 3: zot
  • zot reads config.json from the chart's config: (a Secret zot-config). Render that Secret in templates/config.yaml instead (stringData.config.json: {{ tpl (toJson .Values.zotConfig) . }} where zotConfig is today's zot.config content with externalUrl and the OIDC issuer templated), set zot.config: {} and point the chart at the existing Secret (check helm show values for the existing-secret key, e.g. existingSecret/secretName; if the chart has none, mount the Secret with extraVolumes/extraVolumeMounts at the path the chart used and ledger it).
  • Delete the moved keys from values-dev.yaml.
  • Step 4: Verify

Run: scripts/check-env-config | grep -E 'argocd|forgejo|zot' | head; for c in system/argocd platform/forgejo platform/zot; do for e in prod dev; do scripts/render-chart $c $e > /dev/null || echo "FAIL $c $e"; done; done Expected: no failure lines for these three; renders succeed.

  • Step 5: Commit — git commit -am "feat: Argo CD, Forgejo and zot get their domain settings from wrapper templates"

docs.title: Task 5: Production-only components and the time zone
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: platform/woodpecker, platform/renovate, apps/matrix, system/kured

  • Step 1: woodpecker — WOODPECKER_HOST, WOODPECKER_FORGEJO_URL: move to a wrapper ConfigMap read through the chart's env-from input (helm show values platform/woodpecker/charts/woodpecker-*.tgz | grep -n -i 'envfrom\|extraSecretNamesForEnvFrom'); its HTTPRoute template (already ours) uses ci.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }}.
  • Step 2: renovate — the endpoint in its config: render the config in the wrapper (templates/secret.yaml already exists) or use the chart's existing-config input; https://git.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }}/api/v1.
  • Step 3: matrix — its own templates/httproute.yaml uses the global for chat./matrix.; dendrite's server_name and base_url: if dendrite's chart does not template them, render its config Secret in the wrapper (check helm show values apps/matrix/charts/dendrite-*.tgz | grep -n -i existing) or ledger it as the remaining production-only literal with a checklist entry.
  • Step 4: kured — configuration.timeZone: '{{ .Values.global.timezone }}' if the chart templates it (render shows the zone); otherwise ledger and keep the value, noting it in the checklist.
  • Step 5: Verify and commit

Run: scripts/check-env-config | grep -E 'woodpecker|renovate|matrix|kured'; for c in platform/woodpecker platform/renovate apps/matrix system/kured; do scripts/render-chart $c >/dev/null || echo "FAIL $c"; done Expected: no lines (or only ledgered, explained literals); renders succeed.

git commit -am "feat: woodpecker, renovate, matrix and kured read the environment's settings"

docs.title: Task 6: Seed repository, configure script, docs
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: system/argocd/values-seed.yaml, infra/_modules/argocd/{bootstrap.sh,main.tf}, infra/production/argocd/terragrunt.hcl, platform/forgejo (seed Job reads global.seedRepository), CLAUDE.md, docs/installation/production/configuration.md - Delete: scripts/configure, empty values-dev.yaml files, the root Makefile's configure target

  • Step 1: values-seed.yaml: repoURL: &repoURL https://github.com/khuedoan/homelab → repoURL: &repoURL https://seed-repository.invalid with a comment "replaced by infra/_modules/argocd with config.json's seed_repository". bootstrap.sh: when $values is the seed file, pipe the rendered manifests through sed "s|https://seed-repository.invalid|$SEED_REPOSITORY|g" and fail if the placeholder remains (grep -q seed-repository.invalid → exit 1). The module takes seed_repository (variable, default ""), the production unit reads it from config.json (jsondecode(file("${get_terragrunt_dir()}/../cluster/config.json")).seed_repository) and passes it as SEED_REPOSITORY.
  • Step 2: forgejo's seed Job: seed.repository → {{ .Values.global.seedRepository }} (delete seed.repository from values.yaml and values-dev.yaml).
  • Step 3: git rm scripts/configure; remove the configure target from the root Makefile; docs/installation/production/configuration.md: replace make configure with "edit infra/production/cluster/config.json (domain, time zone, seed repository, addresses)"; the Terraform Cloud workspace in external/versions.tf gets a sentence "change organization to yours (until step 7c)".
  • Step 4: delete every values-dev.yaml that is now empty (for f in system/*/values-dev.yaml platform/*/values-dev.yaml; do [ -z "$(yq 'del(.. | select(tag == "!!null"))' $f | grep -v '^#' | tr -d '[:space:]{}')" ] && git rm $f; done, then re-render those components in dev).
  • Step 5: CLAUDE.md: roadmap 7b done; rules: "Domain, time zone and seed repository live only in infra/<env>/cluster/config.json (global.baseDomain, global.timezone, global.seedRepository); scripts/check-env-config checks it"; replace scripts/check-network-config everywhere; the production checklist item "Run make configure …" becomes "Set infra/production/cluster/config.json (your domain, time zone, seed repository) and external/versions.tf's Terraform Cloud organization (until 7c)"; list any ledgered literal left in production-only components.
  • Step 6: Verify and commit

Run: scripts/check-env-config | tail -1; mkdocs build --strict 2>&1 | tail -1; KUBECONFIG=/dev/null sh -c 'cd infra/production/argocd && terragrunt validate-inputs --non-interactive' 2>&1 | tail -1 Expected: 0 failures; Documentation built; inputs valid.

git commit -am "feat: seed repository from config.json at bootstrap; drop scripts/configure"

docs.title: Task 7: Prove it
docs.text:
• Step 1: basic checks: make -C infra check && scripts/check-env-config | tail -1 && scripts/check-mesh-policies >/dev/null && echo mesh-ok && (cd test && go vet ./... && go test -run 'TestSmokeAppsForEnv|TestIdentity(TOTPWaitsForNextStep|PKCE)|TestGatewayRouteReady|TestGatewayNodeAddressFromInspect' ./...) | tail -1 Expected: all pass.
  • Step 2: make dev-clean; make dev > .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-16-env-settings/make-dev.log 2>&1; echo exit=$?; grep -E '^(--- FAIL|FAIL)|^DONE' .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-16-env-settings/make-dev.log Expected: exit=0, DONE 98 tests.
  • Step 3: git grep -n -E 'khuedoan\.com|127-0-0-1\.nip\.io' -- system platform apps | grep -v ':\s*#' Expected: no output (or only ledgered production-only literals).

docs.title: Infra (Step 7a) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Terragrunt units under infra/ create, bootstrap and remove the sandbox, and bootstrap production's Argo CD, replacing metal/Makefile's k3d targets and system/bootstrap.yml.

Architecture: infra/root.hcl (local state, kubeconfig path) includes per-environment units; module k3d wraps k3d and the socat proxy in terraform_data resources; module argocd renders system/argocd and applies it server-side once, re-applied only when its files change. The root Makefile drives Terragrunt.

Tech Stack: OpenTofu 1.13, Terragrunt 1.1, hashicorp/external 2.4.2, k3d 5.9, Helm, kubectl, GNU make.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-16-infra-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Layout: infra/root.hcl, infra/Makefile, infra/_modules/k3d, infra/_modules/argocd, infra/sandbox/cluster, infra/sandbox/argocd, infra/production/argocd.
  • State: local, <repo>/.state/<env>/<unit>/terraform.tfstate, git-ignored.
  • Kubeconfig: infra/<env>/kubeconfig.yaml (*kubeconfig.yaml is already git-ignored).
  • Bootstrap: kubectl apply --server-side --field-manager argocd-controller --force-conflicts of helm template --include-crds system/argocd; production picks values-seed.yaml when no pod app.kubernetes.io/instance=forgejo is Running, else values.yaml; the sandbox uses values-dev.yaml.
  • Production's bootstrap resource has prevent_destroy.
  • Unchanged: production nodes via make -C metal (Ansible), external/.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A second apply on an unchanged sandbox must change nothing (proxy keyed on the node address, bootstrap keyed on file hashes). Pinned in Task 2 and Task 3 (plan shows no changes) and Task 5.
  2. Destroy must not leave a running proxy, cluster, Docker network or kubeconfig, and must work when the cluster is already gone. Pinned in Task 2 (destroy, then destroy again).
  3. prevent_destroy cannot take a variable: production's protected resource must still be the only one created there. Pinned in Task 3 (plan lists exactly one resource per environment).
  4. The bootstrap hash must ignore files Helm writes (charts/, Chart.lock), or every run re-applies. Pinned in Task 3.
  5. Terragrunt runs cluster before argocd in the sandbox, and run --all destroy removes argocd's state before deleting the cluster. Pinned in Task 4/5 (make dev, make dev-clean).

docs.title: Task 1: Tools and infra/ skeleton
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: flake.nix, flake.lock (only if nixpkgs-unstable is updated), .gitignore - Create: infra/root.hcl, infra/Makefile

Interfaces: - Produces: root.hcl locals env, unit, kubeconfig; input kubeconfig for every unit; make -C infra check.

  • Step 1: Write the check

.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-16-infra/check-task1.sh:

#!/bin/sh
# The dev shell has OpenTofu and Terragrunt; infra/ validates and is formatted
set -e
tofu version | head -1 | grep -q 'OpenTofu v1.13'
terragrunt --version | grep -q 'v1\.'
make -C infra check
echo "task1: ok"

Run: mkdir -p .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-16-infra && chmod +x .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-16-infra/check-task1.sh && direnv exec . .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-16-infra/check-task1.sh Expected: FAIL (OpenTofu 1.11, or terragrunt: not found).

  • Step 2: Dev shell

In flake.nix, replace opentofu # Drop-in replacement for Terraform with:

            unstable.opentofu # Drop-in replacement for Terraform (nixos-26.05 ships 1.11)
            unstable.terragrunt

Run nix eval --raw --impure --expr 'let f = builtins.getFlake (toString ./.); u = import f.inputs.nixpkgs-unstable { system = "x86_64-linux"; }; in u.terragrunt.version'. If it is older than the latest release (gh release view --repo gruntwork-io/terragrunt --json tagName -q .tagName, 1.1.6 on 2026-10-16), run nix flake update nixpkgs-unstable and check again; keep whichever is newest available and ledger the version.

  • Step 3: .gitignore

Append:

# OpenTofu and Terragrunt (state is local until step 8)
.state/
.terragrunt-cache/
.terraform/
  • Step 4: infra/root.hcl
# Included by every unit: infra/<env>/<unit>/terragrunt.hcl
locals {
  env        = split("/", path_relative_to_include())[0]
  unit       = basename(get_original_terragrunt_dir())
  kubeconfig = "${get_repo_root()}/infra/${local.env}/kubeconfig.yaml"
}

# Local state until step 8 (Cloudflare R2 with state encryption)
remote_state {
  backend = "local"
  generate = {
    path      = "backend.tf"
    if_exists = "overwrite_terragrunt"
  }
  config = {
    path = "${get_repo_root()}/.state/${path_relative_to_include()}/terraform.tfstate"
  }
}

inputs = {
  kubeconfig = local.kubeconfig
}

infra/Makefile:

.POSIX:
.PHONY: check

# Offline: HCL is valid and formatted (part of the basic checks)
check:
    terragrunt hcl validate
    tofu fmt -check -recursive .
    terragrunt hcl fmt --check
  • Step 5: Run the check

Run: direnv allow && direnv exec . .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-16-infra/check-task1.sh Expected: task1: ok.

  • Step 6: Commit
git add flake.nix flake.lock .gitignore infra/root.hcl infra/Makefile
git commit -m "feat(infra): OpenTofu and Terragrunt in the dev shell; infra/root.hcl"

docs.title: Task 2: Module k3d and the sandbox cluster unit
docs.text:
Files: - Create: infra/_modules/k3d/main.tf, infra/_modules/k3d/k3d.yaml (moved from metal/k3d-dev.yaml), infra/sandbox/cluster/terragrunt.hcl - Delete: metal/k3d-dev.yaml (git mv)

Interfaces: - Consumes: root.hcl input kubeconfig. - Produces: unit infra/sandbox/cluster (creates k3d cluster homelab-dev, kubeconfig infra/sandbox/kubeconfig.yaml, proxy homelab-dev-proxy); output kubeconfig.

  • Step 1: Remove the running sandbox the old way, then write the check

Run first: direnv exec . make -C metal env=dev clean (the old target still exists).

.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-16-infra/check-task2.sh:

#!/bin/sh
# infra/sandbox/cluster creates, keeps and removes the sandbox cluster and its proxy
set -e
cd infra/sandbox/cluster
terragrunt apply -auto-approve --non-interactive >/dev/null
k3d cluster list homelab-dev >/dev/null
test -s ../kubeconfig.yaml
KUBECONFIG=../kubeconfig.yaml kubectl get nodes --no-headers | grep -q ' Ready '
docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' homelab-dev-proxy | grep -q true
test "$(docker network inspect k3d-homelab-dev -f '{{range .IPAM.Config}}{{.Subnet}}{{end}}')" = 172.28.0.0/16
terragrunt plan -detailed-exitcode --non-interactive >/dev/null   # 0: no changes
terragrunt destroy -auto-approve --non-interactive >/dev/null
! k3d cluster list homelab-dev >/dev/null 2>&1
! docker inspect homelab-dev-proxy >/dev/null 2>&1

infra/_modules/k3d/main.tf:

# The k3d sandbox: one k3s server (k3d.yaml), the latest Gateway API CRDs in k3s's auto-deploy manifests (k3s's
# packaged ones are disabled), and a localhost proxy: under WSL mirrored networking Windows cannot reach ports
# Docker publishes, so a host-network socat forwards 127.0.0.1:80/443/22 to the node (ServiceLB serves the Gateway)
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.13"
  required_providers {
    external = {
      source  = "hashicorp/external"
      version = "2.4.2"
    }
  }
}

variable "kubeconfig" {
  type = string
}

variable "name" {
  type    = string
  default = "homelab-dev"
}

variable "gateway_api_version" {
  type    = string
  default = "v1.6.3"
}

variable "proxy_bind" {
  type    = string
  default = "127.0.0.1"
}

locals {
  config   = abspath("${path.module}/k3d.yaml")
  manifest = abspath("${path.module}/gateway-api-${var.gateway_api_version}.yaml")
  node     = "k3d-${var.name}-server-0"
  proxy    = "${var.name}-proxy"
}

resource "terraform_data" "cluster" {
  triggers_replace = [filesha1(local.config), var.gateway_api_version, var.name]
  input            = { name = var.name, kubeconfig = var.kubeconfig }

  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command = <<-EOT
      set -eu
      [ -s "${local.manifest}" ] || curl -fsSL -o "${local.manifest}" \
        https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/${var.gateway_api_version}/standard-install.yaml
      k3d cluster list ${var.name} >/dev/null 2>&1 || k3d cluster create --config "${local.config}" \
        --volume "${local.manifest}:/var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/manifests/gateway-api.yaml@server:*"
      k3d kubeconfig get ${var.name} > "${var.kubeconfig}"
    EOT
  }

  provisioner "local-exec" {
    when    = destroy
    command = "k3d cluster delete ${self.input.name}; rm -f '${self.input.kubeconfig}'"
  }
}

# The node's address (it can change when the cluster is recreated)
data "external" "node" {
  depends_on = [terraform_data.cluster]
  program    = ["sh", "-c", "printf '{\"ip\":\"%s\"}' \"$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' ${local.node})\""]
}

resource "terraform_data" "proxy" {
  triggers_replace = [data.external.node.result.ip, var.proxy_bind]
  input            = { name = local.proxy }

  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command = <<-EOT
      set -eu
      node="${data.external.node.result.ip}"
      [ -n "$node" ] || { echo "the k3d node ${local.node} is not running"; exit 1; }
      docker rm -f ${local.proxy} >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      if ss -ltnH '( sport = :80 or sport = :443 or sport = :22 )' | grep -q .; then
        echo "ports 80/443/22 are already in use on this host:"; ss -ltnp '( sport = :80 or sport = :443 or sport = :22 )'; exit 1
      fi
      docker run -d --name ${local.proxy} --network host --restart unless-stopped \
        --entrypoint sh alpine/socat:1.8.1.3 -c "\
          socat TCP-LISTEN:80,bind=${var.proxy_bind},fork,reuseaddr TCP:$node:80 & \
          socat TCP-LISTEN:22,bind=${var.proxy_bind},fork,reuseaddr TCP:$node:22 & \
          exec socat TCP-LISTEN:443,bind=${var.proxy_bind},fork,reuseaddr TCP:$node:443" >/dev/null
    EOT
  }

  provisioner "local-exec" {
    when    = destroy
    command = "docker rm -f ${self.input.name} >/dev/null 2>&1 || true"
  }
}

output "kubeconfig" {
  value      = var.kubeconfig
  depends_on = [terraform_data.cluster]
}

infra/_modules/argocd/bootstrap.sh:

#!/bin/sh
# Render system/argocd and apply it once; Argo CD manages itself from then on (system/argocd is in the root
# ApplicationSet), so the field manager is Argo CD's.
# Env: KUBECONFIG, CHART (system/argocd), VALUES (file name in CHART), SEED (file used while Forgejo is not running;
# production's first install syncs from GitHub until Forgejo holds the repository)
set -eu
kubectl create namespace argocd --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null
values="$VALUES"
if [ -n "${SEED:-}" ] && [ -z "$(kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=forgejo \
  --field-selector status.phase=Running -o name)" ]; then
  values="$SEED"
fi
helm dependency build "$CHART" >/dev/null
helm template argocd "$CHART" --namespace argocd --include-crds -f "$CHART/$values" \
  | kubectl apply --server-side --field-manager argocd-controller --force-conflicts -f -

infra/_modules/argocd/main.tf:

# Bootstrap Argo CD from the repository's system/argocd chart. Applied once and again only when the chart's files
# or the chosen values change; every later change reaches the cluster through Argo CD's own sync from git.
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.13"
}

variable "kubeconfig" {
  type = string
}

variable "chart" {
  type        = string
  description = "Absolute path of system/argocd"
}

variable "values" {
  type        = string
  description = "Values file in the chart directory"
}

variable "seed" {
  type        = string
  default     = ""
  description = "Values file used while Forgejo is not running (production's first install)"
}

variable "protect" {
  type        = bool
  default     = false
  description = "Refuse to destroy (production)"
}

locals {
  # Helm writes charts/ and Chart.lock: hash only what the repository holds
  files = sort(setunion(fileset(var.chart, "*.yaml"), fileset(var.chart, "templates/**")))
  hash  = sha1(join("", [for f in local.files : filesha1("${var.chart}/${f}")]))
  environment = {
    KUBECONFIG = var.kubeconfig
    CHART      = var.chart
    VALUES     = var.values
    SEED       = var.seed
  }
  command = "sh ${abspath("${path.module}/bootstrap.sh")}"
}

# prevent_destroy cannot take a variable: one resource per setting, only one of them exists
resource "terraform_data" "bootstrap" {
  count            = var.protect ? 0 : 1
  triggers_replace = [local.hash, var.values, var.seed]

  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command     = local.command
    environment = local.environment
  }
}

resource "terraform_data" "protected" {
  count            = var.protect ? 1 : 0
  triggers_replace = [local.hash, var.values, var.seed]

  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command     = local.command
    environment = local.environment
  }

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}

docs.title: Step 8b: OpenTofu's secrets through External Secrets, self-hosted ntfy — Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Cloudflare's and WireGuard's secrets reach OpenBao as Kubernetes Secrets OpenTofu writes and a PushSecret pushes; alerts go to a self-hosted ntfy published through the Tunnel; external/ and scripts/backup disappear.

Architecture: A new OpenTofu unit infra/<env>/secrets applies Secrets into namespace infra-secrets; the new component platform/infra-secrets pushes them through SecretStore openbao-infra (OpenBao role/policy infra: every branch except generated/). apps/ntfy.yaml runs ntfy (users and tokens generated by platform/global-secrets); Alertmanager posts to it directly.

Tech Stack: OpenTofu + Terragrunt (providers hashicorp/random 3.9.1, OJFord/wireguard 0.4.1+2), OpenBao 2.7.1, External Secrets 2.12 (PushSecret v1alpha1), ntfy v2.31.1, kube-prometheus-stack, app-template, Go tests (terratest).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-infra-secrets-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Feature branch feat/infra-secrets (exists, from dev); PR into dev. Never commit to dev or master.
  • Versions pinned exactly: ntfy v2.31.1, OJFord/wireguard 0.4.1+2, hashicorp/random 3.9.1.
  • Charts and app files hold no domain or IP: hosts as <host>.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }}.
  • A component's ExternalSecrets read SecretStore openbao with keys under its own namespace.
  • Generated secrets: <namespace>/generated/<name>, pushed only by platform/global-secrets through openbao-writer. OpenTofu's: outside generated/, pushed only by platform/infra-secrets through openbao-infra.
  • OpenBao's roles accept only audience openbao.
  • Secret values never reach an argument, a log or the repo; never print them in a shell.
  • Every meshed namespace needs an AuthorizationPolicy allow; in-cluster calls the renders cannot show go to EXTRA in scripts/check-mesh-policies.
  • Basic checks before make dev: scripts/render-chart <dir> and scripts/render-chart <dir> dev for every changed chart or app file; cd test && go vet ./... && go test -run 'TestSmokeAppsForEnv|TestIdentity(TOTPWaitsForNextStep|PKCE)|TestGatewayRouteReady|TestGatewayNodeAddressFromInspect' ./...; mkdocs build --strict; scripts/check-mesh-policies; scripts/check-env-config; scripts/check-secret-stores; make -C infra check. Tools run through direnv exec /home/nixos/homelab ….
  • Sandbox tests run once, at the end (make dev-clean && make dev), because OpenBao only loads policies on first start.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A PushSecret whose source Secret does not exist in that environment (sandbox: no Cloudflare) must not exist: values-dev.yaml of platform/infra-secrets lists only wireguard/private-key (Task 1 render check).
  2. ntfy reachable without credentials would leak every alert publicly: anonymous publish and subscribe must be refused (Task 4 test TestNtfyDeniesAnonymous).
  3. The infra policy must not reach generated/ even with update on secret/data/* (deny wins): Task 1 test TestSecretsInfraRole writes outside and is refused inside.
  4. Re-running make dev (second apply of the unit) must keep the WireGuard key: Task 2 test TestSecretsInfraPush compares the pushed value with the Secret, and the module has no trigger on the key.
  5. Alertmanager's token file must reach ntfy: an alert posted to Alertmanager arrives in topic alerts (Task 5 test TestNtfyAlertmanagerDelivers).

docs.title: Task 1: OpenBao role infra and platform/infra-secrets
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: platform/openbao/values.yaml (policy and role infra) - Create: platform/infra-secrets/Chart.yaml, platform/infra-secrets/values.yaml, platform/infra-secrets/values-dev.yaml, platform/infra-secrets/templates/service-account.yaml, platform/infra-secrets/templates/secret-store.yaml, platform/infra-secrets/templates/push-secrets.yaml - Modify: system/argocd/values-dev.yaml (root directories: platform/infra-secrets after platform/global-secrets) - Modify: scripts/check-secret-stores (two writers) - Modify: platform/openbao/templates/authorization-policy.yaml only if check-mesh-policies asks (ESO makes the calls, already allowed) - Test: test/secrets_test.go (TestSecretsInfraRole)

Interfaces: - Produces: namespace infra-secrets (Argo CD), Secrets expected there named <namespace>.<name> (dots), one key per OpenBao property; values key secrets: = list of {path: <namespace>/<name>, properties: [..]}; service account openbao-infra; OpenBao role infra.

  • Step 1: Write the failing checker change (RED)

In scripts/check-secret-stores, replace WRITER = ("platform/global-secrets", "openbao-writer") with:

# Who pushes, through which SecretStore, and whether its keys are generated/ ones
WRITERS = {
    "platform/global-secrets": ("openbao-writer", True),
    "platform/infra-secrets": ("openbao-infra", False),
}

and the PushSecret branch with:

                elif kind == "PushSecret":
                    refs = [(r.get("kind", "SecretStore"), r.get("name")) for r in spec.get("secretStoreRefs") or []]
                    writer = WRITERS.get(target)
                    if writer is None or refs != [("SecretStore", writer[0])]:
                        failures.append(f"{where}: only {', '.join(f'{t} (SecretStore {s})' for t, (s, _) in WRITERS.items())} push")
                        continue
                    for item in spec.get("data") or []:
                        key = item["match"]["remoteRef"]["remoteKey"]
                        if bool(GENERATED.fullmatch(key)) != writer[1]:
                            failures.append(f"{where}: pushes {key}: {target} writes {'only' if writer[1] else 'nothing under'} <namespace>/generated/")
                        pushed.setdefault(key, where)

Update the docstring's PushSecret bullets to name both writers. Keep the "pushes nobody reads" loop (both writers) and the "reads generated/ nothing pushes" loop.

  • Step 2: Create the chart

platform/infra-secrets/Chart.yaml:

apiVersion: v2
name: infra-secrets
version: 0.0.0

platform/infra-secrets/values.yaml:

# Secrets OpenTofu writes into this namespace (unit infra/<env>/secrets: Secret <namespace>.<name>, one key per
# property) and pushes to OpenBao's secret/<namespace>/<name>; readers use their namespace's SecretStore openbao.
# OpenTofu is the source: a changed value replaces OpenBao's (docs/concepts/secrets-management.md)
secrets:
  - path: cert-manager/cloudflare
    properties: [api_token]
  - path: external-dns/cloudflare
    properties: [api_token, zone_id]
  - path: cloudflared/cloudflare
    properties: [credentials.json]
  - path: wireguard/private-key
    properties: [private-key]

platform/infra-secrets/values-dev.yaml:

# The sandbox has no Cloudflare or WireGuard; the WireGuard key proves the path (test/secrets_test.go)
secrets:
  - path: wireguard/private-key
    properties: [private-key]

templates/service-account.yaml:

# OpenBao's role infra (platform/openbao) logs this account in
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: openbao-infra
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}

templates/secret-store.yaml:

# Writes OpenTofu's secrets into OpenBao: role infra reaches every branch except <namespace>/generated/
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: SecretStore
metadata:
  name: openbao-infra
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
spec:
  provider:
    vault:
      server: http://openbao.openbao.svc.cluster.local:8200
      path: secret
      version: v2
      auth:
        kubernetes:
          mountPath: kubernetes
          role: infra
          # OpenBao's roles accept only this audience
          serviceAccountRef:
            name: openbao-infra
            audiences: [openbao]

templates/push-secrets.yaml:

{{- range .Values.secrets }}
{{- $entry := . }}
---
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1alpha1
kind: PushSecret
metadata:
  name: {{ .path | replace "/" "." }}
  namespace: {{ $.Release.Namespace }}
spec:
  # OpenTofu is the source: a changed value replaces OpenBao's, a lost one is pushed again within the hour
  refreshInterval: 1h
  updatePolicy: Replace
  deletionPolicy: None
  secretStoreRefs:
    - kind: SecretStore
      name: openbao-infra
  selector:
    secret:
      name: {{ .path | replace "/" "." }}
  data:
    {{- range .properties }}
    - match:
        secretKey: {{ . }}
        remoteRef:
          remoteKey: {{ $entry.path }}
          property: {{ . }}
    {{- end }}
{{- end }}

// Role infra (OpenTofu's secrets, platform/infra-secrets) writes every branch except generated/, which it neither
// reads nor writes
func TestSecretsInfraRole(t *testing.T) {
    secretsSandboxOnly(t)
    waitForUnsealed(t)
    grafanaAdmin(t) // pushed by now
    defer admin(t, "kv", "metadata", "delete", "secret/grafana/infra-probe")
    out, err := bao(t, "infra", "infra-secrets", "openbao-infra", "kv", "put", "secret/grafana/infra-probe", "value=x")
    require.NoError(t, err, out)

        {"kv", "put", "secret/grafana/generated/admin", "password=x"},
        {"kv", "put", "secret/grafana/generated/new", "value=x"},

    } {

        assert.Error(t, err, "infra: bao %v", args)
        assert.Contains(t, out, "permission denied", "infra: bao %v", args)
    }
    out, err = bao(t, "infra", "grafana", "default", "kv", "get", "secret/grafana/infra-probe")
    assert.Error(t, err, "grafana logged in as infra")

Append to test/secrets_test.go:

// OpenTofu's WireGuard key (infra/sandbox/secrets) reaches OpenBao through platform/infra-secrets, and comes back after
// its OpenBao value is lost
func TestSecretsInfraPush(t *testing.T) {
    secretsSandboxOnly(t)
    waitForUnsealed(t)
    want := secretValue(t, "infra-secrets", "wireguard.private-key", "private-key")
    require.NotEmpty(t, want)
    // The sandbox has no namespace wireguard (production only): read with the admin role
    read := func() string {
        out, err := bao(t, "admin", "openbao", "openbao-admin", "kv", "get", "-field=private-key", "secret/wireguard/private-key")
        if err != nil {
            return ""
        }
        return out
    }
    require.Eventually(t, func() bool { return read() == want }, 20*time.Minute, 15*time.Second,
        "secret/wireguard/private-key does not hold the Secret's value")

    admin(t, "kv", "metadata", "delete", "secret/wireguard/private-key")
    k8s.RunKubectl(t, k8s.NewKubectlOptions("", "", "infra-secrets"), "annotate", "pushsecret", "wireguard.private-key",
        "force-sync="+fmt.Sprint(time.Now().UnixNano()), "--overwrite")
    assert.Eventually(t, func() bool { return read() == want }, 5*time.Minute, 10*time.Second,
        "the lost value was not pushed again")
}

infra/_modules/secrets/main.tf:

# Secrets OpenTofu creates or receives, written as Kubernetes Secrets into namespace infra-secrets, from where
# platform/infra-secrets pushes them to OpenBao (secret/<namespace>/<name>)
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.13"
  required_providers {
    wireguard = {
      source  = "OJFord/wireguard"
      version = "0.4.1+2"
    }
  }
}

variable "kubeconfig" {
  type = string
}

variable "namespace" {
  type        = string
  default     = "infra-secrets"
  description = "Namespace of platform/infra-secrets, created by Argo CD"
}

variable "secrets" {
  type        = map(map(string))
  default     = {}
  sensitive   = true
  description = "OpenBao path (<namespace>/<name>) to properties, from other units (infra/<env>/cloudflare's output secrets)"
}

variable "protect" {
  type        = bool
  default     = false
  description = "Refuse to replace or destroy the WireGuard key (production): every peer would need the new public key"
}

# The cluster's WireGuard key (apps/wireguard.yaml); peers need its public key (output)
resource "wireguard_asymmetric_key" "wireguard" {}

# prevent_destroy cannot take a variable, so it guards the key from a resource of its own (as infra/_modules/openbao)
resource "terraform_data" "protected" {
  count            = var.protect ? 1 : 0
  triggers_replace = [wireguard_asymmetric_key.wireguard.public_key]

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}

locals {
  secrets = merge(
    var.secrets,
    { "wireguard/private-key" = { "private-key" = wireguard_asymmetric_key.wireguard.private_key } },
  )
  manifest = yamlencode({
    apiVersion = "v1"
    kind       = "List"
    items = [for path, data in local.secrets : {
      apiVersion = "v1"
      kind       = "Secret"
      metadata   = { name = replace(path, "/", "."), namespace = var.namespace }
      stringData = data
    }]
  })
}

# Separate from the Secrets below so its timeout message shows: OpenTofu hides the output of a provisioner whose
# environment holds secrets
resource "terraform_data" "namespace" {
  triggers_replace = [plantimestamp()]

  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command = "sh ${abspath("${path.module}/wait-namespace.sh")}"
    environment = {
      KUBECONFIG = var.kubeconfig
      NAMESPACE  = var.namespace
    }
  }
}

# Applied on every run (an idempotent server-side apply): a rebuilt cluster or a deleted Secret gets the same values
resource "terraform_data" "secrets" {
  triggers_replace = [plantimestamp()]
  depends_on       = [terraform_data.namespace]

  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command = "sh ${abspath("${path.module}/apply-secrets.sh")}"
    environment = {
      KUBECONFIG = var.kubeconfig
      MANIFEST   = local.manifest
    }
  }
}

output "wireguard_public_key" {
  value       = wireguard_asymmetric_key.wireguard.public_key
  description = "The cluster's WireGuard public key, for its peers"
}

infra/_modules/secrets/apply-secrets.sh:

#!/bin/sh
# Applies the Secrets OpenTofu rendered (a v1 List). They come through the environment and reach kubectl on stdin:
# never in an argument or a file
set -eu
: "${KUBECONFIG:?}" "${MANIFEST:?}"
printf '%s' "$MANIFEST" | kubectl apply --server-side --field-manager=infra-secrets -f - >/dev/null
echo "Secrets applied"

Copy infra/_modules/openbao/wait-namespace.sh to infra/_modules/secrets/wait-namespace.sh unchanged.

  paths = ["../argocd"]

dependencies {
  paths = ["../argocd"]

dependency "cloudflare" {
  config_path = "../cloudflare"
  # Validation runs before the unit was applied
  mock_outputs                            = { secrets = {} }

  protect = true
}

test/ntfy_test.go:

package test

import (
    "fmt"
    "io"
    "net/http"
    "strings"
    "testing"
    "time"

    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

const ntfyURL = "https://ntfy.127-0-0-1.nip.io"

// ntfyRequest sends method to path with a bearer token (none when empty) and returns the status and body
func ntfyRequest(t *testing.T, method, path, token, body string) (int, string) {
    req, err := http.NewRequest(method, ntfyURL+path, strings.NewReader(body))
    require.NoError(t, err)
    if token != "" {
        req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
    }
    resp, err := insecureClient.Do(req)
    if err != nil {
        return 0, err.Error()
    }
    defer resp.Body.Close()
    raw, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
    return resp.StatusCode, string(raw)
}

func waitForNtfy(t *testing.T) {
    require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        status, _ := ntfyRequest(t, http.MethodGet, "/v1/health", "", "")
        return status == http.StatusOK
    }, 20*time.Minute, 15*time.Second, "ntfy does not answer through the Gateway")
}

func ntfyToken(t *testing.T, user string) string {
    return "tk_" + secretValue(t, "global-secrets", "ntfy."+user+"-token", "token")
}

// Published through the Tunnel in production: nothing without credentials
func TestNtfyDeniesAnonymous(t *testing.T) {
    secretsSandboxOnly(t)
    waitForNtfy(t)
    status, _ := ntfyRequest(t, http.MethodPost, "/alerts", "", "anonymous")
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusForbidden, status, "anonymous publish")
    status, _ = ntfyRequest(t, http.MethodGet, "/alerts/json?poll=1", "", "")
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusForbidden, status, "anonymous subscribe")
    status, _ = ntfyRequest(t, http.MethodPost, "/v1/account", "", `{"username":"x","password":"y"}`)
    assert.NotEqual(t, http.StatusOK, status, "signup is off")
}

// phone reads topic alerts and cannot publish; alerts publishes and cannot read
func TestNtfyUsers(t *testing.T) {
    secretsSandboxOnly(t)
    waitForNtfy(t)
    phone, alerts := ntfyToken(t, "phone"), ntfyToken(t, "alerts")
    status, _ := ntfyRequest(t, http.MethodPost, "/alerts", phone, "from phone")
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusForbidden, status, "phone published")
    status, _ = ntfyRequest(t, http.MethodGet, "/alerts/json?poll=1", alerts, "")
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusForbidden, status, "alerts subscribed")

    marker := fmt.Sprint("ntfy-test-", time.Now().UnixNano())
    status, body := ntfyRequest(t, http.MethodPost, "/alerts", alerts, marker)
    require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, status, body)
    status, body = ntfyRequest(t, http.MethodGet, "/alerts/json?poll=1&since=10m", phone, "")
    require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, status, body)
    assert.Contains(t, body, marker)
}

apps/ntfy.yaml:

# Alerts (Alertmanager posts to topic alerts); published through the Cloudflare Tunnel in production, so nothing is
# readable or writable without a user (docs/how-to-guides/alerts.md)
controllers:
  main:
    containers:
      main:
        image:
          repository: docker.io/binwiederhier/ntfy
          tag: v2.31.1
        args: [serve]
        env:
          NTFY_BASE_URL: https://ntfy.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }}
          # iOS gets instant push only through ntfy.sh, which receives a poll request (the topic's hash), never the
          # message; the sandbox sends nothing out
          NTFY_UPSTREAM_BASE_URL: '{{ if eq .Values.global.publicGateway "public" }}https://ntfy.sh{{ end }}'
          NTFY_BEHIND_PROXY: "true"
          NTFY_CACHE_FILE: /var/lib/ntfy/cache.db
          NTFY_AUTH_FILE: /var/lib/ntfy/auth.db
          NTFY_AUTH_DEFAULT_ACCESS: deny-all
          NTFY_ENABLE_SIGNUP: "false"
          NTFY_AUTH_ACCESS: alerts:alerts:wo,phone:alerts:ro
        # NTFY_AUTH_USERS and NTFY_AUTH_TOKENS, from OpenBao; no attachment cache dir: attachments are off
        envFrom:
          - secretRef:
              name: ntfy-auth
        probes:
          liveness: &probe
            enabled: true
            custom: true
            spec:
              httpGet:
                path: /v1/health
                port: 80
          readiness: *probe
service:
  main:
    ports:
      http:
        port: 80
        protocol: HTTP
route:
  main:
    hostnames:
      - ntfy.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }}
    parentRefs:
      - name: '{{ .Values.global.publicGateway }}'
        namespace: istio-system
        sectionName: https
persistence:
  data:
    accessMode: ReadWriteOnce
    size: 1Gi
    globalMounts:
      - path: /var/lib/ntfy
externalSecrets:
  auth:
    forceRename: ntfy-auth
    secretStoreRef:
      kind: SecretStore
      name: openbao
    target:
      template:
        engineVersion: v2
        data:
          NTFY_AUTH_USERS: '{{ `{{ htpasswd "alerts" .alerts_password "bcrypt" }}:user,{{ htpasswd "phone" .phone_password "bcrypt" }}:user` }}'
          NTFY_AUTH_TOKENS: '{{ `alerts:tk_{{ .alerts_token }},phone:tk_{{ .phone_token }}` }}'
    data:
      - secretKey: alerts_password
        remoteRef: {key: ntfy/generated/alerts-password, property: password}
      - secretKey: alerts_token
        remoteRef: {key: ntfy/generated/alerts-token, property: token}
      - secretKey: phone_password
        remoteRef: {key: ntfy/generated/phone-password, property: password}
      - secretKey: phone_token
        remoteRef: {key: ntfy/generated/phone-token, property: token}
rawResources:
  # Under the mesh-wide deny-all (system/istio-system): who may call into this namespace
  authorization-policy:
    forceRename: allow
    manifest:
      apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
      kind: AuthorizationPolicy
      spec:
        action: ALLOW
        rules:
          - from:
              - source:
                  namespaces: ['{{ .Release.Namespace }}']
          # the Gateway named by global.publicGateway (public in production, gateway in the sandbox)
          - from:
              - source:
                  principals: ['cluster.local/ns/istio-system/sa/{{ .Values.global.publicGateway }}-istio']
            to:
              - operation:
                  ports: ["80"]
          # Alertmanager (system/monitoring-system)
          - from:
              - source:
                  principals: ['cluster.local/ns/monitoring-system/sa/monitoring-system-kube-pro-alertmanager']
            to:
              - operation:
                  ports: ["80"]

Check htpasswd's output: ESO's v2 template htpasswd returns user:hash; ntfy wants user:hash:role, so the template appends :user. ntfy refuses bcrypt hashes below cost 10; ESO's htpasswd makes $2a$10$ hashes (checked on zot's Secret in the sandbox, 2026-10-17), exactly the minimum.

The excalidraw app file publishes only on global.publicGateway; ntfy follows it (one route: a LAN route on the same host would compete for the DNS record). Read how EXTRA entries are checked (target, principal, port, workload filter, reason) and match the tuple shape.

// An alert posted to Alertmanager reaches topic alerts through ntfy's alertmanager template
func TestNtfyAlertmanagerDelivers(t *testing.T) {
    secretsSandboxOnly(t)
    waitForNtfy(t)
    name := fmt.Sprint("NtfyTest", time.Now().UnixNano())
    alert := fmt.Sprintf(`[{"labels":{"alertname":%q,"namespace":"ntfy-test","severity":"warning"}}]`, name)
    k8s.RunKubectl(t, k8s.NewKubectlOptions("", "", "monitoring-system"), "exec", "alertmanager-monitoring-system-kube-pro-alertmanager-0",
        "-c", "alertmanager", "--", "wget", "-qO-", "--header=Content-Type: application/json",
        "--post-data="+alert, "http://localhost:9093/api/v2/alerts")
    phone := ntfyToken(t, "phone")
    assert.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        status, body := ntfyRequest(t, http.MethodGet, "/alerts/json?poll=1&since=10m", phone, "")
        return status == http.StatusOK && strings.Contains(body, name)
    }, 3*time.Minute, 10*time.Second, "the alert did not reach topic alerts")
}

// The Watchdog keeps a delayed message scheduled (sequence watchdog): it fires only if heartbeats stop
func TestNtfyWatchdogScheduled(t *testing.T) {
    secretsSandboxOnly(t)
    waitForNtfy(t)
    phone := ntfyToken(t, "phone")
    assert.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        status, body := ntfyRequest(t, http.MethodGet, "/alerts/json?poll=1&sched=1", phone, "")
        return status == http.StatusOK && strings.Contains(body, `"sequence_id":"watchdog"`)
    }, 10*time.Minute, 15*time.Second, "no scheduled watchdog message")
}

In system/monitoring-system/values.yaml, replace alertmanager.alertmanagerSpec (relay container, volumes) and alertmanager.config with (copied from upstream nixos, host and Secret renamed):

  alertmanager:
    alertmanagerSpec:
      # templates/ntfy-secret.yaml, mounted at /etc/alertmanager/secrets/ntfy/
      secrets: [ntfy]
    config:
      route:
        receiver: ntfy
        group_by:
          - namespace
        group_wait: 30s
        group_interval: 5m
        repeat_interval: 12h
        routes:
          # A heartbeat every minute (repeat_interval) that replaces one delayed message: if heartbeats stop, the
          # last one fires after 15 minutes
          - receiver: ntfy-watchdog
            matchers:
              - alertname = "Watchdog"
            group_wait: 0s
            group_interval: 1m
            repeat_interval: 1m
      receivers:
        - name: ntfy
          webhook_configs:
            - url: http://ntfy.ntfy/alerts?template=alertmanager
              send_resolved: true
              http_config:
                authorization:
                  credentials_file: /etc/alertmanager/secrets/ntfy/token
        - name: ntfy-watchdog
          webhook_configs:
            - url: http://ntfy.ntfy/
              send_resolved: false
              http_config:
                authorization:
                  credentials_file: /etc/alertmanager/secrets/ntfy/token
              # Alertmanager 0.28+ webhook payload override; check the chart's Alertmanager version supports
              # `payload` (upstream nixos uses it); otherwise post to /alerts/watchdog with headers through a
              # template and record a Ruling
              payload: '{"topic":"alerts","title":"Monitoring heartbeat missing","message":"Watchdog heartbeats stopped for {{ .Values.global.baseDomain }}","delay":"15m","sequence_id":"watchdog"}'

# Alerts

Alertmanager posts alerts to ntfy (`apps/ntfy.yaml`), topic `alerts`, published at `https://ntfy.<domain>` through the
Cloudflare Tunnel. Nothing is readable without a user: `phone` reads, `alerts` (Alertmanager) publishes.

## Subscribe on a phone

1. Install ntfy ([Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=io.heckel.ntfy) or
   [iOS](https://apps.apple.com/app/ntfy/id1625396347)).
2. Settings → Users → add server `https://ntfy.<domain>`, user `phone`, password:
   `kubectl -n global-secrets get secret ntfy.phone-password -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 -d`
3. Subscribe to topic `alerts` on that server.

iOS gets instant notifications through ntfy.sh, which only receives a poll request (a hash of the topic), never the
message.

## Heartbeat

The `Watchdog` alert fires all the time. Each heartbeat replaces a message scheduled 15 minutes ahead ("Monitoring
heartbeat missing"): if Prometheus or Alertmanager stop, it is delivered. If ntfy, the Tunnel or the whole cluster
stop, nothing is: an external dead man's switch is an idea in `CLAUDE.md`.

docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Pod logs and Kubernetes events land in Loki 3 (single binary) through a Grafana Alloy DaemonSet, kept 30 days, queryable in Grafana, in production and the sandbox; the roadmap gains step 9 and renumbers the rest.

Architecture: system/loki (namespace loki) wraps the loki chart (grafana-community) and the alloy chart (grafana). Alloy reads /var/log/pods on its node, keeps positions on the host, and gathers events with clustering (one instance). Grafana's existing Loki data source reaches loki.loki:3100.

Tech Stack: Helm wrapper charts, Loki 3.7.8 (chart 18.17.0), Alloy v1.20.1 (chart 1.13.1), Argo CD, Istio ambient, Go tests (terratest).

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A container with several ports makes Pod discovery emit one target per port: Alloy must not tail the same file twice (each line once) — TestLogsPodLines asserts exactly one entry for the marker.
  2. Alloy restarts (rollout, node reboot): it resumes from its host positions file, neither losing nor repeating lines — TestLogsResumeAfterRestart.
  3. Events must come from one Alloy instance only (clustering), or every event appears once per node — the sandbox has one node, so TestLogsEvents checks the event exists; the review checks clustering config.
  4. Loki's chart ships a rules sidecar that reads ConfigMaps and Secrets cluster-wide, and Alloy's default ClusterRole reads every Secret: both must be gone (render check in Tasks 1 and 2).
  5. Grafana must query Loki in the sandbox now (the data source was dropped there) — TestLogsGrafanaDataSource.

package test

import (
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
    "net/http"
    "net/url"

)

func logsSandboxOnly(t *testing.T) { secretsSandboxOnly(t) }

type lokiEntry struct {
    Labels map[string]string
    Line   string
}

// lokiQuery runs a LogQL range query over the last `since` through the API server's service proxy
func lokiQuery(t *testing.T, query string, since time.Duration) ([]lokiEntry, error) {
    options := k8s.NewKubectlOptions("", "", "loki")
    options.Logger = logger.Discard
    params := url.Values{}
    params.Set("query", query)
    params.Set("start", fmt.Sprint(time.Now().Add(-since).UnixNano()))
    params.Set("limit", "1000")
    out, err := k8s.RunKubectlAndGetOutputE(t, options, "get", "--raw",
        "/api/v1/namespaces/loki/services/loki:3100/proxy/loki/api/v1/query_range?"+params.Encode())
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    var res struct {
        Data struct {
            Result []struct {
                Stream map[string]string `json:"stream"`
                Values [][2]string       `json:"values"`
            } `json:"result"`
        } `json:"data"`
    }
    if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(out), &res); err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    var entries []lokiEntry
    for _, r := range res.Data.Result {
        for _, v := range r.Values {
            entries = append(entries, lokiEntry{Labels: r.Stream, Line: v[1]})
        }
    }
    return entries, nil
}

// Grafana queries Loki through its data source (uid loki), in the sandbox too
func TestLogsGrafanaDataSource(t *testing.T) {
    logsSandboxOnly(t)
    password := secretValue(t, "grafana", "grafana-admin", "admin-password")
    host := routeHost(t, "grafana", "grafana")
    require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        var health struct {
            Status string `json:"status"`
        }
        status, err := getJSONE(http.MethodGet, "https://"+host+"/api/datasources/uid/loki/health", nil, "admin", password, nil, &health)
        return err == nil && status == http.StatusOK && health.Status == "OK"
    }, 20*time.Minute, 15*time.Second, "Grafana's Loki data source is not healthy")
}

// Prometheus scrapes Loki and Alloy
func TestLogsTargetsUp(t *testing.T) {
    logsSandboxOnly(t)
    assert.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        metrics, err := prometheusQuery(t, `count by (job) (up{namespace="loki"} == 1)`)
        if err != nil {
            return false
        }
        jobs := []string{}
        for _, m := range metrics {
            jobs = append(jobs, m["job"])
        }
        joined := strings.Join(jobs, ",")
        return strings.Contains(joined, "loki") && strings.Contains(joined, "alloy")
    }, 20*time.Minute, 30*time.Second, "Loki's and Alloy's targets are not up")
}

Append to test/logs_test.go:

const logsNamespace = "logs-test"

// logPod starts a pod that sleeps; the test makes it print with printTo
func logPod(t *testing.T, name string) *k8s.KubectlOptions {
    options := k8s.NewKubectlOptions("", "", logsNamespace)
    _ = k8s.RunKubectlE(t, k8s.NewKubectlOptions("", "", ""), "create", "namespace", logsNamespace)
    _ = k8s.RunKubectlE(t, options, "delete", "pod", name, "--ignore-not-found", "--wait=true")
    k8s.RunKubectl(t, options, "run", name, "--image=curlimages/curl:8.23.0", "--restart=Never",
        "--labels=app.kubernetes.io/name=logs-test", "--command", "--", "sleep", "3600")
    k8s.RunKubectl(t, options, "wait", "--for=condition=Ready", "pod/"+name, "--timeout=5m")
    t.Cleanup(func() { _ = k8s.RunKubectlE(t, options, "delete", "pod", name, "--wait=false") })
    return options
}

// printTo writes a line to the pod's stdout (its container log)
func printTo(t *testing.T, options *k8s.KubectlOptions, pod, line string) {
    k8s.RunKubectl(t, options, "exec", pod, "--", "sh", "-c", "echo "+line+" > /proc/1/fd/1")
}

func markerEntries(t *testing.T, pod, marker string) []lokiEntry {
    entries, err := lokiQuery(t, fmt.Sprintf(`{namespace=%q, pod=%q} |= %q`, logsNamespace, pod, marker), time.Hour)
    if err != nil {
        return nil
    }
    return entries
}

// A pod's line reaches Loki once, with its labels
func TestLogsPodLines(t *testing.T) {
    logsSandboxOnly(t)
    options := logPod(t, "lines")
    marker := fmt.Sprint("logs-marker-", time.Now().UnixNano())
    printTo(t, options, "lines", marker)
    var entries []lokiEntry
    require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        entries = markerEntries(t, "lines", marker)
        return len(entries) > 0
    }, 10*time.Minute, 10*time.Second, "the marker did not reach Loki")
    time.Sleep(30 * time.Second) // a second tail of the same file would deliver it again by now
    entries = markerEntries(t, "lines", marker)
    require.Len(t, entries, 1, "the marker arrived more than once")
    labels := entries[0].Labels
    assert.Equal(t, logsNamespace, labels["namespace"])
    assert.Equal(t, "lines", labels["pod"])
    assert.Equal(t, "lines", labels["container"])
    assert.Equal(t, "logs-test", labels["app"])
    assert.NotEmpty(t, labels["node"])
}

// A restarted Alloy resumes from its positions: no line lost, none repeated
func TestLogsResumeAfterRestart(t *testing.T) {
    logsSandboxOnly(t)
    options := logPod(t, "resume")
    first := fmt.Sprint("logs-first-", time.Now().UnixNano())
    printTo(t, options, "resume", first)
    require.Eventually(t, func() bool { return len(markerEntries(t, "resume", first)) > 0 },
        10*time.Minute, 10*time.Second, "the first marker did not reach Loki")

    loki := k8s.NewKubectlOptions("", "", "loki")
    k8s.RunKubectl(t, loki, "delete", "pod", "-l", "app.kubernetes.io/name=alloy", "--wait=true")
    second := fmt.Sprint("logs-second-", time.Now().UnixNano())
    printTo(t, options, "resume", second) // written while Alloy restarts
    k8s.RunKubectl(t, loki, "rollout", "status", "daemonset/loki-alloy", "--timeout=5m")
    require.Eventually(t, func() bool { return len(markerEntries(t, "resume", second)) > 0 },
        10*time.Minute, 10*time.Second, "the line written during the restart was lost")
    assert.Len(t, markerEntries(t, "resume", first), 1, "the restarted Alloy sent the first marker again")
}

Append to system/loki/values.yaml:

alloy:
  controller:
    type: daemonset
    volumes:
      extra:
        # Every container's log on this node (containerd; /var/log/containers only links here)
        - name: pod-logs
          hostPath:
            path: /var/log/pods
        # Positions and the write-ahead log survive a restart of the pod
        - name: storage
          hostPath:
            path: /var/lib/alloy
            type: DirectoryOrCreate
  alloy:
    enableReporting: false
    storagePath: /var/lib/alloy
    clustering:
      enabled: true
    # The log files belong to root; the mount is read-only
    securityContext:
      runAsUser: 0
      runAsNonRoot: false
    extraEnv:
      - name: NODE_NAME
        valueFrom:
          fieldRef:
            fieldPath: spec.nodeName
    mounts:
      extra:
        - name: pod-logs
          mountPath: /var/log/pods
          readOnly: true
        - name: storage
          mountPath: /var/lib/alloy
    configMap:
      content: |
        // This node's pods (spec.nodeName), one target per container
        discovery.kubernetes "pods" {
          role = "pod"
          selectors {
            role  = "pod"
            field = "spec.nodeName=" + sys.env("NODE_NAME")
          }
        }

        discovery.relabel "pods" {
          targets = discovery.kubernetes.pods.targets
          rule {
            source_labels = ["__meta_kubernetes_namespace"]
            target_label  = "namespace"
          }
          rule {
            source_labels = ["__meta_kubernetes_pod_name"]
            target_label  = "pod"
          }
          rule {
            source_labels = ["__meta_kubernetes_pod_container_name"]
            target_label  = "container"
          }
          // app.kubernetes.io/name, else app
          rule {
            source_labels = ["__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_app_kubernetes_io_name", "__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_app"]
            separator     = ";"
            regex         = "^;*([^;]+).*$"
            target_label  = "app"
          }
          rule {
            source_labels = ["__meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name"]
            target_label  = "node"
          }
          rule {
            replacement  = "pods"
            target_label = "job"
          }
          // /var/log/pods/<namespace>_<pod>_<uid>/<container>/<n>.log
          rule {
            source_labels = ["__meta_kubernetes_pod_uid", "__meta_kubernetes_pod_container_name"]
            separator     = "/"
            replacement   = "/var/log/pods/*$1/*.log"
            target_label  = "__path__"
          }
        }

        local.file_match "pods" {
          path_targets = discovery.relabel.pods.output
        }

        loki.source.file "pods" {
          targets    = local.file_match.pods.targets
          forward_to = [loki.process.pods.receiver]
        }

        // containerd's CRI format: time, stream, flags, line
        loki.process "pods" {
          stage.cri {}
          forward_to = [loki.write.loki.receiver]
        }

        loki.write "loki" {
          endpoint {
            url = "http://loki:3100/loki/api/v1/push"
          }
        }
  # Read only what the config uses (the chart's default also reads every Secret)
  rbac:
    rules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        resources: ["pods", "namespaces"]
        verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
    clusterRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        resources: ["nodes"]
        verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
  serviceMonitor:
    enabled: true

docs.title: Step 8a: OpenBao behind External Secrets Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: OpenBao in the cluster holds the homelab's secrets. Each namespace reads only secret/<namespace>/* through its own SecretStore openbao. Generated secrets are pushed into OpenBao once. OpenBao unseals itself with a key OpenTofu keeps, and configures itself from git.

Architecture: - OpenTofu unit infra/<env>/openbao creates the unseal key and the Secret openbao/openbao-unseal. - platform/openbao wraps the official chart. It runs a static seal, raft storage and self-initialisation (KV v2, Kubernetes auth, policies apps/writer/admin and their roles). - system/secret-store is an extra source on every Application, like system/egress. It renders the namespace's SecretStore. - platform/global-secrets pushes each generated value to its readers' branches. The ClusterSecretStore is removed and every consumer moves to the new store.

Tech Stack: OpenBao 2.7.1 (chart openbao 0.30.4), External Secrets 2.12.0 (ExternalSecret v1, PushSecret v1alpha1), OpenTofu + Terragrunt (hashicorp/random 3.9.1), Helm, Go terratest, Python checks.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-openbao-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Versions are pinned exactly: OpenBao image quay.io/openbao/openbao:2.7.1, chart openbao 0.30.4 from https://openbao.github.io/openbao-helm, hashicorp/random 3.9.1.
  • Seal: seal "static", key id homelab-1, key file /openbao/unseal/key from Secret openbao/openbao-unseal, key key, 32 raw bytes.
  • KV v2 at secret/. Key layout is secret/<namespace>/<name>. Properties are unchanged (password, secret, PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD, …).
  • Roles:
  • apps: service account default in any namespace, policy apps (read secret/data/<own namespace>/*).
  • writer: default in global-secrets. Policy writer grants create, read and update on secret/data/* and secret/metadata/*.
  • admin: openbao-admin in openbao, policy admin (everything).
  • The store every namespace reads is SecretStore openbao (role apps, SA default, server http://openbao.openbao.svc.cluster.local:8200). The writer's store is SecretStore openbao-writer in global-secrets.
  • Destinations:
  • forgejo.admin → forgejo/admin, argocd/forgejo-admin
  • grafana.admin → grafana/admin
  • paperless.admin → paperless/admin
  • paperless.secret-key → paperless/secret-key
  • registry.ci → zot/ci
  • woodpecker.agent → woodpecker/agent
  • Paths nobody creates yet: woodpecker/forgejo, renovate/forgejo, wireguard/private-key, tailscale/auth-key.
  • Rules from CLAUDE.md:
  • No IP address in charts.
  • Write hosts as <host>.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }}.
  • Every meshed namespace has an allow AuthorizationPolicy.
  • Helm replaces lists, so the prod, dev and seed ApplicationSets each restate sources.
  • Never put personal data or secret values in the repo or in logs.
  • Basic checks:
  • scripts/render-chart <dir> and scripts/render-chart <dir> dev for every changed chart or app file
  • cd test && go vet ./... && go test -run 'TestSmokeAppsForEnv|TestIdentity(HasGroup|TOTPWaitsForNextStep|PKCE)|TestGatewayRouteReady|TestGatewayNodeAddressFromInspect' ./...
  • mkdocs build --strict
  • scripts/check-mesh-policies
  • scripts/check-env-config
  • make -C infra check
  • from Task 4: scripts/check-secret-stores

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. Self-init request failing on a fresh cluster. A typo in the HCL, or Helm's tpl eating the OpenBao template braces, leaves OpenBao unsealed but empty. Expect the sandbox tests to fail on it at once, never a silent half-configured store. Task 2 pins the rendered template line. Task 5's tests read through every role.
  2. First sync ordering. ESO's CRDs, OpenBao and the unseal Secret appear in any order. Expect every SecretStore, PushSecret and ExternalSecret to become ready without manual help: ESO retries on errors, Argo CD re-renders when the capability appears, and the pod waits for the Secret. Task 7's fresh make dev is the proof. Watch zot, whose StatefulSet waits for its Secret.
  3. OpenBao restarting or losing its pod. Expect it to come back unsealed with its data, and self-init not to run twice. Task 5 covers this with TestSecretsSurviveRestart.
  4. A namespace naming another's key. Expect ESO to refuse the read, and scripts/check-secret-stores to refuse the render before merge. Task 4 covers the check. Task 5 covers the refusal with TestSecretsNamespaceBranches.
  5. Re-running make dev on an existing sandbox. Expect the unit not to replace the key (OpenBao would stay sealed with the old data). Task 1 covers this: the key's resource has no trigger, and a second plan shows no changes.
