infra/_modules/openbao/main.tf:

# OpenBao's unseal key (platform/openbao reads it from Secret openbao/openbao-unseal; seal "static"). The key lives in
# this unit's state, outside the cluster: losing it loses everything OpenBao holds
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.13"
  required_providers {
    random = {
      source  = "hashicorp/random"
      version = "3.9.1"
    }
  }
}

variable "kubeconfig" {
  type = string
}

variable "namespace" {
  type        = string
  default     = "openbao"
  description = "Namespace of platform/openbao, created by Argo CD"
}

variable "cluster_id" {
  type        = string
  default     = ""
  description = "Identity of the cluster: a new cluster gets the Secret again (same key)"
}

variable "protect" {
  type        = bool
  default     = false
  description = "Refuse to destroy the key (production)"
}

# prevent_destroy cannot take a variable: one resource per setting, only one of them exists
resource "random_bytes" "key" {
  count  = var.protect ? 0 : 1
  length = 32
}

resource "random_bytes" "protected" {
  count  = var.protect ? 1 : 0
  length = 32

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}

locals {
  key = one(concat(random_bytes.key[*].base64, random_bytes.protected[*].base64))
}

resource "terraform_data" "secret" {
  triggers_replace = [var.cluster_id, var.namespace, sha256(local.key)]

  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command = "sh ${abspath("${path.module}/apply-secret.sh")}"
    environment = {
      KUBECONFIG = var.kubeconfig
      NAMESPACE  = var.namespace
      KEY        = local.key
    }
  }
}

infra/_modules/openbao/apply-secret.sh:

#!/bin/sh
# Writes OpenBao's unseal key into its namespace once Argo CD has created it. The key comes in base64 through the
# environment and reaches kubectl on stdin: never in an argument or a file
set -eu
: "${KUBECONFIG:?}" "${NAMESPACE:?}" "${KEY:?}"
if ! kubectl wait --for=create "namespace/$NAMESPACE" --timeout=30m >/dev/null; then
  echo "namespace $NAMESPACE did not appear in 30 minutes: is Argo CD syncing platform/openbao?" >&2
  exit 1
fi
printf '%s' "$KEY" | base64 -d |
  kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" create secret generic openbao-unseal --from-file=key=/dev/stdin --dry-run=client -o yaml |
  kubectl apply --server-side --field-manager=infra-openbao -f - >/dev/null
echo "Secret $NAMESPACE/openbao-unseal applied"

  • Step 3: Run the offline checks and the plans

  • Step 2: Write the chart

platform/openbao/Chart.yaml:

apiVersion: v2
name: openbao
version: 0.0.0
dependencies:
  - name: openbao
    version: 0.30.4
    repository: https://openbao.github.io/openbao-helm

platform/openbao/values.yaml:

openbao:
  injector:
    enabled: false
  ui:
    enabled: false
  server:
    image:
      tag: 2.7.1
    dataStorage:
      size: 1Gi
    # OpenTofu's unit infra/<env>/openbao writes this Secret; the pod waits for it
    volumes:
      - name: unseal
        secret:
          secretName: openbao-unseal
    volumeMounts:
      - name: unseal
        mountPath: /openbao/unseal
        readOnly: true
    standalone:
      enabled: true
      # The chart passes this through Helm's tpl: OpenBao's own template (policy apps) is wrapped in {{` `}}.
      # Self-initialisation runs once, on an empty storage; changing it later needs the admin role
      # (docs/concepts/secrets-management.md). HOSTNAME is replaced by the pod name at start.
      config: |
        ui = false
        disable_mlock = true

        # Plain HTTP: ztunnel's mTLS carries every connection inside the mesh
        listener "tcp" {
          address         = "[::]:8200"
          cluster_address = "[::]:8201"
          tls_disable     = true
        }

        storage "raft" {
          path    = "/openbao/data"
          node_id = "HOSTNAME"
        }

        seal "static" {
          current_key_id = "homelab-1"
          current_key    = "file:///openbao/unseal/key"
        }

        initialize "mounts" {
          request "kv" {
            operation = "update"
            path      = "sys/mounts/secret"
            data = {
              type    = "kv"
              options = { version = "2" }
            }
          }
          request "kubernetes" {
            operation = "update"
            path      = "sys/auth/kubernetes"
            data      = { type = "kubernetes" }
          }
          request "kubernetes-config" {
            operation = "update"
            path      = "auth/kubernetes/config"
            data      = { kubernetes_host = "https://kubernetes.default.svc" }
          }
          # Its accessor names the namespace in policy apps
          request "kubernetes-read" {
            operation = "read"
            path      = "sys/auth/kubernetes"
          }
        }

        initialize "policies" {
          # A namespace's default service account reads its own branch, secret/<namespace>/
          request "apps" {
            operation = "update"
            path      = "sys/policies/acl/apps"
            data = {
              policy = {
                eval_type   = "string"
                eval_source = "template"
                template    = "{{`path \"secret/data/{{ \"{{\" }}identity.entity.aliases.{{ (index .responses.mounts \"kubernetes-read\").data.accessor }}.metadata.service_account_namespace{{ \"}}\" }}/*\" { capabilities = [\"read\"] }`}}"
              }
            }
          }
          # platform/global-secrets pushes generated secrets; External Secrets reads a path and its metadata before
          # it writes them, so the writer reads too. IfNotExists keeps existing values
          request "writer" {
            operation = "update"
            path      = "sys/policies/acl/writer"
            data = {
              policy = "path \"secret/data/*\" { capabilities = [\"create\", \"read\", \"update\"] }\npath \"secret/metadata/*\" { capabilities = [\"create\", \"read\", \"update\"] }"
            }
          }
          # Emergency access: no root token exists
          request "admin" {
            operation = "update"
            path      = "sys/policies/acl/admin"
            data = {
              policy = "path \"*\" { capabilities = [\"create\", \"read\", \"update\", \"patch\", \"delete\", \"list\", \"sudo\"] }"
            }
          }
        }

        initialize "roles" {
          request "apps" {
            operation = "update"
            path      = "auth/kubernetes/role/apps"
            data = {
              bound_service_account_names      = ["default"]
              bound_service_account_namespaces = ["*"]
              token_policies                   = ["apps"]
              token_ttl                        = "10m"
            }
          }
          request "writer" {
            operation = "update"
            path      = "auth/kubernetes/role/writer"
            data = {
              bound_service_account_names      = ["default"]
              bound_service_account_namespaces = ["global-secrets"]
              token_policies                   = ["writer"]
              token_ttl                        = "10m"
            }
          }
          request "admin" {
            operation = "update"
            path      = "auth/kubernetes/role/admin"
            data = {
              bound_service_account_names      = ["openbao-admin"]
              bound_service_account_namespaces = ["openbao"]
              token_policies                   = ["admin"]
              token_ttl                        = "1h"
            }
          }
        }

docs.text:

Interfaces: - Consumes: SecretStore openbao (Task 3), role writer (Task 2). - Produces: values at the destinations listed in Global Constraints. The generated Kubernetes Secrets in global-secrets stay, and test/ reads them.

  • Step 1: Write the failing check

scripts/check-secret-stores:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Every ExternalSecret reads OpenBao through its namespace's SecretStore, inside its namespace's branch.

Renders every component and app file in production and the sandbox (scripts/render-chart) and fails on:
- an ExternalSecret that reads anything but SecretStore openbao (system/secret-store);
- a key outside secret/<namespace>/, where the namespace is the component's (Argo CD's destination);
- a PushSecret outside platform/global-secrets, or through any store but its openbao-writer;
- any ClusterSecretStore.
ExternalSecrets that only run generators (platform/global-secrets) read no store.
"""

import glob
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import yaml


class Loader(yaml.SafeLoader):
    """SafeLoader that reads a bare `=` (YAML 1.1's value tag, used by some charts) as a string."""


Loader.add_constructor("tag:yaml.org,2002:value", lambda loader, node: loader.construct_scalar(node))

WRITER = ("platform/global-secrets", "openbao-writer")


def render(target, env):
    # Chart downloads sometimes reset the connection: try three times
    for attempt in range(3):
        out = subprocess.run(["scripts/render-chart", target, env], capture_output=True, text=True)
        if out.returncode == 0:
            return [d for d in yaml.load_all(out.stdout, Loader=Loader) if d]
        time.sleep(5)
    sys.exit(f"render failed: {target} {env}\n{out.stderr}")


def targets():
    dirs = sorted(glob.glob("system/*/") + glob.glob("platform/*/") + glob.glob("apps/*/"))
    return [d.rstrip("/") for d in dirs if glob.glob(d + "Chart.yaml")] + sorted(glob.glob("apps/*.yaml"))


def keys(spec):
    for item in spec.get("data") or []:
        yield item["remoteRef"]["key"]
    for item in spec.get("dataFrom") or []:
        if "extract" in item:
            yield item["extract"]["key"]
        elif "find" in item:
            yield None  # find searches the whole store: never allowed


def generators_only(spec):
    sources = spec.get("dataFrom") or []
    return not spec.get("data") and sources and all("generatorRef" in (s.get("sourceRef") or {}) for s in sources)


def main():
    failures = []
    for env in ("prod", "dev"):
        for target in targets():
            namespace = os.path.basename(target).removesuffix(".yaml")
            for doc in render(target, env):
                kind, name = doc.get("kind"), (doc.get("metadata") or {}).get("name")
                spec = doc.get("spec") or {}
                where = f"{target} ({env}): {kind}/{name}"
                if kind == "ClusterSecretStore":
                    failures.append(f"{where}: use the namespace's SecretStore openbao (system/secret-store)")
                elif kind == "ExternalSecret":
                    if generators_only(spec):
                        continue
                    ref = spec.get("secretStoreRef") or {}
                    if (ref.get("kind", "SecretStore"), ref.get("name")) != ("SecretStore", "openbao"):
                        failures.append(f"{where}: reads {ref.get('kind', 'SecretStore')}/{ref.get('name')}, not SecretStore/openbao")
                    for key in keys(spec):
                        if key is None or not key.startswith(namespace + "/"):
                            failures.append(f"{where}: key {key} is outside its branch {namespace}/")
                elif kind == "PushSecret":
                    stores = [(r.get("kind", "SecretStore"), r.get("name")) for r in spec.get("secretStoreRefs") or []]
                    if (target, stores) != (WRITER[0], [("SecretStore", WRITER[1])]):
                        failures.append(f"{where}: only {WRITER[0]} pushes, through SecretStore {WRITER[1]}")
    for f in failures:
        print(f, file=sys.stderr)
    print(f"check-secret-stores: {len(failures)} failures")
    sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Run: chmod +x scripts/check-secret-stores && scripts/check-secret-stores 2>&1 | tail -15 Expected: FAIL. It reports reads ClusterSecretStore/global-secrets for each of the 9 consumers in both environments, and use the namespace's SecretStore openbao for global-secrets' store.

# reader's branch of OpenBao, secret/<namespace>/<name> (templates/push-secrets.yaml); readers use their namespace's
# SecretStore openbao. Never rotated automatically; see docs/concepts/secrets-management.md.
secrets:

    key: password
    special: true
    # Argo CD reads the GitOps repository with it
    destinations: [forgejo/admin, argocd/forgejo-admin]
  - name: woodpecker.agent
    key: secret
    destinations: [woodpecker/agent]
  - name: paperless.admin

    special: true
    destinations: [paperless/admin]

    key: PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY
    length: 64
    destinations: [paperless/secret-key]
  - name: grafana.admin
    key: password
    special: true
    destinations: [grafana/admin]

# Environment-specific additions, so the list above does not have to be restated

kind: PushSecret
metadata:

  namespace: {{ $.Release.Namespace }}
spec:
  # An existing value is never replaced; the hourly check pushes a missing one again (an OpenBao that lost its data)

    {{- end }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}

docs.text:
Files: - Create: test/secrets_test.go - Modify: Makefile (smoke_filter adds Secrets)

Interfaces: - Consumes: pod openbao/openbao-0 (container openbao, bao CLI, BAO_ADDR set by the chart), roles apps/writer/admin, ServiceAccount openbao-admin, secretValue (test/sso_test.go). - Produces: TestSecrets*, run by make dev.

  • Step 1: Write the tests

test/secrets_test.go:

package test

import (
    "encoding/json"
    "os"
    "os/exec"
    "strings"
    "testing"
    "time"

    "github.com/gruntwork-io/terratest/modules/k8s"
    "github.com/gruntwork-io/terratest/modules/logger"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func secretsSandboxOnly(t *testing.T) {
    if os.Getenv("ENV") != "dev" {
        t.Skip("OpenBao tests run against the sandbox only")
    }
}

// bao runs the OpenBao CLI in OpenBao's pod, logged in with a token of service account namespace/account and the
// given role. The token reaches the pod on stdin and is never logged
func bao(t *testing.T, role, namespace, account string, args ...string) (string, error) {
    options := k8s.NewKubectlOptions("", "", namespace)
    options.Logger = logger.Discard
    token, err := k8s.RunKubectlAndGetOutputE(t, options, "create", "token", account, "--duration=10m")
    require.NoError(t, err)
    script := `BAO_TOKEN="$(bao write -field=token auth/kubernetes/login role="$0" jwt=-)" && export BAO_TOKEN && exec bao "$@"`
    cmd := exec.Command("kubectl", append([]string{"-n", "openbao", "exec", "-i", "openbao-0", "-c", "openbao", "--",
        "sh", "-c", script, role}, args...)...)
    cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(token)
    out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    return strings.TrimSpace(string(out)), err
}

// waitForUnsealed waits until OpenBao's pod answers, initialised and unsealed
func waitForUnsealed(t *testing.T) {
    require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        out, err := exec.Command("kubectl", "-n", "openbao", "exec", "openbao-0", "-c", "openbao", "--",
            "bao", "status", "-format=json").Output()
        if err != nil {
            return false
        }
        var status struct {
            Initialized bool `json:"initialized"`
            Sealed      bool `json:"sealed"`
        }
        return json.Unmarshal(out, &status) == nil && status.Initialized && !status.Sealed
    }, 30*time.Minute, 10*time.Second, "OpenBao is not initialised and unsealed")
}

// grafanaAdmin reads Grafana's admin password from its branch, as Grafana's namespace, once global-secrets has
// pushed it
func grafanaAdmin(t *testing.T) string {
    var password string
    require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        out, err := bao(t, "apps", "grafana", "default", "kv", "get", "-field=password", "secret/grafana/admin")
        password = out
        return err == nil && out != ""
    }, 20*time.Minute, 15*time.Second, "secret/grafana/admin is not readable")
    return password
}

func TestSecretsUnsealed(t *testing.T) {
    secretsSandboxOnly(t)
    waitForUnsealed(t)
}

// A namespace reads its own branch, not another's, and writes nowhere
func TestSecretsNamespaceBranches(t *testing.T) {
    secretsSandboxOnly(t)
    waitForUnsealed(t)
    assert.NotEmpty(t, grafanaAdmin(t))

    out, err := bao(t, "apps", "grafana", "default", "kv", "get", "-field=password", "secret/zot/ci")
    assert.Error(t, err, "grafana read zot's branch")
    assert.Contains(t, out, "permission denied")

    out, err = bao(t, "apps", "grafana", "default", "kv", "put", "secret/grafana/probe", "value=x")
    assert.Error(t, err, "grafana wrote to OpenBao")
    assert.Contains(t, out, "permission denied")
}

// The writer is global-secrets' default service account only
func TestSecretsWriterRole(t *testing.T) {
    secretsSandboxOnly(t)
    waitForUnsealed(t)
    out, err := bao(t, "writer", "grafana", "default", "kv", "get", "secret/grafana/admin")
    assert.Error(t, err, "grafana logged in as writer")
    assert.Contains(t, out, "not authorized")
}

// Emergency access: the admin role, for service account openbao-admin
func TestSecretsAdmin(t *testing.T) {
    secretsSandboxOnly(t)
    waitForUnsealed(t)
    out, err := bao(t, "admin", "openbao", "openbao-admin", "policy", "list")
    require.NoError(t, err, out)
    for _, policy := range []string{"apps", "writer", "admin"} {
        assert.Contains(t, strings.Fields(out), policy)
    }
}

// Grafana's admin Secret comes from OpenBao and equals the generated value
func TestSecretsReachConsumers(t *testing.T) {
    secretsSandboxOnly(t)
    waitForUnsealed(t)
    generated := secretValue(t, "global-secrets", "grafana.admin", "password")
    assert.Equal(t, generated, grafanaAdmin(t), "OpenBao's value differs from the generated one")
    require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        return secretValue(t, "grafana", "grafana-admin", "admin-password") == generated
    }, 20*time.Minute, 15*time.Second, "grafana-admin does not hold the generated password")
}

// After its pod is replaced OpenBao unseals itself and keeps its data. Consumers keep their Secrets meanwhile; External
// Secrets retries the reads that fail while the pod restarts
func TestSecretsSurviveRestart(t *testing.T) {
    secretsSandboxOnly(t)
    waitForUnsealed(t)
    before := grafanaAdmin(t)
    k8s.RunKubectl(t, k8s.NewKubectlOptions("", "", "openbao"), "delete", "pod", "openbao-0", "--wait=true")
    waitForUnsealed(t)
    assert.Equal(t, before, grafanaAdmin(t))
}

secretValue in test/sso_test.go uses k8s.GetSecret, which fails the test while the Secret is missing. TestSecretsReachConsumers calls it inside Eventually only for grafana-admin, which Grafana's sync creates long before these tests run. If it flakes, ledger a ruling and switch to k8s.GetSecretE.

In Makefile, smoke_filter becomes 'Smoke|Identity|SSO|Gateway|Forgejo|Mesh|Monitoring|Egress|Secrets'.

Run: cd test && go vet ./... && go test -run 'TestSmokeAppsForEnv|TestIdentity(HasGroup|TOTPWaitsForNextStep|PKCE)|TestGatewayRouteReady|TestGatewayNodeAddressFromInspect|TestSecrets' ./... Expected: ok. The TestSecrets* tests skip without ENV=dev.

Run: cd test && ENV=dev KUBECONFIG=$PWD/../infra/sandbox/kubeconfig.yaml timeout 90 go test -run TestSecretsAdmin -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -5 Expected: FAIL. waitForUnsealed keeps failing: no pod openbao-0 in the sandbox. timeout stops it. Task 7 turns it green.

git commit -m "test(secrets): OpenBao unseals, keeps data, scopes reads per namespace, feeds consumers"

Keep the sections "Generated secrets" (with the values snippet) and "Extra third-party secrets" (it still names external/; mark it "until step 8b"). Replace the Overview, the info box, the diagram and "How secrets are pulled" with:

# Secrets management

## Overview

- [OpenBao](https://openbao.org) (`platform/openbao`) holds the cluster's secrets in its KV store `secret/`.
- Every namespace reads its own branch, `secret/<namespace>/<name>`, through its `SecretStore` `openbao`
  (`system/secret-store`, rendered by every Application) and [External Secrets](https://external-secrets.io)
  `ExternalSecret`s. OpenBao refuses a read of another namespace's branch.
- Generated secrets come from `platform/global-secrets`, which pushes each one to its readers' branches.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph global-secrets[global-secrets namespace]
    generators[Password generators] -- generate once --> source[Secrets]
    source -- PushSecret, IfNotExists --> writer[SecretStore openbao-writer]
  end
  writer -- role writer --> openbao[(OpenBao secret/)]
  subgraph app[application namespace]
    store[SecretStore openbao] -- role apps: secret/<namespace>/ --> openbao
    ExternalSecret --- store
    ExternalSecret -- create --> Secret
    App -- read --> Secret
  end
```

## Reading a secret

```yaml
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: grafana-admin
spec:
  secretStoreRef:
    kind: SecretStore
    name: openbao
  data:
    - secretKey: password
      remoteRef:
        key: grafana/admin  # secret/grafana/admin: the namespace's own branch
        property: password
```

`scripts/check-secret-stores` refuses, before merge, an `ExternalSecret` that reads another store or another
namespace's branch. A secret two namespaces need is pushed to both branches (`destinations` in
`platform/global-secrets/values.yaml`).

## Unsealing and configuration

- OpenBao unseals itself (`seal "static"`) with a 32-byte key that the OpenTofu unit `infra/<env>/openbao` creates,
  keeps in its state (`.state/`, readable only by you; Cloudflare R2 with state encryption from step 8c) and writes into
  Secret `openbao/openbao-unseal`. Losing the key loses everything OpenBao holds.
- On first start OpenBao configures itself from `platform/openbao/values.yaml` (`initialize` stanzas):
  - the KV v2 store `secret/` and Kubernetes auth;
  - the policies `apps` (read `secret/<namespace>/`), `writer` (push: `create`, `read`, `update` on everything,
    because External Secrets reads before it writes) and `admin`;
  - their roles: `apps` for every namespace's `default` service account, `writer` for `global-secrets`' and `admin`
    for `openbao/openbao-admin`.
- These stanzas run only on an empty storage: editing them later changes nothing on a running OpenBao. Apply the
  change by hand with the admin role (below), or, in the sandbox, `make dev-clean`.
- No root token and no recovery keys exist.
- OpenBao's data has no backup until step 10.

## Emergency access

```sh
token=$(kubectl -n openbao create token openbao-admin --duration=1h)
kubectl -n openbao exec -it openbao-0 -c openbao -- sh -c 'bao login -method=kubernetes role=admin jwt=-' <<<"$token"
kubectl -n openbao exec -it openbao-0 -c openbao -- sh
```

Anyone who can create tokens for `openbao-admin` (cluster admins) holds every secret.

Change the rotation steps under "Generated secrets" to:

1. With the admin role: `bao kv metadata delete secret/<namespace>/<name>` for each destination of the entry.
2. `kubectl -n global-secrets delete secret <name>`. External Secrets generates a new value; its PushSecret writes it
   to the empty destinations within an hour (`kubectl -n global-secrets annotate pushsecret <name>
   force-sync=$(date +%s) --overwrite` pushes it at once).
3. Restart every app that uses it (for example `kubectl -n forgejo rollout restart deploy/forgejo`).
4. For an admin password, also change it inside the app to the new value.

docs.title: Mesh Recovery After a Node Restart Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: After a node restarts, its pods rejoin the ambient mesh without anyone stepping in, and a sandbox test proves it on every make dev.

Architecture: - system/istio-system keeps istioOwnedCNIConfig and drops ambient.ipv6: false. - It gains a CronJob watchdog. When a node's ztunnel has been running but not Ready for more than 180s, the watchdog deletes that node's istio-cni pod, whose agent then rebuilds its snapshot without the dead netns. - istiod runs 2 spread replicas in production. - A Go test restarts the k3d node and waits for full recovery. It runs alone at the end of make dev.

Tech Stack: Istio 1.31.2 Helm charts (base, istiod, cni, ztunnel); a Kubernetes CronJob running a POSIX sh script on alpine/kubectl:1.37.1; Go tests (terratest helpers, kubectl, docker).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-mesh-node-restart-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Use the latest stable release of every chart and image, pinned exactly: Istio charts 1.31.2; watchdog image alpine/kubectl:1.37.1@sha256:8c72f6f732ce7ef11cdb1bea25faa4f4a521872a12c89e3f40ba9edb52a4d4f2.
  • Watchdog rule: for each node, if the ztunnel container has been running for more than 180s and is not Ready, and that node's istio-cni container has been running for more than 180s, delete that node's istio-cni pod.
  • Watchdog schedule: every minute; concurrencyPolicy: Forbid; startingDeadlineSeconds: 50; Job activeDeadlineSeconds: 50; ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 300; history limits 1.
  • Watchdog pod: UID 65534, runAsNonRoot, read-only root filesystem, every capability dropped, small requests. RBAC is a Role in istio-system only: pods get, list, delete.
  • istiod in production: pilot.autoscaleMin: 2 and topology spread on kubernetes.io/hostname (maxSkew: 1, ScheduleAnyway). Sandbox: autoscaleMin: 1.
  • The test is named TestNodeRestart. No test name may contain a word of make dev's main filter (Smoke|Identity|SSO|Gateway|Forgejo|Mesh|Monitoring|Egress|Secrets|Ntfy|Logs), because go test -run is not anchored.
  • The node-restart test waits at most 12 minutes, and make dev runs it alone, after the main run.
  • Charts and app files hold no IP address or domain. Comments say why, not what; match the surrounding comment style.
  • Commits end with the session's attribution lines. Never commit to dev or master.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. ztunnel crash-looping or waiting (no state.running.startedAt): the watchdog must not act, because it cannot tell how long ztunnel has been up. Pinned by TestIstioCNIWatchdog/ztunnel_not_running.
  2. A node without an istio-cni pod (deleted, or not yet recreated): the watchdog must skip that node and must not fail the run for the other nodes. Pinned by TestIstioCNIWatchdog/no_istio-cni_pod.
  3. BusyBox date in the image cannot parse 2026-10-18T03:25:27Z with -d alone. The script must work in the real image, not only with GNU date on the workstation. Pinned by Task 3, Step 6, which runs the script's date helper inside alpine/kubectl:1.37.1.
  4. A recovered node with an app still answering 503 while its pod warms up (Grafana took 45s): the test must keep polling until every app returns its recorded code, not fail on the first 503. Pinned by TestNodeRestartBlockers/app_code_differs, which reports it as a blocker so the loop retries.
  5. Completed Job pods (Succeeded/Failed, such as the watchdog's own Jobs or seed Jobs) must not count as stuck. Pinned by TestNodeRestartBlockers/finished_job_ignored.

  • Step 1: Write the pure function's unit test first

Create test/node_restart_test.go:

package test

import (
    "fmt"
    "os/exec"
    "strings"
    "testing"
    "time"

    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestNodeRestartBlockers(t *testing.T) {
    ok := map[string]int{"excalidraw": 200}
    running := restartPod{Namespace: "excalidraw", Name: "excalidraw-1", Phase: "Running", Redirection: "enabled"}
    for _, c := range []struct {
        name    string
        pods    []restartPod
        ztunnel []bool
        got     map[string]int
        want    string
    }{
        {"recovered", []restartPod{running}, []bool{true}, ok, ""},
        {"ztunnel not ready", []restartPod{running}, []bool{false}, ok, "ztunnel"},
        {"no ztunnel pod", []restartPod{running}, nil, ok, "ztunnel"},
        {"pod pending", []restartPod{{Namespace: "excalidraw", Name: "excalidraw-1", Phase: "Pending", Redirection: "pending"}}, []bool{true}, ok, "excalidraw/excalidraw-1"},
        {"not redirected", []restartPod{{Namespace: "excalidraw", Name: "excalidraw-1", Phase: "Running", Redirection: "pending"}}, []bool{true}, ok, "not redirected"},
        {"opted out", []restartPod{{Namespace: "cert-manager", Name: "webhook-1", Phase: "Running", OptedOut: true}}, []bool{true}, ok, ""},
        {"outside the mesh", []restartPod{{Namespace: "kube-system", Name: "coredns-1", Phase: "Running"}}, []bool{true}, ok, ""},
        {"finished job ignored", []restartPod{running, {Namespace: "istio-system", Name: "istio-cni-watchdog-1", Phase: "Succeeded"}, {Namespace: "forgejo", Name: "seed-1", Phase: "Failed"}}, []bool{true}, ok, ""},
        {"app code differs", []restartPod{running}, []bool{true}, map[string]int{"excalidraw": 503}, "excalidraw answers 503"},
        {"app unreachable", []restartPod{running}, []bool{true}, map[string]int{}, "excalidraw answers 0"},
    } {
        t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            meshed := map[string]bool{"excalidraw": true, "cert-manager": true}
            blockers := strings.Join(restartBlockers(c.pods, meshed, c.ztunnel, ok, c.got), "\n")
            if c.want == "" {
                assert.Empty(t, blockers)
            } else {
                assert.Contains(t, blockers, c.want)
            }
        })
    }
}

  • Step 3: Add the type, the function and the cluster test

Append to test/node_restart_test.go:

// restartPod is what TestNodeRestart needs from a pod.
type restartPod struct {
    Namespace, Name, Phase, Redirection string
    OptedOut                            bool // labelled istio.io/dataplane-mode=none
}

// restartBlockers lists what still keeps the cluster from being recovered after a node restart: ztunnel not Ready,
// pods not running (finished Job pods aside), meshed pods not redirected to ztunnel, and apps that do not answer
// with the code they gave before the restart (0: unreachable).
func restartBlockers(pods []restartPod, meshed map[string]bool, ztunnelReady []bool, want, got map[string]int) []string {
    var blockers []string
    if len(ztunnelReady) == 0 {
        blockers = append(blockers, "no ztunnel pod")
    }
    for i, ready := range ztunnelReady {
        if !ready {
            blockers = append(blockers, fmt.Sprintf("ztunnel %d not Ready", i))
        }
    }
    for _, p := range pods {
        switch {
        case p.Phase == "Succeeded" || p.Phase == "Failed":
        case p.Phase != "Running":
            blockers = append(blockers, fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s is %s", p.Namespace, p.Name, p.Phase))
        case meshed[p.Namespace] && !p.OptedOut && p.Redirection != "enabled":
            blockers = append(blockers, fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s not redirected to ztunnel (%q)", p.Namespace, p.Name, p.Redirection))
        }
    }
    for app, code := range want {
        if got[app] != code {
            blockers = append(blockers, fmt.Sprintf("%s answers %d, %d before the restart", app, got[app], code))
        }
    }
    return blockers
}

// appCodes is each sandbox app's status code through the Gateway (0 when unreachable).
func appCodes(t *testing.T, hosts map[string]string) map[string]int {
    codes := map[string]int{}
    for app, host := range hosts {
        resp, err := insecureClient.Get("https://" + host)
        if err != nil {
            codes[app] = 0
            continue
        }
        codes[app] = resp.StatusCode
        _ = resp.Body.Close()
    }
    return codes
}

// clusterState reads the pods, the meshed namespaces and the ztunnel pods' readiness; ok is false while the API
// server does not answer.
func clusterState(t *testing.T) (pods []restartPod, meshed map[string]bool, ztunnelReady []bool, ok bool) {
    var list struct {
        Items []struct {
            Metadata struct {
                Namespace   string            `json:"namespace"`
                Name        string            `json:"name"`
                Labels      map[string]string `json:"labels"`
                Annotations map[string]string `json:"annotations"`
            } `json:"metadata"`
            Spec struct {
                HostNetwork bool `json:"hostNetwork"`
            } `json:"spec"`
            Status struct {
                Phase             string `json:"phase"`
                ContainerStatuses []struct {
                    Ready bool `json:"ready"`
                } `json:"containerStatuses"`
            } `json:"status"`
        } `json:"items"`
    }
    if !getResource(t, "default", &list, "pods", "--all-namespaces") {
        return nil, nil, nil, false
    }
    var namespaces struct {
        Items []struct {
            Metadata struct {
                Name string `json:"name"`
            } `json:"metadata"`
        } `json:"items"`
    }
    if !getResource(t, "default", &namespaces, "namespaces", "--selector=istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient") {
        return nil, nil, nil, false
    }
    meshed = map[string]bool{}
    for _, n := range namespaces.Items {
        meshed[n.Metadata.Name] = true
    }
    for _, p := range list.Items {
        if p.Metadata.Namespace == "istio-system" && p.Metadata.Labels["app"] == "ztunnel" {
            ztunnelReady = append(ztunnelReady, len(p.Status.ContainerStatuses) > 0 && p.Status.ContainerStatuses[0].Ready)
        }
        pods = append(pods, restartPod{
            Namespace:   p.Metadata.Namespace,
            Name:        p.Metadata.Name,
            Phase:       p.Status.Phase,
            Redirection: p.Metadata.Annotations["ambient.istio.io/redirection"],
            OptedOut:    p.Metadata.Labels["istio.io/dataplane-mode"] == "none" || p.Spec.HostNetwork,
        })
    }
    return pods, meshed, ztunnelReady, true
}

// TestNodeRestart restarts the sandbox's node and waits until the mesh and the apps are back as they were: the
// istio-cni watchdog (system/istio-system) must break the deadlock described in
// docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-mesh-node-restart-design.md. make dev runs it alone, after the other tests.
func TestNodeRestart(t *testing.T) {
    meshSandboxOnly(t)
    hosts := map[string]string{}
    for _, app := range smokeApps("dev") {
        hosts[app.name] = routeHost(t, app.namespace, app.name)
    }
    var want map[string]int
    require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        want = appCodes(t, hosts)
        pods, meshed, ztunnel, ok := clusterState(t)
        return ok && len(restartBlockers(pods, meshed, ztunnel, want, want)) == 0 && !hasServerError(want)
    }, 10*time.Minute, 15*time.Second, "the sandbox is not healthy before the restart")
    t.Logf("before the restart: %v", want)

    out, err := exec.Command("docker", "restart", k3dNode).CombinedOutput()
    require.NoError(t, err, "docker restart %s: %s", k3dNode, out)
    restarted := time.Now()

    var blockers []string
    recovered := assert.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        pods, meshed, ztunnel, ok := clusterState(t)
        if !ok {
            blockers = []string{"API server not answering"}
            return false
        }
        blockers = restartBlockers(pods, meshed, ztunnel, want, appCodes(t, hosts))
        return len(blockers) == 0
    }, 12*time.Minute, 15*time.Second, "the sandbox did not recover from a node restart")
    if recovered {
        t.Logf("recovered %s after the restart", time.Since(restarted).Round(time.Second))
    } else {
        t.Logf("still blocking:\n%s", strings.Join(blockers, "\n"))
    }
}

// hasServerError reports a 5xx or unreachable app: the codes recorded before the restart must be the apps'
// healthy answers.
func hasServerError(codes map[string]int) bool {
    for _, code := range codes {
        if code == 0 || code >= 500 {
            return true
        }
    }
    return false
}

  • Step 1: Write the script's test, with a fake kubectl

Create test/cni_watchdog_test.go:

package test

import (
    "fmt"
    "os"
    "os/exec"
    "path/filepath"
    "strings"
    "testing"
    "time"

    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// fakeKubectl answers the watchdog's two queries from files and records deletions.
const fakeKubectl = `#!/bin/sh
case "$*" in
  *"delete pod"*) echo "$*" >> "$FIXTURES/deleted" ;;
  *app=ztunnel*) cat "$FIXTURES/ztunnel" ;;
  *istio-cni-node*) node=$(echo "$*" | sed -n 's/.*spec.nodeName=\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p'); cat "$FIXTURES/cni-$node" 2>/dev/null ;;
esac
`

// runWatchdog runs system/istio-system/files/cni-watchdog.sh against ztunnel lines ("node ready startedAt") and
// istio-cni lines per node ("pod startedAt"), and returns the kubectl deletions it made.
func runWatchdog(t *testing.T, ztunnel string, cni map[string]string) string {
    dir := t.TempDir()
    require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "kubectl"), []byte(fakeKubectl), 0o755))
    require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "ztunnel"), []byte(ztunnel), 0o644))
    for node, lines := range cni {
        require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "cni-"+node), []byte(lines), 0o644))
    }
    cmd := exec.Command("sh", "../system/istio-system/files/cni-watchdog.sh")
    cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "PATH="+dir+":"+os.Getenv("PATH"), "FIXTURES="+dir, "NOT_READY_SECONDS=180")
    out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    require.NoError(t, err, "watchdog failed:\n%s", out)
    deleted, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "deleted"))
    return strings.TrimSpace(string(deleted))
}

func ago(seconds int) string {
    return time.Now().UTC().Add(-time.Duration(seconds) * time.Second).Format(time.RFC3339)
}

func TestIstioCNIWatchdog(t *testing.T) {
    for _, c := range []struct {
        name    string
        ztunnel string
        cni     map[string]string
        deleted string
    }{
        {"stuck node", fmt.Sprintf("node-a false %s\n", ago(300)), map[string]string{"node-a": "istio-cni-a " + ago(300) + "\n"}, "-n istio-system delete pod istio-cni-a --wait=false"},
        {"ztunnel just started", fmt.Sprintf("node-a false %s\n", ago(60)), map[string]string{"node-a": "istio-cni-a " + ago(300) + "\n"}, ""},
        {"ztunnel ready", fmt.Sprintf("node-a true %s\n", ago(300)), map[string]string{"node-a": "istio-cni-a " + ago(300) + "\n"}, ""},
        {"istio-cni just restarted", fmt.Sprintf("node-a false %s\n", ago(300)), map[string]string{"node-a": "istio-cni-a " + ago(60) + "\n"}, ""},
        {"ztunnel not running", "node-a false \n", map[string]string{"node-a": "istio-cni-a " + ago(300) + "\n"}, ""},
        {"no istio-cni pod", fmt.Sprintf("node-a false %s\nnode-b false %s\n", ago(300), ago(300)), map[string]string{"node-b": "istio-cni-b " + ago(300) + "\n"}, "-n istio-system delete pod istio-cni-b --wait=false"},
        {"only the stuck node", fmt.Sprintf("node-a true %s\nnode-b false %s\n", ago(300), ago(300)), map[string]string{"node-a": "istio-cni-a " + ago(300) + "\n", "node-b": "istio-cni-b " + ago(300) + "\n"}, "-n istio-system delete pod istio-cni-b --wait=false"},
    } {
        t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            assert.Equal(t, c.deleted, runWatchdog(t, c.ztunnel, c.cni))
        })
    }
}

  • Step 3: Write the script

Create system/istio-system/files/cni-watchdog.sh:

#!/bin/sh
# Restarts a node's istio-cni when that node's ztunnel has been running but not Ready for NOT_READY_SECONDS: after a
# node restart, istio-cni's snapshot can hold network namespaces of pod sandboxes that were torn down, and ztunnel
# then retries them forever; a new istio-cni builds its snapshot again (docs/reference/architecture/networking.md).
# ztunnel without a start time (waiting, crash-looping) is left alone: its age is unknown.
set -eu
limit=${NOT_READY_SECONDS:-180}
now=$(date -u +%s)

# GNU date parses RFC 3339 with -d; BusyBox (the image) needs the format
epoch() {
    date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null || date -u -D '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' -d "$1" +%s
}

kubectl -n istio-system get pods -l app=ztunnel -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.nodeName} {.status.containerStatuses[0].ready} {.status.containerStatuses[0].state.running.startedAt}{"\n"}{end}' |
    while read -r node ready started; do
        [ "$ready" = false ] && [ -n "${started:-}" ] || continue
        [ $((now - $(epoch "$started"))) -gt "$limit" ] || continue
        cni=$(kubectl -n istio-system get pods -l k8s-app=istio-cni-node --field-selector "spec.nodeName=$node" -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.containerStatuses[0].state.running.startedAt}{"\n"}{end}')
        set -- $cni
        if [ $# -ne 2 ]; then
            echo "$node: ztunnel not Ready, no running istio-cni pod"
            continue
        fi
        if [ $((now - $(epoch "$2"))) -le "$limit" ]; then
            echo "$node: ztunnel not Ready, istio-cni $1 started less than ${limit}s ago"
            continue
        fi
        echo "$node: ztunnel not Ready for more than ${limit}s, restarting istio-cni $1"
        kubectl -n istio-system delete pod "$1" --wait=false
    done

Append to system/istio-system/values.yaml:

# follows a node restart
cniWatchdog:
  # The official kubectl image has no shell
  image: alpine/kubectl:1.37.1@sha256:8c72f6f732ce7ef11cdb1bea25faa4f4a521872a12c89e3f40ba9edb52a4d4f2
  notReadySeconds: 180

Create system/istio-system/templates/cni-watchdog.yaml:

apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: istio-cni-watchdog
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: istio-cni-watchdog
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: [pods]
    verbs: [get, list, delete]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: istio-cni-watchdog
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: istio-cni-watchdog
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: istio-cni-watchdog
    namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: istio-cni-watchdog
data:
  cni-watchdog.sh: |
{{ .Files.Get "files/cni-watchdog.sh" | indent 4 }}
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: istio-cni-watchdog
spec:
  schedule: "* * * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  startingDeadlineSeconds: 50
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      activeDeadlineSeconds: 50
      backoffLimit: 0
      ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 300
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: istio-cni-watchdog
          restartPolicy: Never
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 65534
            runAsGroup: 65534
            seccompProfile:
              type: RuntimeDefault
          containers:
            - name: watchdog
              image: {{ .Values.cniWatchdog.image }}
              command: [sh, /scripts/cni-watchdog.sh]
              env:
                - name: NOT_READY_SECONDS
                  value: {{ .Values.cniWatchdog.notReadySeconds | quote }}
              securityContext:
                allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
                readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                capabilities:
                  drop: [ALL]
              resources:
                requests:
                  cpu: 10m
                  memory: 32Mi
              volumeMounts:
                - name: scripts
                  mountPath: /scripts
          volumes:
            - name: scripts
              configMap:
                name: istio-cni-watchdog

Interfaces: - Consumes: the names from Tasks 1–3 (istio-cni-watchdog, TestNodeRestart, TestNodeRestartBlockers, TestIstioCNIWatchdog). - Produces: documentation only.

  • Step 1: CLAUDE.md, the offline tests

In the Rules bullet on basic checks, replace go test -run 'TestSmokeAppsForEnv|TestIdentity(TOTPWaitsForNextStep|PKCE)|TestGatewayRouteReady|TestGatewayNodeAddressFromInspect' ./... with go test -run 'TestSmokeAppsForEnv|TestIdentity(TOTPWaitsForNextStep|PKCE)|TestGatewayRouteReady|TestGatewayNodeAddressFromInspect|TestNodeRestartBlockers|TestIstioCNIWatchdog' ./....

  • Step 2: CLAUDE.md, Sandbox

Change the make dev filter sentence in the Kanidm bullet from (make devrunsSmoke|…|Logs) to (make devrunsSmoke|…|Logs, thenTestNodeRestartalone: it restarts the node), and add after the Istio mesh bullet:

- A node restart can leave the mesh deadlocked: pods recreated before the node's ztunnel connects fail istio-cni's 5-second `cmdAdd`, containerd tears their sandboxes down, istio-cni's snapshot keeps the dead network namespaces and ztunnel retries them forever (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-mesh-node-restart-design.md`). The CronJob `istio-system/istio-cni-watchdog` (`files/cni-watchdog.sh`) deletes a node's istio-cni pod when that node's ztunnel has run 180 s without becoming Ready; `TestNodeRestart` proves the sandbox recovers (about 4 to 9 minutes). `cni.istioOwnedCNIConfig` stays on: k3s rewrites `10-flannel.conflist` at every start.
  • Step 3: CLAUDE.md, the production list

Add to "Before the first production deploy":

- Node-restart recovery (the istio-cni watchdog, `istioOwnedCNIConfig`) only ran on the one-node sandbox, where every node restart deadlocks the mesh without the watchdog; istiod's two replicas spread over nodes were only rendered. Give k3s's CoreDNS two replicas on different nodes in step 12 (`kube-system` is outside Argo CD), so a rebooted node's ztunnel finds DNS and istiod at once. A power loss that restarts every node is unmeasured on real hardware.
  • Step 4: The networking page

Append to ## Service mesh in docs/reference/architecture/networking.md, before ## Egress:

### Node restarts

When a node restarts, the kubelet recreates its pods while the node's ztunnel may still be waiting for istiod. istio-cni cannot hand those pods to ztunnel within its 5-second limit, containerd tears their sandboxes down, and istio-cni's snapshot keeps their dead network namespaces, which ztunnel then retries forever: the node's meshed pods stay `Pending` and ztunnel stays not Ready. The CronJob `istio-system/istio-cni-watchdog` deletes a node's istio-cni pod when that node's ztunnel has run for 3 minutes without becoming Ready; the new istio-cni builds its snapshot again and the pods start. Look at `kubectl -n istio-system get pods` and the watchdog Jobs' logs. istio-cni writes its own CNI config file (`istioOwnedCNIConfig`), because k3s rewrites `10-flannel.conflist` at every start.
  • Step 5: Build the docs

Run: mkdocs build --strict 2>&1 | tail -3 Expected: INFO - Documentation built in ... with no warning.

  • Step 6: Commit
git add CLAUDE.md docs/reference/architecture/networking.md
git commit -m "docs: node restarts, the istio-cni watchdog and its production checklist"

docs.title: OpenTofu State on R2 with Encryption Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Production's OpenTofu state lives in the R2 bucket homelab-production-tfstate, every environment's state is encrypted with a passphrase that a tested script can rotate, and Cloudflare credentials come from cf auth login.

Architecture: - infra/root.hcl generates two files for every unit: - backend.tf: production gets the http backend on R2's object API with cf's OAuth token; the sandbox keeps local state. - encryption.tf: pbkdf2 and aes_gcm. A fallback appears only for a rotation (the previous passphrase) or a migration (unencrypted). - Three small POSIX scripts, each tested offline against fake commands or a throwaway Terragrunt tree: - scripts/cloudflare-credentials: account and token; - scripts/ensure-state-bucket: creates the bucket; - scripts/rotate-state-passphrase: re-encrypts every unit's state. - cf is built in flake.nix from nixpkgs PR #569193's derivation.

Tech Stack: OpenTofu 1.11 (state encryption, http backend), Terragrunt 1.1, Nix (stdenv.mkDerivation with pnpm), POSIX sh, curl and jq, Go tests.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-state-r2-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Bucket homelab-production-tfstate; object <unit>/tfstate.json; address https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<account>/r2/buckets/<bucket>/objects/<unit>/tfstate.json; update_method = "PUT"; header Authorization: Bearer <token>; no lock.
  • Only production uses R2 and cf. Sandbox units never call cf, and make dev needs no Cloudflare login.
  • Encryption in every environment: key_provider "pbkdf2", method "aes_gcm", applied to state and plan, enforced = true.
  • Passphrase: HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE from ~/.config/homelab/state.env (mode 600, loaded by .envrc), handed to OpenTofu only as TF_VAR_state_passphrase.
  • Never print it, log it, write it to a generated file, or commit it. Claude never reads state.env.
  • The user creates the file and keeps a copy in a password manager.
  • cf pinned at cf@1.0.0-beta.18 (only betas exist).
  • ~/.config/homelab/cloudflare.env and its .envrc line are removed.
  • Production migration happens only after the user ran ! cf auth login and confirmed. The local .state/production/ files stay until the user deletes them.
  • No test name contains a word of make dev's main filter (Smoke|Identity|SSO|Gateway|Forgejo|Mesh|Monitoring|Egress|Secrets|Ntfy|Logs) or NodeRestart.
  • Commits end with the session's attribution lines. Never commit to dev or master.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. make -C infra check and terragrunt hcl validate without a passphrase: parsing root.hcl must not fail. Only commands that touch state may refuse. The check is pinned in Task 3, Step 7, which runs make -C infra check with the variable unset.
  2. The OAuth token in generated files: backend.tf in .terragrunt-cache carries the Bearer token, as upstream's does. .terragrunt-cache/ must stay git-ignored and user-only. Task 4, Step 6 checks git check-ignore and the permissions hook.
  3. A unit with no state (production argocd, openbao and secrets today): rotation must skip it rather than push an empty state. Pinned by TestStatePassphraseRotation/empty_unit_skipped.
  4. init -reconfigure against -migrate-state: the two flags conflict. A migration run must not get -reconfigure. Task 4's HOMELAB_STATE_MIGRATE switch covers it, and Task 5 uses it.
  5. A failed rotation halfway: every unit is pulled before anything is pushed, so a pull failure changes nothing. Pinned by TestStatePassphraseRotation/wrong_previous_changes_nothing.

docs.title: Task 2: Cloudflare credentials and the state bucket
docs.text:
Files: - Create: scripts/cloudflare-credentials - Create: scripts/ensure-state-bucket - Create: test/state_scripts_test.go

Interfaces: - Produces: - scripts/cloudflare-credentials <env> prints one JSON line: {"account_id":"...","token":"..."}. Both are empty strings unless <env> is production. It exits non-zero when cf fails. - scripts/ensure-state-bucket <bucket> gets its credentials from cloudflare-credentials production and creates the bucket if GET answers 404. It exits non-zero, with the API's message, on any other error.

  • Step 1: Write the tests

Create test/state_scripts_test.go:

package test

import (
    "os"
    "os/exec"
    "path/filepath"
    "strings"
    "testing"

    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// fakeBin writes executable scripts into a temporary directory placed first on PATH.
func fakeBin(t *testing.T, scripts map[string]string) (dir string, env []string) {
    dir = t.TempDir()
    for name, body := range scripts {
        require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, name), []byte("#!/bin/sh\n"+body), 0o755))
    }
    return dir, append(os.Environ(), "PATH="+dir+":"+os.Getenv("PATH"), "FIXTURES="+dir)
}

func runScript(t *testing.T, env []string, script string, args ...string) (string, error) {
    cmd := exec.Command("sh", append([]string{"../scripts/" + script}, args...)...)
    cmd.Env = env
    out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    return strings.TrimSpace(string(out)), err
}

func TestStateCloudflareCredentials(t *testing.T) {
    dir, env := fakeBin(t, map[string]string{
        "cf": `[ -z "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] || { echo "token leaked into cf" >&2; exit 3; }
[ -f "$FIXTURES/cf-fails" ] && { echo "not logged in" >&2; exit 1; }
printf '{"authSource":"OAuth token from %s/token.json","accounts":[{"id":"acc-1"},{"id":"acc-2"}]}\n' "$FIXTURES"`,
    })
    require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "token.json"), []byte(`{"oauth_token":"tok-123"}`), 0o600))
    env = append(env, "CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=old-token")

    out, err := runScript(t, env, "cloudflare-credentials", "sandbox")
    require.NoError(t, err)
    assert.JSONEq(t, `{"account_id":"","token":""}`, out, "the sandbox never calls cf")

    out, err = runScript(t, env, "cloudflare-credentials", "production")
    require.NoError(t, err)
    assert.JSONEq(t, `{"account_id":"acc-1","token":"tok-123"}`, out)

    out, err = runScript(t, append(env, "CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=acc-2"), "cloudflare-credentials", "production")
    require.NoError(t, err)
    assert.JSONEq(t, `{"account_id":"acc-2","token":"tok-123"}`, out)

    require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "cf-fails"), nil, 0o644))
    out, err = runScript(t, env, "cloudflare-credentials", "production")
    assert.Error(t, err)
    assert.Contains(t, out, "not logged in")
}

func TestStateBucket(t *testing.T) {
    for _, c := range []struct {
        name, getCode, postCode string
        created, fails          bool
    }{
        {"missing bucket created", "404", "200", true, false},
        {"existing bucket kept", "200", "", false, false},
        {"API error", "403", "", false, true},
        {"create fails", "404", "409", true, true},
    } {
        t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            dir, env := fakeBin(t, map[string]string{
                "cloudflare-credentials": `echo '{"account_id":"acc-1","token":"tok-123"}'`,
                // Records each call; -o writes the body, -w prints the status code
                "curl": `echo "$*" >> "$FIXTURES/calls"
out=; while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do case "$1" in -o) out=$2; shift;; esac; shift; done
case "$(tail -1 "$FIXTURES/calls")" in
  *"-X POST"*) code=$(cat "$FIXTURES/post");;
  *) code=$(cat "$FIXTURES/get");;
esac
echo '{"errors":[{"message":"fake '"$code"'"}]}' > "$out"; printf %s "$code"`,
            })
            require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "get"), []byte(c.getCode), 0o644))
            require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "post"), []byte(c.postCode), 0o644))
            out, err := runScript(t, append(env, "CLOUDFLARE_CREDENTIALS="+filepath.Join(dir, "cloudflare-credentials")), "ensure-state-bucket", "homelab-production-tfstate")
            calls, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "calls"))
            assert.Contains(t, string(calls), "accounts/acc-1/r2/buckets/homelab-production-tfstate")
            assert.NotContains(t, string(calls), "tok-123", "the token must not be on curl's command line")
            assert.Equal(t, c.created, strings.Contains(string(calls), "-X POST"))
            if c.fails {
                assert.Error(t, err)
                assert.Contains(t, out, "fake")
            } else {
                assert.NoError(t, err, out)
            }
        })
    }
}
  • Step 2: Run them to see them fail

Run: cd test && go test -run 'TestStateCloudflareCredentials|TestStateBucket' ./... 2>&1 | grep -E 'No such file|can.t open|^(FAIL|ok)' | head -4 Expected: FAIL. The scripts do not exist ("No such file or directory").

  • Step 3: Write scripts/cloudflare-credentials
#!/bin/sh
# Prints {"account_id": ..., "token": ...} for OpenTofu (infra/root.hcl): production's from cf's OAuth login
# (`cf auth login`), empty strings for every other environment, which never talks to Cloudflare.
# CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID picks the account when the login sees several.
set -eu
env=${1:?usage: cloudflare-credentials <env>}
if [ "$env" != production ]; then
    echo '{"account_id":"","token":""}'
    exit
fi
identity=$(env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN -u CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY -u CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL CF_SEND_TELEMETRY=false cf --quiet auth whoami)
token_file=$(printf '%s' "$identity" | jq -r '.authSource | sub("^OAuth token from "; "")')
account=${CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID:-$(printf '%s' "$identity" | jq -r '.accounts[0].id')}
jq -cn --arg account "$account" --slurpfile token "$token_file" '{account_id: $account, token: $token[0].oauth_token}'
  • Step 4: Write scripts/ensure-state-bucket
#!/bin/sh
# Creates production's OpenTofu state bucket on R2 when it does not exist (a before_hook of `init`, infra/root.hcl).
# The token goes to curl through a header file, never its command line.
set -eu
bucket=${1:?usage: ensure-state-bucket <bucket>}
credentials=$("${CLOUDFLARE_CREDENTIALS:-$(dirname "$0")/cloudflare-credentials}" production)
account=$(printf '%s' "$credentials" | jq -r .account_id)
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
(umask 077; printf '%s' "$credentials" | jq -r '"Authorization: Bearer " + .token' > "$work/auth")
api="https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$account/r2/buckets"

code=$(curl -sS -H "@$work/auth" -o "$work/body" -w '%{http_code}' "$api/$bucket")
case $code in
    200) exit ;;
    404) ;;
    *) echo "ensure-state-bucket: GET $bucket: HTTP $code: $(jq -r '[.errors[].message] | join("; ")' "$work/body" 2>/dev/null)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
code=$(curl -sS -X POST -H "@$work/auth" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"name\":\"$bucket\"}" -o "$work/body" -w '%{http_code}' "$api")
if [ "$code" != 200 ]; then
    echo "ensure-state-bucket: create $bucket: HTTP $code: $(jq -r '[.errors[].message] | join("; ")' "$work/body" 2>/dev/null)" >&2
    exit 1
fi
echo "ensure-state-bucket: created $bucket"

Then run chmod +x scripts/cloudflare-credentials scripts/ensure-state-bucket.

  • Step 5: Run the tests to see them pass

Run: cd test && go test -run 'TestStateCloudflareCredentials|TestStateBucket' -v ./... 2>&1 | grep -E '^(\s*--- |ok|FAIL)' | tail -8; shellcheck ../scripts/cloudflare-credentials ../scripts/ensure-state-bucket && echo shellcheck-ok Expected: every subtest passes, then ok and shellcheck-ok.

  • Step 6: Commit
git add scripts/cloudflare-credentials scripts/ensure-state-bucket test/state_scripts_test.go
git commit -m "feat(infra): Cloudflare credentials from cf's OAuth login, and the R2 state bucket script"

docs.title: Task 3: State encryption in every environment, and its rotation
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: infra/root.hcl - Create: scripts/rotate-state-passphrase - Create: test/state_rotation_test.go - Modify: .envrc

Interfaces: - Consumes: scripts/cloudflare-credentials (Task 2) is not used yet. - Produces: - infra/root.hcl generates encryption.tf, with fallbacks when HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE_PREVIOUS or HOMELAB_STATE_MIGRATE=1 is set. - scripts/rotate-state-passphrase <env>.

  • Step 1: The user creates the passphrase (stop and ask)

Ask the user to run both commands, then copy the passphrase into their password manager: - ! sh -c 'umask 077; mkdir -p ~/.config/homelab; printf "export HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE=%s\n" "$(openssl rand -base64 32)" > ~/.config/homelab/state.env' - ! direnv allow

Do not read the file. Wait for their confirmation. Verify only that it is set: direnv exec . sh -c 'test ${#HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE} -ge 16 && echo passphrase-set' must print passphrase-set. This needs .envrc from Step 2 to load it, so do Step 2 before this check.

  • Step 2: .envrc loads state.env

Add the following to .envrc, keeping the cloudflare.env line until Task 4:

# OpenTofu's state passphrase (outside the repository; docs/installation/production/external-resources.md)
source_env_if_exists ~/.config/homelab/state.env
  • Step 3: Clean the sandbox while its state is still unencrypted

Run: direnv exec . make dev-clean > /tmp/claude-1000/-home-nixos-homelab/44339b87-568a-46fd-9484-aed834c50ef8/scratchpad/clean-8c.log 2>&1; echo clean=$? Expected: clean=0.

  • Step 4: Write the rotation test

Create test/state_rotation_test.go:

package test

import (
    "os"
    "os/exec"
    "path/filepath"
    "strings"
    "testing"

    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

const (
    passphraseA = "passphrase-a-0123456789"
    passphraseB = "passphrase-b-9876543210"
)

// stateTree builds a throwaway repository with this repository's infra/root.hcl and scripts, and two sandbox units:
// "marker" (a terraform_data resource, no provider) and "empty" (no resources).
func stateTree(t *testing.T) string {
    root := t.TempDir()
    mustWrite := func(path, body string, mode os.FileMode) {
        require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(filepath.Join(root, path)), 0o755))
        require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, path), []byte(body), mode))
    }
    for _, f := range []string{"infra/root.hcl", "scripts/rotate-state-passphrase", "scripts/cloudflare-credentials"} {
        body, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("..", f))
        require.NoError(t, err)
        mustWrite(f, string(body), 0o755)
    }
    mustWrite("infra/_modules/marker/main.tf", `resource "terraform_data" "marker" { input = "visible-marker" }`+"\n", 0o644)
    mustWrite("infra/_modules/empty/main.tf", "\n", 0o644)
    for _, unit := range []string{"marker", "empty"} {
        mustWrite("infra/sandbox/"+unit+"/terragrunt.hcl", `include "root" {
  path = find_in_parent_folders("root.hcl")
}
terraform {
  source = "${find_in_parent_folders("_modules")}//`+unit+`"
}
`, 0o644)
    }
    require.NoError(t, exec.Command("git", "-C", root, "init", "-q").Run())
    return root
}

// tg runs terragrunt in a unit with the given passphrases ("" leaves a variable unset).
func tg(t *testing.T, root, unit, current, previous string, args ...string) (string, error) {
    cmd := exec.Command("terragrunt", append(args, "--non-interactive", "--log-level", "error")...)
    cmd.Dir = filepath.Join(root, "infra/sandbox", unit)
    cmd.Env = stateEnv(current, previous)
    out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    return string(out), err
}

func stateEnv(current, previous string) []string {
    var env []string
    for _, e := range os.Environ() {
        if !strings.HasPrefix(e, "HOMELAB_STATE_") && !strings.HasPrefix(e, "TF_VAR_") {
            env = append(env, e)
        }
    }
    if current != "" {
        env = append(env, "HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE="+current)
    }
    if previous != "" {
        env = append(env, "HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE_PREVIOUS="+previous)
    }
    return env
}

func rotate(t *testing.T, root, current, previous string) (string, error) {
    cmd := exec.Command("sh", "scripts/rotate-state-passphrase", "sandbox")
    cmd.Dir = root
    cmd.Env = stateEnv(current, previous)
    out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    return string(out), err
}

func stateFile(t *testing.T, root, unit string) string {
    body, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, ".state/sandbox", unit, "terraform.tfstate"))
    return string(body)
}

func TestStatePassphraseRotation(t *testing.T) {
    root := stateTree(t)
    out, err := tg(t, root, "marker", passphraseA, "", "apply", "-auto-approve")
    require.NoError(t, err, out)
    _, err = tg(t, root, "empty", passphraseA, "", "apply", "-auto-approve")
    require.NoError(t, err)

    t.Run("state encrypted at rest", func(t *testing.T) {
        state := stateFile(t, root, "marker")
        assert.Contains(t, state, "encrypted_data")
        assert.NotContains(t, state, "visible-marker")
    })

    t.Run("refusals change nothing", func(t *testing.T) {
        before := stateFile(t, root, "marker")
        for _, c := range []struct{ name, current, previous string }{
            {"no previous", passphraseB, ""},
            {"no current", "", passphraseA},
            {"equal", passphraseA, passphraseA},
            {"too short", "short", passphraseA},
        } {
            out, err := rotate(t, root, c.current, c.previous)
            assert.Error(t, err, "%s: %s", c.name, out)
            assert.NotContains(t, out, passphraseA, "a passphrase was printed")
        }
        assert.Equal(t, before, stateFile(t, root, "marker"))
    })

    t.Run("wrong previous changes nothing", func(t *testing.T) {
        before := stateFile(t, root, "marker")
        out, err := rotate(t, root, passphraseB, "wrong-passphrase-000000")
        assert.Error(t, err, out)
        assert.Equal(t, before, stateFile(t, root, "marker"))
    })

    t.Run("rotated", func(t *testing.T) {
        out, err := rotate(t, root, passphraseB, passphraseA)
        require.NoError(t, err, out)
        assert.NotContains(t, out, passphraseA)
        assert.NotContains(t, out, passphraseB)
        pulled, err := tg(t, root, "marker", passphraseB, "", "state", "pull")
        require.NoError(t, err, pulled)
        assert.Contains(t, pulled, "visible-marker")
        _, err = tg(t, root, "marker", passphraseA, "", "state", "pull")
        assert.Error(t, err, "the old passphrase still reads the state")
    })

    t.Run("empty unit skipped", func(t *testing.T) {
        _, err := tg(t, root, "empty", passphraseB, "", "state", "pull")
        assert.NoError(t, err)
    })
}

generate "encryption" {
  path      = "encryption.tf"
  if_exists = "overwrite_terragrunt"
  contents  = <<-EOF
    variable "state_passphrase" {
      type      = string
      sensitive = true
    }
    %{~if local.state_passphrase_previous != ""}
    variable "state_passphrase_previous" {
      type      = string
      sensitive = true
    }
    %{~endif}
    terraform {
      encryption {
        key_provider "pbkdf2" "current" {
          passphrase = var.state_passphrase
        }
        method "aes_gcm" "current" {
          keys = key_provider.pbkdf2.current
        }
        %{~if local.state_passphrase_previous != ""}
        key_provider "pbkdf2" "previous" {
          passphrase = var.state_passphrase_previous
        }
        method "aes_gcm" "previous" {
          keys = key_provider.pbkdf2.previous
        }
        %{~endif}
        %{~if local.state_migrate}
        method "unencrypted" "migrate" {}
        %{~endif}
        state {
          method   = method.aes_gcm.current
          enforced = true
          %{~if local.state_passphrase_previous != "" || local.state_migrate}
          fallback {
            method = ${local.state_passphrase_previous != "" ? "method.aes_gcm.previous" : "method.unencrypted.migrate"}
          }
          %{~endif}
        }
        plan {
          method   = method.aes_gcm.current
          enforced = true
        }
      }
    }
  EOF
}

  • Step 7: Write scripts/rotate-state-passphrase
#!/bin/sh
# Re-encrypts every OpenTofu state of an environment with a new passphrase (docs/installation/production/external-resources.md):
# put the new passphrase in HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE and the old one in HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE_PREVIOUS, run this,
# then update the password manager and ~/.config/homelab/state.env and drop _PREVIOUS. Every state is pulled before
# any is pushed, so a wrong old passphrase changes nothing. Passphrases are never printed.
set -eu
env=${1:?usage: rotate-state-passphrase <env>}
: "${HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE:?set HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE to the new passphrase}"
: "${HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE_PREVIOUS:?set HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE_PREVIOUS to the old passphrase}"
if [ "$HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE" = "$HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE_PREVIOUS" ]; then
    echo "rotate-state-passphrase: the new passphrase equals the old one" >&2
    exit 1
fi
if [ ${#HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE} -lt 16 ]; then
    echo "rotate-state-passphrase: the new passphrase is shorter than 16 characters" >&2
    exit 1
fi
root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
work=$(mktemp -d)
chmod 700 "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
tg() { terragrunt --non-interactive --log-level error "$@"; }

units=
for dir in "$root"/infra/"$env"/*/; do
    [ -f "$dir/terragrunt.hcl" ] || continue
    unit=$(basename "$dir")
    (cd "$dir" && tg state pull) > "$work/$unit.json" || { echo "rotate-state-passphrase: cannot read $env/$unit with the old passphrase; nothing changed" >&2; exit 1; }
    if [ -s "$work/$unit.json" ]; then
        units="$units $unit"
    else
        echo "$env/$unit: no state, skipped"
    fi
done
for unit in $units; do
    (cd "$root/infra/$env/$unit" && tg state push -force "$work/$unit.json")
    echo "$env/$unit: re-encrypted"
done
for unit in $units; do
    (cd "$root/infra/$env/$unit" && HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE_PREVIOUS= tg state pull >/dev/null) || { echo "rotate-state-passphrase: $env/$unit does not read with the new passphrase alone" >&2; exit 1; }
done
echo "Done. Update the password manager and ~/.config/homelab/state.env with the new passphrase, then unset HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE_PREVIOUS."

Delete the remote_state block and its comment, and add:

# Production's state is on R2 (one object per unit, read and written through Cloudflare's API with cf's OAuth token;
# no lock: one operator); the sandbox's stays local. Both are encrypted (encryption.tf). A string keeps the two
# backends' different shapes in one expression; the token lands in .terragrunt-cache, which is git-ignored and
# user-only, as upstream's remote_state does.
generate "backend" {
  path      = "backend.tf"
  if_exists = "overwrite_terragrunt"
  contents  = local.production ? <<-EOF
    terraform {
      backend "http" {
        address       = "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/${local.cloudflare.account_id}/r2/buckets/${local.state_bucket}/objects/${local.unit}/tfstate.json"
        update_method = "PUT"
        headers = {
          Authorization = "Bearer ${local.cloudflare.token}"
        }
      }
    }
  EOF
  : <<-EOF
    terraform {
      backend "local" {
        path = "${get_repo_root()}/.state/${path_relative_to_include()}/terraform.tfstate"
      }
    }
  EOF
}

docs.title: Step 8d: State through R2's S3 API Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Production's OpenTofu state uses the s3 backend on R2's S3 endpoint with a lock file, its credentials from lab infra state credentials (ported from upstream nixos), so no token sits in backend.tf.

Architecture: cli/internal/state and cli/internal/cli/{cloudflare,infra_state}.go come from upstream with their tests. infra/root.hcl generates an s3 backend plus an r2-state.config whose credential_process runs lab; lab infra state ensure replaces scripts/ensure-state-bucket. Offline tests run OpenTofu against a fake S3 server with a stub lab.

Tech Stack: Go 1.26, cobra v1.10.2, github.com/cloudflare/cloudflare-go v0.119.0, github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2 v1.47.3, OpenTofu 1.13 (s3 backend, use_lockfile), Terragrunt.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-state-s3-lock-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Branch feat/state-s3-lock (stacked on feat/test-scopes); never commit to dev or master.
  • Imports: github.com/duongle-steven/homelab/cli/... (upstream's github.com/khuedoan/homelab/cli/... rewritten).
  • Latest stable pins: cloudflare-go v0.119.0, aws-sdk-go-v2 v1.47.3 (upstream pins v0.115.0 and v1.39.2).
  • The sandbox's backend stays local; production's becomes s3 with use_lockfile = true, use_path_style = true, key <unit>/tfstate.json, bucket homelab-production-tfstate.
  • lab runs as go -C <repo>/cli run ./cmd/lab; HOMELAB_LAB overrides it, HOMELAB_STATE_ENDPOINT overrides https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com (both for tests).
  • Never print the OAuth token, R2 credentials or the state passphrase. Touching production state (Task 3) needs the user's go-ahead.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. credential_process and a multi-word lab command: the AWS SDK runs it through a shell, so go -C … run ./cmd/lab … must work. Pinned by Task 2's tests, whose stub is a script path, and by Task 3's real run.
  2. A missing object under s3: rotation must still skip the unit (no object = empty pull). Pinned in Task 2 (TestStateRotationSkipsMissingObjects).
  3. A stale lock after an interrupted command: the lock key is <unit>/tfstate.json.tflock; the docs name force-unlock. Pinned in Task 2 (TestStateS3Lock sees the lock written and removed).
  4. The token in generated files: neither backend.tf nor r2-state.config may contain the OAuth token. Pinned in Task 2 (TestStateTokenRefresh).
  5. make -C infra check without a login: parsing must not run lab or cf (HOMELAB_CLOUDFLARE_OFFLINE=1 keeps placeholders). Pinned in Task 2, Step 7.
