docs.text:
Files: - Modify: infra/root.hcl (locals, generate "backend", new generate "r2_credentials", the state_bucket hook) - Delete: scripts/ensure-state-bucket; TestStateBucket in test/state_scripts_test.go - Modify: test/state_token_refresh_test.go (fake S3 instead of fake R2), test/scopes.yaml (drop scripts/ensure-state-bucket from skip) - Test: test/state_token_refresh_test.go (TestStateTokenRefresh, TestStateRotationSkipsMissingObjects, TestStateS3Lock, TestStateBucketEnsuredOnInit)

Interfaces: - Consumes: lab infra state ensure|credentials (Task 1). - Produces: production's generated backend.tf (s3) and r2-state.config; env overrides HOMELAB_LAB, HOMELAB_STATE_ENDPOINT.

  • Step 1: Replace the fake R2 with a fake S3 and write the tests

Replace the fakeR2 type, prodTree and the four production tests in test/state_token_refresh_test.go with:

package test

import (
    "encoding/xml"
    "io"
    "net/http"
    "net/http/httptest"
    "os"
    "os/exec"
    "path/filepath"
    "sort"
    "strconv"
    "strings"
    "sync"
    "testing"

    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// fakeS3 is the part of R2's S3 API the s3 backend uses (path style): objects, conditional puts for the lock file,
// and ListObjectsV2.
type fakeS3 struct {
    mu      sync.Mutex
    objects map[string][]byte
    puts    []string
    url     string
}

func (f *fakeS3) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    f.mu.Lock()
    defer f.mu.Unlock()
    // /<bucket>/<key>
    parts := strings.SplitN(strings.TrimPrefix(r.URL.Path, "/"), "/", 2)
    key := ""
    if len(parts) == 2 {
        key = parts[1]
    }
    switch {
    case r.Method == http.MethodGet && key == "":
        prefix := r.URL.Query().Get("prefix")
        type content struct{ Key string }
        var result struct {
            XMLName  xml.Name  `xml:"ListBucketResult"`
            Contents []content `xml:"Contents"`
            KeyCount int       `xml:"KeyCount"`
        }
        var keys []string
        for k := range f.objects {
            if strings.HasPrefix(k, prefix) {
                keys = append(keys, k)
            }
        }
        sort.Strings(keys)
        for _, k := range keys {
            result.Contents = append(result.Contents, content{Key: k})
        }
        result.KeyCount = len(keys)
        w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/xml")
        _ = xml.NewEncoder(w).Encode(result)
    case r.Method == http.MethodGet || r.Method == http.MethodHead:
        body, ok := f.objects[key]
        if !ok {
            w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/xml")
            w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNotFound)
            if r.Method == http.MethodGet {
                _, _ = io.WriteString(w, `<Error><Code>NoSuchKey</Code><Message>missing</Message></Error>`)
            }
            return
        }
        w.Header().Set("Content-Length", strconv.Itoa(len(body)))
        if r.Method == http.MethodGet {
            _, _ = w.Write(body)
        }
    case r.Method == http.MethodPut:
        if _, exists := f.objects[key]; exists && r.Header.Get("If-None-Match") == "*" {
            w.WriteHeader(http.StatusPreconditionFailed)
            _, _ = io.WriteString(w, `<Error><Code>PreconditionFailed</Code><Message>exists</Message></Error>`)
            return
        }
        body, _ := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
        f.objects[key] = body
        f.puts = append(f.puts, key)
    case r.Method == http.MethodDelete:
        delete(f.objects, key)
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
    default:
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNotImplemented)
    }
}

func (f *fakeS3) keys() []string {
    f.mu.Lock()
    defer f.mu.Unlock()
    var keys []string
    for k := range f.objects {
        keys = append(keys, k)
    }
    sort.Strings(keys)
    return keys
}

func (f *fakeS3) putKeys() []string {
    f.mu.Lock()
    defer f.mu.Unlock()
    return append([]string{}, f.puts...)
}

// prodTree is stateTree plus production units ("marker", and "fresh", never applied) on a fake S3, with a stub lab
// (static credentials; ensure records its call) and cloudflare-credentials returning $FAKE_TOKEN.
func prodTree(t *testing.T) (string, *fakeS3, func(unit, token string, extra []string, args ...string) (string, error)) {
    root := stateTree(t)
    write := func(path, body string, mode os.FileMode) {
        require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(filepath.Join(root, path)), 0o755))
        require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, path), []byte(body), mode))
    }
    write("scripts/cloudflare-credentials", "#!/bin/sh\nprintf '{\"account_id\":\"acc-1\",\"token\":\"%s\"}\\n' \"$FAKE_TOKEN\"\n", 0o755)
    write("bin/lab", `#!/bin/sh
case "$1 $2 $3" in
  "infra state credentials") echo '{"Version":1,"AccessKeyId":"test-key","SecretAccessKey":"test-secret"}' ;;
  "infra state ensure") echo "$*" >> "$(dirname "$0")/ensure.log"; echo "State bucket ready." ;;
  *) echo "stub lab: $*" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
`, 0o755)
    for _, unit := range []string{"marker", "fresh"} {
        module := map[string]string{"marker": "marker", "fresh": "empty"}[unit]
        write("infra/production/"+unit+"/terragrunt.hcl", `include "root" {
  path = find_in_parent_folders("root.hcl")
}
terraform {
  source = "${find_in_parent_folders("_modules")}//`+module+`"
}
`, 0o644)
    }
    s3 := &fakeS3{objects: map[string][]byte{}}
    server := httptest.NewServer(s3)
    t.Cleanup(server.Close)
    s3.url = server.URL
    run := func(unit, token string, extra []string, args ...string) (string, error) {
        cmd := exec.Command("terragrunt", append(args, "--non-interactive", "--log-level", "error")...)
        cmd.Dir = filepath.Join(root, "infra/production", unit)
        cmd.Env = append(append(stateEnv(passphraseA, ""), "FAKE_TOKEN="+token, "HOMELAB_STATE_ENDPOINT="+server.URL,
            "HOMELAB_LAB="+filepath.Join(root, "bin/lab")), extra...)
        out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
        return string(out), err
    }
    return root, s3, run
}

// generated returns the contents of every file the unit's Terragrunt cache generated under that name
func generated(t *testing.T, root, unit, name string) string {
    matches, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(root, "infra/production", unit, ".terragrunt-cache", "*", "*", "*", name))
    require.NoError(t, err)
    var all strings.Builder
    for _, m := range matches {
        body, err := os.ReadFile(m)
        require.NoError(t, err)
        all.Write(body)
    }
    return all.String()
}

// cf refreshes its OAuth token: the generated backend and credentials config never carry it, so plan needs no init.
// Also proves production needs no .state/ directory.
func TestStateTokenRefresh(t *testing.T) {
    root, s3, run := prodTree(t)
    out, err := run("marker", "token-one", nil, "apply", "-auto-approve")
    require.NoError(t, err, out)
    assert.Equal(t, []string{"homelab-production-tfstate/marker/tfstate.json"}, prefixed(s3.keys(), "homelab-production-tfstate/"), "the state reached the fake bucket")

    backend := generated(t, root, "marker", "backend.tf")
    require.Contains(t, backend, `backend "s3"`)
    for _, file := range []string{"backend.tf", "r2-state.config"} {
        assert.NotContains(t, generated(t, root, "marker", file), "token-one", "%s carries the OAuth token", file)
    }

    out, err = run("marker", "token-two", nil, "plan", "-detailed-exitcode")
    require.NoError(t, err, "plan after a token refresh: %s", out)
    assert.Equal(t, backend, generated(t, root, "marker", "backend.tf"), "backend.tf changed with the token")
}

func prefixed(keys []string, prefix string) []string {
    var out []string
    for _, k := range keys {
        out = append(out, prefix+k)
    }
    return out
}

// The state lands encrypted, and a lock file is written and removed around each command
func TestStateS3Lock(t *testing.T) {
    _, s3, run := prodTree(t)
    out, err := run("marker", "token-one", nil, "apply", "-auto-approve")
    require.NoError(t, err, out)
    assert.Contains(t, s3.putKeys(), "marker/tfstate.json.tflock", "no lock file was written")
    assert.Equal(t, []string{"marker/tfstate.json"}, s3.keys(), "the lock file stayed")
    s3.mu.Lock()
    state := string(s3.objects["marker/tfstate.json"])
    s3.mu.Unlock()
    assert.Contains(t, state, "encrypted_data")
    assert.NotContains(t, state, "visible-marker")
}

// init runs lab infra state ensure with the account and bucket
func TestStateBucketEnsuredOnInit(t *testing.T) {
    root, _, run := prodTree(t)
    out, err := run("marker", "token-one", nil, "init")
    require.NoError(t, err, out)
    log, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, "bin/ensure.log"))
    require.NoError(t, err, "ensure did not run")
    assert.Contains(t, string(log), "--account-id acc-1 --bucket homelab-production-tfstate")
}

// A production unit never applied has no object: rotation must not push it, and it names the account it rotates in
func TestStateRotationSkipsMissingObjects(t *testing.T) {
    root, s3, run := prodTree(t)
    out, err := run("marker", "token-one", nil, "apply", "-auto-approve")
    require.NoError(t, err, out)

    cmd := exec.Command("sh", "scripts/rotate-state-passphrase", "production")
    cmd.Dir = root
    cmd.Env = append(stateEnv(passphraseB, passphraseA), "FAKE_TOKEN=token-one", "HOMELAB_STATE_ENDPOINT="+s3.url,
        "HOMELAB_LAB="+filepath.Join(root, "bin/lab"))
    rotated, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    require.NoError(t, err, string(rotated))
    assert.Contains(t, string(rotated), "acc-1")
    assert.Contains(t, string(rotated), "production/fresh: no state, skipped")
    assert.Equal(t, []string{"marker/tfstate.json"}, s3.keys(), "an empty state was pushed for the unit never applied")
}

In locals, replace state_api with:

Replace the production branch of generate "backend" and its comment:

# Production's state is on R2 through its S3 API (one object per unit, a lock file while a command runs), with
# expiring credentials from lab (r2-state.config); the sandbox's stays local. Both are encrypted (encryption.tf).
# Neither generated file holds a secret.
generate "backend" {
  path      = "backend.tf"
  if_exists = "overwrite_terragrunt"
  contents  = <<-EOF
    terraform {
    %{~if local.production}
      backend "s3" {
        bucket                      = "${local.state_bucket}"
        key                         = "${local.unit}/tfstate.json"
        region                      = "auto"
        endpoints                   = { s3 = "${local.state_endpoint}" }
        use_path_style              = true
        use_lockfile                = true
        profile                     = "r2-state"
        shared_config_files         = ["./r2-state.config"]
        skip_credentials_validation = true
        skip_region_validation      = true
        skip_requesting_account_id  = true
        skip_metadata_api_check     = true
        skip_s3_checksum            = true
      }
    %{~else}
      backend "local" {
        path = "${get_repo_root()}/.state/${path_relative_to_include()}/terraform.tfstate"
      }
    %{~endif}
    }
  EOF
}

generate "r2_credentials" {
  path      = "r2-state.config"
  if_exists = "overwrite_terragrunt"
  disable   = !local.production
  contents  = <<-EOF
    [profile r2-state]
    credential_process = ${local.lab} infra state credentials --account-id ${local.cloudflare.account_id} --bucket ${local.state_bucket}
  EOF
}

docs.title: Test Scopes Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: make dev runs only the sandbox tests a branch's changes can affect, chosen by lab test scope (the first command of a Go CLI in cli/) from test/scopes.yaml, with full and from-scratch runs kept for merges and releases.

Architecture: A Go package cli/internal/scope loads the map, turns changed files into go test -run regexes (main run and "alone" run) and checks that the map covers every component. A cobra command lab test scope wires it to git and prints one line. The root Makefile asks it for the two regexes and runs them as today; cli/Makefile holds the CLI's unit tests and the map check, both part of the basic checks.

Tech Stack: Go 1.26 (dev shell's go1.26.8), github.com/spf13/cobra v1.10.2, go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 v3.0.5, github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/v4 v4.10.3, POSIX make.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• CLI module github.com/duongle-steven/homelab/cli; upstream's layout: cli/cmd/lab/main.go, cli/internal/cli (cobra root lab, SilenceUsage, SilenceErrors, Execute), packages under cli/internal/<area>.
  • test/go.mod's module becomes github.com/duongle-steven/homelab/test.
  • Pinned versions: cobra v1.10.2, go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 v3.0.5, doublestar/v4 v4.10.3 (latest stable on 2026-10-18).
  • lab test scope prints exactly one line on stdout (possibly empty); sorted, deduplicated |-joined terms; errors go to stderr with a non-zero exit; never interactive.
  • The map lives in test/scopes.yaml; groups name tests, not components; an unknown file selects full.
  • make dev defaults: scope=auto, base=origin/dev; tests=<regex> overrides; an empty selection stops before the push; alone tests run after the main run.
  • The Makefile runs the CLI with go run ./cmd/lab from cli/ (no Nix packaging in this step).
  • Branches from dev, PR into dev; basic checks, then make dev.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A regex with a top-level alternation inside parentheses (TestIdentity(TOTP|PKCE)): splitting on | must keep the parenthesised group whole. Pinned in Task 1 (TestSplitTerms).
  2. A renamed or deleted file: both the old and the new path count (--no-renames), and a deleted test file selects nothing for itself instead of failing to parse. Pinned in Task 3 (TestCommandRenameCountsBothPaths) and Task 1 (TestFileTestsDeletedFile).
  3. A main-run term that also matches an alone test (a group naming Node would run TestNodeRestart alongside the others): --check must refuse it. Pinned in Task 2 (TestCheckMainTermPicksAloneTest).
  4. The branch is dev itself, or the base is missing: an empty diff prints nothing (the rule says to run scope=full after a merge); a missing base fails with the fix in the message. Pinned in Task 3 (TestCommandMissingBase, TestCommandNoChanges).
  5. Uncommitted changes: make dev already refuses them; the selector reads only committed changes (<base>...HEAD), which is what make dev pushes. Pinned in Task 3 (TestCommandIgnoresWorkingTree).

cli/internal/scope/scope_test.go:

package scope

import (
    "os"
    "path/filepath"
    "reflect"
    "strings"
    "testing"
)

func testConfig() Config {
    return Config{
        Skip:   []string{"docs/**", "**/*.md"},
        Always: "Smoke",
        Alone:  []string{"NodeRestart"},
        Full:   "Smoke|Identity|Logs|NodeRestart",
        Groups: []Group{
            {Paths: []string{"Makefile"}, Tests: FullKeyword},
            {Paths: []string{"system/loki/**"}, Tests: "Logs"},
            {Paths: []string{"system/istio-system/**"}, Tests: "Identity|NodeRestart"},
            {Paths: []string{"system/kured/**"}, Tests: ""},
        },
    }
}

func noTests(string) ([]string, error) { return nil, nil }

func selectRegex(t *testing.T, c Config, files []string, names TestNames) (string, string) {
    t.Helper()
    s, err := c.Select(files, names)
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }
    return c.Regex(s, false), c.Regex(s, true)
}

func TestSelect(t *testing.T) {
    c := testConfig()
    for _, tc := range []struct {
        name        string
        files       []string
        main, alone string
    }{
        {"only skipped", []string{"docs/a.md", "README.md"}, "", ""},
        {"one group", []string{"system/loki/values.yaml"}, "Logs|Smoke", ""},
        {"two groups", []string{"system/loki/values.yaml", "system/istio-system/values.yaml"}, "Identity|Logs|Smoke", "NodeRestart"},
        {"group without tests", []string{"system/kured/values.yaml"}, "Smoke", ""},
        {"unknown file", []string{"scripts/new"}, "Identity|Logs|Smoke", "NodeRestart"},
        {"full group", []string{"Makefile", "docs/a.md"}, "Identity|Logs|Smoke", "NodeRestart"},
        {"no changes", nil, "", ""},
    } {
        t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            main, alone := selectRegex(t, c, tc.files, noTests)
            if main != tc.main || alone != tc.alone {
                t.Errorf("got main %q alone %q, want %q %q", main, alone, tc.main, tc.alone)
            }
        })
    }
}

func TestSelectTestFile(t *testing.T) {
    names := func(file string) ([]string, error) {
        if file != "test/logs_test.go" {
            t.Fatalf("unexpected file %s", file)
        }
        return []string{"TestLogsPodLines", "TestLogsEvents"}, nil
    }
    main, alone := selectRegex(t, testConfig(), []string{"test/logs_test.go"}, names)
    if main != "Smoke|TestLogsEvents|TestLogsPodLines" || alone != "" {
        t.Errorf("got %q %q", main, alone)
    }
}

func TestSelectTestFileAlone(t *testing.T) {
    names := func(string) ([]string, error) { return []string{"TestNodeRestart", "TestNodeRestartBlockers"}, nil }
    main, alone := selectRegex(t, testConfig(), []string{"test/node_restart_test.go"}, names)
    if main != "Smoke" || alone != "TestNodeRestart|TestNodeRestartBlockers" {
        t.Errorf("got %q %q", main, alone)
    }
}

func TestManualSelection(t *testing.T) {
    c := testConfig()
    s := ManualSelection("Logs|NodeRestart")
    if got := c.Regex(s, false); got != "Logs" {
        t.Errorf("main %q: a manual regex adds no always", got)
    }
    if got := c.Regex(s, true); got != "NodeRestart" {
        t.Errorf("alone %q", got)
    }
}

func TestFullSelection(t *testing.T) {
    c := testConfig()
    s := Selection{Full: true}
    if got := c.Regex(s, false); got != "Identity|Logs|Smoke" {
        t.Errorf("main %q", got)
    }
    if got := c.Regex(s, true); got != "NodeRestart" {
        t.Errorf("alone %q", got)
    }
}

func TestSplitTerms(t *testing.T) {
    got := SplitTerms("Smoke|TestIdentity(TOTP|PKCE)|SSO")
    want := []string{"Smoke", "TestIdentity(TOTP|PKCE)", "SSO"}
    if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
        t.Errorf("got %q", got)
    }
    if SplitTerms("") != nil {
        t.Error("an empty regex has no terms")
    }
}

func writeFile(t *testing.T, dir, name, body string) string {
    t.Helper()
    path := filepath.Join(dir, name)
    if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }
    if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o644); err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }
    return path
}

func TestLoad(t *testing.T) {
    dir := t.TempDir()
    good := writeFile(t, dir, "good.yaml", `skip: ["docs/**"]
always: Smoke
alone: [NodeRestart]
full: Smoke|NodeRestart
groups:
  - paths: ["system/loki/**"]
    tests: Logs
components: ["system/*/"]
`)
    c, err := Load(good)
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }
    if c.Groups[0].Tests != "Logs" || c.Components[0] != "system/*/" {
        t.Errorf("loaded %+v", c)
    }
    for name, body := range map[string]string{
        "unknown key":   "full: Smoke\nunknown: 1\n",
        "no full":       "always: Smoke\n",
        "group no path": "full: Smoke\ngroups:\n  - tests: Logs\n",
        "bad regex":     "full: Smoke\ngroups:\n  - paths: [a]\n    tests: \"Logs(\"\n",
        "bad glob":      "full: Smoke\nskip: [\"docs/[\"]\n",
    } {
        _, err := Load(writeFile(t, dir, strings.ReplaceAll(name, " ", "-")+".yaml", body))
        if err == nil {
            t.Errorf("%s: loaded", name)
        }
    }
    if _, err := Load(filepath.Join(dir, "missing.yaml")); err == nil {
        t.Error("a missing file loaded")
    }
}

func TestFileTests(t *testing.T) {
    root := t.TempDir()
    writeFile(t, root, "test/logs_test.go", `package test

import "testing"

func TestLogsB(t *testing.T) {}
func TestLogsA(t *testing.T) {}
func helper() {}
`)
    names, err := FileTests(root)("test/logs_test.go")
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }
    if !reflect.DeepEqual(names, []string{"TestLogsB", "TestLogsA"}) {
        t.Errorf("got %q", names)
    }
    all, err := AllTests(root)
    if err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(all, []string{"TestLogsA", "TestLogsB"}) {
        t.Errorf("AllTests: %q %v", all, err)
    }
}

func TestFileTestsDeletedFile(t *testing.T) {
    names, err := FileTests(t.TempDir())("test/gone_test.go")
    if err != nil || names != nil {
        t.Errorf("a deleted test file: %q %v", names, err)
    }
}

// Package scope picks the sandbox tests a change can affect, from test/scopes.yaml.
package scope

import (
    "bytes"
    "fmt"
    "os"
    "regexp"
    "sort"
    "strings"

    "github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/v4"
    "go.yaml.in/yaml/v3"
)

// FullKeyword as a group's tests selects the whole suite.
const FullKeyword = "full"

// Config is test/scopes.yaml.
type Config struct {
    // Changes that run no sandbox test
    Skip []string `yaml:"skip"`
    // Tests added to every non-empty selection
    Always string `yaml:"always"`
    // Terms whose tests run after the others (they disturb the cluster)
    Alone []string `yaml:"alone"`
    // The whole suite, alone tests included
    Full   string  `yaml:"full"`
    Groups []Group `yaml:"groups"`
    // Globs of what the map must cover (a trailing slash names directories)
    Components []string `yaml:"components"`
}

// Group maps changed paths to tests: a regex of test names, "" (only Always) or FullKeyword.
type Group struct {
    Paths []string `yaml:"paths"`
    Tests string   `yaml:"tests"`
}

// Load reads and validates a map.
func Load(path string) (Config, error) {
    body, err := os.ReadFile(path)
    if err != nil {
        return Config{}, err
    }
    var c Config
    decoder := yaml.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(body))
    decoder.KnownFields(true)
    if err := decoder.Decode(&c); err != nil {
        return Config{}, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", path, err)
    }
    if c.Full == "" {
        return Config{}, fmt.Errorf("%s: full is empty", path)
    }
    globs := append(append([]string{}, c.Skip...), c.Components...)
    regexes := append([]string{c.Always, c.Full}, c.Alone...)
    for i, g := range c.Groups {
        if len(g.Paths) == 0 {
            return Config{}, fmt.Errorf("%s: group %d has no paths", path, i+1)
        }
        globs = append(globs, g.Paths...)
        if g.Tests != FullKeyword {
            regexes = append(regexes, g.Tests)
        }
    }
    for _, glob := range globs {
        if !doublestar.ValidatePattern(strings.TrimSuffix(glob, "/")) {
            return Config{}, fmt.Errorf("%s: invalid glob %q", path, glob)
        }
    }
    for _, r := range regexes {
        if _, err := regexp.Compile(r); err != nil {
            return Config{}, fmt.Errorf("%s: invalid regex %q: %w", path, r, err)
        }
    }
    return c, nil
}

// Selection is what a change runs: the whole suite (Full), or Terms plus Always when Any file was not skipped.
// A Manual selection (make dev tests=...) runs exactly its Terms.
type Selection struct {
    Full, Any, Manual bool
    Terms             []string
}

// TestNames lists the Test functions a changed test file defines (none for a deleted file).
type TestNames func(file string) ([]string, error)

// Select maps changed files (relative to the repository root) to a Selection: skipped files add nothing; a file in
// groups adds their tests; a test file in no group adds the tests it defines; any other file selects the whole suite.
func (c Config) Select(files []string, names TestNames) (Selection, error) {
    var s Selection
    for _, file := range files {
        if matchAny(c.Skip, file) {
            continue
        }
        s.Any = true
        matched := false
        for _, g := range c.Groups {
            if !matchAny(g.Paths, file) {
                continue
            }
            matched = true
            if g.Tests == FullKeyword {
                s.Full = true
            } else {
                s.Terms = append(s.Terms, SplitTerms(g.Tests)...)
            }
        }
        if matched {
            continue
        }
        if isTestFile(file) {
            defined, err := names(file)
            if err != nil {
                return Selection{}, err
            }
            s.Terms = append(s.Terms, defined...)
            continue
        }
        s.Full = true
    }
    return s, nil
}

// ManualSelection runs exactly the given regex.
func ManualSelection(regex string) Selection {
    return Selection{Any: true, Manual: true, Terms: SplitTerms(regex)}
}

// Regex returns the go test -run regex of the main run, or with alone set of the run after it; "" runs nothing.
func (c Config) Regex(s Selection, alone bool) string {
    var terms []string
    switch {
    case s.Full:
        terms = SplitTerms(c.Full)
    case s.Manual:
        terms = s.Terms
    case s.Any:
        terms = append(append([]string{}, s.Terms...), SplitTerms(c.Always)...)
    }
    seen := map[string]bool{}
    var out []string
    for _, term := range terms {
        if term == "" || seen[term] || c.isAlone(term) != alone {
            continue
        }
        seen[term] = true
        out = append(out, term)
    }
    sort.Strings(out)
    return strings.Join(out, "|")
}

// SplitTerms splits a regex on its top-level |, keeping parenthesised alternations whole.
func SplitTerms(regex string) []string {
    if regex == "" {
        return nil
    }
    var terms []string
    depth, start := 0, 0
    for i, r := range regex {
        switch r {
        case '(':
            depth++
        case ')':
            depth--
        case '|':
            if depth == 0 {
                terms = append(terms, regex[start:i])
                start = i + 1
            }
        }
    }
    return append(terms, regex[start:])
}

func (c Config) isAlone(term string) bool {
    for _, a := range c.Alone {
        if strings.Contains(term, a) {
            return true
        }
    }
    return false
}

func (c Config) known(file string) bool {
    if matchAny(c.Skip, file) || isTestFile(file) {
        return true
    }
    for _, g := range c.Groups {
        if matchAny(g.Paths, file) {
            return true
        }
    }
    return false
}

func matchAny(globs []string, file string) bool {
    for _, glob := range globs {
        if ok, _ := doublestar.Match(glob, file); ok {
            return true
        }
    }
    return false
}

func isTestFile(file string) bool {
    ok, _ := doublestar.Match("test/*_test.go", file)
    return ok
}

package scope

import (
    "errors"
    "go/ast"
    "go/parser"
    "go/token"
    "io/fs"
    "os"
    "path/filepath"
    "sort"
    "strings"
)

// FileTests reads a test file's Test functions with go/parser; a file that no longer exists defines none.
func FileTests(root string) TestNames {
    return func(file string) ([]string, error) {
        path := filepath.Join(root, file)
        if _, err := os.Stat(path); errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
            return nil, nil
        }
        parsed, err := parser.ParseFile(token.NewFileSet(), path, nil, parser.SkipObjectResolution)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        var names []string
        for _, decl := range parsed.Decls {
            if fn, ok := decl.(*ast.FuncDecl); ok && fn.Recv == nil && strings.HasPrefix(fn.Name.Name, "Test") {
                names = append(names, fn.Name.Name)
            }
        }
        return names, nil
    }
}

// AllTests lists every Test function in test/*_test.go, sorted.
func AllTests(root string) ([]string, error) {
    files, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(root, "test", "*_test.go"))
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    var all []string
    for _, path := range files {
        rel, err := filepath.Rel(root, path)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        names, err := FileTests(root)(filepath.ToSlash(rel))
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        all = append(all, names...)
    }
    sort.Strings(all)
    return all, nil
}

package scope

import (
    "reflect"
    "testing"
)

var checkTests = []string{"TestIdentityLogin", "TestLogsPodLines", "TestNodeRestart", "TestNodeRestartBlockers", "TestSmoke"}

func checkConfig() Config {
    c := testConfig()
    c.Components = []string{"system/*/", "apps/*.yaml"}
    return c

package scope

import (
    "fmt"
    "regexp"
    "sort"
    "strings"

    "github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/v4"
)

// Check lists what the map misses: components with a tracked file that no group or skip knows (it would run the
// whole suite), regexes that match no test, and main-run terms that would also pick an alone test.
func (c Config) Check(tracked, tests []string) []string {
    var problems []string
    uncovered := map[string]bool{}
    for _, file := range tracked {
        if component := c.component(file); component != "" && !c.known(file) {
            uncovered[component] = true
        }
    }
    for component := range uncovered {
        problems = append(problems, component+": in no group of test/scopes.yaml (add it to a group, or to skip)")
    }
    sort.Strings(problems)

    var aloneTests []string
    for _, test := range tests {
        if c.isAlone(test) {
            aloneTests = append(aloneTests, test)
        }
    }
    check := func(where, term string) {
        re := regexp.MustCompile(term) // Load validated it
        if !matchesAny(re, tests) {
            problems = append(problems, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %q matches no test", where, term))
            return
        }
        if c.isAlone(term) {
            return
        }
        for _, test := range aloneTests {
            if re.MatchString(test) {
                problems = append(problems, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %q would run alone test %s with the others", where, term, test))
                return
            }
        }
    }
    for _, term := range SplitTerms(c.Always) {
        check("always", term)
    }
    for _, term := range SplitTerms(c.Full) {
        check("full", term)
    }
    for _, term := range c.Alone {
        check("alone", term)
    }
    for i, g := range c.Groups {
        if g.Tests == FullKeyword {
            continue
        }
        for _, term := range SplitTerms(g.Tests) {
            check(fmt.Sprintf("group %d", i+1), term)
        }
    }
    return problems
}

// component names the component a tracked file belongs to ("" for none): the file itself for a file glob, the
// matching leading directories for a directory glob (trailing slash).
func (c Config) component(file string) string {
    parts := strings.Split(file, "/")
    for _, glob := range c.Components {
        if !strings.HasSuffix(glob, "/") {
            if ok, _ := doublestar.Match(glob, file); ok {
                return file
            }
            continue
        }
        dirGlob := strings.TrimSuffix(glob, "/")
        depth := strings.Count(dirGlob, "/") + 1
        if len(parts) <= depth {
            continue
        }
        dir := strings.Join(parts[:depth], "/")
        if ok, _ := doublestar.Match(dirGlob, dir); ok {
            return dir
        }
    }
    return ""
}

func matchesAny(re *regexp.Regexp, names []string) bool {
    for _, name := range names {
        if re.MatchString(name) {
            return true
        }
    }
    return false
}

package cli

import (
    "bytes"
    "os"
    "os/exec"
    "path/filepath"
    "strings"
    "testing"
)

const testMap = `skip: ["docs/**"]
always: Smoke
alone: [NodeRestart]
full: Smoke|Logs|NodeRestart
groups:
  - paths: ["system/loki/**"]
    tests: Logs
components: ["system/*/"]
`

// repo makes a git repository with test/scopes.yaml and a test file on branch dev, then a branch feature.
func repo(t *testing.T) string {
    t.Helper()
    dir := t.TempDir()
    run := func(args ...string) {
        t.Helper()
        cmd := exec.Command("git", args...)
        cmd.Dir = dir
        cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=t", "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=t@t", "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=t", "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=t@t")
        if out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
            t.Fatalf("git %v: %v\n%s", args, err, out)
        }
    }
    write(t, dir, "test/scopes.yaml", testMap)
    write(t, dir, "test/logs_test.go", "package test\n\nimport \"testing\"\n\nfunc TestLogsPodLines(t *testing.T) {}\nfunc TestSmoke(t *testing.T) {}\nfunc TestNodeRestart(t *testing.T) {}\n")
    write(t, dir, "system/loki/values.yaml", "a: 1\n")
    run("init", "-q", "-b", "dev")
    run("add", ".")
    run("commit", "-q", "-m", "base")
    run("checkout", "-q", "-b", "feature")
    t.Chdir(dir)
    return dir
}

func write(t *testing.T, dir, name, body string) {
    t.Helper()
    path := filepath.Join(dir, name)
    if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }
    if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o644); err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }
}

func commit(t *testing.T, dir string, args ...string) {
    t.Helper()
    for _, a := range [][]string{append([]string{"add", "-A"}, args...), {"commit", "-q", "-m", "change"}} {
        cmd := exec.Command("git", a...)
        cmd.Dir = dir
        cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=t", "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=t@t", "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=t", "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=t@t")
        if out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
            t.Fatalf("git %v: %v\n%s", a, err, out)
        }
    }
}

func lab(t *testing.T, args ...string) (string, error) {
    t.Helper()
    var out, errOut bytes.Buffer
    cmd := newRootCmd()
    cmd.SetArgs(append([]string{"test", "scope"}, args...))
    cmd.SetOut(&out)
    cmd.SetErr(&errOut)
    err := cmd.Execute()
    return out.String() + errOut.String(), err
}

func TestCommandSelects(t *testing.T) {
    dir := repo(t)
    write(t, dir, "system/loki/values.yaml", "a: 2\n")
    commit(t, dir)
    out, err := lab(t, "--base", "dev")
    if err != nil || out != "Logs|Smoke\n" {
        t.Errorf("got %q %v", out, err)
    }
    out, err = lab(t, "--base", "dev", "--alone")
    if err != nil || out != "\n" {
        t.Errorf("alone: got %q %v", out, err)
    }
}

func TestCommandNoChanges(t *testing.T) {
    repo(t)
    out, err := lab(t, "--base", "dev")
    if err != nil || out != "\n" {
        t.Errorf("got %q %v", out, err)
    }
}

func TestCommandFullAndManual(t *testing.T) {
    repo(t)
    for _, tc := range []struct {
        args []string
        want string
    }{
        {[]string{"--full"}, "Logs|Smoke\n"},
        {[]string{"--full", "--alone"}, "NodeRestart\n"},
        {[]string{"--tests", "Logs|NodeRestart"}, "Logs\n"},
        {[]string{"--tests", "Logs|NodeRestart", "--alone"}, "NodeRestart\n"},
    } {
        out, err := lab(t, tc.args...)
        if err != nil || out != tc.want {
            t.Errorf("%v: got %q %v", tc.args, out, err)
        }
    }
}

func TestCommandMissingBase(t *testing.T) {
    repo(t)
    out, err := lab(t, "--base", "origin/dev")
    if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "git fetch origin dev") {
        t.Errorf("got %q %v", out, err)
    }
}

func TestCommandRenameCountsBothPaths(t *testing.T) {
    dir := repo(t)
    if err := os.Rename(filepath.Join(dir, "system/loki"), filepath.Join(dir, "system/logs")); err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }
    commit(t, dir)
    out, err := lab(t, "--base", "dev")
    // system/logs is unknown (full), system/loki is the Logs group: the union is the whole suite
    if err != nil || out != "Logs|Smoke\n" {
        t.Errorf("got %q %v", out, err)
    }
    out, _ = lab(t, "--base", "dev", "--alone")
    if out != "NodeRestart\n" {
        t.Errorf("alone: got %q, a rename into an unknown path runs everything", out)
    }
}

func TestCommandIgnoresWorkingTree(t *testing.T) {
    dir := repo(t)
    write(t, dir, "system/loki/values.yaml", "uncommitted: true\n")
    out, err := lab(t, "--base", "dev")
    if err != nil || out != "\n" {
        t.Errorf("got %q %v: only committed changes count", out, err)
    }
}

func TestCommandCheck(t *testing.T) {
    dir := repo(t)
    if out, err := lab(t, "--check"); err != nil {
        t.Errorf("clean map: %q %v", out, err)
    }
    write(t, dir, "system/newthing/values.yaml", "a: 1\n")
    commit(t, dir)
    out, err := lab(t, "--check")
    if err == nil || !strings.Contains(out, "system/newthing: in no group") {
        t.Errorf("got %q %v", out, err)
    }
}

func TestCommandInvalidMap(t *testing.T) {
    dir := repo(t)
    write(t, dir, "test/scopes.yaml", "full: Smoke\nunknown: 1\n")
    commit(t, dir)
    if out, err := lab(t, "--base", "dev"); err == nil {
        t.Errorf("an invalid map loaded: %q", out)
    }
}

package scope

import (
    "fmt"
    "os/exec"
    "strings"
)

// Root is the repository's top directory.
func Root() (string, error) {
    out, err := git("", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel")
    return strings.TrimSpace(out), err
}

// Changed lists the files the commits since base change, old and new paths of renames included. Uncommitted changes
// do not count: make dev tests the commit at HEAD.
func Changed(root, base string) ([]string, error) {
    if _, err := git(root, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", base+"^{commit}"); err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("base %s does not exist: git fetch origin dev, or make dev scope=full", base)
    }
    out, err := git(root, "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", base+"...HEAD")
    return lines(out), err
}

// Tracked lists the repository's tracked files.
func Tracked(root string) ([]string, error) {
    out, err := git(root, "ls-files")
    return lines(out), err
}

func git(dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
    cmd := exec.Command("git", args...)
    cmd.Dir = dir
    out, err := cmd.Output()
    if err != nil {
        if exit, ok := err.(*exec.ExitError); ok {
            return "", fmt.Errorf("git %s: %w: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), err, strings.TrimSpace(string(exit.Stderr)))
        }
        return "", fmt.Errorf("git %s: %w", strings.Join(args, " "), err)
    }
    return string(out), nil
}

func lines(out string) []string {
    var files []string
    for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
        if line != "" {
            files = append(files, line)
        }
    }
    return files
}

// Package cli is the lab command (upstream nixos's CLI layout; its other commands come in a later step).
package cli

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "os"
    "os/signal"
    "syscall"

    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
)

func newRootCmd() *cobra.Command {
    root := &cobra.Command{
        Use:           "lab",
        Short:         "Homelab tools",
        Example:       "  lab test scope --base origin/dev",
        SilenceUsage:  true,
        SilenceErrors: true,
    }
    root.AddCommand(newTestCmd())
    return root
}

// Execute runs the lab CLI and exits on failure.
func Execute() {
    ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
    defer stop()
    if err := newRootCmd().ExecuteContext(ctx); err != nil {
        // A diagnostic-write failure cannot change the already-failed exit status.
        _, _ = fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "Error:", err)
        os.Exit(1)
    }
}

package cli

import (
    "fmt"
    "path/filepath"

    "github.com/spf13/cobra"

    "github.com/duongle-steven/homelab/cli/internal/scope"
)

func newTestCmd() *cobra.Command {
    test := &cobra.Command{Use: "test", Short: "Choose and check the sandbox tests"}
    test.AddCommand(newTestScopeCmd())
    return test
}

func newTestScopeCmd() *cobra.Command {
    var base, tests, config string
    var alone, full, check bool
    cmd := &cobra.Command{
        Use:   "scope",
        Short: "Print the go test -run regex of the sandbox tests a change can affect",
        Long: "Reads test/scopes.yaml and the files changed since --base, and prints one line: the regex of the main run, " +
            "or with --alone of the tests that run after it; nothing when every change is skipped. --check verifies " +
            "that the map covers every component and names existing tests.",
        Args: cobra.NoArgs,
        RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
            root, err := scope.Root()
            if err != nil {
                return err
            }
            if !filepath.IsAbs(config) {
                config = filepath.Join(root, config)
            }
            c, err := scope.Load(config)
            if err != nil {
                return err
            }
            if check {
                tracked, err := scope.Tracked(root)
                if err != nil {
                    return err
                }
                names, err := scope.AllTests(root)
                if err != nil {
                    return err
                }
                problems := c.Check(tracked, names)
                for _, p := range problems {
                    fmt.Fprintln(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), p)
                }
                if len(problems) > 0 {
                    return fmt.Errorf("test/scopes.yaml: %d problem(s)", len(problems))
                }
                return nil
            }
            var s scope.Selection
            switch {
            case tests != "":
                s = scope.ManualSelection(tests)
            case full:
                s = scope.Selection{Full: true}
            default:
                files, err := scope.Changed(root, base)
                if err != nil {
                    return err
                }
                if s, err = c.Select(files, scope.FileTests(root)); err != nil {
                    return err
                }
            }
            fmt.Fprintln(cmd.OutOrStdout(), c.Regex(s, alone))
            return nil
        },
    }
    flags := cmd.Flags()
    flags.StringVar(&base, "base", "origin/dev", "compare HEAD with this ref (merge base)")
    flags.BoolVar(&alone, "alone", false, "print the tests that run alone, after the main run")
    flags.BoolVar(&full, "full", false, "the whole suite")
    flags.StringVar(&tests, "tests", "", "exactly these tests (a go test -run regex)")
    flags.BoolVar(&check, "check", false, "verify the map instead of printing a selection")
    flags.StringVar(&config, "config", "test/scopes.yaml", "the map, relative to the repository root")
    cmd.MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive("full", "tests", "check")
    return cmd
}

package scope

import (
    "path/filepath"
    "strings"
    "testing"
)

// The repository's own map selects what the spec's table says
func TestRepositoryMap(t *testing.T) {
    root, err := filepath.Abs("../../..")
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }
    c, err := Load(filepath.Join(root, "test", "scopes.yaml"))
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }
    full := "Egress|Forgejo|Gateway|Identity|Logs|Mesh|Monitoring|Ntfy|SSO|Secrets|Smoke"
    for _, tc := range []struct {
        file, main, alone string
    }{
        {"docs/index.md", "", ""},
        {"CLAUDE.md", "", ""},
        {"system/loki/values.yaml", "Logs|Smoke", ""},
        {"system/istio-system/values.yaml", "Egress|Gateway|Identity|Mesh|Smoke", "NodeRestart"},
        {"infra/root.hcl", "Identity|Ntfy|SSO|Secrets|Smoke", ""},
        {"platform/forgejo/values.yaml", "Forgejo|GatewayForgejoSSH|SSOForgejo|Smoke", ""},
        {"apps/paperless.yaml", "SSOPaperless|Smoke", ""},
        {"apps/blog.yaml", "Smoke", ""},
        {"system/kured/values.yaml", "Smoke", ""},
        {"test/state_rotation_test.go", "", ""},
        {"Makefile", full, "NodeRestart"},
        {"scripts/something-new", full, "NodeRestart"},
    } {
        s, err := c.Select([]string{tc.file}, FileTests(root))
        if err != nil {
            t.Fatal(err)
        }
        if main, alone := c.Regex(s, false), c.Regex(s, true); main != tc.main || alone != tc.alone {
            t.Errorf("%s: got %q %q, want %q %q", tc.file, main, alone, tc.main, tc.alone)
        }
    }
    s, err := c.Select([]string{"test/logs_test.go"}, FileTests(root))
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }
    if main := c.Regex(s, false); !strings.Contains(main, "TestLogsPodLines") || !strings.Contains(main, "Smoke") {
        t.Errorf("test/logs_test.go: %q", main)
    }
}

docs.text:
Files: - Modify: Makefile:1-20

Interfaces: - Consumes: lab test scope flags (Task 3), test/scopes.yaml (Task 4). - Produces: make dev [scope=auto|full] [base=<ref>] [tests=<regex>], make dev-fresh.

  • Step 1: Record the sandbox branch before the dry runs

Run: git ls-remote origin sandbox | cut -c1-12 Expected: the commit make dev last pushed (note it).

  • Step 2: Rewrite the dev target

Replace the variables block and the dev target in Makefile with:

env ?= production
KUBECONFIG = $(shell pwd)/infra/$(env)/kubeconfig.yaml
KUBE_CONFIG_PATH = $(KUBECONFIG)
smoke_filter ?= Smoke
terragrunt_apply = terragrunt run --all apply --non-interactive -- -auto-approve
# make dev: the sandbox tests the branch's changes can affect (test/scopes.yaml), or scope=full, or tests=<regex>
scope ?= auto
base ?= origin/dev
tests ?=
lab = cd cli && go run ./cmd/lab test scope

default: metal infra smoke-test clean

# The sandbox syncs GitHub branch sandbox (system/argocd/values-dev.yaml): test the commit you are on
dev:
    @if [ -n "$(tests)" ]; then sel="--tests '$(tests)'"; \
    elif [ "$(scope)" = full ]; then sel=--full; \
    else git fetch -q origin dev && sel="--base $(base)"; fi; \
    main=$$(eval "$(lab) $$sel") && alone=$$(eval "$(lab) $$sel --alone") || exit 1; \
    if [ -z "$$main$$alone" ]; then echo "make dev: nothing to test in the sandbox (every change is in test/scopes.yaml's skip)"; exit 0; fi; \
    echo "make dev: main run '$$main', then alone '$$alone'"; \
    $(MAKE) sandbox-push && \
    (cd infra/sandbox && $(terragrunt_apply)) && \
    if [ -n "$$main" ]; then $(MAKE) env=sandbox ENV=dev INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY=1 smoke_filter="$$main" sandbox-refresh smoke-test; fi && \
    if [ -n "$$alone" ]; then $(MAKE) env=sandbox ENV=dev INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY=1 smoke_filter="$$alone" smoke-test; fi

# From scratch, the whole suite: before a dev → master PR and a release
dev-fresh:
    $(MAKE) dev-clean
    $(MAKE) dev scope=full

The alone run keeps today's comment: add # Alone tests (TestNodeRestart restarts the node) run after the others above the last if line.

  • Step 3: Dry-run a skipped change

Run (a throwaway branch, deleted afterwards):

# Sandbox tests

`make dev` builds or updates the sandbox and runs the tests the branch's changes can affect.

| Command | Runs |
|---|---|
| `make dev` | The tests `test/scopes.yaml` maps the branch's changes to (`git diff origin/dev...HEAD`), plus `Smoke`; nothing when every change is skipped (docs and the like); the whole suite when a file is in no entry |
| `make dev scope=full` | The whole suite on the existing sandbox: after merging into `dev` |
| `make dev-fresh` | `make dev-clean`, then the whole suite on a new sandbox: before a `dev` → `master` PR or a release |
| `make dev tests='Logs\|Secrets'` | Exactly those tests (a `go test -run` regex) |

`TestNodeRestart` restarts the node, so it always runs alone, after the others.

To see what a branch would run without running it:

```sh
cd cli && go run ./cmd/lab test scope            # the main run
cd cli && go run ./cmd/lab test scope --alone    # what runs alone afterwards

docs.title: Step 10a: GitHub Actions Basic Checks Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Pull requests into dev and master run the basic checks on GitHub Actions in the Nix dev shell and report one status, checks, which a repository ruleset requires.

Architecture: scripts/ci-check <check>|all holds every basic check's command (CI and the workstation call the same script); lab test charts names the charts a diff touches; scripts/lint gathers yamllint, shellcheck and actionlint. .github/workflows/checks.yaml runs scripts/ci-check once per check in a matrix inside nix develop, and a final job checks sums the matrix. .github/rulesets/protect-dev-master.json is applied with gh api.

Tech Stack: GitHub Actions (actions/checkout v7.0.1, cachix/install-nix-action v31.11.2, nix-community/cache-nix-action v7.0.2), Nix flakes, Go 1.26 (cobra), actionlint 1.7.12, yamllint, shellcheck, gh.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-19-ci-checks-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Branch feat/ci-checks from dev (worktree /home/nixos/homelab-ci); never commit to dev or master.
  • Actions pinned by full commit SHA, version in a comment: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1, cachix/install-nix-action@448cde739abec1eaf0646249e3d25bb8d9bc7702 # v31.11.2, nix-community/cache-nix-action@7df957e333c1e5da7721f60227dbba6d06080569 # v7.0.2.
  • permissions: contents: read; no ${{ }} expression inside a run: script (pass values through env:).
  • One required status: the job checks. The ruleset is applied only after the workflow passed once, and every gh api call that changes GitHub settings waits for the user's approval.
  • Tool versions come only from flake.nix.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A push that creates a branch (github.event.before is forty zeros): lab test charts must render every chart, not fail on an unknown base. Pinned in Task 1 (TestChartsZeroBaseRendersAll).
  2. A deleted chart or app file in the diff: it must be skipped, not rendered (render-chart would fail). Pinned in Task 1 (TestChartsSkipsDeleted).
  3. A pull request from a fork: read-only token, no cache save; the checks still run. Pinned by the workflow's permissions and by not depending on secrets (Task 3, actionlint and review).
  4. Script injection: a branch name or PR title must never reach a shell unquoted; values reach run: only through env:. Pinned in Task 3 (a grep step: no ${{ inside run: blocks).
  5. A cancelled matrix job (newer push): checks must report failure for that run, not success. Pinned in Task 3 (checks tests needs.check.result == success, which is cancelled then).

package scope

import (
    "os"
    "path"
    "path/filepath"
    "sort"
    "strings"

    "github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/v4"
)

// chartRoots hold wrapper charts (a directory with Chart.yaml) and, under apps/, app files
var chartRoots = []string{"system", "platform", "apps"}

// Changes to these render every chart: they feed every render (scripts/render-chart, the values it passes, the apps
// ApplicationSet's app-template pin in system/argocd)
var renderAll = []string{"scripts/render-chart", "scripts/env-values", "infra/*/cluster/config.json", "system/argocd/values*.yaml"}

// Charts lists the render targets (chart directories and apps/<name>.yaml) the changed files touch, or all of them;
// targets that no longer exist are left out.
func Charts(root string, files []string, all bool) ([]string, error) {
    targets := map[string]bool{}
    for _, f := range files {
        for _, pattern := range renderAll {
            if ok, _ := doublestar.Match(pattern, f); ok {
                all = true
            }
        }
    }
    if all {
        return allCharts(root)
    }
    for _, f := range files {
        if t := target(root, f); t != "" {
            targets[t] = true
        }
    }
    return sorted(targets), nil
}

// target is the chart directory or app file a path belongs to, "" when none exists
func target(root, f string) string {
    if path.Dir(f) == "apps" && strings.HasSuffix(f, ".yaml") {
        if exists(filepath.Join(root, f)) {
            return f
        }
        return ""
    }
    for dir := path.Dir(f); strings.Contains(dir, "/"); dir = path.Dir(dir) {
        if exists(filepath.Join(root, dir, "Chart.yaml")) {
            if top := strings.SplitN(dir, "/", 2)[0]; contains(chartRoots, top) {
                return dir
            }
            return ""
        }
    }
    return ""
}

func allCharts(root string) ([]string, error) {
    targets := map[string]bool{}
    for _, top := range chartRoots {
        charts, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(root, top, "*", "Chart.yaml"))
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        for _, c := range charts {
            rel, err := filepath.Rel(root, filepath.Dir(c))
            if err != nil {
                return nil, err
            }
            targets[filepath.ToSlash(rel)] = true
        }
    }
    apps, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(root, "apps", "*.yaml"))
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    for _, a := range apps {
        targets["apps/"+filepath.Base(a)] = true
    }
    return sorted(targets), nil
}

func exists(p string) bool {
    _, err := os.Stat(p)
    return err == nil
}

func contains(list []string, s string) bool {
    for _, l := range list {
        if l == s {
            return true
        }
    }
    return false
}

func sorted(set map[string]bool) []string {
    out := []string{}
    for k := range set {
        out = append(out, k)
    }
    sort.Strings(out)
    return out
}

#!/bin/sh
# The basic checks, one per name, as GitHub Actions runs them (.github/workflows/checks.yaml) and as the workstation
# runs them before a commit (scripts/ci-check all). Run in the dev shell (nix develop). render renders the charts
# changed since $BASE (default origin/dev; lab test charts).
set -eu
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
offline_tests='TestSmokeAppsForEnv|TestIdentity(TOTPWaitsForNextStep|PKCE)|TestGatewayRouteReady|TestGatewayNodeAddressFromInspect|TestNodeRestart(Blockers|WatchdogJobs)|TestIstioCNIWatchdog|TestState'
checks='render go cli infra docs mesh env-config secret-stores lint'

check() {
    case "$1" in
        render)
            targets=$(go -C cli run ./cmd/lab test charts --base "${BASE:-origin/dev}")
            for t in $targets; do
                echo "render $t"
                scripts/render-chart "$t" >/dev/null
                scripts/render-chart "$t" dev >/dev/null
            done ;;
        go) (cd test && go vet ./... && go test -run "$offline_tests" ./...) ;;
        cli) make -C cli test check ;;
        infra) env -u HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE make -C infra check ;;
        docs) mkdocs build --strict ;;
        mesh) scripts/check-mesh-policies ;;
        env-config) scripts/check-env-config ;;
        secret-stores) scripts/check-secret-stores ;;
        lint) scripts/lint ;;
        *) echo "ci-check: unknown check $1 (one of: $checks, all)" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
}

if [ "${1:?usage: ci-check <check>|all}" = all ]; then
    for c in $checks; do echo "== $c"; check "$c"; done
else
    check "$1"
fi

# The basic checks (scripts/ci-check) on every pull request into dev or master and every push to them, in the Nix dev
# shell. The ruleset (.github/rulesets/protect-dev-master.json) requires the job "checks".
name: checks

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [dev, master]
  push:
    branches: [dev, master]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  # A newer push to a pull request replaces its run; runs on dev and master always finish
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  check:
    name: ${{ matrix.check }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        check: [render, go, cli, infra, docs, mesh, env-config, secret-stores, lint]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # lab test charts diffs against the base
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: cachix/install-nix-action@448cde739abec1eaf0646249e3d25bb8d9bc7702 # v31.11.2
      - uses: nix-community/cache-nix-action@7df957e333c1e5da7721f60227dbba6d06080569 # v7.0.2
        with:
          primary-key: nix-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('flake.nix', 'flake.lock') }}
          restore-prefixes-first-match: nix-${{ runner.os }}-
          gc-max-store-size-linux: 8G
      - name: scripts/ci-check ${{ matrix.check }}
        env:
          CHECK: ${{ matrix.check }}
          # The pull request's base, or the previous commit of a push (forty zeros for a new branch: lab renders all)
          BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
        run: nix develop --command scripts/ci-check "$CHECK"

  # The one required status: fails unless every check succeeded (a cancelled or skipped check fails it too)
  checks:
    if: always()
    needs: check
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - name: every check succeeded
        env:
          RESULT: ${{ needs.check.result }}
        run: test "$RESULT" = success

# Continuous integration

Every pull request into `dev` or `master`, and every push to them, runs the basic checks on GitHub Actions
(`.github/workflows/checks.yaml`), in the same Nix dev shell as the workstation.

| Job | Command |
|---|---|
| `render`, `go`, `cli`, `infra`, `docs`, `mesh`, `env-config`, `secret-stores`, `lint` | `scripts/ci-check <job>` |
| `checks` | succeeds only when every job above did: the one status the ruleset requires |

Run them all locally before a commit (the basic checks), in the dev shell:

```sh
scripts/ci-check all
```

`render` renders the charts the branch changes (`cd cli && go run ./cmd/lab test charts` lists them).

## A failed run

Open the failed job in the pull request's checks: its last step is the `scripts/ci-check` command, which reproduces
locally. A newer push cancels the older run of a pull request, which then shows as cancelled.

## Protected branches

The ruleset `protect-dev-master` (`.github/rulesets/protect-dev-master.json`): changes reach `dev` and `master` only
through pull requests whose `checks` passed (no approval needed), never by a direct push, a force-push or a deletion.
Repository admins may merge a pull request whose checks failed (`gh pr merge --admin`), for a GitHub Actions outage
only: run `scripts/ci-check all` first. Branch `sandbox` is not protected (`make dev` force-pushes it).

```sh
# Create it (once)
gh api --method POST 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets' --input .github/rulesets/protect-dev-master.json
# Its ID
id=$(gh api 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets' --jq '.[] | select(.name == "protect-dev-master") | .id')
# Update it after editing the file
gh api --method PUT "repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets/$id" --input .github/rulesets/protect-dev-master.json
# Show it, and the rules a branch gets
gh api "repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets/$id"
gh api 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/dev'
# Remove it
gh api --method DELETE "repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets/$id"
```

`gh` fills `{owner}/{repo}` from the repository you are in.

## Adding a check

Add a case to `scripts/ci-check` and its name to the `checks` list there and to the workflow's matrix.

docs.text:
Files: none in git (GitHub settings), unless a run shows a mistake in the ruleset file.

  • Step 1: Ask the user (stop): applying the ruleset changes GitHub settings. Show the file and the command.

  • Step 2: Apply and read it back

Run: gh api --method POST 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets' --input .github/rulesets/protect-dev-master.json --jq '.id, .enforcement'; gh api 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/dev' --jq '.[].type' Expected: an ID and active; the types deletion, non_fast_forward, pull_request, required_status_checks.

  • Step 3: A direct push is refused

Run: git push --dry-run origin HEAD:dev 2>&1 | tail -2 is not enough (dry runs skip rules); instead push an empty commit to a scratch ref: git commit --allow-empty -m "test: ruleset" && git push origin HEAD:dev 2>&1 | grep -iE 'rule|refus|GH013' ; git reset --hard HEAD~1 Expected: GitHub refuses (GH013: Repository rule violations); dev is unchanged (git ls-remote origin dev equals origin/dev).

  • Step 4: A failing check blocks a pull request
git switch -c test/ruleset-block origin/dev
printf 'key: [unclosed\n' > ruleset-probe.yaml
git add ruleset-probe.yaml && git commit -m "test: a failing check (lint) to prove the ruleset blocks"
git push -u origin test/ruleset-block
gh pr create --draft --base dev --title "test: ruleset blocks a failing check" --body "Throwaway: proves protect-dev-master blocks a pull request whose checks fail. Closed without merging."
gh pr checks --watch --interval 30; gh pr view --json mergeStateStatus --jq .mergeStateStatus
gh pr close --delete-branch
git switch feat/ci-checks && git branch -D test/ruleset-block

Expected: lint fails, checks fails, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED; the pull request is closed and its branch gone.

docs.title: Step 10b: The Sandbox on GitHub Actions Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: GitHub Actions builds a fresh sandbox and runs the suite on pushes to dev, on pull requests labelled sandbox, and on demand, testing a commit Argo CD is told about at bootstrap.

Architecture: Argo CD stops managing itself (upstream nixos's model): infra/_modules/argocd alone applies system/argocd, rewriting the homelab repository's revisions to a chosen one (set-revision.sh); the CRD-gated templates move to system/argocd-config, which Argo CD syncs. make dev revision=<sha> tests that commit without pushing branch sandbox; .github/workflows/sandbox.yaml calls it.

Tech Stack: Argo CD ApplicationSets, Helm, yq, OpenTofu/Terragrunt, k3d, GitHub Actions, Go tests.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-19-ci-sandbox-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Branch feat/ci-sandbox from dev, in the main checkout /home/nixos/homelab (never make dev from a worktree).
  • Actions pinned by SHA as in checks.yaml (actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1, cachix/install-nix-action@448cde739abec1eaf0646249e3d25bb8d9bc7702 # v31.11.2, nix-community/cache-nix-action@7df957e333c1e5da7721f60227dbba6d06080569 # v7.0.2); actions/upload-artifact at its latest release, pinned the same way (look it up: gh api repos/actions/upload-artifact/releases/latest).
  • permissions: contents: read; no ${{ }} inside run:.
  • Without a revision, the bootstrap's output is unchanged.
  • The sandbox needs no secret; the state passphrase is random per run.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. The migration on an existing cluster: removing system/argocd from root makes the ApplicationSet delete Application argocd, whose resources-finalizer would delete Argo CD itself. Pinned in Task 2 (the bootstrap drops that finalizer first; make dev on the existing sandbox, then Argo CD still runs).
  2. Revisions of other repositories: app-template's targetRevision (a chart version) and the seed placeholder must not change. Pinned in Task 1 (TestArgoCDRevision).
  3. A fork's head SHA: reachable only through refs/pull/<n>/head. Pinned in Task 5 (dispatch with such a SHA).
  4. Nothing to test on a push: the job must succeed fast without building the sandbox. Pinned in Task 4 (the workflow's scope step) and Task 5 (a docs-only push after merge, or the dispatch with a docs-only range).
  5. Ports on the runner: the k3d module's localhost proxy refuses busy ports 80/443/22. Pinned in Task 3 (HOMELAB_SANDBOX_PROXY=0 skips it; the tests dial the node).

docs.title: Task 1: set-revision.sh and its offline test
docs.text:
Files: - Create: infra/_modules/argocd/set-revision.sh, test/argocd_revision_test.go - Modify: scripts/ci-check (offline test list gains TestArgoCDRevision)

Interfaces: - Produces: sh infra/_modules/argocd/set-revision.sh <revision> reads rendered manifests on stdin, writes them on stdout; with an empty revision it copies stdin unchanged. The repository is the root ApplicationSet's first git generator's repoURL.

  • Step 1: Write the failing test (test/argocd_revision_test.go)
package test

import (
    "os/exec"
    "strings"
    "testing"

    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// render renders system/argocd for the sandbox the way the bootstrap does, through set-revision.sh
func renderArgoCD(t *testing.T, revision string) string {
    t.Helper()
    cmd := exec.Command("sh", "-c", `scripts/render-chart system/argocd dev | sh infra/_modules/argocd/set-revision.sh "$0"`, revision)
    cmd.Dir = ".."
    out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    require.NoError(t, err, string(out))
    return string(out)
}

// The bootstrap points every source and generator of the homelab repository at the chosen commit, and nothing else
func TestArgoCDRevision(t *testing.T) {
    plain := renderArgoCD(t, "")
    require.Contains(t, plain, "revision: sandbox")
    pinned := renderArgoCD(t, "abc123")
    assert.NotContains(t, pinned, "revision: sandbox")
    assert.NotContains(t, pinned, "targetRevision: sandbox")
    assert.Contains(t, pinned, "revision: abc123")
    assert.Contains(t, pinned, "targetRevision: abc123")
    // app-template's chart version is another repository's revision
    for _, line := range strings.Split(plain, "\n") {
        if strings.Contains(line, "targetRevision:") && !strings.Contains(line, "sandbox") {
            assert.Contains(t, pinned, line, "a revision of another repository changed")
        }
    }
    assert.Equal(t, strings.Count(plain, "sandbox"), strings.Count(pinned, "abc123")+strings.Count(pinned, "sandbox"),
        "every homelab revision was rewritten, and only those")
}
  • Step 2: Run it to see it fail

Run: direnv exec . env -C test go test -run TestArgoCDRevision ./... 2>&1 | grep -E -- '--- |^(ok|FAIL)|No such file' | head -3 Expected: FAIL (set-revision.sh: No such file).

  • Step 3: Write infra/_modules/argocd/set-revision.sh
#!/bin/sh
# Point every source and generator of the homelab repository in rendered Argo CD manifests (stdin) at one revision
# (stdout): the sandbox on GitHub Actions tests a commit without pushing branch sandbox. The repository is the root
# ApplicationSet's first git generator's; other repositories (app-template's chart) keep theirs. No revision: unchanged.
set -eu
revision=${1:-}
if [ -z "$revision" ]; then
    exec cat
fi
manifests=$(cat)
repo=$(printf '%s\n' "$manifests" | yq 'select(.kind == "ApplicationSet" and .metadata.name == "root") | .spec.generators[0].matrix.generators[0].git.repoURL')
[ -n "$repo" ] && [ "$repo" != null ] || { echo "set-revision: no root ApplicationSet git generator" >&2; exit 1; }
printf '%s\n' "$manifests" | REPO="$repo" REVISION="$revision" yq '
  (.. | select(tag == "!!map" and .repoURL == strenv(REPO) and has("revision")) | .revision) = strenv(REVISION) |
  (.. | select(tag == "!!map" and .repoURL == strenv(REPO) and has("targetRevision")) | .targetRevision) = strenv(REVISION)'

In scripts/ci-check, append |TestArgoCDRevision inside offline_tests (after TestState).

  • Step 4: Run it

Run: direnv exec . env -C test go test -run TestArgoCDRevision -v ./... 2>&1 | grep -E -- '--- |^(ok|FAIL)'; direnv exec . scripts/lint; echo lint=$? Expected: PASS; lint=0.

  • Step 5: Commit
git add infra/_modules/argocd/set-revision.sh test/argocd_revision_test.go scripts/ci-check
git commit -m "feat(infra): set-revision.sh points the homelab repository's Argo CD sources at one revision"

docs.text:
Files: - Create: system/argocd-config/Chart.yaml, system/argocd-config/values.yaml; move system/argocd/templates/kanidm-client.yaml and forgejo-repository.yaml there (git mv) - Modify: system/argocd/values.yaml, values-dev.yaml, values-seed.yaml (root generator: system/argocd → system/argocd-config), infra/_modules/argocd/main.tf (variable revision; one resource; triggers), infra/_modules/argocd/bootstrap.sh (finalizer migration; set-revision.sh), infra/sandbox/argocd/terragrunt.hcl (revision), infra/production/argocd/terragrunt.hcl (drop protect), test/scopes.yaml (system/argocd-config/** in full), scripts/render-chart comment if it names the moved templates

Interfaces: - Consumes: set-revision.sh <revision> (Task 1). - Produces: module variable revision (string, default ""); env HOMELAB_SANDBOX_REVISION read by the sandbox unit.

  • Step 1: Read what the moved templates need

Run: head -20 system/argocd/templates/kanidm-client.yaml system/argocd/templates/forgejo-repository.yaml; grep -n 'Values' system/argocd/templates/kanidm-client.yaml system/argocd/templates/forgejo-repository.yaml Expected: the values they read (e.g. global.baseDomain, Argo CD's host). Copy exactly those keys into system/argocd-config/values.yaml (with the same defaults as system/argocd/values.yaml) so the templates render unchanged; record each in the ledger.

  • Step 2: Create the chart and move the templates
# system/argocd-config/Chart.yaml
apiVersion: v2
name: argocd-config
description: Argo CD's resources that need other components' CRDs (its Kanidm client, the Forgejo repository credential); Argo CD syncs them, infra/_modules/argocd bootstraps Argo CD itself
version: 0.0.0

git mv system/argocd/templates/kanidm-client.yaml system/argocd/templates/forgejo-repository.yaml system/argocd-config/templates/

In the three values files, replace - path: system/argocd in the root generator's directories with - path: system/argocd-config. Its Application deploys into namespace argocd (the root template's destination is the directory's base name: check values.yaml's template; if it is {{ .path.basename }}, add an argocd-config → argocd rule the same way other components set their namespace, or set the destination in a templatePatch; ledger the choice).

  • Step 3: Render and check

Run: direnv exec . sh -c 'for e in "" dev; do scripts/render-chart system/argocd-config $e | grep -c "^kind:"; scripts/render-chart system/argocd $e | grep -cE "KanidmOAuth2Client|name: argocd-repo-forgejo"; done; scripts/check-env-config >/dev/null && echo env=0; scripts/check-mesh-policies >/dev/null && echo mesh=0; scripts/check-secret-stores >/dev/null && echo stores=0' Expected: 2 and 0 for both environments; env=0, mesh=0, stores=0.

  • Step 4: The module and bootstrap

infra/_modules/argocd/main.tf: add

variable "revision" {
  type        = string
  default     = ""
  description = "Commit or branch every homelab source and generator syncs (set-revision.sh); empty keeps the values file's"
}

pass REVISION = var.revision in local.environment, add var.revision to triggers_replace, and replace the two resources by one (Argo CD no longer manages itself, so every environment re-applies on change):

# Re-applied whenever the chart's files, the values, the revision or the cluster change: Argo CD does not manage
# itself (upstream nixos's model). It has no destroy-time action: destroying it leaves Argo CD running.
resource "terraform_data" "bootstrap" {
  triggers_replace = [local.hash, var.values, var.seed, var.cluster_id, var.revision]

  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command     = local.command
    environment = local.environment
  }
}

Remove variable "protect" and the header's "every later change reaches the cluster through Argo CD's own sync"; rewrite the header: "Apply Argo CD from the repository's system/argocd chart, again whenever its files, the values, the revision or the cluster change; Argo CD syncs everything else (system/argocd-config among it), not itself." Production state holds terraform_data.protected[0]: add moved { from = terraform_data.protected[0] to = terraform_data.bootstrap } and moved { from = terraform_data.bootstrap[0] to = terraform_data.bootstrap } so neither environment re-runs only because of the rename.

(Ruling recorded here: prevent_destroy cannot coexist with re-applying, which replaces the resource; the resource has no destroy-time action, so the guard protected nothing in the cluster. It goes.)

bootstrap.sh: after the helm template … > "$manifests" line, add

# The sandbox on GitHub Actions syncs one commit (REVISION) instead of branch sandbox
sh "$(dirname "$0")/set-revision.sh" "${REVISION:-}" < "$manifests" > "$manifests.rev" && mv "$manifests.rev" "$manifests"

and before the first apply call:

# Argo CD no longer manages itself: the root ApplicationSet drops Application argocd, whose resources finalizer
# would delete Argo CD with it. Release it first (a no-op on a new cluster).
if kubectl -n argocd get application argocd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    kubectl -n argocd patch application argocd --type merge -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":null}}' >/dev/null
fi

Update the script's header comment ("apply it once; Argo CD manages itself from then on" → "apply it; Argo CD does not manage itself"). bootstrap.sh is called as sh <path>: $0 is that path. trap also removes "$manifests.rev".

infra/sandbox/argocd/terragrunt.hcl inputs: revision = get_env("HOMELAB_SANDBOX_REVISION", ""). infra/production/argocd/terragrunt.hcl: remove protect = true; replace its comment with "Re-applied when system/argocd changes; the first run after Forgejo runs switches from the seed to ops/homelab".

test/scopes.yaml: add - system/argocd-config/** next to - system/argocd/** in full.

Run: direnv exec . scripts/ci-check all > <scratchpad>/ci-10b.log 2>&1; echo all=$? then commit (Step 6), then direnv exec . make dev > <scratchpad>/dev-10b.log 2>&1; echo dev=$?; grep -aE '^make dev:|^DONE|PASS TestNodeRestart |--- FAIL' <scratchpad>/dev-10b.log | tail -5; KUBECONFIG=infra/sandbox/kubeconfig.yaml direnv exec . kubectl -n argocd get applications argocd argocd-config --no-headers 2>&1 | cut -c1-80; KUBECONFIG=infra/sandbox/kubeconfig.yaml direnv exec . kubectl -n argocd get deploy argocd-server -o name Expected: all=0; dev=0, 123 tests and TestNodeRestart pass; Application argocd NotFound, argocd-config Synced Healthy; deployment.apps/argocd-server exists (the finalizer migration kept Argo CD).
