    sync := &cobra.Command{
        Use:   "sync",
        Short: "Provision org ops on Forgejo: ops/homelab, deploy and argocd, master's protection, their tokens in OpenBao",
        Long:  "Idempotent: what is right is kept, what is wrong is fixed, what is missing is created. Waits up to 30 minutes for Forgejo. No secret is printed.",
        Args:  cobra.NoArgs,
        RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
            e, err := forgejoEnv(cmd)
            if err != nil {
                return err
            }
            ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(cmd.Context(), 35*time.Minute)
            defer cancel()
            s, err := openSession(ctx, e)
            if err != nil {
                return err
            }
            defer func() { _ = s.close(context.Background()) }()
            admin, err := s.kube.CoreV1().Secrets("forgejo").Get(ctx, "forgejo-admin", metav1.GetOptions{})
            if err != nil {
                return fmt.Errorf("forgejo/forgejo-admin: %w", err)
            }
            syncCtx, syncCancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 30*time.Minute)
            defer syncCancel()
            if err := forgejo.Sync(syncCtx, s.ep, string(admin.Data["password"]), s.store); err != nil {
                return err
            }
            argocd, err := s.store.Read(ctx, forgejo.ArgoCDPath)
            if err != nil {
                return err
            }
            if err := refreshArgoCDCredential(ctx, s.kube, s.dyn, argocd["token"], 5*time.Minute); err != nil {
                return err
            }
            _, err = fmt.Fprintln(cmd.OutOrStdout(), "Forgejo's org ops is in sync.")
            return err
        },
    }
    push := &cobra.Command{
        Use:   "push",
        Short: "Deploy: push HEAD to ops/homelab's master as deploy",
        Long:  "Production: only after verify's guards pass, never forced (roll back with a revert through a pull request). Sandbox: a commit with HEAD's tree on top of what the sandbox's Forgejo holds.",
        Args:  cobra.NoArgs,
        RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
            e, err := forgejoEnv(cmd)
            if err != nil {
                return err
            }
            var commit string
            if e.Name == "production" {
                if commit, err = verifyProduction(cmd.Context(), e); err != nil {
                    return err
                }
            }
            ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(cmd.Context(), 5*time.Minute)
            defer cancel()
            s, err := openSession(ctx, e)
            if err != nil {
                return err
            }
            defer func() { _ = s.close(context.Background()) }()
            deploy, err := s.store.Read(ctx, forgejo.DeployPath)
            if err != nil {
                return err
            }
            if deploy["token"] == "" {
                return fmt.Errorf("no deploy token in OpenBao (secret/%s): run lab infra forgejo sync first", forgejo.DeployPath)
            }
            if commit == "" {
                if commit, err = forgejo.SandboxCommit(ctx, s.ep, e.Root, deploy["token"]); err != nil {
                    return err
                }
            }
            deployed, err := forgejo.Deployed(ctx, s.ep, e.Root, deploy["token"])
            if err != nil {
                return err
            }
            if deployed == commit {
                _, err = fmt.Fprintf(cmd.OutOrStdout(), "ops/homelab's master already is %.12s: nothing to push.\n", commit)
                return err
            }
            if err := forgejo.Push(ctx, s.ep, e.Root, deploy["token"], commit); err != nil {
                return err
            }
            _, err = fmt.Fprintf(cmd.OutOrStdout(), "Deployed %.12s to ops/homelab.\n", commit)
            return err
        },
    }
    group.AddCommand(sync, push)

Replace TestArgoCDChooseValues in test/ci_scripts_test.go:

// choose-values.sh picks the values file the Argo CD bootstrap applies: the seed on a first install until Argo CD's
// own credential reads ops/homelab's master (Forgejo runs, lab synced the token and pushed), never again once Argo CD
// reads Forgejo, and never because the cluster could not be asked
func TestArgoCDChooseValues(t *testing.T) {
    const forgejo = "http://forgejo-http.forgejo:3000/ops/homelab"
    const seedValues = `{"values":"values-seed.yaml","environment":"seed"}`
    const forgejoValues = `{"values":"values-dev.yaml","environment":"dev"}`
    for _, c := range []struct {
        name, seed, rootRepo, token, master, want string
        kubectlFails, execFails, fails           bool
    }{
        {name: "sandbox: no seed", want: forgejoValues, kubectlFails: true},
        {name: "first install, no credential yet", seed: "values-seed.yaml", want: seedValues},
        {name: "credential, nothing pushed", seed: "values-seed.yaml", token: "t1", want: seedValues},
        {name: "credential reads master: switch", seed: "values-seed.yaml", rootRepo: "https://github.com/example/homelab", token: "t1", master: "t1", want: forgejoValues},
        {name: "wrong credential", seed: "values-seed.yaml", token: "t1", master: "t2", want: seedValues},
        // Review Focus 5: the Secret exists but Forgejo's pod is down
        {name: "Forgejo down", seed: "values-seed.yaml", token: "t1", master: "t1", execFails: true, want: seedValues},
        {name: "switched, Forgejo down: stay", seed: "values-seed.yaml", rootRepo: forgejo, execFails: true, want: forgejoValues},
        {name: "cluster unreachable", seed: "values-seed.yaml", kubectlFails: true, fails: true},
    } {
        t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            kubectl := `case "$*" in
  *applicationset*) echo "$ROOT_REPO" ;;
  *"get secret argocd-repo-forgejo"*) [ -z "$TOKEN" ] || printf '%s' "$TOKEN" | base64 ;;
  *exec*) [ -z "$EXEC_FAILS" ] || exit 1; [ "$(cat)" = "$MASTER" ] && [ -n "$MASTER" ] ;;
  *) echo "unexpected kubectl $*" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac`
            if c.kubectlFails {
                kubectl = `echo "unable to connect" >&2; exit 1`
            }
            _, env := fakeBin(t, map[string]string{"kubectl": kubectl})
            cmd := exec.Command("sh", "../infra/_modules/argocd/choose-values.sh")
            cmd.Env = append(env, "ROOT_REPO="+c.rootRepo, "TOKEN="+c.token, "MASTER="+c.master)
            if c.execFails {
                cmd.Env = append(cmd.Env, "EXEC_FAILS=1")
            }
            cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(`{"values":"values-dev.yaml","environment":"dev","seed":"` + c.seed + `","forgejo_repository":"` + forgejo + `","kubeconfig":"/dev/null"}`)
            out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
            if c.fails {
                require.Error(t, err, string(out))
                return
            }
            require.NoError(t, err, string(out))
            assert.JSONEq(t, c.want, string(out))
        })
    }
}

// make infra env=production deploys in one command: the guards, the infrastructure, Forgejo's org ops, the push, then
// the Argo CD bootstrap again (the switch to Forgejo on a first install); force=1 applies the infrastructure only
func TestMakeInfraProduction(t *testing.T) {
    stubs := map[string]string{
        "lab":        `echo "lab $*" >> "$FIXTURES/calls"; [ "$*" != "infra forgejo verify" ] || [ -z "$VERIFY_FAILS" ]`,
        "terragrunt": `echo "terragrunt $(basename "$PWD") $*" >> "$FIXTURES/calls"`,
        "go":         `exit 0`,
    }
    for _, c := range []struct {
        name string
        vars []string
        env  []string
        want []string
    }{
        {"deploy", nil, nil, []string{
            "lab infra forgejo verify",
            "terragrunt production run --all apply --non-interactive -- -auto-approve",
            "lab infra forgejo sync",
            "lab infra forgejo push",
            "terragrunt argocd apply --non-interactive -- -auto-approve",
        }},
        {"force=1", []string{"force=1"}, nil, []string{
            "terragrunt production run --all apply --non-interactive -- -auto-approve",
        }},
        {"guards fail", nil, []string{"VERIFY_FAILS=1"}, []string{"lab infra forgejo verify"}},
    } {
        t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            dir, env := fakeBin(t, stubs)
            args := append([]string{"-s", "-C", "..", "infra", "env=production", "lab_cli=" + filepath.Join(dir, "lab"), "terragrunt=" + filepath.Join(dir, "terragrunt")}, c.vars...)

# Every unit of infra/<env>: Argo CD's bootstrap, OpenBao's key, OpenTofu's secrets (the sandbox's run in make dev).
# Production deploys in the same command: the guards (origin/master, checks, the merged pull request's sandbox), the
# infrastructure, Forgejo's org ops, the push of this commit to ops/homelab, then the bootstrap again (the switch to
# Forgejo on a first install). force=1 applies the infrastructure only and deploys nothing (a state migration).
# Building lab first keeps a cold Go build out of credential_process, which the AWS SDK times out after a minute.
infra:
    @if [ "$(env)" = sandbox ]; then $(MAKE) -s sandbox-checkout; fi
    go -C cli build -o /dev/null ./cmd/lab
    @if [ "$(env)" = production ] && [ "$(force)" != 1 ]; then $(lab_cli) infra forgejo verify; fi
    cd infra/$(env) && $(terragrunt_apply)
    @if [ "$(env)" = production ] && [ "$(force)" != 1 ]; then \
        $(lab_cli) infra forgejo sync && $(lab_cli) infra forgejo push && \
        (cd infra/production/argocd && $(terragrunt) apply --non-interactive -- -auto-approve); \
    fi

Interfaces: - Consumes: lab infra forgejo sync|push --env sandbox (Task 4); the cluster side (Task 5).

  • Step 1: Write the sandbox tests
// test/forgejo_test.go
package test

import (
    "net/http"
    "os"
    "os/exec"
    "path/filepath"
    "strings"
    "testing"

    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// lab runs the CLI from cli/ (as the Makefile does) and returns its combined output.
func lab(t *testing.T, args ...string) string {
    t.Helper()
    cmd := exec.Command("go", append([]string{"run", "./cmd/lab"}, args...)...)
    cmd.Dir = "../cli"
    out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    require.NoError(t, err, "lab %v:\n%s", args, out)
    return string(out)
}

// forgejoGit runs git against the sandbox's ops/homelab as user with secret (a token or a password), on the node
// and with the sandbox CA, and returns its output and error.
func forgejoGit(t *testing.T, dir, user, secret string, args ...string) (string, error) {
    t.Helper()
    ca := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "ca.crt")
    require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(ca, []byte(configMapValue(t, "forgejo", "homelab-dev-ca", "ca.crt")), 0o600))
    askpass := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "askpass")
    require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(askpass, []byte("#!/bin/sh\ncase \"$1\" in Username*) echo \"$GIT_USER\" ;; *) echo \"$GIT_SECRET\" ;; esac\n"), 0o700))
    full := append([]string{"-C", dir, "-c", "credential.helper=", "-c", "http.sslCAInfo=" + ca,
        "-c", "http.curloptResolve=" + forgejoHost + ":443:" + sandboxAddress(t)}, args...)
    cmd := exec.Command("git", full...)
    cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0", "GIT_ASKPASS="+askpass, "GIT_USER="+user, "GIT_SECRET="+secret,
        "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=t", "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=t@t", "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=t", "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=t@t")
    out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    return string(out), err
}

func baoValue(t *testing.T, path, property string) string {
    t.Helper()
    // The tests read OpenBao the documented way: an admin login inside OpenBao's pod, the token never printed
    script := "kubectl -n openbao create token openbao-admin --audience=openbao --duration=10m | kubectl -n openbao exec -i openbao-0 -c openbao -- " +
        "sh -c 'export BAO_TOKEN=$(bao write -field=token auth/kubernetes/login role=admin jwt=-); bao kv get -field=" + property + " secret/" + path + "; bao token revoke -self >/dev/null'"
    out, err := exec.Command("sh", "-c", script).Output()
    require.NoError(t, err)
    return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
}

// TestForgejoDeploy runs lab infra forgejo sync twice and push, as make infra env=production does, against the
// sandbox's Forgejo, then checks what production relies on.
func TestForgejoDeploy(t *testing.T) {
    if os.Getenv("ENV") != "dev" {
        t.Skip("Forgejo tests run against the sandbox only")
    }
    waitForApp(t, "https://"+forgejoHost+"/api/healthz")
    lab(t, "infra", "forgejo", "sync", "--env", "sandbox")
    deploy, argocd := baoValue(t, "forgejo/deploy", "token"), baoValue(t, "argocd/forgejo", "token")
    require.NotEmpty(t, deploy)
    require.NotEmpty(t, argocd)
    lab(t, "infra", "forgejo", "sync", "--env", "sandbox")
    assert.Equal(t, deploy, baoValue(t, "forgejo/deploy", "token"), "a second sync replaced deploy's token")
    assert.Equal(t, argocd, baoValue(t, "argocd/forgejo", "token"), "a second sync replaced argocd's token")

    lab(t, "infra", "forgejo", "push", "--env", "sandbox")
    assert.Contains(t, lab(t, "infra", "forgejo", "push", "--env", "sandbox"), "nothing to push")

    // Forgejo's master has the checkout's tree
    clone := t.TempDir()
    out, err := forgejoGit(t, clone, "argocd", argocd, "clone", "--quiet", "https://"+forgejoHost+"/ops/homelab.git", ".")
    require.NoError(t, err, out)
    tree, err := exec.Command("git", "-C", clone, "rev-parse", "HEAD^{tree}").Output()
    require.NoError(t, err)
    head, err := exec.Command("git", "rev-parse", "HEAD^{tree}").Output()
    require.NoError(t, err)
    assert.Equal(t, strings.TrimSpace(string(head)), strings.TrimSpace(string(tree)))

    // The protection: argocd reads but cannot push; deploy can neither force-push nor delete master
    _, err = forgejoGit(t, clone, "argocd", argocd, "commit", "--quiet", "--allow-empty", "-m", "argocd")
    require.NoError(t, err)
    out, err = forgejoGit(t, clone, "argocd", argocd, "push", "--quiet", "origin", "HEAD:refs/heads/master")
    assert.Error(t, err, "argocd pushed to master:\n%s", out)
    orphan, err := forgejoGit(t, clone, "deploy", deploy, "commit-tree", "HEAD^{tree}", "-m", "orphan")
    require.NoError(t, err)
    out, err = forgejoGit(t, clone, "deploy", deploy, "push", "--quiet", "--force", "origin", strings.TrimSpace(orphan)+":refs/heads/master")
    assert.Error(t, err, "deploy force-pushed master:\n%s", out)
    out, err = forgejoGit(t, clone, "deploy", deploy, "push", "--quiet", "origin", ":refs/heads/master")
    assert.Error(t, err, "deploy deleted master:\n%s", out)

    // Argo CD's credential reads master with the read-only token
    repoSecret := waitForSecret(t, "argocd", "argocd-repo-forgejo")
    assert.Equal(t, "argocd", string(repoSecret["username"]))
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, getJSON(t, "GET", "https://"+forgejoHost+"/api/v1/repos/ops/homelab/branches/master", nil,
        string(repoSecret["username"]), string(repoSecret["password"]), nil, nil))
}

If configMapValue does not exist in test/, add it next to secretValue (in test/sso_test.go, which defines secretValue):

func configMapValue(t *testing.T, namespace, name, key string) string {
    t.Helper()
    out, err := exec.Command("kubectl", "-n", namespace, "get", "configmap", name, "-o", "jsonpath={.data."+strings.ReplaceAll(key, ".", `\.`)+"}").Output()
    require.NoError(t, err)
    return string(out)
}

On the sandbox, as forgejo_admin (password from kubectl -n forgejo get secret forgejo-admin, through the askpass, never on the command line): clone ops/homelab, commit an empty commit, push it to a new branch admin-probe (allowed) and then try HEAD:refs/heads/master. Record the result in the PR body and the ledger. If it was accepted, master now holds the probe: push the same tree back with lab infra forgejo push --env sandbox (a sandbox commit on top, so the sandbox recovers) and delete branch admin-probe. The docs (Task 8) state the result.

docs.title: Step 10d: Renovate through our own GitHub App — Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Renovate in the production cluster opens pull requests into dev on GitHub as our own GitHub App, with a one-hour installation token from ESO and the App's key kept by OpenTofu.

Architecture: infra/_modules/kept-value keeps a value given once (the App's private key) in OpenTofu's state; infra/_modules/secrets publishes it as renovate/github-app through platform/infra-secrets into OpenBao. platform/renovate copies it into namespace renovate, an ESO GithubAccessToken generator mints the token every 30 minutes into renovate-secret, and the Renovate chart's CronJob runs at 05:00. renovate.json5 targets dev and labels its pull requests sandbox; sandbox.yaml cancels older dev runs.

Tech Stack: OpenTofu (builtin terraform_data), Terragrunt, Helm (Renovate chart 46.372.0, image 44.172.0), External Secrets 2.12 (generators.external-secrets.io/v1alpha1 GithubAccessToken), Go tests (testify), nixpkgs renovate (config validator), GitHub Actions.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-20-renovate-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Chart renovate 46.372.0 from https://docs.renovatebot.com/helm-charts (its image 44.172.0, the chart's default, pinned in values).
  • The token ExternalSecret: refreshPolicy: Periodic, refreshInterval: 30m; never CreatedOnce.
  • Generator permissions exactly: contents: write, pull_requests: write, workflows: write, issues: write, checks: read, statuses: read; repositories: [homelab].
  • OpenBao path renovate/github-app, property private-key; the key file comes from HOMELAB_GITHUB_APP_KEY (a path) only; never printed, never committed.
  • Renovate config: platform: github, autodiscover: true, autodiscoverFilter: ["duongle-steven/*"], onboarding: false, requireConfig: "required"; repository config baseBranches: ["dev"], labels: ["sandbox"], no automerge.
  • CronJob 0 5 * * *, time zone Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh (written in platform/renovate/values.yaml: the chart cannot read global.timezone; listed with kured in CLAUDE.md).
  • Renovate stays out of the sandbox's component list (system/argocd/values-dev.yaml).
  • Every task ends with direnv exec . scripts/ci-check all passing before its commit; commits end with the session's attribution lines.

docs.title: Rulings (where this plan refines the spec)
docs.text:
• The time zone is written in platform/renovate/values.yaml (spec: "in global.timezone"): the subchart's cronjob.timeZone cannot be templated from a global, like kured's; CLAUDE.md's list of settings outside config.json gains it.
  • The kept key is its own module, infra/_modules/kept-value (spec: "a terraform_data in infra/_modules/secrets"), so its behaviour is tested with tofu alone, offline. A value given while an empty one is stored (the unit applied before the App existed) fails with a message to apply with -replace, instead of being ignored silently.
  • The App's IDs and bot id exist only once the App does: Task 1 writes the how-to, then execution stops for the user to create and install the App and send the App ID, installation ID, slug and bot id (none is secret).

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A make infra env=production run before the App exists (no HOMELAB_GITHUB_APP_KEY): nothing about Renovate may fail the infrastructure apply — Task 2 tests an empty value.
  2. The key given after an empty value was stored: must fail loudly, never be dropped — Task 2 tests it.
  3. A rotated key given without -replace: must fail, not keep the old key silently — Task 2 tests it.
  4. The token ExternalSecret copied from global-secrets' style with CreatedOnce: Renovate would stop after an hour — Task 3's offline test pins Periodic.
  5. A manual workflow_dispatch of sandbox.yaml cancelling a dev run, or the reverse — Task 5 sets separate groups and checks them with yq.

docs.title: Task 1: the how-to, then the App (user)
docs.text:
Files: Create docs/how-to-guides/renovate.md; modify mkdocs.yml.

  • Step 1: Write the how-to
# Renovate

Renovate runs in the production cluster (`platform/renovate`, daily at 05:00) and opens pull requests into `dev` on
GitHub as the GitHub App `homelab-renovate`. Its pull requests run `checks` and, labelled `sandbox`, the sandbox.
The App's private key goes through OpenTofu into OpenBao; External Secrets mints a one-hour installation token from it
every 30 minutes (`renovate-secret`).

## Create the App (once)

1. GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → New GitHub App: name `homelab-renovate`, homepage the
   repository's URL, **Webhook: off**.
2. Repository permissions: Contents, Pull requests, Workflows, Issues (Renovate's Dependency Dashboard): **Read and
   write**; Commit statuses, Checks: **Read-only**; Metadata: Read-only (always). No organization or account
   permissions. "Only on this account".
3. Create it, note the **App ID**, then **Generate a private key** (a `.pem` downloads once).
4. Install App → your account → **Only select repositories** → `homelab`. The installation's URL ends with its
   **installation ID** (`.../settings/installations/<id>`).
5. The bot's user id, for Renovate's commit author: `gh api '/users/homelab-renovate[bot]' --jq .id`.

App ID, installation ID and bot id are not secrets: they live in `platform/renovate/values.yaml`.

## Give the key to production (once, and after a rotation)

```sh
HOMELAB_GITHUB_APP_KEY=~/Downloads/homelab-renovate.<date>.private-key.pem make infra env=production

OpenTofu keeps the key in its encrypted state (infra/production/secrets); later runs need no file, so delete it. If the unit was applied before the key existed, apply once with the key and -replace=module.github_app_key.terraform_data.kept in infra/production/secrets (terragrunt apply -replace=...); the plain run refuses rather than ignoring the key.

docs.title: Rotate the key
docs.text:
Generate a new key on the App's page, then in infra/production/secrets:

HOMELAB_GITHUB_APP_KEY=<new.pem> terragrunt apply -replace=module.github_app_key.terraform_data.kept

Delete the old key on GitHub once Renovate ran with the new one.

docs.title: Add a repository
docs.text:
Install the App on it (App → Configure → Repository access) and add a renovate.json5; the next run finds it (autodiscover, limited to duongle-steven/*). Renovate skips repositories without a config. 

Add `- how-to-guides/renovate.md` to `mkdocs.yml`'s how-to section, after `deploy-to-forgejo.md`.

- [ ] **Step 2: Build the docs, commit**

Run: `direnv exec . mkdocs build --strict --quiet` — Expected: exit 0.

```bash
git add docs/how-to-guides/renovate.md mkdocs.yml
git commit -m "docs: Renovate's GitHub App how-to"

  • Step 3: STOP — the user creates and installs the App

Ask the user to follow "Create the App" (steps 1–5), keep the .pem locally (never paste it), and send the App ID, installation ID and bot id. Ledger them as Task 1: App homelab-renovate: app_id <n>, installation_id <n>, bot id <n>.

docs.title: Task 2: the kept key (infra/_modules/kept-value) and its path to OpenBao
docs.text:
Files: Create infra/_modules/kept-value/main.tf, test/kept_value_test.go; modify infra/_modules/secrets/main.tf, infra/production/secrets/terragrunt.hcl, platform/infra-secrets/values.yaml, scripts/ci-check, test/scopes.yaml.

Interfaces: Produces module kept-value (variable value string sensitive default ""; output value sensitive); infra/_modules/secrets variable github_app_key (string, sensitive, default ""); OpenBao record renovate/github-app {private-key} only when a key is kept.

  • Step 1: Write the failing test
// test/kept_value_test.go
package test

import (
    "os"
    "os/exec"
    "path/filepath"
    "strings"
    "testing"

    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// kept-value keeps a value given once (the GitHub App's key) when later applies give none, refuses a different one
// without -replace, and takes it with -replace: the key file is needed only once
func TestKeptValue(t *testing.T) {
    module, err := filepath.Abs("../infra/_modules/kept-value")
    require.NoError(t, err)
    dir := t.TempDir()
    require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "main.tf"), []byte(`
variable "value" {
  type      = string
  default   = ""
  sensitive = true
}
module "kept" {
  source = "`+module+`"
  value  = var.value
}
output "value" {
  value     = nonsensitive(module.kept.value)
}
`), 0o644))
    tofu := func(args ...string) (string, error) {
        cmd := exec.Command("tofu", append([]string{"-chdir=" + dir}, args...)...)
        cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "TF_IN_AUTOMATION=1")
        out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
        return string(out), err
    }
    apply := func(value string, extra ...string) (string, error) {
        return tofu(append([]string{"apply", "-auto-approve", "-input=false", "-no-color", "-var", "value=" + value}, extra...)...)
    }
    output := func() string {
        out, err := tofu("output", "-raw", "value")
        require.NoError(t, err, out)
        return strings.TrimSpace(out)
    }
    out, err := tofu("init", "-input=false", "-no-color")
    require.NoError(t, err, out)

    out, err = apply("key-a")
    require.NoError(t, err, out)
    assert.Equal(t, "key-a", output())

    out, err = apply("")
    require.NoError(t, err, out)
    assert.Equal(t, "key-a", output(), "an empty value replaced the kept one")

    out, err = apply("key-b")
    assert.Error(t, err, "a different value was taken without -replace:\n%s", out)
    assert.Contains(t, out, "-replace")
    assert.Equal(t, "key-a", output())

    out, err = apply("key-b", "-replace=module.kept.terraform_data.kept")
    require.NoError(t, err, out)
    assert.Equal(t, "key-b", output())
}

// A unit applied before the value existed keeps an empty one: the value given later must fail loudly, not vanish
func TestKeptValueGivenAfterEmpty(t *testing.T) {
    module, err := filepath.Abs("../infra/_modules/kept-value")
    require.NoError(t, err)
    dir := t.TempDir()
    require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "main.tf"), []byte(`
variable "value" {
  type      = string
  default   = ""
  sensitive = true
}
module "kept" {
  source = "`+module+`"
  value  = var.value
}
`), 0o644))
    run := func(args ...string) (string, error) {
        out, err := exec.Command("tofu", append([]string{"-chdir=" + dir}, args...)...).CombinedOutput()
        return string(out), err
    }
    out, err := run("init", "-input=false", "-no-color")
    require.NoError(t, err, out)
    out, err = run("apply", "-auto-approve", "-input=false", "-no-color")
    require.NoError(t, err, out)
    out, err = run("apply", "-auto-approve", "-input=false", "-no-color", "-var", "value=key-a")
    assert.Error(t, err, "a value given after an empty one was ignored:\n%s", out)
    assert.Contains(t, out, "-replace")
}

Add TestKeptValue to offline_tests in scripts/ci-check (the regex TestKeptValue covers both) and test/kept_value_test.go to skip in test/scopes.yaml.

  • Step 2: Run it to see it fail

Run: direnv exec . sh -c 'cd test && go test -count=1 -run TestKeptValue ./...' Expected: FAIL (tofu init cannot find the module directory).

  • Step 3: Write the module
# infra/_modules/kept-value/main.tf
# A value given once (the GitHub App's private key) and kept in this unit's encrypted state: later applies may give
# none. A different value is refused until applied with -replace=<module>.terraform_data.kept, so a key is never
# dropped or swapped silently.
variable "value" {
  type      = string
  default   = ""
  sensitive = true
}

resource "terraform_data" "kept" {
  input = var.value

  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [input]
    postcondition {
      condition     = var.value == "" || var.value == self.output
      error_message = "A different value is kept: apply with -replace=<this module>.terraform_data.kept to take the new one."
    }
  }
}

output "value" {
  value     = terraform_data.kept.output
  sensitive = true
}
  • Step 4: Run the tests

Run: direnv exec . sh -c 'cd test && go test -count=1 -v -run TestKeptValue ./...' 2>&1 | grep -E -- '--- (PASS|FAIL)' Expected: both PASS. If OpenTofu evaluates the postcondition before self.output holds the new value on -replace, compare with self.input instead and rerun.

  • Step 5: Wire it into the secrets unit

In infra/_modules/secrets/main.tf, add after variable "protect":

variable "github_app_key" {
  type        = string
  default     = ""
  sensitive   = true
  description = "Renovate's GitHub App private key (production; docs/how-to-guides/renovate.md): given once, then kept"
}

module "github_app_key" {
  source = "../kept-value"
  value  = var.github_app_key
}

and in locals.secrets, merge the record only when a key is kept:

  secrets = merge(
    var.secrets,
    { "wireguard/private-key" = { "private-key" = wireguard_asymmetric_key.wireguard.private_key } },
    module.github_app_key.value == "" ? {} : { "renovate/github-app" = { "private-key" = module.github_app_key.value } },
  )

In infra/production/secrets/terragrunt.hcl inputs add:

  # Renovate's GitHub App key, only when given (docs/how-to-guides/renovate.md): the state keeps it
  github_app_key = get_env("HOMELAB_GITHUB_APP_KEY", "") == "" ? "" : file(get_env("HOMELAB_GITHUB_APP_KEY"))

In platform/infra-secrets/values.yaml (production list only; values-dev.yaml keeps its own list) add:

  - path: renovate/github-app
    properties: [private-key]
  • Step 6: Validate the units

Run: direnv exec . make -C infra check — Expected: exit 0 (fmt, validate). Run direnv exec . sh -c 'cd test && go test -count=1 -run "TestState" ./...' — Expected: ok (the sandbox's secrets unit is unchanged without a key).

  • Step 7: Basic checks, commit

Run direnv exec . scripts/ci-check all — Expected: exit 0.

git add infra/_modules/kept-value infra/_modules/secrets infra/production/secrets platform/infra-secrets test/kept_value_test.go scripts/ci-check test/scopes.yaml
git commit -m "feat(infra): the GitHub App's key, given once (HOMELAB_GITHUB_APP_KEY) and kept by OpenTofu, reaches OpenBao as renovate/github-app"

docs.title: Task 3: platform/renovate on GitHub
docs.text:
Files: Modify platform/renovate/Chart.yaml, platform/renovate/values.yaml, system/egress/values.yaml; delete platform/renovate/templates/secret.yaml; create platform/renovate/templates/github-app.yaml, test/renovate_test.go; modify scripts/ci-check, test/scopes.yaml.

Interfaces: Consumes the App's IDs (Task 1's ledger line) and OpenBao renovate/github-app (Task 2). Produces Secret renovate-secret (RENOVATE_TOKEN).

  • Step 1: Write the failing offline test
// test/renovate_test.go
package test

import (
    "os/exec"
    "strings"
    "testing"

    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func renderRenovate(t *testing.T, expr string) string {
    t.Helper()
    cmd := exec.Command("sh", "-c", `scripts/render-chart platform/renovate | yq -N "$0"`, expr)
    cmd.Dir = ".."
    out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    require.NoError(t, err, string(out))
    return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
}

// Renovate's token comes from our GitHub App, scoped to homelab and minted again every 30 minutes (never created
// once: it expires after an hour); its CronJob runs at 05:00 local time
func TestRenovateGitHubApp(t *testing.T) {
    assert.Equal(t, `{"checks":"read","contents":"write","issues":"write","pull_requests":"write","statuses":"read","workflows":"write"}`,
        renderRenovate(t, `select(.kind == "GithubAccessToken") | .spec.permissions | to_entries | sort_by(.key) | from_entries | to_json(0)`))
    assert.Equal(t, `["homelab"]`, renderRenovate(t, `select(.kind == "GithubAccessToken") | .spec.repositories | to_json(0)`))
    token := `select(.kind == "ExternalSecret" and .spec.target.name == "renovate-secret")`
    assert.Equal(t, "30m", renderRenovate(t, token+` | .spec.refreshInterval`))
    assert.Contains(t, []string{"Periodic", "null"}, renderRenovate(t, token+` | .spec.refreshPolicy`))
    assert.Equal(t, "GithubAccessToken", renderRenovate(t, token+` | .spec.dataFrom[0].sourceRef.generatorRef.kind`))
    assert.Equal(t, "0 5 * * *", renderRenovate(t, `select(.kind == "CronJob") | .spec.schedule`))
    assert.Equal(t, "Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh", renderRenovate(t, `select(.kind == "CronJob") | .spec.timeZone`))
    all := renderRenovate(t, `.`)
    assert.NotContains(t, all, "forgejo")
    assert.NotContains(t, all, "renovate/forgejo")
}

// Renovate runs in production only
func TestRenovateNotInTheSandbox(t *testing.T) {
    cmd := exec.Command("yq", `.. | select(has("path")) | .path`, "system/argocd/values-dev.yaml")
    cmd.Dir = ".."
    out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    require.NoError(t, err, string(out))
    assert.NotContains(t, string(out), "platform/renovate")
}

Add TestRenovate to offline_tests in scripts/ci-check; test/renovate_test.go to skip in test/scopes.yaml.

Run: direnv exec . sh -c 'cd test && go test -count=1 -run TestRenovate ./...' — Expected: FAIL (no GithubAccessToken; forgejo in the render).

  • Step 2: Chart and values

platform/renovate/Chart.yaml: dependency renovate version 46.372.0.

platform/renovate/values.yaml:

# Renovate on GitHub as our App homelab-renovate (docs/how-to-guides/renovate.md); production only. The IDs are not
# secrets: ESO's GithubAccessToken generator needs them as literals.
githubApp:
  appID: "<app_id from the ledger>"
  installationID: "<installation_id from the ledger>"
renovate:
  image:
    tag: 44.172.0
  cronjob:
    schedule: '0 5 * * *'
    # The chart cannot read global.timezone (like kured): keep it equal to config.json's timezone
    timeZone: Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh
    concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  renovate:
    config: |
      {
        "platform": "github",
        "autodiscover": true,
        "autodiscoverFilter": ["duongle-steven/*"],
        "onboarding": false,
        "requireConfig": "required",
        "gitAuthor": "homelab-renovate[bot] <<bot id from the ledger>+homelab-renovate[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>"
      }
  existingSecret: renovate-secret

(Replace the three placeholders with Task 1's numbers before running anything; never commit a placeholder.)

  • Step 3: The token's path

git rm platform/renovate/templates/secret.yaml and create platform/renovate/templates/github-app.yaml:

# The App's private key (OpenTofu → infra-secrets → OpenBao renovate/github-app) for ESO's generator
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: renovate-github-app
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
spec:
  secretStoreRef:
    kind: SecretStore
    name: openbao
  target:
    name: renovate-github-app
  data:
    - secretKey: private-key
      remoteRef:
        key: renovate/github-app
        property: private-key
---
apiVersion: generators.external-secrets.io/v1alpha1
kind: GithubAccessToken
metadata:
  name: renovate
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
spec:
  appID: {{ .Values.githubApp.appID | quote }}
  installID: {{ .Values.githubApp.installationID | quote }}
  # Narrower than the App: only what Renovate needs, only homelab
  repositories: [homelab]
  permissions:
    contents: write
    pull_requests: write
    workflows: write
    issues: write
    checks: read
    statuses: read
  auth:
    privateKey:
      secretRef:
        name: renovate-github-app
        key: private-key
---
# An installation token lives an hour: mint a new one every 30 minutes (Periodic; never CreatedOnce), so a run starts
# with at least 30 minutes left
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: {{ .Values.renovate.existingSecret }}
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
spec:
  refreshPolicy: Periodic
  refreshInterval: 30m
  target:
    name: {{ .Values.renovate.existingSecret }}
    template:
      engineVersion: v2
      data:
        RENOVATE_TOKEN: {{` "{{ .token }}" `}}
  dataFrom:
    - sourceRef:
        generatorRef:
          apiVersion: generators.external-secrets.io/v1alpha1
          kind: GithubAccessToken
          name: renovate

In system/egress/values.yaml: renovate: [{port: 443}].

  • Step 4: Run the tests and the checks

Run: direnv exec . sh -c 'cd test && go test -count=1 -run TestRenovate ./...' — Expected: ok. If the generator's output key is not token, read ESO's CRD/docs for GithubAccessToken's output and fix the template, not the test. Run direnv exec . sh -c 'scripts/check-env-config && scripts/check-secret-stores && scripts/check-mesh-policies' | tail -3 — Expected: 0 failures (check-env-config may need the Renovate time zone allowed like kured's: add it the same way, ledger the change).

  • Step 5: Basic checks, commit
git add -A platform/renovate system/egress test/renovate_test.go scripts/ci-check test/scopes.yaml
git commit -m "feat(renovate): GitHub through our App (ESO GithubAccessToken every 30m), chart 46.372.0, 05:00"

docs.title: Task 4: the repository config and its validator
docs.text:
Files: Rewrite renovate.json5; modify flake.nix, scripts/lint.

  • Step 1: Make the validator fail on today's config

In flake.nix's default dev shell packages, add renovate (alphabetical). In scripts/lint, add at the end:

# Renovate's repository config and the global one in platform/renovate (docs/how-to-guides/renovate.md)
renovate-config-validator --strict renovate.json5
global=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
trap 'rm -f "$global"' EXIT
yq '.renovate.renovate.config' platform/renovate/values.yaml > "$global"
RENOVATE_CONFIG_FILE="$global" renovate-config-validator --strict

Run: direnv exec . scripts/lint — Expected: FAIL on renovate.json5 with --strict (config:base and matchPackagePatterns are deprecated and need migrating).

  • Step 2: Rewrite the config
// Renovate (platform/renovate, docs/how-to-guides/renovate.md): pull requests into dev, labelled sandbox so the
// sandbox runs before a merge; nothing merges automatically
{
  $schema: 'https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json',
  extends: ['config:recommended'],
  baseBranches: ['dev'],
  labels: ['sandbox'],
  lockFileMaintenance: {
    enabled: true,
    schedule: ['before 5am on monday'],
  },
  packageRules: [
    {
      matchUpdateTypes: ['minor', 'patch'],
      groupName: 'all non-major dependencies',
      groupSlug: 'all-minor-patch',
    },
  ],
}

Run: direnv exec . scripts/lint — Expected: exit 0. If the nixpkgs validator (44.79) rejects an option the image (44.172) accepts, ledger it and drop --strict for that file only.

  • Step 3: Basic checks, commit
git add renovate.json5 flake.nix flake.lock scripts/lint
git commit -m "feat: renovate.json5 targets dev and labels sandbox (config:recommended); the validator in scripts/lint"

docs.title: Task 5: only the newest dev is tested in full
docs.text:
Files: Modify .github/workflows/sandbox.yaml.

  • Step 1: The concurrency groups

Replace sandbox.yaml's concurrency block with:

concurrency:
  # A push to dev cancels the run of an older push (the newest dev covers it; test an older commit with revision);
  # a manual run gets a group of its own, so neither cancels the other
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' }}
  • Step 2: Check the groups (Review Focus 5)

Run: yq '.concurrency' .github/workflows/sandbox.yaml && direnv exec . scripts/lint — Expected: the block above; actionlint passes. docs.title: Generated Secrets Straight to OpenBao Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Generated secrets go from ESO's Password generators straight to OpenBao through PushSecrets, with no intermediate Secret, in a component renamed platform/generated-secrets; tests and docs read OpenBao.

Architecture: Each entry of platform/generated-secrets/values.yaml renders a Password generator and a PushSecret whose selector.generatorRef names it (IfNotExists, one data item per destination). OpenBao's role writer is bound to namespace generated-secrets. Tests read generated values with the admin role (baoValue).

Tech Stack: External Secrets 2.12 (PushSecret generatorRef), OpenBao, Helm, Go tests (test/), Python check (scripts/check-secret-stores).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-21-generated-secrets-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Component platform/generated-secrets, namespace generated-secrets; no ExternalSecret and no Secret in it.
  • PushSecret: selector.generatorRef (apiVersion: generators.external-secrets.io/v1alpha1, kind: Password), updatePolicy: IfNotExists, deletionPolicy: None, refreshInterval: 1h, SecretStore openbao-writer; each destination one data item with match.secretKey: password, remoteRef.remoteKey: <destination>, remoteRef.property: <entry key>.
  • values.yaml's format is unchanged (name, key, length, special, destinations, extraSecrets).
  • No cross-namespace read in OpenBao's policy; a value two namespaces need is two destinations of one entry.
  • Never print a secret: tests compare hashes or values in memory.
  • Basic checks: direnv exec . scripts/ci-check all; commit, then make dev from the main checkout only.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A PushSecret reconciled again (hourly, force-sync, ESO restart) must leave every existing destination unchanged — Task 2's sandbox test force-syncs twice and compares hashes.
  2. Both destinations of ntfy.alerts-token must hold the same value after a fresh install — Task 2 compares them.
  3. A destination deleted from OpenBao (a rotation) must be written again at the next push — Task 2 deletes one probe entry's destination and force-syncs.
  4. The existing local sandbox (role writer bound to global-secrets in OpenBao's storage) cannot push from the new namespace — Task 4 rebuilds it with make dev-fresh, and the docs say so.
  5. A Password entry with special: true keeps its symbols and length — Task 1's offline test checks the generator spec per entry.

Interfaces: - Produces: namespace generated-secrets; per entry a Password <name> and a PushSecret <name>.

  • Step 1: Write the failing offline test (test/generated_secrets_test.go)
package test

import (
    "encoding/json"
    "os/exec"
    "testing"

    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

type generatedEntry struct {
    Name         string   `json:"name"`
    Key          string   `json:"key"`
    Length       int      `json:"length"`
    Special      bool     `json:"special"`
    Destinations []string `json:"destinations"`
}

func renderGenerated(t *testing.T, env, expr string) string {
    t.Helper()
    cmd := exec.Command("sh", "-c", `scripts/render-chart platform/generated-secrets "$1" | yq -N -o=json -I=0 "$0"`, expr, env)
    cmd.Dir = ".."
    out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    require.NoError(t, err, string(out))
    return string(out)
}

// Generated secrets go straight to OpenBao: per entry a Password generator and a PushSecret that runs it, writes only
// missing destinations (IfNotExists) and never deletes; no ExternalSecret or Secret holds a copy that could differ
// from OpenBao's value (ESO's CreatedOnce regenerates under a stale cache)
func TestGeneratedSecrets(t *testing.T) {
    values, err := exec.Command("yq", "-o=json", "-I=0", ".secrets + .extraSecrets", "../platform/generated-secrets/values.yaml").Output()
    require.NoError(t, err)
    var entries []generatedEntry
    require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(values, &entries))
    require.NotEmpty(t, entries)
    for _, env := range []string{"prod", "dev"} {
        kinds := renderGenerated(t, env, `[.kind] | .[]`)
        assert.NotContains(t, kinds, `"ExternalSecret"`, env)
        assert.NotContains(t, kinds, `"Secret"`, env)
        for _, e := range entries {
            length := e.Length
            if length == 0 {
                length = 32
            }
            symbols := 0
            if e.Special {
                symbols = 6
            }
            var gen struct {
                Length  int `json:"length"`
                Symbols int `json:"symbols"`
            }
            require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(renderGenerated(t, env, `select(.kind == "Password" and .metadata.name == "`+e.Name+`") | .spec`)), &gen), e.Name)
            assert.Equal(t, length, gen.Length, e.Name)
            assert.Equal(t, symbols, gen.Symbols, e.Name)

            var push struct {
                RefreshInterval string `json:"refreshInterval"`
                UpdatePolicy    string `json:"updatePolicy"`
                DeletionPolicy  string `json:"deletionPolicy"`
                SecretStoreRefs []struct {
                    Name string `json:"name"`
                } `json:"secretStoreRefs"`
                Selector struct {
                    GeneratorRef struct {
                        Kind string `json:"kind"`
                        Name string `json:"name"`
                    } `json:"generatorRef"`
                } `json:"selector"`
                Data []struct {
                    Match struct {
                        SecretKey string `json:"secretKey"`
                        RemoteRef struct {
                            RemoteKey string `json:"remoteKey"`
                            Property  string `json:"property"`
                        } `json:"remoteRef"`
                    } `json:"match"`
                } `json:"data"`
            }
            require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(renderGenerated(t, env, `select(.kind == "PushSecret" and .metadata.name == "`+e.Name+`") | .spec`)), &push), e.Name)
            assert.Equal(t, "1h", push.RefreshInterval, e.Name)
            assert.Equal(t, "IfNotExists", push.UpdatePolicy, e.Name)
            assert.Equal(t, "None", push.DeletionPolicy, e.Name)
            require.Len(t, push.SecretStoreRefs, 1, e.Name)
            assert.Equal(t, "openbao-writer", push.SecretStoreRefs[0].Name, e.Name)
            assert.Equal(t, "Password", push.Selector.GeneratorRef.Kind, e.Name)
            assert.Equal(t, e.Name, push.Selector.GeneratorRef.Name, e.Name)
            var remoteKeys []string
            for _, d := range push.Data {
                assert.Equal(t, "password", d.Match.SecretKey, e.Name)
                assert.Equal(t, e.Key, d.Match.RemoteRef.Property, e.Name)
                remoteKeys = append(remoteKeys, d.Match.RemoteRef.RemoteKey)
            }
            assert.Equal(t, e.Destinations, remoteKeys, e.Name)
        }
    }
}

// OpenBao's writer is the generated-secrets namespace's default service account, nothing else
func TestGeneratedSecretsWriterBinding(t *testing.T) {
    out, err := exec.Command("grep", "-n", "bound_service_account_namespaces = \\[\"generated-secrets\"\\]", "../platform/openbao/values.yaml").CombinedOutput()
    require.NoError(t, err, string(out))
}

{{- range concat .Values.secrets .Values.extraSecrets }}
---
apiVersion: generators.external-secrets.io/v1alpha1
kind: Password
metadata:
  name: {{ .name }}
  namespace: {{ $.Release.Namespace }}
spec:
  length: {{ .length | default 32 }}
  digits: 6
  symbols: {{ if .special }}6{{ else }}0{{ end }}
  allowRepeat: true
  noUpper: false
{{- end }}

and templates/push-secrets.yaml:

{{- range concat .Values.secrets .Values.extraSecrets }}
{{- $entry := . }}
{{- if .destinations }}
---
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1alpha1
kind: PushSecret
metadata:
  name: {{ .name }}
  namespace: {{ $.Release.Namespace }}
spec:
  # Every reconcile runs the generator once and writes that value to the destinations that do not exist (IfNotExists):
  # an existing value is never replaced, a missing one (an OpenBao that lost its data, a rotation) within the hour.
  # All destinations of a first push hold the same value. No Secret keeps a copy that could differ from OpenBao's.
  refreshInterval: 1h
  updatePolicy: IfNotExists
  deletionPolicy: None
  secretStoreRefs:
    - kind: SecretStore
      name: openbao-writer
  selector:
    generatorRef:
      apiVersion: generators.external-secrets.io/v1alpha1
      kind: Password
      name: {{ .name }}
  data:
    {{- range .destinations }}
    - match:
        secretKey: password
        remoteRef:
          remoteKey: {{ . }}
          property: {{ $entry.key }}
    {{- end }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}

# existing value by hand first (docs/concepts/secrets-management.md). Never rotated automatically.

docs.text:

  • Step 1: The helper and the readers

In test/secrets_test.go add:

// generatedValue is a generated secret as every app reads it, from OpenBao (secret/<path>, admin role), once pushed
func generatedValue(t *testing.T, path, property string) string {
    t.Helper()
    var value string
    require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
        value = baoValueE(path, property)
        return value != ""
    }, 20*time.Minute, 15*time.Second, "secret/%s is not pushed", path)
    return value
}

and in test/forgejo_test.go split baoValue so the poll does not fail the test on the first miss:

func baoValue(t *testing.T, path, property string) string {
    t.Helper()
    value := baoValueE(path, property)
    require.NotEmpty(t, value, "secret/%s#%s", path, property)
    return value
}

// baoValueE reads OpenBao the documented way: an admin login inside OpenBao's pod, the token never printed; empty on
// any error
func baoValueE(path, property string) string {
    script := "kubectl -n openbao create token openbao-admin --audience=openbao --duration=10m | kubectl -n openbao exec -i openbao-0 -c openbao -- " +
        "sh -c 'export BAO_TOKEN=$(bao write -field=token auth/kubernetes/login role=admin jwt=-); bao kv get -field=" + property + " secret/" + path + "; bao token revoke -self >/dev/null'"
    out, err := exec.Command("sh", "-c", script).Output()
    if err != nil {
        return ""
    }
    return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
}

Then: - test/ntfy_test.go: return "tk_" + generatedValue(t, "ntfy/generated/"+user+"-token", "token") - test/gateway_test.go:142 and test/sso_test.go:177: password := generatedValue(t, "zot/generated/ci", "password") - TestSecretsWriterRole: bao(t, "writer", "generated-secrets", "default", ...) (both calls). - TestSecretsReachConsumers: generated := generatedValue(t, "grafana/generated/admin", "password"), and drop the now-tautological assert.Equal(t, generated, grafanaAdmin(t), ...).

  • Step 2: Write the new sandbox test (in test/secrets_test.go)
// Generated secrets live only in OpenBao: no Secret in generated-secrets, a push again leaves every value as it is,
// one entry's destinations hold the same value, and a destination deleted (a rotation) is written again
func TestSecretsGeneratedOnlyInOpenBao(t *testing.T) {
    secretsSandboxOnly(t)
    waitForUnsealed(t)
    options := k8s.NewKubectlOptions("", "", "generated-secrets")
    options.Logger = logger.Discard
    secrets, err := k8s.RunKubectlAndGetOutputE(t, options, "get", "secrets", "-o", "name")
    require.NoError(t, err)
    assert.Empty(t, strings.TrimSpace(secrets), "a Secret in generated-secrets")

    hash := func(path, property string) string {
        sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(generatedValue(t, path, property)))
        return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
    }
    // Both destinations of one entry: the same push wrote them
    assert.Equal(t, hash("ntfy/generated/alerts-token", "token"), hash("monitoring-system/generated/ntfy", "token"))

    before := hash("grafana/generated/admin", "password")
    forceSync := func(name string) {
        _, err := k8s.RunKubectlAndGetOutputE(t, options, "annotate", "pushsecret", name, fmt.Sprintf("force-sync=%d", time.Now().UnixNano()), "--overwrite")
        require.NoError(t, err)
    }
    for range 2 {
        forceSync("grafana.admin")
        time.Sleep(20 * time.Second)
        assert.Equal(t, before, hash("grafana/generated/admin", "password"), "a push replaced an existing value")
    }

    // A rotation: the destination deleted, the next push writes a new value
    probe := hash("woodpecker/generated/agent", "secret")
    admin(t, "kv", "metadata", "delete", "secret/woodpecker/generated/agent")
    forceSync("woodpecker.agent")
    assert.NotEqual(t, probe, hash("woodpecker/generated/agent", "secret"), "the deleted destination was not written again")
}

(woodpecker.agent has no reader in the sandbox, so rotating it disturbs nothing.) Add the imports crypto/sha256 and encoding/hex if missing.

docs.title: Woodpecker for Other Repositories on Forgejo Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Repositories in Forgejo org ci get CI from Woodpecker in the cluster, building images with Buildah into zot, signed in only by members of ci (Kanidm homelab-admins, homelab-editors); the sandbox proves it end to end.

Architecture: platform/woodpecker (chart woodpecker 3.7.5, app 3.19.0) wired to read its Forgejo OAuth client and agent secret from OpenBao; lab infra forgejo sync creates org ci, its team developers and the OAuth2 application woodpecker, and writes its credentials to woodpecker/forgejo; Forgejo's Kanidm login source maps groups to ci's teams. Step pods run unprivileged in user namespaces; Buildah builds with chroot isolation and vfs.

Tech Stack: Woodpecker 3.19 (Kubernetes backend), Forgejo 17 chart (groupTeamMap), Buildah 1.43, Go (cli/, forgejo-sdk v3; test/, chromedp), Helm, yq.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-21-woodpecker-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Org ci is separate from ops: sync keeps refusing any team grant on ops/homelab.
  • Woodpecker: WOODPECKER_OPEN: true, WOODPECKER_ORGS: ci, WOODPECKER_ADMIN: forgejo_admin, WOODPECKER_EXPERT_WEBHOOK_HOST: http://woodpecker-server.woodpecker (not WOODPECKER_WEBHOOK_HOST).
  • Agents: WOODPECKER_BACKEND_K8S_USER_NAMESPACES: true; no WOODPECKER_PLUGINS_PRIVILEGED; every WOODPECKER_BACKEND_K8S_*_ALLOW_FROM_STEP explicitly false (tolerations included, its default is true).

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A Kanidm user outside homelab-admins/homelab-editors must not register in Woodpecker — Task 4 refuses dev-viewer.
  2. A step pod must not be privileged, must run in a user namespace and must not use the agent's service account — Task 1 renders the agent env, Task 4 inspects a running step pod.
  3. sync must keep the OAuth client and woodpecker/forgejo when they are right and must not touch ops — Task 3's unit tests and TestForgejoDeploy.
  4. Removing someone from the Kanidm group must drop their ci membership at the next login (groupTeamMapRemoval) — Task 2 renders it; Task 4 checks dev-editor is in ci/developers after login.
  5. Sandbox-only TLS skipping must not leak into production values — Task 1's render test checks production has no SKIP_VERIFY.

  • Step 1: Write the failing render test (test/woodpecker_test.go)
package test

import (
    "os/exec"
    "strings"
    "testing"

    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func renderWoodpecker(t *testing.T, env, expr string) string {
    t.Helper()
    cmd := exec.Command("sh", "-c", `scripts/render-chart platform/woodpecker $1 | yq -N "$0"`, expr, env)
    cmd.Dir = ".."
    out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    require.NoError(t, err, string(out))
    return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
}

// docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-21-woodpecker-design.md, decisions 1, 3 and 4
func TestWoodpeckerRender(t *testing.T) {
    server := `select(.kind == "StatefulSet" and .metadata.name == "woodpecker-server") | .spec.template.spec.containers[0]`
    agent := `select(.kind == "StatefulSet" and .metadata.name == "woodpecker-agent") | .spec.template.spec.containers[0]`
    env := func(e, container, name string) string {
        return renderWoodpecker(t, e, container+` | .env[] | select(.name == "`+name+`") | .value`)
    }
    for _, e := range []string{"", "dev"} {
        t.Run("env="+e, func(t *testing.T) {
            assert.Equal(t, "ci", env(e, server, "WOODPECKER_ORGS"))
            assert.Equal(t, "true", env(e, server, "WOODPECKER_FORGEJO"))
            assert.Equal(t, "http://woodpecker-server.woodpecker", env(e, server, "WOODPECKER_EXPERT_WEBHOOK_HOST"))
            assert.Empty(t, env(e, server, "WOODPECKER_WEBHOOK_HOST"), "Woodpecker 2's name")
            assert.Empty(t, env(e, server, "WOODPECKER_PLUGINS_PRIVILEGED"))
            assert.Equal(t, "woodpecker-environment,woodpecker-secret",
                renderWoodpecker(t, e, server+` | [.envFrom[].secretRef.name] | sort | join(",")`))
            assert.Equal(t, "woodpecker-agent", renderWoodpecker(t, e, agent+` | [.envFrom[].secretRef.name] | join(",")`))
            assert.Equal(t, "true", env(e, agent, "WOODPECKER_BACKEND_K8S_USER_NAMESPACES"))
            for _, allow := range []string{"SERVICE_ACCOUNT_NAME", "POD_NODE_SELECTOR", "POD_LABELS", "POD_ANNOTATIONS",
                "POD_AFFINITY", "RUNTIME_CLASS", "POD_TOLERATIONS"} {
                assert.Equal(t, "false", env(e, agent, "WOODPECKER_BACKEND_K8S_"+allow+"_ALLOW_FROM_STEP"), allow)
            }
            // The chart's own agent Secret is not rendered: the value comes from OpenBao
            assert.Empty(t, renderWoodpecker(t, e, `select(.kind == "Secret" and .metadata.name == "woodpecker-default-agent-secret") | .metadata.name`))
            assert.Equal(t, "woodpecker/generated/agent", renderWoodpecker(t, e,
                `select(.kind == "ExternalSecret" and .metadata.name == "woodpecker-agent") | .spec.data[0].remoteRef.key`))
        })
    }
    assert.Empty(t, env("", server, "WOODPECKER_FORGEJO_SKIP_VERIFY"), "production verifies Forgejo's certificate")
    assert.Equal(t, "1", renderWoodpecker(t, "dev", `select(.kind == "StatefulSet" and .metadata.name == "woodpecker-agent") | .spec.replicas`))
}

Check the chart's actual rendered names first (scripts/render-chart platform/woodpecker | yq 'select(.kind == "StatefulSet") | .metadata.name', and the agent Secret's name with createAgentSecret: true) and adjust the selectors, not the assertions.

docs.title: Step 11a: Backups Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Volume data that is not in git survives mistakes (hourly local snapshots) and the loss of every node (daily copies on R2), and comes back only by a command.

Architecture: - Velero (system/velero) backs up labelled PVCs only, through CSI snapshots and its data mover (Kopia), to an S3 bucket: R2 in production, an in-cluster S3 server in the sandbox. - Local snapshots: an hourly CronJob takes plain VolumeSnapshots and prunes them, with no dependency on the internet. - The sandbox gets CSI snapshots from csi-driver-host-path and runs Forgejo on CloudNativePG, so the sandbox proves the same path production uses. - lab backup (cli/internal/backup) pushes, lists, enables and restores.

Tech Stack: - Velero with velero-plugin-for-aws; - csi-driver-host-path and snapshot-controller (sandbox); - versitygw (sandbox S3); - CloudNativePG; - OpenTofu (infra/_modules/backup, Cloudflare provider); - Go: cobra, client-go dynamic, fake clients in tests; - the Go sandbox tests in test/.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-backups-design.md (the changes of Task 0 are written into it first).

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Versions: latest stable release of every chart, image and tool, pinned exactly. Pin a digest when an image has no version tag. If Velero's chart ships an older app version than Velero's latest release, pin the image to the latest release.
  • Scope: backups hold PersistentVolumeClaims and their data only, never other Kubernetes resources.
  • Groups:
  • daily (off-site every day, plus local snapshots): OpenBao, Kanidm, Forgejo (forgejo-data and forgejo-db), Woodpecker's server, ntfy, Matrix (Dendrite and its PostgreSQL).
  • manual (off-site only through lab backup push, plus local snapshots): Actual Budget, paperless, OpenCloud.
  • none: zot, Loki, ollama, jellyfin, and everything else.
  • Local snapshots: hourly, kept 48 hours, taken and restored without the internet.
  • Off-site retention: 30 copies kept per schedule and per app (a count, never an age: see Task 0).
  • Restore: only by command. OpenBao and the apps come from the same backup run, and Forgejo's two volumes from the same run, snapshotted one right after the other.
  • Uploads of group manual: never without the person seeing the size first.
  • Credentials: the Kopia repository password and the R2 credentials live in OpenTofu's state on R2, never only in OpenBao.
  • Mesh and egress rules from CLAUDE.md hold (AuthorizationPolicy allow, port 15008 in a chart's NetworkPolicies, the webhook pod label). Velero's namespace gets egress 443 in production only.
  • No VolSync left anywhere: system/volsync-system, the privileged-movers annotation, the scopes.yaml entries, the docs.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A fresh install that is never restored and never enabled must keep its backups. A fresh install sees the bucket's old backups. Nothing may delete them, whether by expiry, prune or a schedule (Task 7's prune test and Task 9's TestBackup step "fresh state is read-only").
  2. A restore must not pick a backup the new cluster made of its own empty volumes. The default is the newest backup that completed before this cluster's creation (kube-system's creationTimestamp) (Task 9, TestPickBackupIgnoresOwnBackups).
  3. Argo CD must not undo a restore in progress. It must not scale the app back up or recreate an empty PVC while lab replaces it (Task 9, TestRestorePausesSync, and TestBackup).
  4. A PVC added later without a group must fail the basic checks, not silently stay out of the backups (Task 4, scripts/check-backup-groups with a fixture).
  5. The size prompt with no TTY or with --yes: lab backup push without a terminal and without --yes must refuse, not upload (Task 9, TestPushRefusesWithoutConfirmation).

docs.title: Task 0: Spec changes found while planning (needs the user's approval before Task 1)
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-backups-design.md - Modify: CLAUDE.md (roadmap line 11a)

Write these into the spec. These deviations were found while planning:

  1. Read-only by default instead of make infra restore=1 (decision 8).
  2. Velero is synced by Argo CD from git as soon as a cluster exists, before anyone can pass a flag. A forgotten flag would let a fresh install's Velero expire the old backups.
  3. So in git the backup location is ReadOnly and every schedule paused, and Argo CD ignores those two fields.
  4. lab backup enable switches them once: on a brand-new homelab, or after a restore was checked. lab backup disable switches back.
  5. A PrometheusRule fires when no backup succeeded for 26 hours. That also catches a cluster never enabled.
  6. Retention by count, not by age:
  7. Velero's own expiry is set far out (ttl: 87600h).
  8. A prune CronJob keeps the newest 30 completed backups per schedule and per app, and runs only while the location is ReadWrite.
  9. A cluster dead for months therefore loses nothing.
  10. Kanidm goes through Velero like every other volume (crash-consistent SQLite).
  11. kaniop 0.19's own backups (KanidmBackupSchedule) require their own S3 repository: a second restore path, as with CloudNativePG.
  12. If Task 2's spike shows kaniop cannot take a restored volume, fall back to kaniop's backups and say so in the PR.

  13. The sandbox gets CSI snapshots from csi-driver-host-path, its default StorageClass. Its S3 server is versitygw. Local snapshots and Velero's CSI data mover then run in the sandbox too; only Ceph's specifics stay on the production checklist.

  14. Step 1: Write the four changes into the spec's decisions 5, 8 and 9 and into its non-goals, and mark the spec "amended 2026-10-22 (planning)". Update CLAUDE.md's 11a line: replace make infra env=production restore=1 keeps the backups read-only with read-only until lab backup enable, 30 copies kept by count.

  15. Step 2: Commit docs: 11a's spec amended (read-only by default, retention by count, CSI in the sandbox).

docs.title: Task 3: Spike: restore under the operators (throwaway, by hand, on the sandbox)
docs.text:
Nothing from this task is committed except its findings. It answers the questions the later tasks depend on.

  • Step 1: By hand, on the sandbox:
  • install csi-driver-host-path, which ships its VolumeSnapshotClass;
  • install snapshot-controller with its CRDs;
  • install versitygw (posix backend on an emptyDir, static credentials);
  • install Velero (CSI feature, node agent, the AWS plugin, data mover) pointing at versitygw;
  • make a hostpath StorageClass the default, then recreate Forgejo's namespace so its PVCs land on it.
  • Step 2: Forgejo. Push a repository and open an issue. Back up namespace forgejo with snapshotMoveData: true, labelled PVCs only. Then:
  • pause Argo CD's automated sync on Application forgejo;
  • scale Forgejo to 0 and hibernate the CNPG cluster (cnpg.io/hibernation=on);
  • delete both PVCs;
  • velero restore create --include-resources persistentvolumeclaims,persistentvolumes;
  • un-hibernate, scale up, resume sync.

Record: - Does CNPG start on the restored volume (system identifier, the forgejo-db-app password)? - Does Forgejo show the repository and the issue? - Does Argo CD stay synced? - [ ] Step 3: Kanidm. Create a person, back up, restore the same way. Is Kanidm's StatefulSet scaled by kaniop, so Kanidm's replicas: 0 must be patched instead? Does kaniop reconcile its admin and OAuth2 secrets against the restored database? - [ ] Step 4: OpenBao. Write a key, then: 1. bao operator raft snapshot save from inside the pod, with a token from a role bound to the pod's own projected token with audience openbao; 2. delete the key; 3. restore the PVC and run bao operator raft snapshot restore -force.

Is the key back, and does it unseal by itself? - [ ] Step 5: Local path. Delete a PVC and recreate it with dataSource set to a VolumeSnapshot. Does Argo CD report a diff? - [ ] Step 6: Write the answers into the plan under "Spike findings" (below), adjust Tasks 6–9 where an answer differs from what they assume, commit docs: 11a's spike findings, and make dev-clean && make dev to drop the hand-made changes.

Spike findings (2026-10-22, sandbox, Velero 1.18.4, CloudNativePG 1.30.1, kaniop 0.19.0, csi-driver-host-path 1.19.0, versitygw 1.9.0):

  1. The CSI data mover works against versitygw. Backup spike-1 of forgejo-data and forgejo-db-1 (PVCs and PVs only, label selector) completed with 4 items; its snapshots were cleaned up after the move.
  2. A restore with the workloads stopped needs restorePVC.ignoreDelayBinding: true in the node agent's ConfigMap (--node-agent-configmap). Without it, WaitForFirstConsumer classes keep each DataDownload waiting for a consumer pod.
  3. The short name backup is CloudNativePG's Backup. lab, tests and docs use backups.velero.io and restores.velero.io.
  4. Pausing one Application: ignoreApplicationDifferences: [{jsonPointers: [/spec/syncPolicy/automated]}] on its ApplicationSet keeps the pause. Without it, the ApplicationSet restores automated within seconds.
  5. CloudNativePG: the volume restores, but Velero drops the PVC's ownerReferences, and without them CNPG declares the cluster "unrecoverable" (pausing its reconciliation does not help). The order that works:
  6. cnpg.io/hibernation=on;
  7. wait for no pods;
  8. cnpg.io/reconciliationLoop=disabled;
  9. delete the PVCs;
  10. restore;
  11. set each PVC's controller ownerReference to the Cluster (its current uid);
  12. remove the reconciliation annotation, then the hibernation annotation;
  13. restart Forgejo's pod, whose init container crash-looped while the database was down.

Forgejo then showed the repository, its commit and its issue, and Argo CD stayed Synced and Healthy (Velero's extra labels make no diff). 6. Kanidm: Velero restores its volume. Kanidm is stopped through kaniop's Kanidm CR (spec.replicaGroups[0].replicas: 0, then back to 1). The deleted person came back, so kaniop's own backups are not needed. 7. kaniop writes kanidm-admin-passwords and every <client>-kanidm-oauth2-credentials only when the Secret is missing. - When Kanidm's data is replaced, the Secrets keep stale values: the idm_admin login fails and every app's SSO breaks. - So after a Kanidm restore, lab deletes those Secrets in every namespace and restarts their readers. kaniop recreates them from Kanidm's data within seconds; verified by comparing hashes. 8. OpenBao: bao operator raft snapshot save and restore -force work with the admin role, and OpenBao stays unsealed (static seal). - Velero's hooks run only for pods in the backup, and backups hold PVCs only, so the snapshot cannot be a hook. - Instead, a CronJob in namespace openbao, hourly at :55, uses OpenBao's image, service account openbao-snapshot and a new role snapshot (projected token, audience openbao, policy read on sys/storage/raft/snapshot). It writes raft.snap into its own PVC openbao-snapshots (group daily). The raft volume data-openbao-0 is group none. - Restore means restoring openbao-snapshots, then a Job (service account openbao-admin, role admin) runs bao operator raft snapshot restore -force against http://openbao.openbao:8200. 9. The local path: a PVC recreated with the old one's labels, annotations and ownerReferences plus dataSource: VolumeSnapshot restored Forgejo, through the same CNPG order as finding 5. Argo CD reported no diff. 10. Velero's CSI support requires the VolumeSnapshotClass label velero.io/csi-volumesnapshot-class: "true". Rook's class needs it too (cephBlockPoolsVolumeSnapshotClass.labels).

Effect on the later tasks: - Task 6: - the node agent's ConfigMap (finding 2); - the class label (finding 10); - the OpenBao snapshot CronJob, its role and its PVC (finding 8), instead of the hook; - csi-hostpath's classes as in the spike. - Task 9: - RestoreApp follows findings 5, 6, 7 and 9 per kind of workload; - OpenBao follows finding 8; - all names are backups.velero.io/restores.velero.io. - Task 4: OpenBao's daily is its openbao-snapshots PVC.

Add it to the root ApplicationSet's templatePatch for velero, since RespectIgnoreDifferences=true is already on. - Schedule daily: 0 2 * * * in global.timezone, paused: true in git (ignored the same way), template.ttl: 87600h, snapshotMoveData: true, labelSelector: {matchLabels: {homelab/backup: daily}}, includedResources: [persistentvolumeclaims, persistentvolumes]. - Plus whatever the data mover needs. The spike tells whether volumesnapshots must be included. - Velero's pre-backup hook for OpenBao: a bao operator raft snapshot save into /openbao/data/snapshots/raft.snap. - It is declared as pod annotations on OpenBao (pre.hook.backup.velero.io/*) in platform/openbao/values.yaml. The pod is not in the backup, so if Velero runs hooks only on included pods, the spike's way applies instead: a CronJob five minutes before the schedule, in namespace openbao. - It logs in with a new role snapshot, bound to openbao's service account, with a projected token of audience openbao and a policy reading sys/storage/raft/snapshot. Add both to initialize. - Prune CronJob prune: hourly, image alpine/kubectl pinned as in system/istio-system, script files/prune.sh. - It does nothing unless BackupStorageLocation/default is ReadWrite. - Otherwise it groups completed Backups by the label velero.io/schedule-name, or homelab/app for manual ones, keeps the newest 30 of each, and deletes the rest by creating DeleteBackupRequests. - Snapshot CronJob snapshots: hourly, same image, files/snapshots.sh. - For each PVC labelled homelab/backup in (daily, manual), sorted so a namespace's PVCs are taken one right after the other, it creates VolumeSnapshot <pvc>-<yyyymmddhh> with labels homelab/snapshot: hourly, homelab/pvc: <pvc>. - It deletes that label's snapshots older than 48 hours. - ClusterRole: PVCs get/list; volumesnapshots get/list/create/delete. - Metrics and alert: a ServiceMonitor, and a PrometheusRule VeleroNoRecentBackup: time() - max(velero_backup_last_successful_timestamp{schedule="daily"}) > 26*3600, or the metric absent, for 1h. Alertmanager's existing route sends it to ntfy. - Mesh: - templates/authorization-policy.yaml allow: Prometheus on the metrics ports, plus the node agent's in-namespace calls. - The node agent and the data mover's pods: check whether they need istio.io/dataplane-mode: none (they are not webhooks). scripts/check-mesh-policies passes. - Modify: system/egress/values.yaml: velero → 443, production only (CLAUDE.md's internet table and scripts/check-env-config). - Create (sandbox only): - system/csi-hostpath/: csi-driver-host-path's deploy manifests vendored as templates at a pinned release, plus snapshot-controller and its CRDs (the piraeus chart that system/rook-ceph already uses, same version). - Its classes: StorageClass csi-hostpath with the default annotation, and a default VolumeSnapshotClass. - The sandbox node's StorageClass: infra/_modules/k3d/k3d.yaml keeps local-path but drops its default annotation (k3s --disable=local-storage would remove it; keep it for anything created before Argo CD). - Modify: system/velero/values-dev.yaml: - versitygw as templates/s3-dev.yaml, rendered when .Values.devS3.enabled: a Deployment and Service s3 in namespace velero, posix backend on a 2Gi PVC labelled homelab/backup: none; - its credentials from a generated secret velero.s3 (destinations velero/generated/s3) added through platform/generated-secrets/values-dev.yaml's extraSecrets, with a sandbox-only Kopia password the same way; - the BSL pointing at http://s3.velero:7070; - no egress. - Modify: - system/argocd/values-dev.yaml: system/velero and system/csi-hostpath; - test/scopes.yaml: a Backup group (velero, csi-hostpath, the openbao hook, cli/internal/backup, the tests), with full and the related groups; - Argo CD's sync-wave or retry notes if csi-hostpath must exist before other PVCs. On a fresh sandbox every PVC must land on csi-hostpath, not on local-path: Argo CD retries a PVC whose StorageClass does not exist yet only if no default is set. Decide from the spike and write the reason next to the setting. - Test (offline): test/velero_test.go TestVeleroRender, which renders production and dev and asserts: - the BSL is ReadOnly, and the schedule paused with ttl 87600h, snapshotMoveData, and the selector homelab/backup: daily; - no schedule includes anything but PVC-related kinds; - the prune and snapshot CronJobs exist; - dev has s3 and production does not; - production's egress for velero is 443.

- What RestoreApp does: 1. Pause the Application's automated sync. 2. Stop the app's workloads. Deployments and StatefulSets go to 0; a CNPG Cluster is hibernated; for a kaniop Kanidm, follow the spike's finding. 3. Wait for the pods to be gone. 4. Delete the PVCs, keeping their labels and annotations. 5. Restore them: - offsite: a Velero Restore of persistentvolumeclaims,persistentvolumes from the run, namespace app; - local: new PVCs with the old metadata and dataSource = that PVC's newest VolumeSnapshot at or before at. 6. For OpenBao, bao operator raft snapshot restore -force from the restored file, through exec with the admin role, as the docs' commands do. 7. Un-hibernate and scale back up. 8. Resume the sync, and wait for the Application to be Synced and Healthy.

On error it stops and prints what remains paused. It never resumes the sync over a half-restored volume. - What RestoreCluster does: 1. Refuses unless the location is ReadOnly. 2. Restores openbao first, then the rest. 3. Then force-syncs every ExternalSecret (annotation force-sync) and restarts every Deployment and StatefulSet outside openbao, kube-system and argocd, so every reader takes the restored secrets. 4.
