docs.title: Secrets Rotation (Step 11b) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: lab secrets rotate <name>|--all replaces any secret in a catalog by its official method (overlap when the other side allows it), a daily CronJob rotates the due ones, and a failure alerts through ntfy and Telegram.

Architecture: - A new Go package cli/internal/rotate holds the catalog (an embedded YAML), the engine (safety checks, ordering, the record) and one Method per kind of secret. - Refreshing ExternalSecrets, restarting workloads and waiting for them move out of cli/internal/backup into cli/internal/workload, which both use. - The CronJob (platform/secrets-rotation) runs lab secrets rotate --scheduled from the lab image, which GitHub Actions builds with ko.

Tech Stack: Go (cobra, client-go, github.com/openbao/openbao/api/v2, the Forgejo SDK already in cli/), ko, Helm charts as in platform/, Alertmanager telegram_configs, Terragrunt/OpenTofu for Cloudflare's tokens.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-24-secrets-rotation-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Latest stable release of every tool, chart, image and Go module, pinned exactly (images by digest when they have no version tag); hold one back only for a stated compatibility constraint.
  • No secret value in git, command arguments, logs, error messages or test output: errors name the path, never the value (as cli/internal/secrets does). The Telegram chat id is treated as a secret.
  • Branch feat/secrets-rotation from dev; PR into dev; never commit to dev or master.
  • Before each commit: direnv exec . scripts/ci-check all passes. Run make dev only from /home/nixos/homelab, never from a worktree. The last make dev before the PR covers the whole branch, and a make dev-fresh at the end.
  • A new component gets its entry in test/scopes.yaml in the task that adds it.
  • Every commit ends with the attribution lines of the session's system reminder.
  • Settings that depend on the environment come from infra/<env>/cluster/config.json globals; charts hold no domain or address.
  • Deferred minors go in docs/superpowers/deferred-minors.md; rulings and findings go in the ledger (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-24-secrets-rotation/progress.md).
  • Tell the user about GitHub Actions runs that would repeat local tests or pile up before adding them (memory flag-ci-compute-cost).

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A rotation interrupted half-way (Ctrl-C, the Job's pod killed, OpenBao restarting) after the new value was written but before every reader switched: rerunning the same command must finish it. It must not create a third value, and with an overlap it must never revoke the old value before the readers moved. Test: TestRotateResumesAfterInterruption (Task 4).
  2. --all or --scheduled reaching a manual entry (GitHub App key, Telegram, Tunnel) without a terminal: skip it and name it in the report, never hang waiting for input. Test: TestRotateSkipsManualWithoutTerminal (Task 4).
  3. A reader that does not come back (its ExternalSecret cannot refresh, its pod crash-loops): stop, keep the old value valid where there is an overlap, and report which reader failed. Test: TestRotateKeepsOldOnReaderFailure (Task 4).
  4. A mistyped name: an error naming the closest catalog names, with nothing touched. Test: TestRotateUnknownName (Task 4).
  5. Values leaking in errors, e.g. an OpenBao or Forgejo error that echoes a request body: every error a method returns is checked to contain no generated value. Test: TestMethodErrorsHideValues (Task 5).

Answer each question on the running sandbox, by hand. Record the answer and the evidence (commands, never values) in the ledger, then amend the spec's catalog row. Undo every hand change, or run make dev-fresh at the end of the spike if one cannot be undone.

  • Step 1: Woodpecker. Do Woodpecker 3's per-agent tokens let a new agent connect while the old one still runs? Which pod label marks a running step pod (used for the idle wait)?
  • Step 2: paperless. Does paperless read PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY fallbacks (Django's SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS), or does a new key end every session?
  • Step 3: kaniop.
  • How do you trigger one regeneration of a KanidmOAuth2Client secret (spec.secretRotation, an annotation, or deleting the Secret)?
  • Does any reader pick up the new Secret without a restart?
  • Does deleting kanidm-admin-passwords still regenerate both admin passwords (11a's finding)?
  • Step 4: CloudNativePG. How do you rotate forgejo-db's app password (CloudNativePG's documented way), and does Forgejo need a restart?
  • Step 5: Alertmanager and ntfy.

  • Does ntfy accept two tokens for one user in NTFY_AUTH_TOKENS?
  • Does the pinned Alertmanager support chat_id_file in telegram_configs? If not, render the whole Alertmanager config Secret through ESO.
  • Step 6: Velero and Kopia. Can a repository's password change through Velero, or is backup.kopia-password "never" (reason: every repository is encrypted with it, and Velero has no change-password)?
  • Step 7: OpenTofu's tokens. With create_before_destroy on cloudflare_account_token, one apply destroys the old token before cert-manager and external-dns switch. Confirm that both retry (cert-manager's DNS01 and external-dns's next sync), which makes them class 1 instead of overlap. Plan only, against production's state: terragrunt plan -replace=..., with the user's approval. The same applies to backup.r2-token: avoid 02:00, when Velero's daily backup runs.

docs.title: Task 4: The engine and lab secrets rotate|list
docs.text:
Files: - Create: cli/internal/rotate/rotate.go, cli/internal/rotate/record.go, cli/internal/rotate/rotate_test.go - Modify: cli/internal/cli/secrets.go, cli/internal/cli/root.go

Interfaces: - Consumes: Entry, Load, Find (Task 3); workload.Client (Task 2); secrets.Store (existing); backup.Client.Runs (existing). - Produces:

// A Method changes one entry in phases, so an interrupted run resumes: Prepare writes the new value (or finds the one
// a previous run wrote), Switch moves the readers to it, Verify checks they work, Revoke ends the old value (a no-op
// without an overlap).
type Method interface {
    Prepare(ctx context.Context, e Entry) error
    Switch(ctx context.Context, e Entry) error
    Verify(ctx context.Context, e Entry) error
    Revoke(ctx context.Context, e Entry) error
}
type Options struct {
    All, Scheduled, Yes, Interactive bool
    SkipBackupCheck                  string // the reason; empty = check
    Now                              time.Time
}
type Result struct {
    Name    string
    Outcome string // rotated, skipped (and why), failed (and the phase)
    Err     error
}
type Rotator struct {
    Entries  []Entry
    Methods  map[Method]Method // by entry method
    Store    Records           // record.go
    Backups  func(ctx context.Context) ([]backup.Run, error)
    Idle     func(ctx context.Context, what string) (bool, error)
    Out      io.Writer
    Poll, Wait time.Duration
}
func (r *Rotator) Plan(names []string, o Options) ([]Entry, error) // the order --all uses; unknown names error
func (r *Rotator) Run(ctx context.Context, plan []Entry, o Options) ([]Result, error)
  • Record (record.go): the custom metadata of the entry's first OpenBao path holds the rotation state, through a new secrets.Store.Metadata(ctx, path) (map[string]string, error) and secrets.Store.SetMetadata(ctx, path, map[string]string) error.
  • Keys: rotation-phase (prepared, switched, verified, done), rotated-at (RFC 3339), rotated-by, rotation-method, rotation-reason (the backup-check override).
  • Entries without an OpenBao path (OpenTofu's, GitHub's) use the same keys on secret/rotation/<name>. That path is reachable only by the admin role and the new rotator role (Task 9).
  • Order for --all:
  • generated secrets and ntfy;
  • Forgejo;
  • Kanidm clients;
  • Woodpecker and zot (with the idle wait);
  • OpenTofu's;
  • manual ones last.

never, script and automatic entries are listed with their reason and skipped. - Run: - checks the backup first: a Completed scheduled run started less than 24 hours before o.Now, unless SkipBackupCheck; - then, per entry: waits for idleness, resumes from the recorded phase, runs the phases, records each one and stops at the first failure; - returns every entry's result. - lab secrets list prints each entry's name, method, class, period, last rotation and next due date. - lab secrets rotate <name>... | --all: - prints the plan, the workloads that will restart (marking those with one replica, which stop briefly) and the people who must act, then asks for confirmation (confirm from cli/backup.go); - --yes skips the confirmation; - --scheduled implies --yes, picks only due entries and skips manual ones; - --skip-backup-check=<reason> overrides the backup check; - exits non-zero when any entry failed or a due entry is past its due date plus 14 days.

  • TestRotateResumesAfterInterruption: the phase is switched, so only Verify and Revoke run.

  • TestRotateSkipsManualWithoutTerminal

  • TestRotateWaitsForIdle: it times out with an error naming Woodpecker.

docs.title: Power Cut (Step 11c) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Act on the spike's findings: prune orphaned Velero snapshots, add lab secrets force-unlock and a release that retries, and a fixed TestNodePowerCut.

Architecture: - Snapshots: system/velero/files/prune.sh gains a pass over the VolumeSnapshots labelled velero.io/backup-name. - Lock: cli/internal/rotate/lock.go gains ForceUnlock and a retrying release; cli/internal/cli/secrets.go wires lab secrets force-unlock. - Test: test/node_restart_test.go gains TestNodePowerCut, which shares TestNodeRestart's helpers and adds "really back" checks.

Tech Stack: POSIX sh, Go (client-go, cobra), the test module's terratest helpers.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-25-power-cut-design.md (Findings and Decisions)

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• No secret value in arguments, logs or test output (markers are test strings, never secrets).
  • Latest stable versions, pinned (no new dependency is expected).
  • make dev only from /home/nixos/homelab; scripts/ci-check all before each commit; commits end with the session's attribution lines.
  • The fixed test measures recovery as the spec says: the node Ready after the cut, no pod Unknown or not ready, and the apps answering through the Gateway, within 20 minutes.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A VolumeSnapshot of a backup still running must never be pruned. Only snapshots whose backup no longer exists are deleted. Test: TestVeleroPruneOrphanSnapshots keeps a snapshot whose backup is InProgress.
  2. force-unlock with a stale holder (the run that died was replaced by a live one) must refuse. Test: TestForceUnlockRefusesAnotherHolder.
  3. A release that keeps failing (the API server down for minutes) must not hang the command. It gives up after its retries, and the Lease expires as before. Test: TestLockReleaseRetriesThenGivesUp.
  4. The pre-cut pod states the API server reports must not count as recovered. Test: TestPowerCutRecovered (offline) rejects pods whose start is before the cut.

docs.title: Task 1: prune deletes orphaned Velero snapshots
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: system/velero/files/prune.sh, system/velero/templates/prune.yaml (a ClusterRole for the cluster-wide snapshot listing) - Test: test/velero_scripts_test.go

  • Step 1: Write the failing test. TestVeleroPruneOrphanSnapshots:
  • The fake kubectl answers get volumesnapshots.snapshot.storage.k8s.io -A -l velero.io/backup-name from a velerosnapshots fixture (lines namespace name backup).
  • With backups daily-1 (Completed) and daily-2 (InProgress), and snapshots for daily-1, daily-2 and gone-3, the actions are exactly deleted <ns>/<snapshot of gone-3>.
  • The orphan pass also runs while the location is ReadOnly: an orphan belongs to no backup a restore could need.
  • Step 2: Run the test. cd test && go test -run TestVeleroPruneOrphanSnapshots ./ fails.
  • Step 3: Implement. Add a pass at the top of prune.sh, before the ReadOnly exit:
  • list backup names;
  • list the Velero-labelled VolumeSnapshots;
  • delete those whose velero.io/backup-name is not a backup (--wait=false).

Give the prune role list/delete on volumesnapshots across namespaces (ClusterRole + ClusterRoleBinding, like snapshots.yaml's). If Velero's VolumeSnapshotClass retains contents, prune the matching VolumeSnapshotContents too and say so in the comment. - [ ] Step 4: Run the tests. go test -run 'TestVeleroPrune' ./ passes, and scripts/render-chart system/velero renders. - [ ] Step 5: Commit. fix(velero): prune deletes the snapshots of backups that are gone (a power cut during a backup left one)

docs.title: Task 2: lab secrets force-unlock and a release that retries
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: cli/internal/rotate/lock.go, cli/internal/rotate/rotate_test.go, cli/internal/cli/secrets.go, cli/internal/cli/secrets_test.go

Interfaces: - Produces: - func (l *LeaseLocker) ForceUnlock(ctx context.Context, name, holder string) (Lease, error). It deletes Lease rotate-<name> only if its holder equals holder (a ResourceVersion precondition), and returns what it removed: type Lease struct{ Holder string; Acquired, Renewed time.Time }. - lab secrets force-unlock <name> <holder> [--yes] [--env]: prints the holder and times, asks (confirm), and calls ForceUnlock. - The release retries its Get/Delete with backoff for up to two minutes (LeaseLocker.ReleaseFor, default 2*time.Minute), then gives up silently, as now.

  • Step 1: Write the failing tests.
  • TestForceUnlock: a held Lease is removed and the returned holder matches.
  • TestForceUnlockRefusesAnotherHolder: the error names the actual holder, and the Lease stays.
  • TestLockReleaseRetries: the first two deletes fail (reactor), the third succeeds, and the Lease is gone.
  • TestLockReleaseRetriesThenGivesUp: with ReleaseFor: 50ms, release returns.
  • TestSecretsForceUnlockAsksFirst, in cli: without --yes and without a terminal it errors and the Lease stays.
  • Step 2: Run the tests. go test ./internal/rotate/ ./internal/cli/ fails.
  • Step 3: Implement. Make the "being rotated by" error also say or lab secrets force-unlock <name> <holder>.
  • Step 4: Run the checks. make -C cli test check passes.
  • Step 5: Commit. feat(lab): lab secrets force-unlock, and a lock release that retries while the API server comes back

restartPod gains Started time.Time (the container's state.running.startedAt). - [ ] Step 2: Run the test. It fails. - [ ] Step 3: Implement. docs.title: Detection (Step 15a) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Three new basic checks fail a pull request: leaks (gitleaks on its commits), images (Trivy on its new images) and iac (Trivy on OpenTofu and Dockerfiles).

Architecture: Three scripts/check-* scripts, called by scripts/ci-check and run as matrix jobs in checks.yaml. Offline tests in test/ run each script against fixtures, with a fake trivy where a scan would need the network.

Tech Stack: POSIX sh, gitleaks, Trivy, yq, GitHub Actions, Go tests.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-detection-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• gitleaks comes from nixos-26.05 (8.30.1). Trivy comes from unstable (0.76.0), with a comment that 0.76.1 is not packaged yet.
  • Only what the change brings is scanned: $BASE..HEAD for leaks, and the images new at HEAD for images. iac scans its small set in full.
  • images fails on CRITICAL with a fix. iac fails on HIGH and CRITICAL.
  • Every entry in .trivyignore.yaml has a reason (statement). CVE entries also have an expired_at at most 90 days away.
  • No secret value in any output: gitleaks runs with --redact.
  • scripts/lint passes: shellcheck and actionlint.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. BASE is forty zeros (a new branch's first push) or missing: leaks must still scan something sensible (HEAD's own commit), not everything and not nothing. Test: TestCheckLeaks with BASE=0000….
  2. An image pinned by digest, or with a registry port (registry.x:5000/a@sha256:…) is parsed whole. Test: TestCheckImages fixture.
  3. A render that fails in images must fail the check, never pass as "no new image". Test: TestCheckImages with a broken chart.
  4. An expired .trivyignore.yaml entry stops ignoring. That is Trivy's behaviour; TestCheckIaC uses a fake that checks the flag is passed.

docs.title: Task 1: leaks
docs.text:
Files: - Create: scripts/check-leaks, .gitleaks.toml - Modify: flake.nix (gitleaks), scripts/ci-check (leaks), .github/workflows/checks.yaml (matrix) - Test: test/detection_test.go (TestCheckLeaks)

  • Step 1: Write the failing test. TestCheckLeaks. In a temp git repository, commit a clean file, then a file holding a fake AWS key that gitleaks detects (built at runtime so this repository holds no key-shaped literal).
  • BASE = the clean commit: the check fails, and the output holds no key characters (it is redacted).
  • BASE = HEAD: it passes.
  • BASE = forty zeros: it scans HEAD's commit only.
  • Step 2: Run it. It fails: no script.
  • Step 3: Implement. scripts/check-leaks: gitleaks git --redact --no-banner --log-opts "$range". The range is $BASE..HEAD, or HEAD^..HEAD for zeros or an empty BASE. Add gitleaks to the dev shell, leaks to ci-check's checks, and leaks to the matrix.
  • Step 4: Run it. go test -run TestCheckLeaks passes. scripts/ci-check leaks passes on this branch.
  • Step 5: Commit. feat(ci): leaks, gitleaks on a pull request's commits

docs.title: Task 2: iac
docs.text:
Files: - Create: scripts/check-iac, .trivyignore.yaml - Modify: flake.nix (unstable trivy), cli/Dockerfile (USER 65532:65532), scripts/ci-check, checks.yaml (matrix; Trivy's cache step, shared with Task 3) - Test: TestCheckIaC

  • Step 1: Write the failing test. TestCheckIaC runs scripts/check-iac with TRIVY pointing at a fake that records its arguments and fails when told to.
  • The arguments include config, --severity HIGH,CRITICAL, --exit-code 1, --ignorefile .trivyignore.yaml and the four targets.
  • A failing fake fails the check.
  • Step 2: Run it. It fails.
  • Step 3: Implement.
  • The script runs one trivy config per target (infra, cli, Dockerfile, metal/roles/pxe_server/files) and skips .terragrunt-cache and .terraform.
  • .trivyignore.yaml: DS-0002 for the root Dockerfile (upstream's docs image, not deployed here) and for metal's two images (dnsmasq binds port 67 as root), each with its path and statement.
  • cli/Dockerfile gets USER 65532:65532.
  • CI caches ~/.cache/trivy by day.
  • Step 4: Run it. The test passes. scripts/ci-check iac passes with the real Trivy.
  • Step 5: Commit. feat(ci): iac, Trivy on OpenTofu and the Dockerfiles

docs.title: Task 3: images
docs.text:
Files: - Create: scripts/check-images - Modify: scripts/ci-check, checks.yaml - Test: TestCheckImages

Interfaces: - scripts/check-images lists targets with go -C cli run ./cmd/lab test charts --base "$BASE", renders each with scripts/render-chart at HEAD and at $BASE (a git worktree of BASE; a target missing there has no old images), and scans the new images. - IMAGES_ONLY=1 prints the new images without scanning, for the test.

  • Step 1: Write the failing test. TestCheckImages runs on a temp copy of a small chart. With IMAGES_ONLY=1:
  • one image changed between BASE and HEAD, plus one digest-pinned image with a registry port: only the changed and the new image are printed;
  • a target whose render fails fails the check.

With a fake TRIVY that reports a finding, the check fails. - [ ] Step 2: Run it. It fails. - [ ] Step 3: Implement. Extract images with yq '.. | select(has("image")) | .image | select(tag == "!!str")' over the renders, then sort and deduplicate. Scan with trivy image --severity CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed --exit-code 1 --ignorefile .trivyignore.yaml, and --skip-db-update when TRIVY_SKIP_DB_UPDATE=1 (CI's cache hit). - [ ] Step 4: Run it. The test passes. scripts/ci-check images on this branch prints that nothing is new. - [ ] Step 5: Commit. feat(ci): images, Trivy on the images a change brings

docs.title: Kiali (Step 14d) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: A read-only Kiali for admins on the LAN Gateway, with Istio's metrics scraped so its graph has data.

Architecture: - Metrics: system/istio-system gains PodMonitors for ztunnel, istiod and the Gateways' Envoy, and whatever lets Prometheus reach them. - Kiali: a new component system/kiali wraps kiali-server 2.33.0. It signs in with Kanidm's openid and holds its own HTTPRoute, AuthorizationPolicy and Kanidm client.

Tech Stack: Helm, kube-prometheus-stack's PodMonitor, Istio ambient, kaniop, Go sandbox tests.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-kiali-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• kiali-server chart 2.33.0 from https://kiali.org/helm-charts, pinned.
  • Kiali has view_only_mode: true and disable_rbac: true. Only homelab-admins gets a scope on Kanidm client kiali.
  • The route kiali.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }} is on istio-system/gateway only, never public.
  • No IP address or domain in the chart (scripts/check-env-config).
  • No PVC.
  • The new secret has an entry in cli/internal/rotate/catalog.yaml.
  • scripts/check-mesh-policies passes.
  • scripts/ci-check all runs before each commit. make dev runs only from /home/nixos/homelab.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A signed-in non-admin (homelab-editors, homelab-users, no group) must not reach Kiali. Test: TestSSOKiali refuses dev-editor, dev-viewer and dev-outsider.
  2. A write through Kiali's API (as an admin) must be refused, since the instance is read-only. Test: TestSSOKiali PATCHes an Istio object through Kiali and expects a refusal.
  3. Kiali on the public Gateway must never render. Test: TestKialiRender (offline) finds exactly one HTTPRoute, with parent gateway.
  4. An empty graph (metrics missing, or Prometheus blocked by the mesh): the graph API must return edges. Test: TestMeshMetrics checks the series, and TestSSOKiali checks the graph has at least one edge.

docs.title: Task 1: Istio's metrics in Prometheus
docs.text:
Files: - Create: system/istio-system/templates/pod-monitors.yaml - Modify: whatever lets Prometheus scrape, if needed: system/istio-system's policies, or monitoring-system's network policy - Test: test/mesh_metrics_test.go; test/scopes.yaml already maps system/istio-system/** to Mesh

Interfaces: - Produces Prometheus series that Task 2's graph reads: - istio_tcp_sent_bytes_total{reporter="destination"} from ztunnel; - istio_requests_total from the Gateways' Envoy; - pilot_xds_pushes from istiod.

  • Step 1: Write the failing test. TestMeshMetrics(t), sandbox only (meshSandboxOnly). Within 5 minutes, Prometheus's API (exec into the Prometheus pod or port-forward, like the monitoring tests) returns at least one series for each of:
  • istio_tcp_sent_bytes_total
  • istio_requests_total{source_workload="gateway-istio"}
  • pilot_xds_pushes

Generate traffic first: one request through the Gateway to a smoke app. - [ ] Step 2: Run it. make dev tests='MeshMetrics' fails: no series. - [ ] Step 3: Implement. Write one PodMonitor each for: - ztunnel (app=ztunnel, port 15020, /stats/prometheus); - istiod (app=istiod, port 15014, /metrics); - the Gateways (gateway.networking.k8s.io/gateway-name exists, port 15020, /stats/prometheus).

Drop envoy_.* series from the Gateways and ztunnel's high-cardinality internal series with metricRelabelings, keeping istio_.*. Open the paths scripts/check-mesh-policies names and add the in-cluster calls to its EXTRA. - [ ] Step 4: Run it. make dev tests='MeshMetrics' passes. The offline render scripts/render-chart system/istio-system dev succeeds. - [ ] Step 5: Commit. feat(istio-system): Prometheus scrapes ztunnel, istiod and the Gateways (Kiali's graph, Grafana)

docs.title: Task 2: system/kiali
docs.text:
Files: - Create in system/kiali/: - Chart.yaml: dependency kiali-server 2.33.0; - values.yaml and values-dev.yaml; - templates/: kanidm-client.yaml, httproute.yaml, authorization-policy.yaml, and the secret mapping if the chart needs one. - Modify: - system/argocd/values-dev.yaml: add system/kiali to root; - platform/kanidm/values.yaml: add kiali to oauth2ClientNamespaces; - system/monitoring-system/templates/authorization-policy.yaml: admit Kiali's service account on Prometheus's 9090; - cli/internal/rotate/catalog.yaml: entry kanidm-client.kiali (kind kaniop-client, settings {client: kiali, namespace: kiali}; class from how Kiali reads the secret: 2 with its Deployment as reader if it reads it at start); - test/scopes.yaml: system/kiali/** maps to SSOKiali|KialiRender; - system/argocd/values.yaml: Argo CD editors' exec list, only if the convention lists system components (it lists apps/*: none expected). - Test: test/kiali_test.go (TestKialiRender offline; TestSSOKiali)

Interfaces: - Consumes Task 1's series. - Uses appLogin, ensureCredentials, getJSON and waitForApp from the identity helpers.

  • Step 1: Write the failing tests.

  • TestKialiRender(t), offline: render system/kiali (prod and dev) with scripts/render-chart. Assert:

    • exactly one HTTPRoute, whose parent is gateway;
    • the Kiali config has view_only_mode: true, strategy: openid and disable_rbac: true;
    • the KanidmOAuth2Client's scopeMap names only homelab-admins;
    • no PersistentVolumeClaim is rendered.

GET /kiali/api/namespaces/graph?namespaces=excalidraw,istio-system&graphType=workload returns at least one edge, retried for up to 5 minutes after one request through the Gateway. - A write as dev-admin (PATCH /kiali/api/namespaces/istio-system/istio/... on an AuthorizationPolicy) does not succeed. - dev-editor, dev-viewer and dev-outsider do not get a Kiali session (Kanidm refuses them: no scope). - [ ] Step 2: Run them. go test -run TestKialiRender fails (no chart). make dev tests='SSOKiali' fails. - [ ] Step 3: Implement. docs.title: Policy (Step 15b-1) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Kyverno in Audit with the restricted Pod Security policies, pinned images and allowed registries. A policy basic check blocks violations in CI. Every fixable workload is fixed, every inherent one has a written exception, and PSA baseline is the second layer.

Architecture: - system/kyverno wraps the kyverno and kyverno-policies charts (3.9.2) and adds two custom ValidatingPolicy objects. - scripts/check-policy runs the kyverno CLI on every render. - Exceptions are PolicyExceptions in the excused component's own chart or app file.

Tech Stack: Kyverno 1.19.2 (CEL ValidatingPolicy), Helm, POSIX sh, Go tests.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-policy-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Charts kyverno 3.9.2 and kyverno-policies 3.9.2. The kyverno CLI 1.19.2 comes from unstable, since nixos-26.05 ships 1.18.2.
  • The policies are Audit in the cluster, and the check fails CI on any fail or error.
  • podSecurityUserNamespaces: true, for Woodpecker's step pods.
  • Every PolicyException names its policies and its workloads, and gives its reason in an annotation.
  • Kyverno's pods carry istio.io/dataplane-mode: none (the API server calls them), and its webhooks use failurePolicy: Ignore.
  • Mesh and egress rules still hold: scripts/check-mesh-policies and scripts/check-env-config pass.
  • scripts/ci-check all, lint and gofmt pass before every commit.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A fix that breaks an app. A securityContext an image cannot run under (it writes to /, or needs root) must not ship. Test: the sandbox suite (make dev full) passes.
  2. An exception broader than its workload, such as a whole namespace or every policy. Test: TestCheckPolicy fails when the exceptions file is dropped. A review reads each exception's match conditions.
  3. Kyverno down or slow at admission must not block deploys while in Audit (failurePolicy: Ignore). Test: TestPolicy checks the webhook configuration's failurePolicy.
  4. The PSA label on a namespace that needs privileged, set too strictly, would stop its pods on any restart. Test: the sandbox suite (TestNodeRestart restarts every pod).

docs.title: Security logs (step 15c) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: k3s's API audit log and OpenBao's audit device reach Loki, are kept longer than other logs, are searchable in Grafana, and a few dangerous events raise alerts through the existing Alertmanager.

Architecture: One audit policy file is passed to the API server by k3d (sandbox) and by metal/roles/k3s (production, rendered only). Alloy tails the audit file on the node, and relabels OpenBao's audit lines out of its pod log. Loki keeps job=~"audit/.*" streams longer (retention_stream), and its ruler evaluates LogQL alert rules from a ConfigMap and sends them to Alertmanager.

Tech Stack: k3s 1.37 audit policy (audit.k8s.io/v1), Loki 3.7.8 (chart 18.17.0, ruler, lokitool), Alloy, OpenBao 2.7.1, kube-prometheus-stack's Alertmanager, Grafana's dashboard sidecar, Go tests (terratest).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-28-security-logs-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• No secret value ever reaches Loki: a Secret's body is never logged (level Metadata at most for Secrets, ConfigMaps, TokenReviews, SubjectAccessReviews, ServiceAccount tokens), and OpenBao's HMAC of values stays on.
  • No level RequestResponse anywhere; stage RequestReceived omitted (omitStages).
  • Labels: job="audit/k3s" and job="audit/openbao".
  • Retention: audit 90 days (2160h) in production, other logs 30 days as today; the sandbox keeps 7 days for everything. If the measured volume says 90 days will not fit 10Gi, shorten to 60 days, then 45 or 30. Never raise the PVC.
  • A person: not system:serviceaccount:…, system:node:…, system:kube-… or system:apiserver; system:admin is a person.
  • Expected actors left out: Argo CD, ESO, the rotation CronJob, Velero, kaniop, Kyverno (their ServiceAccounts).
  • OpenBao's no-audit window is 2h; k3s's is 15m.
  • The two person alerts (exec/attach/port-forward and Secret read) are grouped by user in Alertmanager, so one tooling run sends one notification.
  • Pinned versions: Loki's chart and image stay as they are; lokitool comes from nixpkgs' grafana-loki, which must match Loki's version (3.7.8); say so beside it if it does not.
  • Never run make dev from the worktree; tests run from the main checkout after the branch is checked out there.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A secret value in an audit line. A Secret create/update by Argo CD or ESO would put the value in a Request level body if a later rule catches it before the Secret rule. Expected: the Secret rule comes first. Pinned by TestAuditPolicyRender (rule order) and TestSecurityLogsNoSecretValues (Task 5).
  2. A k3s restart or audit file rotation. Alloy must resume the rotated file without loss or repeat, and the no-audit alert must not fire. Expected: audit.log rotates at 100 MB, Alloy follows by name. Pinned by TestNodeRestart running after this branch with no AuditLogsMissing firing (Task 4's check in its last step).
  3. OpenBao's server log lines labelled as audit, or audit lines left as job="pods". Expected: only JSON lines with a type of request or response get audit/openbao. Pinned by TestSecurityLogsOpenBao (Task 2), which also checks the marker read is not under job="pods".
  4. Expected actors raising person alerts. Argo CD reading Secrets or Velero exec'ing (it does not, but kaniop and ESO read Secrets constantly) must not fire. Expected: the "person" filter drops every system:serviceaccount: user. Pinned by TestSecurityLogsQuietWhenIdle (Task 4): after the suite's start, no AuditSecretReadByPerson alert names a ServiceAccount.
  5. The ruler silently loading nothing. A LogQL typo makes Loki drop a group. Expected: every group loads and each rule's health is ok. Pinned offline by lokitool rules lint in TestSecurityLogsRules and in the sandbox by TestSecurityLogsRulesLoaded (Task 4).

docs.text:

  • Modify metal/roles/k3s/defaults/main.yml, metal/roles/k3s/tasks/*.yml: copy the policy, the same flags.
  • Modify system/loki/values.yaml, values-dev.yaml: Alloy's audit source and OpenBao relabel, retention_stream, the ruler.
  • Create system/loki/files/audit-rules.yaml, system/loki/templates/audit-rules.yaml: the rules and their ConfigMap.
  • Modify system/monitoring-system/values.yaml: the route grouping the person alerts by user.
  • Modify system/monitoring-system/templates/authorization-policy.yaml: Loki may call Alertmanager on 9093.
  • Create system/monitoring-system/templates/security-dashboard.yaml, system/monitoring-system/files/security-dashboard.json.
  • Modify platform/openbao/values.yaml: the audit device.
  • Modify flake.nix: grafana-loki (for lokitool) in the default dev shell.
  • Create test/security_logs_test.go; modify scripts/ci-check (offline tests), test/scopes.yaml.
  • Create docs/how-to-guides/security-logs.md; modify mkdocs.yml, CLAUDE.md, docs/superpowers/deferred-minors.md.

docs.title: Task 1: k3s's audit log into Loki
docs.text:
Files: - Create: metal/roles/k3s/files/audit-policy.yaml - Modify: infra/_modules/k3d/main.tf, infra/_modules/k3d/k3d.yaml, metal/roles/k3s/defaults/main.yml, the k3s role's task that writes config.yaml (copy the policy beside it) - Modify: system/loki/values.yaml (Alloy) - Test: test/security_logs_test.go

Interfaces: - Produces: on every server node, /var/log/kubernetes/audit/audit.log (JSON lines, audit.k8s.io/v1 Event); Loki streams {job="audit/k3s", node="<node>"} whose line is the raw event JSON. Later tasks' LogQL uses | json fields user_username, verb, objectRef_resource, objectRef_subresource, objectRef_namespace, objectRef_name, responseStatus_code, sourceIPs. - Produces: auditPolicyPath = "../metal/roles/k3s/files/audit-policy.yaml" and helper auditEntries(t, query string, since time.Duration) []lokiEntry (wraps lokiQuery from logs_test.go, retrying until non-empty for 5 minutes) in test/security_logs_test.go.

  • Step 1: Write the failing offline test TestAuditPolicyRender

It parses the policy file (sigs.k8s.io/yaml into a local struct of rules[].level, resources[].group/resources, verbs, users, nonResourceURLs, plus omitStages) and asserts: - omitStages contains RequestReceived; no rule has level RequestResponse. - The first rule naming secrets, configmaps, tokenreviews, subjectaccessreviews, serviceaccounts/token, pods/exec, pods/attach or pods/portforward has level Metadata, and no earlier rule matches those resources with another level than None. - Some rule at level Request names rbac.authorization.k8s.io (roles, clusterroles, rolebindings, clusterrolebindings), policyexceptions (group policies.kyverno.io), kyverno policies, admissionregistration.k8s.io, namespaces, apiextensions.k8s.io customresourcedefinitions, with verbs create, update, patch, delete. - The last rule is level: Metadata with no selectors. - infra/_modules/k3d/k3d.yaml passes --kube-apiserver-arg=audit-policy-file=/etc/rancher/k3s/audit-policy.yaml, audit-log-path=/var/log/kubernetes/audit/audit.log, audit-log-maxsize=100, audit-log-maxbackup=3, and metal/roles/k3s/defaults/main.yml's kube-apiserver-arg holds the same four values.

  • Step 2: Run it: FAIL (no file)

Run: cd test && go test -count=1 -run TestAuditPolicyRender ./...

  • Step 3: Write the policy and the wiring

  • Policy order: None rules first (the spec's read-only noise: get/list/watch by system:kube-*, system:node:* groups system:nodes; leases; endpoints, endpointslices; events; nonResourceURLs /healthz*, /readyz*, /livez*, /metrics, /version), then the Metadata rule for sensitive resources, then the Request rule, then the catch-all Metadata. A None rule must never name the sensitive resources.

  • k3d: mount the file with --volume "<abspath>:/etc/rancher/k3s/audit-policy.yaml@server:*" in main.tf beside the Gateway API manifest, and add filesha1(<policy>) to triggers_replace (a policy change rebuilds the sandbox cluster, as a k3d.yaml change does). The four flags go in k3d.yaml's extraArgs.
  • metal: copy the file to /etc/rancher/k3s/audit-policy.yaml before k3s starts (servers only); the four flags in k3s_server_config.kube-apiserver-arg.

  • Alloy: a hostPath volume /var/log/kubernetes/audit (DirectoryOrCreate, mounted read-only), a local.file_match on audit.log with labels job="audit/k3s" and node from K8S_NODE_NAME, loki.source.file into loki.write.loki (no stage.cri: the file is plain JSON). Agents have no audit file; the match finds nothing there.

  • Step 4: Run it: PASS

Run: cd test && go test -count=1 -run TestAuditPolicyRender ./...; add TestAuditPolicyRender to offline_tests in scripts/ci-check.

  • Step 5: Write the sandbox test TestSecurityLogsK3sExec

logPod(t, "audit") (from logs_test.go), then printTo a marker. Assert within 5 minutes that {job="audit/k3s"} | json | objectRef_subresource="exec" | objectRef_name="audit" returns a line whose user_username is the kubeconfig's user (system:admin in k3d) and whose objectRef_namespace is logs-test.

  • Step 6: Commit, then scripts/ci-check all; the sandbox run is Task 5's.

docs.title: Task 2: OpenBao's audit device
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: platform/openbao/values.yaml, system/loki/values.yaml (Alloy's loki.process "pods") - Test: test/security_logs_test.go

Interfaces: - Produces: Loki streams {job="audit/openbao", namespace="openbao", pod=…}, line = OpenBao's audit JSON (type, auth.display_name, auth.policies, request.path, request.operation, request.remote_address, error). Pod log lines of OpenBao that are not audit stay job="pods". - Consumes: auditEntries (Task 1).

  • Step 1: Write the sandbox test TestSecurityLogsOpenBao

With the admin role (the helper the secrets tests use to write OpenBao), write secret/smoke/audit-marker with a random value, read it back, then assert within 5 minutes: - {job="audit/openbao"} |= "secret/data/smoke/audit-marker" has a response line for the read. - No line in {namespace="openbao"} over the last 10 minutes contains the random value (fetch and strings.Contains in Go; never put the value in a query or an argument). - {job="pods", namespace="openbao"} |= "secret/data/smoke/audit-marker" is empty. Delete the marker in t.Cleanup.

  • Step 2: Declare the device

In the server config: audit "file" "stdout" { options = { file_path = "/dev/stdout" } } (OpenBao 2.x declarative audit devices). Check on 2.7.1 by rendering and, on the sandbox, bao audit list with the admin role. If 2.7.1 refuses config-declared devices, add an initialize "audit" stanza with request sys/audit/stdout (type file, options.file_path=/dev/stdout) instead, and note that a running OpenBao needs it once by hand (the guide says how).

  • Step 3: Relabel in Alloy

In loki.process "pods" after stage.cri: a stage.match with selector {namespace="openbao", container="openbao"} |~ "^\\{.*\"type\":\"(request|response)\"" whose stage.static_labels sets job = "audit/openbao".

  • Step 4: Commit. The sandbox run is Task 5's.

docs.title: Task 3: retention
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: system/loki/values.yaml, system/loki/values-dev.yaml - Test: test/security_logs_test.go

  • Step 1: Write the offline test TestSecurityLogsRetention

Render system/loki (scripts/render-chart system/loki) and system/loki dev; from the Loki config in the rendered ConfigMap assert limits_config.retention_period is 720h (production) / 168h (dev), and retention_stream holds one entry with selector {job=~"audit/.*"} and period 2160h (production) / 168h (dev). Add it to offline_tests.

  • Step 2: Run: FAIL. Step 3: set the values (dev restates the whole retention_stream list: Helm replaces lists). Step 4: Run: PASS. Step 5: Commit.

The volume measurement and the final period are Task 5's last steps.

docs.title: Task 4: alert rules, the ruler and Alertmanager
docs.text:
Files: - Create: system/loki/files/audit-rules.yaml, system/loki/templates/audit-rules.yaml - Modify: system/loki/values.yaml (ruler), system/monitoring-system/values.yaml, system/monitoring-system/templates/authorization-policy.yaml, flake.nix - Test: test/security_logs_test.go

Interfaces: - Produces: ConfigMap loki/loki-audit-rules, key audit-rules.yaml (Prometheus-style rule groups with LogQL), mounted at /etc/loki/rules/fake/ (tenant fake, auth_enabled: false); every alert carries labels severity and source="audit", the person alerts also user, and an annotation summary naming the user, the object and a LogQL query to paste in Explore. - Alert names (exact): AuditExecByPerson (warning), AuditSecretReadByPerson (warning), AuditClusterAdminBinding (critical), AuditAnonymousAllowed (critical), AuditManyDenied (warning), AuditPolicyExceptionChanged (warning), OpenBaoRootToken (critical), OpenBaoManyFailedLogins (warning), OpenBaoConfigChanged (critical), AuditLogsMissing (critical, two rules: job="audit/k3s" over 15m, job="audit/openbao" over 2h).

  • Step 1: Write the offline test TestSecurityLogsRules

Render system/loki; extract the ConfigMap's audit-rules.yaml to a temp file; run lokitool rules lint <file> and lokitool rules check <file> (both exit 0); parse it and assert the set of alert names equals the list above, each with its severity, source="audit", and a non-empty summary; the person rules' expressions contain the person filter (a regex excluding system:serviceaccount:.*|system:node:.*|system:kube-.*|system:apiserver) and AuditClusterAdminBinding/AuditPolicyExceptionChanged exclude Argo CD's ServiceAccounts. Also render system/monitoring-system and assert a route matching source="audit" and alertname=~"AuditExecByPerson|AuditSecretReadByPerson" with group_by: [alertname, user], and that allow admits cluster.local/ns/loki/sa/loki on port 9093. Add to offline_tests.

  • Step 2: Run: FAIL.

  • Step 3: Write the rules, the ruler and the wiring

  • Rules: count_over_time / sum by (user_username, …) over the window that fits each row (5m for "many"; [5m] > 0 for single events, for: 0m); absent_over_time for AuditLogsMissing. Expected actors are excluded by ServiceAccount in every rule (namespaces argocd, external-secrets, secrets-rotation, velero, kanidm (kaniop: check its namespace), kyverno). OpenBao's "known flows": requests whose auth.policies are only the rotator, writer, infra or a store's read policy are excluded; admin is not. Thresholds for the "many" rules start at 20 in 5 minutes and are tuned in Task 5.

  • Ruler in Loki's values: loki.rulerConfig with storage: {type: local, local: {directory: /etc/loki/rules}}, rule_path: /var/loki/rules-temp, alertmanager_url: http://monitoring-system-kube-pro-alertmanager.monitoring-system:9093, enable_api: true; the ConfigMap mounted through singleBinary.extraVolumes/extraVolumeMounts. (Check the chart: if the monolithic target needs ruler enabled explicitly, do that.)

Keep 90 days if it fits; else 60, else 45, else 30. Write the numbers and the period in the PR body, values.yaml beside retention_stream, and CLAUDE.md's production line. Tune the "many" thresholds from the same idle hour.

docs.title: Supply Chain Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Running images are watched for CVEs and baked-in secrets, lab's image is signed with its SBOM and checked by Kyverno, and the workflows are checked by zizmor.

Architecture: - A new component system/trivy-operator holds the operator, its accepted findings and three Prometheus alerts. - lab-image.yaml signs keyless with cosign and attests a Syft SBOM. - system/kyverno gains a production-only ImageValidatingPolicy. - A new basic check workflows runs zizmor offline.

Tech Stack: - trivy-operator chart 0.36.x (the latest at the time of the work); - cosign 3.1.x and Syft 1.55.x in GitHub Actions, through their pinned actions; - zizmor 1.31.1 from unstable; - Kyverno 1.19 policies.kyverno.io/v1 ImageValidatingPolicy; - Go tests in test/ (terratest).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-29-supply-chain-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Latest stable, pinned exactly. Actions are pinned by commit digest with the version in a comment, as in checks.yaml.
  • Trivy Operator scans only vulnerability and exposedSecret. Config audit, RBAC, infra assessment, compliance and SBOM generation are off.
  • ignoreUnfixed: false, severities HIGH,CRITICAL.
  • Three alerts, warning and for: 1h: ImageCriticalVulnerability, ImageCriticalVulnerabilityUnfixed, ImageExposedSecret. HIGH findings alert on nothing.
  • An accepted finding has a reason and an expiry. An expired one no longer applies.
  • scanJobsConcurrentLimit: 1 and memory limits in the sandbox.
  • lab's signature: issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com, subject https://github.com/duongle-steven/homelab/.github/workflows/lab-image.yaml@refs/heads/master. Keyless: no new secret in cli/internal/rotate/catalog.yaml.
  • The lab policy is rendered in production only, in Audit.
  • Every new namespace gets:
  • an allow AuthorizationPolicy;
  • an egress entry if it calls out;
  • Pod Security restricted or a PolicyException with homelab/reason;
  • a test/scopes.yaml entry;
  • homelab/backup on any claim.
  • No token in arguments or logs. The test's cosign key password is passed through the environment, never as a flag value.
  • scripts/ci-check all passes before each commit. make dev runs only from the main checkout.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• An acceptance whose expiry has passed must stop silencing its CVE.
  • Trivy's .trivyignore exp: handles this; TestTrivyOperatorRender asserts every entry has a future exp:.
  • The render test also asserts the file is the one the operator mounts (trivy.ignoreFile).
  • Two workloads sharing one image must not double-alert or hide each other.
  • The alerts group by namespace and resource_name from the report's metric labels.
  • TestTrivyOperatorRender asserts the by clause.
  • A scan Job that is OOM-killed in the sandbox leaves no report and no alert, silently.
  • TestTrivyOperator asserts a report exists for a known workload.
  • Task 4 measures the scan Jobs' peak memory.
  • The lab policy's subject must pin refs/heads/master, not a regex accepting any branch.
  • A branch's run would otherwise pass.
  • TestLabImagePolicy asserts the exact string.
  • A zizmor finding that is ignored without a reason.
  • The workflows check's test asserts every .github/zizmor.yml ignore carries a comment.

docs.title: Task 3: system/trivy-operator
docs.text:
Files: - Create: system/trivy-operator/, with: - Chart.yaml (the trivy-operator dependency from https://aquasecurity.github.io/helm-charts/, latest); - values.yaml, values-dev.yaml; - files/trivyignore (header comment: one CVE per line, exp:YYYY-MM-DD, and a # reason line above each); - templates/authorization-policy.yaml, templates/prometheus-rules.yaml. - values.yaml sets the scanners per the Global Constraints, ignoreUnfixed: false, severity: HIGH,CRITICAL, operator.metricsVulnIdEnabled: true, exposedSecretsMetrics, the ServiceMonitor, and trivy.ignoreFile from files/trivyignore (wrapper template or --set-file, as the chart allows). - Modify: - system/argocd/values.yaml and values-dev.yaml: system/trivy-operator in the root generators; - system/egress/values.yaml: trivy-operator: [{port: 443}] # the vulnerability DB and registries; - test/scopes.yaml: system/trivy-operator/** → TrivyOperator; - system/monitoring-system/files/security-dashboard.json: a row "Images" with findings by severity, fixed or not; - scripts/check-backup-groups, if the chart renders a claim. - Test: test/trivy_operator_test.go.

Interfaces: - Produces: - namespace trivy-operator; - alerts named as the Global Constraints say, labelled source=trivy; - renderTrivyOperator(t, env, expr string) string for Task 4.

  • Step 1: Write the failing test. TestTrivyOperatorRender for both envs asserts:
  • only vulnerability and exposedSecret are enabled;
  • ignoreUnfixed is false;

docs.title: Task 4: sandbox proof, baseline and docs
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: test/trivy_operator_test.go (TestTrivyOperator), test/supply_chain_test.go (TestSupplyChain), system/trivy-operator/files/trivyignore (the accepted baseline). - Create: docs/how-to-guides/supply-chain.md. - Modify: mkdocs.yml nav, and CLAUDE.md: - roadmap 15e done; - the blog's signature waits for its pipeline, with a key in OpenBao; - "Before the first production deploy": lab's signature is verified only after the first signed release, and the operator's scans on three nodes are unmeasured.

docs.title: Step 12a-1: staging nodes Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Three NixOS VMs in WSL, installed by nixie from one node definition shared with production, joined into a three-server k3s cluster with kube-vip and rook-ceph, upgraded in place one node at a time, and measured; metal/ (Ansible) removed.

Architecture: Upstream nixos's infra/_modules/metal flake (NixOS configuration, disko, profiles) and its Terragrunt unit infra/<env>/metal (hooks: nixie, lab cluster enroll, lab cluster kubeconfig) are ported and adapted to this repository's k3s choices. Staging's machines are libvirt VMs created by an OpenTofu unit infra/staging/vms on a libvirt NAT network whose DHCP gives fixed leases by MAC; nixie answers their PXE boot as a proxyDHCP. A new lab cluster upgrade rebuilds the nodes in place, one at a time.

Tech Stack: NixOS 26.05 (k3s 1.37 from nixos-unstable's k3s_1_37), disko, nixie, nixos-anywhere, OpenTofu + Terragrunt, libvirt (provider dmacvicar/libvirt 0.9.9), Go (cli/, upstream's internal/cluster), rook-ceph.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-31-staging-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• One node definition for staging and production (infra/_modules/metal/flake); metal/, nix develop .#metal, make metal and make clean's PXE line are removed in this plan.
  • Installed by nixie (PXE), never by nixos-anywhere alone or a prebuilt image.
  • VMs: 3 × 3.5 GB (3584 MiB), 2 vCPUs, zram swap. If the core does not fit: drop apps → squeeze the core (OSD toward 900 MB) → 3.75 GB per VM with WSL at 12 GB → WSL 13 GB last. Three nodes always.
  • Staging never runs with the sandbox: make staging refuses while k3d-homelab-dev-server-0 runs, make dev refuses while a staging VM runs; both refuse when C: has less than 30 GB free.
  • Latest stable, pinned exactly: Gateway API v1.7.0 (sandbox's k3d too), kube-vip v1.3.1, libvirt provider 0.9.9, nixie by commit in flake.lock; k3s 1.37 (k3s_1_37, matching the sandbox's rancher/k3s:v1.37.1-k3s1).
  • This repository's k3s choices, not upstream's: ServiceLB on; kube-vip serves the API VIP and only Services of class kube-vip.io/kube-vip-class; audit policy and flags (15c); --secrets-encryption; control-plane metrics (etcd-expose-metrics, controller-manager/scheduler bind-address=0.0.0.0, kube-proxy metrics-bind-address); disable: traefik, local-storage, gateway-api-crd; disable-helm-controller.
  • infra/<env>/cluster/config.json keeps its format and gains init_host; machines live in infra/<env>/metal/hosts.json (mac_address, ip, disk). Production's MACs stay placeholders.
  • Changes to ~/nixos-config (outside the repo) are shown to the user and made only after their yes.
  • Never make dev/make staging from a worktree; never print tokens (the k3s join token goes over SFTP, as upstream).

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• A VM that PXE-boots but whose MAC is not in hosts.json: nixie must ignore it, not install something — Task 3's test boots no foreign VM, so the review checks nixie's flags.
  • make staging with a node already installed: nothing reinstalls it (machine_id_hash / state), only the upgrade runs — Task 4's Step 3 and Task 5's Step 3.
  • An upgrade that leaves a node NotReady or Ceph unhealthy: lab cluster upgrade stops before the next node — Task 5's TestUpgradeStopsOnUnhealthy.
  • WSL memory: a run that would push WSL into swap thrash — Task 7 records free memory and swap per phase.
  • The VIP while its holder is down: the API answers through the VIP from another node — Task 6's TestStagingVIPMoves.

docs.title: Task 1: The node flake (offline)
docs.text:
Files: - Create: infra/_modules/metal/flake/{flake.nix,flake.lock,default.nix,configuration.nix,disks.nix,authorized_keys}, profiles/{installer,k3s-server,kube-vip,network,rook-ceph,zram}.nix (from git show upstream/nixos:infra/_modules/metal/flake/...) - Create: infra/_modules/metal/{main.tf,variables.tf,versions.tf} (upstream's: writes flake/hosts.json and flake/cluster.json, both git-ignored) - Move: metal/roles/k3s/files/audit-policy.yaml → infra/_modules/metal/flake/audit-policy.yaml - Modify: infra/sandbox/cluster/terragrunt.hcl:11, infra/_modules/k3d/{main.tf:33,k3d.yaml:38} (new path, Gateway API v1.7.0), test/security_logs_test.go:28-29,194-197, test/scopes.yaml:71 - Test: test/metal_test.go

The flake reads cluster.json = the env's config.json (fields init_host, vip, network).

  • Step 1: Write the failing tests in test/metal_test.go (offline, like TestAuditPolicyRender): evaluate the flake with a fixture hosts.json/cluster.json (3 hosts, init_host the first) through nix eval --json path:<tmp copy>#nixosConfigurations.<host>.config.services.k3s:
  • TestMetalK3sFlags: clusterInit true only on init_host; others serverAddr == "https://<vip>:6443"; extraFlags contain --secrets-encryption, --node-ip=<ip>, --tls-san=<vip>, every flag of the audit set (the list TestAuditPolicyRender asserts today for metal/roles/k3s); disable equals ["traefik","local-storage","gateway-api-crd"] (servicelb absent); package.version starts with 1.37..
  • TestMetalKubeVip: the kube-vip manifest's image is ghcr.io/kube-vip/kube-vip:v1.3.1, env svc_enable=true, and the loadBalancerClass filter lb_class_only=true with class kube-vip.io/kube-vip-class; no kube-vip-cloud-controller manifest.
  • TestMetalZram: zramSwap.enable true on every host.

  • Step 2: cd test && go test -run 'TestMetal' ./... → FAIL (no flake).
  • Step 3: Port and adapt. Copy upstream's flake; nixpkgs nixos-26.05 plus nixpkgs-unstable for services.k3s.package = k3s_1_37; replace upstream's extraFlags/disable with the constraints' set (audit flags from metal/roles/k3s/defaults/main.yml:30-37, the policy file through environment.etc."rancher/k3s/audit-policy.yaml", log dir /var/log/kubernetes/audit); kube-vip: drop the cloud controller and its pool, add lb_class_only/ lb_class_name; Gateway API manifest v1.7.0 with its hash; profiles/zram.nix (zramSwap.enable = true, memoryPercent = 50); authorized_keys holds the workstation's public key (~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub, a public key, not a secret). .gitignore: infra/_modules/metal/flake/{hosts,cluster}.json.
  • Step 4: go test -run 'TestMetal|TestAuditPolicyRender' ./... → PASS; scripts/ci-check go infra lint → pass.
  • Step 5: Commit feat(metal): the NixOS node flake from upstream nixos, with this repository's k3s.

docs.title: Task 3: lab cluster enroll and lab cluster kubeconfig
docs.text:
Task 4's hooks call these, so they come first.

Files: - Create: cli/internal/cluster/*.go and cli/internal/cli/cluster_{enroll,kubeconfig}.go with their tests, from upstream/nixos (module path github.com/duongle-steven/homelab/cli), go.mod gains github.com/pkg/sftp and golang.org/x/crypto/ssh at their latest versions.

docs.title: Task 4: Staging's VMs and the nixie install (the risk: the first live task)
docs.text:
Files: - Outside the repo (user approves the diff first): ~/nixos-config: virtualisation.libvirtd.enable = true;, users.users.nixos.extraGroups = [ "docker" "libvirtd" ];, then sudo nixos-rebuild switch. - Create: infra/_modules/staging-vms/{main.tf,variables.tf,versions.tf}, infra/staging/vms/terragrunt.hcl, infra/staging/metal/{terragrunt.hcl,hosts.json}, infra/staging/cluster/config.json - Modify: infra/root.hcl (staging: local encrypted state like the sandbox)

Interfaces: - Produces: libvirt network homelab-staging (NAT, 192.168.122.0/24-style range of the builder's choice, DHCP with one fixed lease per hosts.json MAC, no PXE options: nixie adds them), domains <host> (3584 MiB, 2 vCPUs, boot order network then disk, a sparse qcow2 system disk ≥ 80 GB and the rook-data partition on it per disks.nix). infra/staging/cluster/config.json = production's format + init_host, staging's VIP and service_vips in the libvirt network, domain a *.nip.io name for the VIP. - infra/staging/metal/terragrunt.hcl = upstream's (hooks nixie, lab cluster enroll --environment staging, lab cluster kubeconfig --environment staging --output infra/staging/kubeconfig.yaml), depending on vms.

  • Step 1: One VM first. With the sandbox stopped (k3d cluster stop homelab-dev) and hosts.json holding one host, cd infra/staging && terragrunt run --all apply: the VM PXE-boots nixie's installer, nixie installs it, the enroll hook passes for a one-node cluster. If nixie cannot answer PXE on the libvirt bridge, stop and bring the failure to the user before working around it (the install method is the user's decision).
  • Step 2: ssh admin@<ip> hostname → the host's name; ssh admin@<ip> systemctl is-active k3s → active.
  • Step 3: Three hosts in hosts.json; apply again → kubectl --kubeconfig infra/staging/kubeconfig.yaml get nodes lists three Ready control-plane nodes; a second apply reinstalls nothing (nixie's recorded machine_id_hash).
  • Step 4: Commit feat(staging): three libvirt VMs installed by nixie and joined into k3s.

docs.title: Task 5: lab cluster upgrade (in place, one node at a time)
docs.text:
Files: - Create: cli/internal/cluster/upgrade.go, upgrade_test.go, cli/internal/cli/cluster_upgrade.go - Modify: infra/staging/metal/terragrunt.hcl (an after_hook "upgrade" after enroll), and production's unit the same (infra/production/metal/, created here with placeholder hosts.json)

Interfaces: - Produces: lab cluster upgrade --environment <env>; Upgrade(ctx, environment string, progress io.Writer) error; internally an interface upgrader with drain(node), rebuild(node) (nixos-rebuild switch --flake path:infra/_modules/metal/flake#<name> --target-host root@<ip>), ready(node), healthy() (every node Ready and, once a CephCluster exists, its status.ceph.health == "HEALTH_OK"), uncordon(node). - Behaviour: skips a node whose /run/current-system already equals the flake's build for it (nix build the toplevel, compare store paths over SSH); otherwise drain → rebuild → ready (10 min) → healthy (15 min) → uncordon; stops at the first failure, leaving that node cordoned and naming it.

  • Step 1: Failing tests with a fake upgrader: TestUpgradeSkipsCurrentNodes (no drain when current), TestUpgradeOneAtATime (drain/rebuild/ready/healthy/uncordon per node, the seed first, then the joiners by name), TestUpgradeStopsOnUnhealthy (healthy fails on node 1 → node 2 untouched, error names node 1).
  • Step 2: FAIL → implement → PASS (make -C cli test check).
  • Step 3: Live: change a harmless option (environment.etc."homelab-upgrade-probe".text), cd infra/staging && terragrunt run --all apply → the three nodes are drained and rebuilt in turn, ssh admin@<ip> cat /etc/homelab-upgrade-probe on each; a second run upgrades nothing. Revert the probe.
  • Step 4: Commit feat(cli): lab cluster upgrade rebuilds the nodes in place, one at a time.

docs.text:

docs.title: Staging platform (12a-2) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Argo CD, the platform and as many apps as fit run on staging through production's deploy path, and a release that changes what staging runs needs staging's mark.

Architecture: A shared values layer (values-local.yaml) gives staging and the sandbox the local CA and the tests' fixtures; staging's Argo CD is production's set minus an exclusion list in system/argocd/values-staging.yaml, bootstrapped from GitHub branch staging, then switched to ops/homelab on staging's Forgejo. make staging runs the suite there and writes a GitHub commit status staging; lab infra forgejo verify derives the gated paths and looks for that mark.

Tech Stack: Helm, Argo CD ApplicationSets, OpenTofu/Terragrunt, Go (cli/, test/), POSIX sh, yq, gh.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-01-staging-platform-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Prerequisite: the pull request removing ollama is merged into dev, and this branch is rebased on it.
  • Ideally staging is production; the reduction is one exclusion list, nothing else differs except values-staging.yaml where staging must.
  • Layers: production values.yaml; staging values.yaml, values-local.yaml, values-staging.yaml; sandbox values.yaml, values-local.yaml, values-dev.yaml.
  • The sandbox's renders are identical before and after the split.
  • Fallback order: drop apps; squeeze the core (Ceph's OSD toward 900 MB, Prometheus off); 3.75 GB per VM with WSL at 12 GB; WSL at 13 GB. Three nodes and Istio stay. Whatever is left out goes in the exclusion list; 12a-2 ships with what fits.
  • Gated paths: infra/staging/release-paths.yaml plus every component and app staging deploys (production's set minus the proved commit's exclusion list). Compared against ops/homelab's master on Forgejo; no Forgejo: all changed.
  • The mark needs every test green, the destructive ones included (TestBackupRestore, TestNodeRestart, TestRotation).
  • CLAUDE.md's rules: pinned latest versions, config.json for environment settings, the secrets catalog, backup labels, PolicyExceptions, mesh policies, test/scopes.yaml, deferred minors. Never print secrets; never run make staging or make dev from a worktree; staging and the sandbox never run together.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• A release where only a docs file changed after the mark: verify passes without a rerun (Task 6's TestStagingGateAcceptsEarlierMark).
  • A release that changes an excluded app only: no mark needed; a release that empties the exclusion list: every component counts (Task 6's TestStagingGateExcludedApp, TestStagingGateUsesProvedExclusions).
  • A first production install with no Forgejo: everything counts as changed, so the mark is required (Task 6's TestStagingGateNoDeployedCommit).
  • --skip-staging with an empty or blank reason: refused (Task 6's TestSkipStagingNeedsReason).
  • A staging run interrupted after the switch to Forgejo: the next make staging keeps Argo CD on Forgejo, never back to the seed (Task 3: choose-values.sh's existing rule, asserted by TestStagingBootstrapKeepsForgejo).

docs.title: Task 1: The shared values layer
docs.text:
Files: - Create: <component>/values-local.yaml for each of the 17 components with a values-dev.yaml, holding what both non-production environments need: the local CA and its trust (cert-manager's homelab-dev-ca issuer named letsencrypt-prod, trust-manager's bundle, SSL_CERT_DIR), the tests' fixtures (Kanidm's smoke client and dev-admin, Woodpecker's admin, the rotation CronJob on lab's image built from the checkout), and the S3 stand-in for Velero (versitygw). What only the one-node sandbox needs (retentions, sizes, worker counts, the hostpath CSI, the CoreDNS rewrite of *.127-0-0-1.nip.io, retries) stays in values-dev.yaml. - Modify: scripts/render-chart (load values-local.yaml for every env but prod, before values-<env>.yaml), scripts/env-values (accept staging), system/argocd/values-dev.yaml (root's valueFiles: values.yaml, values-local.yaml, values-dev.yaml), scripts/check-* that list values files - Create: scripts/compare-renders (renders every component and app for an env at two revisions with scripts/render-chart, prints differing names; exit 1 on any) - Test: test/values_layers_test.go

Interfaces: - Produces: scripts/render-chart <dir> staging renders values.yaml, values-local.yaml, values-staging.yaml; scripts/env-values <prod|dev|staging> <root|apps>.

  • Step 1: Write the failing test

TestValuesLayers: for system/cert-manager, scripts/render-chart with env staging contains the homelab-dev-ca issuer and with env prod does not; for system/monitoring-system, the staging render keeps production's Prometheus retention while the dev render keeps the sandbox's one day (assert both values from the files).

  • Step 2: Run it: cd test && direnv exec .. go test -run TestValuesLayers -count=1 . → FAIL (no layer).
  • Step 3: Split the 17 files and teach the scripts and values-dev.yaml the layer.
  • Step 4: Run TestValuesLayers → PASS; scripts/compare-renders dev origin/dev HEAD → no differences.

docs.text:
Files: - Create: system/argocd/values-staging.yaml (production's ApplicationSets restated where Helm replaces lists: root's directories with staging's extra exclude: true entries under one comment naming the machine they were sized for; apps' files likewise (an excluded app: exclude: true if Argo CD's git files generator accepts it, else apps listed as in values-dev.yaml); valueFiles values.yaml, values-local.yaml, values-staging.yaml; global.publicGateway: gateway, global.devCA: "true"; the sandbox's retries) - Create: infra/staging/{openbao,secrets,argocd}/terragrunt.hcl (like the sandbox's; argocd: values = "values-staging.yaml", environment = "staging", seed = "values-staging.yaml", seed_revision = "staging") - Modify: infra/_modules/argocd/{main.tf,bootstrap.sh} (input seed_revision: when choose-values.sh picks the seed and seed_revision is set, the render's Forgejo repository becomes seed_repository at that revision, through set-revision.sh; production keeps values-seed.yaml) - Modify: Makefile staging (force-push HEAD to GitHub branch staging, apply infra/staging, wait for Argo CD's sync, lab infra forgejo sync then push --env staging, apply infra/staging/argocd again to switch; drop the hand-applied rook-ceph render) - Test: test/argocd_revision_test.go

docs.text:
Files: - Modify: system/argocd/values-staging.yaml (the exclusion list as measured), values-staging.yaml of components squeezed by the fallback order, infra/staging/vms (memory, only if the fallback reaches it), platform/*/values-local.yaml where a fixture is missing on staging, cli/internal/rotate/catalog.yaml (environments gains staging where an entry runs there), Makefile (staging runs the suite: ENV=staging, the main groups then BackupRestore|NodeRestart|NodePowerCut|Rotation alone, like make dev) - Modify: docs/installation/staging.md (what runs, the exclusion list and why, the measured table)

docs.title: Task 6: The mark and the release gate
docs.text:
Files: - Create: infra/staging/release-paths.yaml (globs: infra/_modules/metal/**, infra/_modules/argocd/**, infra/staging/**, infra/production/**, system/argocd/**, system/istio-system/**, system/rook-ceph/**, cli/internal/forgejo/**, cli/internal/cluster/**, Makefile) - Create: cli/internal/guard/staging.go, scripts/staging-mark - Modify: cli/internal/guard/{verify.go,github.go} (CommitStatus), cli/internal/cli/infra_forgejo.go (--skip-staging), Makefile (staging ends with scripts/staging-mark HEAD only when every test passed) - Test: cli/internal/guard/staging_test.go, test/release_paths_test.go

Interfaces: - Produces: - func GatedPaths(root, provedCommit string) ([]string, error): release-paths.yaml's globs plus system/<x>/**, platform/<x>/**, apps/<x>.yaml, apps/<x>/** for every component production deploys that the proved commit's values-staging.yaml does not exclude - func StagingGate(ctx, root, repository, deployed, release string, candidates []string, gh GitHub) error: deployed empty means everything changed; passes when a candidate (newest first) has status staging success and git diff --name-only <candidate> <release> touches none of GatedPaths(root, candidate), or when git diff --name-only <deployed> <release> touches none - func (g GitHub) CommitStatus(ctx, repository, sha, context string) (string, error) (state, "" if none) - scripts/staging-mark <sha>: gh api repos/<repo>/statuses/<sha> with context staging, state success - verify --skip-staging=<reason>: refused when blank; prints the reason and records it as status staging success with description skipped: <reason> on the release commit through scripts/staging-mark

  • Step 1: Write the failing tests in staging_test.go (a git fixture repo and a fake GitHub):
  • TestStagingGateAcceptsEarlierMark: marked commit, then a docs-only commit → pass
  • TestStagingGateRefusesUnmarked: system/rook-ceph/values.yaml changed, no mark → error naming the path
  • TestStagingGateExcludedApp: only apps/excalidraw.yaml changed, excalidraw excluded → pass
  • TestStagingGateUsesProvedExclusions: the release empties the exclusion list but the proved commit excluded excalidraw → excalidraw's change still needs no mark from that proof
  • TestStagingGateNoDeployedCommit: deployed empty, no mark → error
  • TestSkipStagingNeedsReason: --skip-staging=" " → error

and TestReleasePathsExist in test/release_paths_test.go: every glob in release-paths.yaml matches a file. - [ ] Step 2: Run cd cli && direnv exec .. go test ./internal/guard/ -run 'TestStagingGate|TestSkipStaging' → FAIL. - [ ] Step 3: Implement; Verify reads the deployed commit from ops/homelab's master (the session sync uses; empty when Forgejo is absent) and the candidates git rev-list --first-parent <deployed>..<pull head>. - [ ] Step 4: Run make -C cli test check and go test -run TestReleasePathsExist ./test/ → PASS. - [ ] Step 5: Commit feat(cli): verify needs staging's mark for a release that changes what staging runs.

docs.title: Testbed (12a-2) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Turn the workstation's "staging" into a light testbed that proves what needs several nodes, make a real staging optional, prove Argo CD reading Forgejo on the sandbox, and make the release gate name which environment proved a release.

Architecture: New commits on top of the branch's earlier attempt, which stays as history: rename first, then remove what the design drops, then the testbed's first layer, the generic gate, the sandbox's deploy test, the measured layers and the docs. The testbed's Argo CD syncs GitHub branch testbed from an allow-list in system/argocd/values-testbed.yaml; the gate reads infra/<env>/release-paths.yaml and system/argocd/values-<env>.yaml for the environment production's config.json names.

Tech Stack: Helm, Argo CD ApplicationSets, OpenTofu/Terragrunt, NixOS, libvirt, Go (cli/, test/), POSIX sh, yq, gh.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-02-testbed-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Environments: sandbox required; one of testbed or staging proves releases; a staging never loads values-local.yaml.
  • Values: production and staging load values.yaml (then values-staging.yaml); testbed values.yaml, values-local.yaml, values-testbed.yaml; sandbox values.yaml, values-local.yaml, values-dev.yaml.
  • The sandbox's renders stay identical (check with scripts/render-all; apps' and Kanidm's differ run to run).
  • Testbed: three VMs of 3.5 GB, 2 vCPUs, at most 4 vCPUs; WSL 13 GB with 4 GB swap; no image cache; no Forgejo; no OpenBao.
  • Layer bar: from make testbed-fresh, over 30 minutes after the last Application is healthy: no k3s restart, no etcd leader change, no API or lease error, WSL at least 2 GB available (revised by the user 2026-11-03; heartbeat warnings are counted).
  • Layer 1 is the floor: if it fails at 4 vCPUs, stop and ask the user; do not relax the bar or ship without it.
  • A run stopped for low memory is not restarted without asking. Stop by hand when WSL falls under 1.5 GB.
  • Live runs only from the main checkout; testbed and sandbox never together; ci-check all only with both stopped.
  • release_proof is required in production's config.json; --skip-proof=<reason> needs a non-blank reason.
  • CLAUDE.md's rules apply: pinned versions, config.json, catalog, backup labels, policy, mesh, test/scopes.yaml, deferred minors.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• make testbed-fresh on a cluster that never came up, or with the VMs stopped: testbed-clean still removes everything (Task 1 keeps staging-clean's recipe; run live in Task 6).
  • A renamed path left behind (infra/staging, scripts/staging-*, TestStaging, branch staging): no reference survives outside the old specs and plans (Task 1's TestNoStagingLeftovers).
  • Production's config.json without release_proof, or naming an unknown environment: verify refuses and says what to set (Task 4's TestLoadReleaseProof).
  • A release that only changes something in not_run, and one that brings it back: the first needs no mark, the second does (Task 4's TestProofGateNotRun).
  • The temporary Application of the deploy test left behind by a failing run: the next run still passes and nothing stays (Task 5's cleanup in TestForgejoArgoCDSyncs).

docs.title: Task 1: Rename staging to testbed
docs.text:
Files: - Move: infra/staging → infra/testbed; infra/_modules/staging-vms → infra/_modules/testbed-vms; scripts/staging-{guard,mark,nixie,trust,wake} → scripts/testbed-*; system/*/values-staging.yaml → values-testbed.yaml; test/staging_test.go → test/testbed_test.go; test/staging_nixie_test.go → test/testbed_scripts_test.go; docs/installation/staging.md → docs/installation/testbed.md - Modify: Makefile (targets testbed, testbed-fresh, testbed-clean, testbed-stop, ENV=testbed, branch testbed), scripts/render-chart (values-local.yaml only for dev and testbed), test/env_helpers_test.go (envDirs key testbed), test/scopes.yaml, mkdocs.yml, .gitignore, the comments in values-local.yaml files ("staging and the sandbox" → "the sandbox and the testbed"), cli/internal/rotate/catalog.go if it names staging - Test: test/release_paths_test.go, test/values_layers_test.go

Interfaces: - Produces: environment name testbed; make testbed*; scripts/testbed-*; system/*/values-testbed.yaml; infra/testbed/.

  • Step 1: Write the failing tests. TestNoStagingLeftovers runs git grep -il staging excluding docs/superpowers/, docs/installation/testbed.md, CLAUDE.md, the gate's cli/internal/guard/, and asserts nothing else is listed. In TestValuesLayers, env staging renders no homelab-dev-ca Bundle while env testbed and dev do.
  • Step 2: Run cd test && direnv exec .. go test -run 'TestNoStagingLeftovers|TestValuesLayers' -count=1 . Expected: FAIL.
  • Step 3: Rename with git mv, update every reference, and change render-chart's layer condition. The .state/staging directory is local: make testbed-clean must find .state/testbed, so destroy the current VMs first with the old make staging-clean before moving anything. Delete GitHub branch staging (git push origin --delete staging), which this branch's runs created.
  • Step 4: Run the same tests. Expected: PASS. Then direnv exec . make -C cli test check and direnv exec . env -u HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE make -C infra check. Expected: exit 0.
  • Step 5: Commit refactor(testbed): staging on the workstation becomes the testbed.

docs.title: Task 2: Remove what the design drops
