docs.title: Step 12a-3 power Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: The homelab comes back by itself after every node loses power, and stops and restarts in order when someone chooses to.

Architecture: lab cluster shutdown (Go, from the workstation, beside cluster.Upgrade) records what it changes in a ConfigMap marker, stops what runs and powers the nodes off. One script in the node flake undoes it, run by a systemd unit at boot on every node and over SSH by lab cluster startup. Live tests on the testbed cut all three VMs and prove recovery.

Tech Stack: Go (cobra, cli/internal/cluster), NixOS (writeShellApplication, systemd), bash, Go tests with terratest (test/), virsh.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-power-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• From the main checkout only. Never beside the sandbox; C: keeps 30 GB free; stop by hand when WSL falls under 1.5 GB; a run stopped for low memory is not restarted without asking the user.
  • Before any testbed or sandbox command: pgrep -x terragrunt; pgrep -x make. No foreground sleep (timeout N tail -0f /dev/null, or background). Absolute KUBECONFIG paths. Never make -n.
  • virsh destroy only on homelab-1|2|3.
  • Do not run scripts/ci-check all while the sandbox or testbed is up.
  • Names: marker ConfigMap kube-system/cluster-shutdown; label homelab/power-keep: "true"; script and command on the nodes cluster-startup; unit cluster-startup.service; probe namespace power-probe.
  • Values from the spec: Job wait 5 minutes by default; noout off when every OSD is back or after 30 minutes at most; recovery limit 30 minutes; startup acts when a majority of the marker's nodes are on a new boot; CloudNativePG measurement at 2 vCPUs.
  • Commit trailers: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>, Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DkFEsNWboxteok4WLPJh6q.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• A second lab cluster shutdown after a partial one: the marker keeps the first run's controller replicas and CronJob names, never replaces them with what is now suspended or zero (test in Task 1).
  • The API away for a long time at boot: the script keeps trying and never exits as if there were no marker (test in Task 2).
  • A joiner not yet enrolled, with no /etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml: the unit exits 0 and does not loop (test in Task 2).
  • A CronJob named by the marker removed from git meanwhile, or another node deleting the marker mid-run: NotFound is success, the run finishes (test in Task 2).
  • The script restarted, or run by another node, while noout waits: the 30 minutes count from the first start, kept in the marker, not from each restart (test in Task 2).

docs.title: Task 1: lab cluster shutdown
docs.text:
Files: - Create: cli/internal/cluster/shutdown.go, cli/internal/cluster/shutdown_test.go, cli/internal/cli/cluster_shutdown.go - Modify: cli/internal/cli/root.go:30, infra/_modules/metal/flake/configuration.nix

Interfaces: - Produces: func Shutdown(ctx context.Context, environment string, jobWait time.Duration, progress io.Writer) error; type marker struct { Replicas int; CronJobs []string /* "ns/name" */; Boots map[string]string /* node to boot ID */ }, stored in the ConfigMap's data keys replicas, cronjobs (one per line), boots (node=id, one per line). startup-began (RFC 3339) belongs to the script. Task 2 reads these keys. - Consumes: loadConfig, commands.kubectl, commands.ssh from upgrade.go.

  • Step 1: Write the failing tests in shutdown_test.go, against an interface stopper with a fake that records calls, in fakeUpgrader's style:
  • TestShutdownOrder: calls are exactly write marker, stop controller, suspend (each CronJob, marker updated before its patch), wait for Jobs, noout, power off all nodes.
  • TestShutdownSkipsSuspendedAndKept: a CronJob with spec.suspend: true and one labelled homelab/power-keep are neither patched nor in the marker.
  • TestShutdownAgainKeepsTheMarker: marker present with Replicas: 2 and a/b; live controller at 0, a/b already suspended: the marker ends with Replicas: 2 and still a/b.
  • TestShutdownJobWaitIsBounded: Jobs never finish, jobWait 10 ms: it continues to power off and progress names the Job.
  • TestShutdownNoCeph: noout reports no CephCluster: the step is skipped, not an error.
  • TestShutdownFailureSaysStartup: a failure before power off returns an error containing lab cluster startup.
  • Step 2: Run them to see them fail

Run: cd cli && direnv exec .. go test ./internal/cluster/ -run TestShutdown. Expected: FAIL, undefined. - [ ] Step 3: Implement. noout: kubectl -n rook-ceph exec deploy/rook-ceph-operator -- ceph --conf=/var/lib/rook/rook-ceph/rook-ceph.config osd set noout; check it on the testbed in Task 4. Controller: StatefulSet argocd/argocd-application-controller. Power off: systemctl poweroff --no-block over commands.ssh, to all nodes concurrently; a dropped connection is success. Boot IDs from each Node's status.nodeInfo.bootID. - [ ] Step 4: Add the command newClusterShutdownCmd in cluster_shutdown.go, flags as newClusterUpgradeCmd plus --job-wait (default 5*time.Minute); only --environment and --flake required. Register it in root.go. - [ ] Step 5: Bound poweroff. In configuration.nix: systemd.targets.poweroff.unitConfig = { JobTimeoutSec = "180s"; JobTimeoutAction = "poweroff-force"; }; with a comment on why (an RBD unmount can stall once the OSDs are gone, and nobody is home). - [ ] Step 6: Run the tests. Run: direnv exec . make -C cli test check. Expected: PASS. - [ ] Step 7: Commit feat(cli): lab cluster shutdown.

docs.title: Task 2: the startup script, its unit and lab cluster startup
docs.text:
Files: - Create: infra/_modules/metal/flake/profiles/cluster-startup.sh, infra/_modules/metal/flake/profiles/cluster-startup.nix, cli/internal/cli/cluster_startup.go, cli/internal/cluster/startup.go, test/cluster_startup_test.go - Modify: infra/_modules/metal/flake/default.nix (modules list), cli/internal/cli/root.go:30, scripts/ci-check (offline_tests)

Interfaces: - Consumes: the marker keys from Task 1. - Produces: cluster-startup [--force] on every node, exit 0 once undone or with nothing to do; func Startup(ctx context.Context, environment string, progress io.Writer) error.

The script's order:

no /etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml            -> exit 0 (a joiner not enrolled)
get marker: NotFound -> exit 0; any other error -> retry every 15 s, no limit
without --force: a majority of the marker's nodes on a new boot? no -> exit 75 (the unit tries again)
record startup-began if absent
resume the marker's CronJobs (NotFound is success)
scale the controller back to the marker's replicas
every OSD Ready, or NOOUT_LIMIT (1800 s) since startup-began -> unset noout (no CephCluster: skip)
report CloudNativePG Clusters not healthy, holding nothing back
delete the marker (NotFound is success)

The first nodes to boot may see no majority yet, so exit 75 is a retry: the unit sets RestartForceExitStatus=75, RestartSec=30. Once the marker is gone, every retry exits 0. A single node rebooting during a shutdown retries until the shutdown powers it off.

  • Step 1: Write the failing tests in test/cluster_startup_test.go: bash runs the script with KUBECTL pointing at a fake that logs each call and answers from a temp directory; K3S_YAML, NOOUT_LIMIT and the retry interval are overridable by environment. Each test asserts the fake's log:
  • TestClusterStartupNoK3s: no K3S_YAML: exit 0, kubectl never called.
  • TestClusterStartupNoMarker: NotFound: exit 0, nothing changed.
  • TestClusterStartupAPIAway: the first 3 calls fail with connection refused, then the marker exists: it retried and undid everything.
  • TestClusterStartupMinorityRebooted: one of three on a new boot: exit 75, nothing changed; with --force: undone.
  • TestClusterStartupUndoes: the named CronJob resumed and no other, replicas restored, noout unset, the marker deleted last.
  • TestClusterStartupGoneMeanwhile: patching the CronJob and deleting the marker answer NotFound: exit 0.
  • TestClusterStartupNoOutLimit: OSDs never Ready, startup-began older than NOOUT_LIMIT in the marker: noout unset, and CronJobs resumed before it.
  • TestClusterStartupKeepsItsClock: startup-began present: not rewritten.
  • Step 2: Run them to see them fail. Run: cd test && direnv exec .. go test -count=1 -run '^TestClusterStartup' .. Expected: FAIL, script missing.
  • Step 3: Implement cluster-startup.sh to the order above, KUBECTL defaulting to k3s kubectl.
  • Step 4: Implement cluster-startup.nix: pkgs.writeShellApplication from builtins.readFile ./cluster-startup.sh with config.services.k3s.package, coreutils, gnugrep, gawk as inputs, in environment.systemPackages; systemd.services.cluster-startup: wantedBy = [ "multi-user.target" ], after = [ "k3s.service" ], no requires and no before, Type=oneshot, TimeoutStartSec=infinity, Restart=on-failure, RestartForceExitStatus=75, RestartSec=30, StartLimitIntervalSec=0.
  • Step 5: Implement Startup (SSH to the first node that answers, run cluster-startup --force, its output to progress) and newClusterStartupCmd (--environment, --flake, --timeout default 1 hour).
  • Step 6: Wire TestClusterStartup into offline_tests, and build a node: direnv exec . nix build ./infra/_modules/metal/flake#nixosConfigurations.homelab-1.config.system.build.toplevel --no-link as lab cluster upgrade does (check its exact flake reference in upgrade.go:rebuild). Expected: builds, shellcheck included.
  • Step 7: Run the tests. Run the test command above and direnv exec . make -C cli test check. Expected: PASS.
  • Step 8: Commit feat(nodes): startup undoes an ordered shutdown by itself.

docs.title: Task 4: the power tests and make testbed-power
docs.text:
Files: - Create: test/power_test.go - Modify: Makefile (target testbed-power beside testbed-stop)

Interfaces: - Consumes: testbedOnly, testbedHosts, testbedSSH, virsh, domstate, testbedKubectl, waitNodeReady from test/testbed_test.go; the mesh and Gateway checks of TestTestbedMesh, extracted into a shared testbedMeshWorks(t); lab by go run as the Makefile runs it.

Names avoid Testbed (make testbed's filter) and the words in test/scopes.yaml's full: TestPowerCutEveryNode, TestPowerShutdownStartup, TestPowerNodeNotReturning, TestPowerCutPostgres.

  • Step 1: Write the probe helper startPowerProbe(t) *powerProbe: namespace power-probe, a PVC on the testbed's Ceph StorageClass (as TestTestbedCeph's volume), a one-replica Deployment (Recreate) that resumes from the file's last number plus one, appends, fdatasyncs (pin the image TestTestbedCeph uses, and if its sync has no -d, use its dd conv=fdatasync form), then prints the number. acked() is what kubectl logs -f, run from the workstation, has read. verify(t) reads the file: every acked number present, strictly increasing, and it grew after recovery. Cleanup removes the namespace.
  • Step 2: Write TestPowerCutEveryNode: require healthy (testbedMeshWorks, Ceph HEALTH_OK); start the probe, wait for 50 acked; virsh destroy all three in parallel goroutines; virsh start all three. Within 30 minutes, with no command on the cluster: API /readyz at the VIP; each node's bootID new and Ready; three nodes carrying etcd.k3s.cattle.io/node-name; Ceph HEALTH_OK with mons and OSDs Ready; testbedMeshWorks; probe.verify. t.Logf each time reached. A failure of the Gateway's VIP dumps the Service's status and each kube-vip's lease and log tail, and its message names the 12a-2 finding.
  • Step 3: Write TestPowerShutdownStartup: fixtures in power-probe: running and held (suspend: true) CronJobs with schedule 0 0 1 1 *, and Job long sleeping an hour. Run lab cluster shutdown --job-wait=1m; assert its output names long; every VM shut off within 5 minutes and still so a minute later. virsh start all three, never calling lab. Within 30 minutes: running not suspended, held suspended, the watchdog's suspend false, ceph osd dump without noout, controller's replicas restored, Applications Synced, the marker gone, probe.verify. Then lab cluster startup exits 0.
  • Step 4: Write TestPowerNodeNotReturning: run lab cluster shutdown; start only the two nodes that do not hold the probe's Pod. Within 15 minutes: running resumed and controller back, the marker still present; with the third off, noout off and the marker gone within 30 minutes and a margin of the first start. defer starts the third and waits for HEALTH_OK, so the testbed ends healthy.
  • Step 5: Write TestPowerCutPostgres: skips unless the CRD clusters.postgresql.cnpg.io exists (it is for Task 6's single run). Reuses TestTestbedPostgresFailover's Cluster and write helpers: write through the primary, destroy all VMs, start them, and within 45 minutes a primary answers with the row. Logs only; removes its namespace.
  • Step 6: Add make testbed-power: sandbox-checkout, scripts/testbed-guard testbed, then one $(MAKE) env=testbed ENV=testbed INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY=1 smoke_filter=<name> smoke-test per test (so go test's hour applies to each), for the first three; tests= overrides the list. Add it to .PHONY if the Makefile lists them.
  • Step 7: Compile and check selection. Run: cd test && direnv exec .. go vet ./... and direnv exec . make -C cli check. Expected: pass, and lab test scope --check satisfied.
  • Step 8: Commit test(testbed): every node losing power, an ordered shutdown, a node not returning.

  • Step 4: If the Gateway's address does not return: one bounded investigation, about half a day of machine time. Fixed: ship the fix with a test. Not fixed: stop and ask the user with the logs; do not record it as passing or move it to 12b.
  • Step 5: Any other failure: superpowers:systematic-debugging, fix with a test, rerun that test. Commit each fix as fix(power): ....

docs.title: Task 6: CloudNativePG, one measurement
docs.text:

Start logging from each node each minute: vmstat, iostat -x or /proc/diskstats, and /proc/meminfo; if iostat is not on the node, use a nix shell once rather than changing the flake.

docs.title: Cluster scan (step 15d) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: make testbed-scan (kube-bench) and make dev-scan (kubescape) fail on any undecided finding and on a scan that did not really run; every open finding is decided; the fixes are made; Secrets in etcd are proven encrypted.

Architecture: Go tests in test/ run the tools and hand their JSON to pure functions, which compare it with .cluster-scan-accepted.yaml. Those functions are tested offline in scripts/ci-check. The live tests sit outside make dev's and make testbed's selections, except TestTestbedSecretsEncrypted.

Tech Stack: Go (testify, terratest's k8s helpers as in test/testbed_test.go), kube-bench, kubescape, NixOS node profile, k3d config, Helm values.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-cluster-scan-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Branch feat/cluster-scan, PR into dev; merge only when the user says "merge".
  • Live runs only from the main checkout; never make -n; testbed and sandbox never up together; no scripts/ci-check all while either is up. Before each: pgrep -x terragrunt; pgrep -x make.
  • Stop a run by hand on two samples a minute apart under 1.5 GB available; do not restart a run killed for memory without the user's go-ahead.
  • Tool reports hold command lines and config: they stay in t.TempDir(), are never committed, and failures name only check number, control ID and <namespace>/<Kind>/<name>, never actual_value.
  • kubescape always with --keep-local.
  • Versions: latest stable pinned exactly; check upstream when building. kube-bench image v0.16.0 or later; kubescape v4.0.17 or later. If a release has k3s-cis-1.11, use it and vendor nothing.
  • The dangerous controls, accepted only by resource: C-0185, C-0187, C-0035, C-0065, C-0191, C-0057, C-0045, C-0048, C-0041, C-0038, C-0046, C-0012, C-0259.
  • A dangerous finding that cannot be fixed small is raised with the user before it is accepted.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A report that is not JSON, empty, or from a tool that exited non-zero: the target fails, never passes. Pinned by TestScanReportsRefused.
  2. Fewer reports than nodes (a Job failed on one node): the target fails naming the node. Pinned in TestScanBench, by requiring one parsed report per testbedHosts entry.
  3. A whole-control acceptance of a dangerous control, or an entry with no reason: the file is refused. Pinned by TestScanAcceptedRefused.
  4. A run stopped midway leaves the privileged namespace: the next run deletes it first, and t.Cleanup deletes it after. Pinned in Task 2, Step 4.
  5. Resources with generated names (svclb-gateway-istio-62125460): an accepted resource is a path.Match pattern, so a rebuild does not fail the target. Pinned by TestScanKubescapeDecided.

docs.title: Task 1: The decision logic, offline
docs.text:
Files: - Create: test/scan_test.go - Create: .cluster-scan-accepted.yaml (empty lists) - Modify: scripts/ci-check:7 (add TestScan(AcceptedRefused|ReportsRefused|BenchDecided|KubescapeDecided)|TestSecretIsEncrypted to offline_tests) - Modify: test/scopes.yaml (skip: .cluster-scan-accepted.yaml)

Interfaces: - Produces, all in test/scan_test.go: - type scanAccepted struct { KubeBench []scanCheckyaml:"kubeBench"; Kubescape struct { Controls []scanControlyaml:"controls"; Resources []scanResourceyaml:"resources"}yaml:"kubescape"}, with scanCheck{Check, Reason}, scanControl{ID, Reason}, scanResource{ID, Resource, Reason} - func loadScanAccepted(raw []byte) (scanAccepted, error) - func undecidedBench(report []byte, accepted scanAccepted) ([]string, error): undecided FAIL check numbers - func undecidedKubescape(report []byte, accepted scanAccepted) ([]string, error): undecided <controlID> <namespace>/<Kind>/<name> - func secretIsEncrypted(raw []byte, value string) error - const scanMinResources = 500

  • Step 1: Write the failing tests
func TestScanAcceptedRefused(t *testing.T)   // no reason on any entry kind; C-0185 under controls: each returns an error naming the entry
func TestScanReportsRefused(t *testing.T)    // both parsers: "", "not json", a warning line before the JSON are errors
func TestScanBenchDecided(t *testing.T)
// fixture: sections 1..5, FAIL 1.2.30 and 4.2.4, WARN 1.2.3. With 4.2.4 accepted: ["1.2.30"]; WARN never returned.
// sections 1,4,5 only: error containing "section 2".
// a result whose reason holds "journalctl: not found": error containing "1.2.1", even if PASS.
func TestScanKubescapeDecided(t *testing.T)
// results use the real shape: results[].resourceID, controls[].controlID, controls[].status.status; summaryDetails.ResourceCounters.
// C-0050 accepted as a control: no finding. C-0057 on istio-system/DaemonSet/ztunnel accepted by resource: no finding;
// on another resource: "C-0057 ns/DaemonSet/other". resource "kube-system/DaemonSet/svclb-*" matches a generated name.
// fewer than scanMinResources, or no istio-system/DaemonSet/ztunnel in the results: error.
func TestSecretIsEncrypted(t *testing.T)
// "k8s:enc:aescbc:v1:aescbckey:<bytes>" with no value: nil; plain value: error; no prefix: error; value inside an encrypted-looking blob: error
  • Step 2: Run them

Run: cd test && direnv exec .. go test -count=1 -run 'TestScan(AcceptedRefused|ReportsRefused|BenchDecided|KubescapeDecided)|TestSecretIsEncrypted' . Expected: FAIL, the functions are undefined.

  • Step 3: Implement

Resource key: the last three /-separated fields of resourceID, as the spike's ks.py did (/ClusterRoleBinding/velero-server for a cluster-scoped one). Match : not found for the audit guard. Sort results.

  • Step 4: Run them, and the checks they touch

Run: the command of Step 2, then direnv exec . make -C cli check. Expected: PASS.

  • Step 5: Commit test(scan): decide a scanner's findings against one file

docs.text:
Files: - Modify: flake.nix (kubescape from its release: fetch the asset with its hash, since nixpkgs has 4.0.8; the reason beside it) - Modify: test/scan_test.go (TestScanKubescape) - Modify: Makefile (dev-scan) - Modify: .cluster-scan-accepted.yaml

Skip unless ENV=dev; run kubescape scan framework allcontrols --keep-local --format json --output <TempDir>/report.json --kubeconfig $KUBECONFIG; a non-zero exit or a missing file fails. Fail with the undecided list, one per line. Keep the tool's own exit code on findings in mind: it must not read as a run failure unless --compliance-threshold is set.
  • Step 2: Run with nothing accepted

Run: k3d cluster start homelab-dev, wait for every pod Ready, make dev-scan. Expected: FAIL, about 86 controls.

  • Step 3: Triage. For each failed control read what it would let someone do, then: accept whole with a reason (limits, labels, probes, signatures, Kyverno's repeats), or accept by resource, or leave for Task 5. Read each C-0012 and C-0259 resource's real value in the render (do not print values) and record why it is or is not a credential; a real one in plain text is a fix, not an acceptance. Raise with the user any dangerous finding with no small fix.

docs.text:

Assert secretIsEncrypted.

docs.title: Public Surface (step 15f) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Only an allow-list of namespaces reaches the internet through Gateway public; Cloudflare's WAF and one rate limit sit in front of it; nuclei scans the public hosts weekly and alerts on what nobody accepted.

Architecture: A namespace → hosts map in system/istio-system/values.yaml drives Gateway public's allowedRoutes selector; an offline test checks every production route against it. infra/_modules/cloudflare gains two cloudflare_rulesets (managed WAF, rate limit), tested with tofu test and a mock provider. A new chart system/public-scan runs nuclei from a CronJob through public DNS; a Job fails when the scan did not really run (Prometheus alert PublicScanMissing), and findings go to Loki (ruler alert PublicScanFinding).

Tech Stack: Helm, Gateway API v1, OpenTofu with Cloudflare provider 5.x, nuclei, Loki ruler, PrometheusRule, Go tests in test/.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-public-surface-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Latest stable everything, pinned exactly: nuclei v3.11.1 (image by digest), nuclei-templates v10.5.1 (tarball by sha256), Cloudflare provider 5.28.1 (bump from 5.28.0 in infra/_modules/cloudflare/versions.tf). Recheck upstream when the task starts.
  • Never print Cloudflare tokens, the zone id or the account id. Never read ~/.config/homelab/state.env or .state/.
  • Nothing is planned or applied against production Cloudflare without the user's go-ahead (Task 6).
  • Alerts and logs the repository writes name only template IDs and hosts, never response bodies or extracted values.
  • Every workload sets its securityContext (RuntimeDefault, no privilege escalation, non-root, read-only root filesystem) or carries a PolicyException with its reason.
  • make dev and every sandbox run only from /home/nixos/homelab, never a worktree; check pgrep -x terragrunt; pgrep -x make first.
  • The public map: blog: [www], excalidraw: [draw], ntfy: [ntfy], matrix: [chat].

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A second route in a listed namespace with a host not in the map (e.g. admin. in matrix): the offline test must fail it, not only check the namespace. Test: Task 1's TestPublicRoutes case "listed namespace, unlisted host".
  2. A LAN route in a listed namespace (dendrite on gateway in matrix): must not be flagged. Test: Task 1, case "listed namespace on the LAN Gateway".
  3. A target answering with a Cloudflare challenge (cf-mitigated: challenge) or 5xx: the Job must fail, not report a clean scan. Test: Task 3's wrapper test cases.
  4. An accepted entry for one host must not hide the same template on another host. Test: Task 3, TestPublicScanAcceptedPerHost.
  5. The rate limit must sit above nuclei's throttle with room (at least 2×): Task 3's offline test compares the two values.

docs.title: Plan rulings
docs.text:
• The scan's targets are a second list in system/public-scan/values.yaml, kept equal to the map by Task 3's offline test (the spec said "not typed twice": Helm cannot read another chart's values, and Argo CD passing one component's values to another adds more than it saves).
  • PublicScanMissing is a PrometheusRule on the CronJob's last success (as SecretRotationOverdue), not a Loki rule: a failed Job and a missing run then look the same.
  • Acceptance happens before nuclei logs: the wrapper runs nuclei once per host with that host's -exclude-ids, so Loki's rule needs no list.

docs.title: Task 1: The allow-list on Gateway public
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: system/istio-system/values.yaml (add public: map with a comment), system/istio-system/templates/gateway.yaml (Gateway public listener https), apps/ntfy.yaml (route annotation) - Create: test/public_surface_test.go - Modify: test/gateway_test.go (sandbox test), scripts/ci-check (offline_tests), test/scopes.yaml (skip the new offline file)

  • Step 1: Write the failing offline test TestPublicRoutes in test/public_surface_test.go:
  • table cases on publicRouteProblems (domain example.org): all fine → empty; namespace off the map → one problem naming <ns>/HTTPRoute/<name>; listed namespace, unlisted host → one problem; missing proxied annotation → one problem; listed namespace on the LAN Gateway (gateway) with any host → no problem.
  • the repository: scripts/render-all prod <tmp>, collect every HTTPRoute whose parentRefs name public (namespace istio-system), with metadata.namespace (renders of apps have none: use the app file's name, apps/matrix → matrix), hostnames, and external-dns.kubernetes.io/cloudflare-proxied == "true"; assert.Empty(publicRouteProblems(...)); and assert the rendered Gateway public's https listener is from: Selector with kubernetes.io/metadata.name In exactly the map's keys, sorted.
  • Step 2: Run cd test && go test -count=1 -run 'TestPublicRoutes' ./... — expect FAIL (no map, ntfy unproxied, from: All).
  • Step 3: Implement: the map in values (comment: what it is, that a public app adds a line here plus the annotation, guide link docs/how-to-guides/public-surface.md); the listener from: Selector, selector.matchExpressions: [{key: kubernetes.io/metadata.name, operator: In, values: <keys sorted>}]; external-dns.kubernetes.io/cloudflare-proxied: "true" on ntfy's route; TestPublicRoutes into offline_tests; test/public_surface_test.go into scopes.yaml's offline skips.

The positive side: an HTTPRoute public-allow-probe in ntfy to public is Accepted: True (deleted after).
  • Step 6: Commit feat(gateway): only listed namespaces reach the public Gateway.

docs.title: Task 2: Cloudflare's WAF and rate limit in OpenTofu
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: infra/_modules/cloudflare/main.tf (two rulesets), variables.tf (rate-limit inputs with defaults), versions.tf (5.28.1) - Create: infra/_modules/cloudflare/tests/edge.tftest.hcl (mock provider, override_data for cloudflare_accounts, cloudflare_zone, the permission groups, and whatever the managed ruleset lookup reads) - Create: test/cloudflare_test.go (TestCloudflareEdgeRules runs tofu -chdir=... init -backend=false and tofu test), add it to offline_tests and the file to scopes.yaml skips (infra/_modules/cloudflare/** is already production-only: check its scope)

Interfaces: - Produces: variables rate_limit_requests (number, default decided in Step 1), rate_limit_period (number, seconds), consumed by Task 3's offline test through infra/_modules/cloudflare/variables.tf defaults (it reads them with a regexp on the file: keep each default on one line default = N).

  • Step 1: Read Cloudflare's current docs (web-fetch): the Free plan's rate-limiting rules (count, periods, mitigation timeouts, counting characteristics, fields allowed in the expression) and how a Free zone gets the Free Managed Ruleset (deployable through the http_request_firewall_managed phase, or always on). Record the facts with their URLs in the task's report. Pick the threshold: generous for Element web's first load (at least 2× the requests a cold load of chat. makes; measure Element web's request count in the sandbox's browser-free way, curl of its index plus the assets it lists, or take Cloudflare's guidance) and at least twice nuclei's rate in Task 3 (rateLimit 5 requests per second → 50 per 10 s, so ≥100 per 10 s).
  • Step 2: Write the failing tofu test: a run "edge" with command = plan asserting: a cloudflare_ruleset in phase http_ratelimit, zone scope, one rule, action block, ratelimit.characteristics containing ip.src, requests_per_period = var.rate_limit_requests, period = var.rate_limit_period; and the managed one (phase http_request_firewall_managed, rule execute of the Free managed ruleset) — or, if Step 1 found it cannot be declared on Free, a check block that reads the zone's managed phase and fails when the Free ruleset is not executed. Run go test -run TestCloudflareEdgeRules → FAIL.
  • Step 3: Implement the rulesets in main.tf, each with a comment (what it guards, the Free plan's limit it fits, that it covers the whole zone because nothing else in it is proxied: spec).
  • Step 4: Run TestCloudflareEdgeRules → PASS; make -C infra check → passes (HOMELAB_CLOUDFLARE_OFFLINE=1).
  • Step 5: Commit feat(cloudflare): the WAF's managed rules and one rate limit on the zone.

docs.title: Task 3: The scan Job (system/public-scan)
docs.text:
Files: - Create: system/public-scan/Chart.yaml, values.yaml, values-dev.yaml, files/scan.sh, templates/cronjob.yaml, templates/configmap.yaml (the script), templates/prometheus-rule.yaml - Modify: system/egress/values.yaml (public-scan: [{port: 443}], comment: the public hosts through Cloudflare, the templates' tarball), system/argocd/values-dev.yaml (- path: system/public-scan in the root list), test/scopes.yaml (group [system/public-scan/**] → PublicScan, add PublicScan to full), scripts/ci-check (offline_tests) - Create: test/public_scan_test.go

Interfaces: - Consumes: publicMap(t) (Task 1); rate_limit_requests/rate_limit_period defaults (Task 2). - Produces: values targets: [label…], accepted: [{template, host, reason}], rateLimit (req/s), minTemplates, image, templates: {version, sha256}, schedule ("0 4 * * 0", Sunday 04:00 in global.timezone), devCA (dev only); Job log lines: nuclei's JSONL (fields template-id, host, info.severity) plus one final line {"public_scan":"done","templates":N}; CronJob name public-scan.

  • Step 1: Write the failing offline tests in test/public_scan_test.go:
  • TestPublicScanTargets: production targets equal the map's labels (same set); dev targets ⊆ the map.
  • TestPublicScanAccepted: every accepted entry has a non-empty template, a host in targets, and a reason; rendered args for host A carry A's IDs only (TestPublicScanAcceptedPerHost: two entries, same template, hosts www and draw with only www accepted → the draw invocation has no -exclude-id).

  • TestPublicScanScript runs files/scan.sh's preflight function against a local httptest server (the script takes PUBLIC_SCAN_CHECK_ONLY=1 and a target URL list): 200 → ok; 503 → fail; 403 with header cf-mitigated: challenge → fail; 200 with body containing <title>Just a moment...</title> → fail. docs.title: 14b-1: just replaces make — Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: four justfiles replace the four Makefiles with the same behaviour and just-style options.

Architecture: a root justfile (mod infra, mod cli, mod test) holds the sandbox and testbed recipes; each module holds its directory's commands and runs there. Parameters are exported ($name) so regexes and reasons reach the shell unparsed; long bodies are bash shebang recipes.

docs.title: 14f-2: the cluster tests on Ginkgo — Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: the 84 cluster tests become Ginkgo specs in test/e2e, selected by labels, with a per-spec timeout from the spec's context, and terratest leaves the module.

Architecture: test/e2e (package e2e, one entry TestE2E) holds one top-level Describe per old test, named after it without Test (Describe("SSOKiali", Label("sso", "kiali"), …)); labels sit only on that container, as string literals, from the fixed set in test/scopes.yaml's labels:. test/internal/kube replaces terratest with calls that take a context.Context. lab test scope reads the specs' labels from the source (go/ast), turns scopes.yaml's label filters into one main filter and one filter per alone spec, and evaluates them with Ginkgo's own types.ParseLabelFilter. just test e2e --env <env> runs go tool ginkgo and adds && <env> to every filter.

Tech Stack: Go 1.26, Ginkgo v2.34.0, Gomega v1.44.0 (latest on 2026-11-08: check again when pinning), testify only in test/offline, chromedp.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-08-test-layout-design.md (step 2, "14f-2")

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• No spec asserts less than its test did, and no wait gets longer; a wait may become a spec timeout.
  • Every scope group, full, always, the alone runs and the recipes' filters (just testbed, testbed-power, testbed-scan, dev-scan, production) select exactly the old tests that ran under them today (Task 1's record), except the spec's two intended differences: no offline test (already true since 14f-1) and no TestTestbed* on the sandbox.
  • Labels: lower case, - between words, only the set below, only on top-level containers.
  • --fail-on-empty on every Ginkgo run; one process (no -p); alone specs are Serial.
  • Reports in test/reports/e2e/ (git-ignored); GitHub Actions uploads them.
  • go tool ginkgo (the tool directive in test/go.mod); no separate install.
  • Main checkout only for just dev and just testbed; ci-check with the sandbox and testbed down.
  • A sandbox or testbed step is a stop: the user starts it (they shut WSL down between sessions). So the groups are proven on the sandbox together in Task 13, one group's filter at a time in conversion order, not as each lands (the spec's wording): a conversion mistake costs a re-run of its group either way, since the test code runs from the checkout and the sandbox does not depend on it.

docs.title: Conversion rules (Tasks 3–10)
docs.text:
• One old TestX → var _ = Describe("X", Label(…), func() { … }), Serial (and Ordered) on alone specs.
  • t.Run steps that build on each other → Ordered container, one It per step; independent subtests (tables) → one It per entry. A subtest's name becomes its It text.
  • Every It takes ctx SpecContext and has SpecTimeout(d): d is at least the longest single wait inside it plus 5 minutes and at least twice its duration in .superpowers/post-merge/test-layout-full.log (PASS TestX (Ns)), rounded up to 5 minutes; testbed specs without a measured duration take the first rule only.
  • Every wait takes the spec's context: kube.* (Task 2), exec.CommandContext, http.NewRequestWithContext, chromedp contexts derived from ctx, Eventually(ctx, f).WithTimeout(old timeout).WithPolling(old tick).
  • Assertions are Gomega (Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred()), Eventually(...).Should(...) keeping the old message); e2e helpers drop t and call Expect themselves. test/internal helpers keep testing.TB (the offline tests use them), and e2e passes GinkgoTB().
  • Environment gates go (LocalOnly, *SandboxOnly, testbedOnly, skipUnlessSandbox, sandboxOnly and the inline ENV checks): the environment labels replace them. The only skips left: an optional app absent and not asked for (skipUnlessDeployed), and the testbed's two "not on its list" skips (CloudNativePG), which are the same kind. skipUnlessSandbox's wait for the identity stack becomes a BeforeEach in the SSO and Woodpecker containers.
  • Cleanups: t.Cleanup/defer that undo cluster changes → DeferCleanup(func(ctx SpecContext) …); t.TempDir() → GinkgoT().TempDir(); t.Parallel() dropped.
  • Paths through repo.Root(); never "..".

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• A spec that passes having checked nothing: a gate turned label where the gate also waited (skipUnlessSandbox), a Skip left behind, an Eventually without .Should. Task 11's dry-run check and the code reading at each task.
  • A wait still blind to the spec's context (a exec.Command, http.Get, time.Sleep, chromedp.NewContext(context.Background())): each conversion task greps for them.
  • A main filter that selects nothing (a branch touching only Velero): lab must print "", not a filter that --fail-on-empty fails. Task 11's tests.
  • A label typed wrong in a spec or a filter (trivy-operater): known only through scopes.yaml; Task 11's just cli check and Task 11's check both fail.
  • An alone spec reached through a manual --tests filter (--tests 'node-restart || logs') must run alone, never in the main run. Task 11's tests.

docs.title: 14f-1: offline tests in their own package — Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: the 131 offline tests leave package test for test/offline and test/internal/*, so the basic checks run them by package and test/ holds only the 84 cluster tests (14f-2 converts those to Ginkgo).

Architecture: Go packages under the existing module github.com/duongle-steven/homelab/test: test/offline (package offline) for render, script and check tests; test/internal/<pkg> for helpers both sides use, each with its own offline tests beside it; the root package test keeps the cluster tests and imports test/internal/*. lab test scope learns that a changed test/internal/<pkg> file selects the cluster tests importing that package.

Tech Stack: Go 1.26, testify, go/parser (in cli/internal/scope).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-08-test-layout-design.md (step 1, "14f-1")

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• No test changes what it asserts; moved tests keep their names (offline names stay Test…, so the lists compare).
  • scripts/ci-check go runs go vet ./... && go test -count=1 -timeout 20m ./offline/... ./internal/... from test/: no list of test names anywhere.
  • test/ (root package) holds only tests that need a cluster; test/kube-bench-cfg/ stays (the scan tests read it).
  • Fixtures an offline test reads move with it (test/fixtures/ → test/offline/fixtures/); repo-relative paths come from one helper (repo.Root(t)), never a count of ../.
  • Main checkout only for just dev; ci-check with the sandbox and testbed down.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• A test that changes side silently (a cluster test moved to offline/, or an offline test left in the root and dropped from the basic checks): Task 2 compares the before/after name lists exactly.
  • A test reading a path relative to its own directory (../apps, fixtures/…) after moving one level deeper: repo.Root(t) everywhere, and Task 2's full offline run proves each.
  • A helper change no longer selecting the cluster tests that use it (it moved to test/internal): Task 1's scope tests.
  • KialiRender in test/scopes.yaml matching no cluster test once the render test leaves the root: Task 1 removes the term, just cli check proves it.
  • go vet ./... no longer compiling the cluster tests: it stays ./... (root included).

docs.title: Argo CD reads the cluster Secret (step 14g) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Remove the bootstrap's yq rewrites of the rendered ApplicationSets.

Architecture: OpenTofu's Argo CD bootstrap writes Argo CD's in-cluster cluster Secret, which carries the repository, the revision, the backup endpoint and one label per optional app. Both ApplicationSets read it through a clusters generator, which wraps the existing matrix.

Tech Stack: Argo CD v3.5.5 ApplicationSets (Go templates), Helm, POSIX sh plus yq and jq, OpenTofu and Terragrunt, Go (testify offline, Ginkgo e2e).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-09-argocd-cluster-secret-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• The Secret:
  • name: in-cluster in namespace argocd.
  • Labels argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type: cluster and homelab/bootstrap: "true"; the second is the selector of every homelab clusters generator.
  • stringData: name: in-cluster, server: https://kubernetes.default.svc.
  • Annotations, camelCase with no prefix, each always present:
  • repository
  • revision
  • backupS3Url (empty string outside production)
  • Optional apps: label homelab/app-<name>: "true" for each optional app asked, and none otherwise.
  • Templates: every template reads the Secret with dot access ({{ .metadata.annotations.repository }}), never index. Both ApplicationSets keep missingkey=error.
  • Bootstrap order: the bootstrap applies the Secret before the CRDs and the ApplicationSets, server-side, with field manager argocd-controller.
  • Removal: nothing deletes the Secret. The module has no destroy action.
  • Repositories:
  • The sandbox's and the testbed's repository is config.json's seed_repository.
  • Production's is http://forgejo-http.forgejo:3000/ops/homelab, or its seed before the switch.
  • Branches: sandbox, testbed, master. revision (just dev --revision) overrides the branch.
  • R2's endpoint never goes in git.
  • config.json is still read through the git files generator with pathParamPrefix: config.
  • values-seed.yaml keeps only the metrics switches.
  • Commits end with: 
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DkFEsNwJMWzH561hFWiUzi
    Never commit to dev or master. Run just dev only from /home/nixos/homelab, never beside the testbed.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. just dev --apps paperless followed by a plain just dev: the homelab/app-paperless label must go. The server-side apply drops labels its manager no longer sets, so the Application goes too. Task 6 checks it on the sandbox.
  2. just dev --revision <sha> followed by a plain just dev: the revision annotation must return to sandbox. Task 6 checks it, and Task 2's test covers the script.
  3. A fresh cluster: the Secret must exist before any ApplicationSet. Otherwise the generators match nothing, and a later Secret only creates Applications, which is harmless. Re-applying with a renamed selector would delete them all. Task 2's order test pins it.
  4. A switched production while Forgejo is down: it must never go back to the seed. Task 1's cases cover it.
  5. A template naming an annotation the Secret does not write: this must fail at once, not at the cluster. Task 4's test checks that every .metadata.annotations.X in the rendered ApplicationSets is one the Secret script writes.

docs.title: Task 1: choose-values.sh decides the repository as well
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: infra/_modules/argocd/choose-values.sh - Test: test/offline/ci_scripts_test.go (TestArgoCDChooseValues)

Interfaces: - Consumes: nothing. - Produces: - stdin JSON {values, environment, seed, kubeconfig, repository, seed_repository}. forgejo_repository is gone; repository replaces it. - stdout {values, environment, repository}. - "Switched" means the cluster Secret's repository annotation equals repository.

  • Step 1: Update TestArgoCDChooseValues.
  • The fake kubectl answers *"get secret in-cluster"* with $ROOT_REPO, the annotation, in place of the applicationset case.
  • The case "first install, no Argo CD CRDs" becomes "first install, no cluster Secret": an empty answer and seedValues.
  • Inputs:
    • repository = forgejo.
    • seed_repository = "https://github.com/example/homelab".
  • Expected outputs:
    • seedValues = {"values":"values-seed.yaml","environment":"seed","repository":"https://github.com/example/homelab"}.
    • forgejoValues = {"values":"values-dev.yaml","environment":"dev","repository":" + forgejo + "}.

  • Keep the other cases, including "switched, Forgejo down: stay" and "cluster unreachable" (fails).

  • Step 2: Run the test and confirm it fails. Run cd test && go test ./offline -run TestArgoCDChooseValues. Expected: FAIL, since the output has no repository.

  • Step 3: Change choose-values.sh.

  • Read the switch from kubectl -n argocd get secret in-cluster --ignore-not-found -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.repository}'. A missing namespace or Secret answers empty, which is a first install; any other error fails.
  • Print repository:
    • seed_repository while on the seed;
    • otherwise repository.

  • Without a seed, never call kubectl (the sandbox case).

  • Step 4: Run the test and confirm it passes. Same command. Expected: PASS.

  • Step 5: Commit with the message feat(argocd): choose-values.sh picks the repository too, from the cluster Secret. Task 2 changes main.tf's query in the same branch, before anything runs it.

docs.title: Task 2: the bootstrap writes the cluster Secret first
docs.text:
Files: - Create: infra/_modules/argocd/cluster-secret.sh - Modify: - infra/_modules/argocd/bootstrap.sh - infra/_modules/argocd/main.tf - infra/sandbox/argocd/terragrunt.hcl, infra/testbed/argocd/terragrunt.hcl and infra/production/argocd/terragrunt.hcl - Test: test/offline/argocd_cluster_secret_test.go (new)

Interfaces: - Consumes: Task 1's stdin and stdout. - Produces: - sh infra/_modules/argocd/cluster-secret.sh prints the Secret's YAML. It reads: - env REPOSITORY (required); - BRANCH (required); - REVISION (optional, overrides BRANCH); - BACKUP_S3_URL (optional); - OPTIONAL_APPS (space-separated, deduplicated). - bootstrap.sh applies it first. - Module variables: - repository (string, required); - branch (string, required); - the existing seed_repository, revision, backup_s3_url and optional_apps. - local.environment gains REPOSITORY (from data.external.values.result.repository) and BRANCH. triggers_replace adds the chosen repository and the branch.

  • Step 1: Write TestArgoCDClusterSecret.
  • Run cluster-secret.sh with REPOSITORY=https://github.com/example/homelab BRANCH=sandbox OPTIONAL_APPS="paperless paperless".
  • Assert, with yq on the output:
    • kind Secret, name in-cluster, namespace argocd;
    • both labels from Global Constraints;
    • annotations repository, revision=sandbox and backupS3Url="";
    • exactly one optional label, homelab/app-paperless: "true";
    • stringData.server == https://kubernetes.default.svc.
  • With REVISION=abc123, revision is abc123.

  • Without REPOSITORY, or without BRANCH, it exits non-zero.

  • Step 2: Write TestArgoCDBootstrapAppliesSecretFirst.

  • Run bootstrap.sh against the real chart, CHART=$root/system/argocd, with VALUES=values-dev.yaml ENVIRONMENT=dev REPOSITORY=… BRANCH=sandbox KUBECONFIG=/dev/null.
  • Use a fake kubectl from fakeBin that appends every applied stdin's kinds to a file. create namespace … -o yaml prints a Namespace, and wait and get application succeed.

  • Assert that the first applied object of kind Secret named in-cluster comes before every CustomResourceDefinition and ApplicationSet.

  • Step 3: Run both tests and confirm they fail. Run cd test && go test ./offline -run 'TestArgoCDClusterSecret|TestArgoCDBootstrapAppliesSecretFirst'. Expected: FAIL, since the script does not exist.

  • Step 4: Write cluster-secret.sh and update the module and units.

  • cluster-secret.sh builds the YAML with jq -n piped to yq -P. The optional labels go through sort -u.
  • bootstrap.sh calls it and pipes the result to apply right after the namespace is created. It still calls the three set-*.sh scripts until Task 4.
  • main.tf:
    • adds repository and branch;
    • sends repository and seed_repository in the data.external.values query and drops the forgejo_repository yamldecode.

  • The units:

    • sandbox: repository = jsondecode(file("${get_terragrunt_dir()}/../cluster/config.json")).seed_repository and branch = "sandbox";
    • testbed: the same, with branch = "testbed";
    • production: repository = "http://forgejo-http.forgejo:3000/ops/homelab" and branch = "master".

  • Step 5: Run the tests and confirm they pass. Same command, plus TestArgoCDChooseValues and just infra check. Expected: PASS.

  • Step 6: Commit with the message feat(argocd): the bootstrap writes Argo CD's in-cluster cluster Secret first.

docs.title: Task 6: prove it on the sandbox and the testbed
docs.text:
Files: none, unless a run finds a fault. A fix goes in with its own test first.

docs.title: Runtime Detection (15g) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Falco runs in every environment and only detects. Its events reach Loki and alert through Alertmanager, and a stalled Falco alerts too.

Architecture: - Chart: system/falco is a wrapper chart of falcosecurity/falco: - the modern_ebpf driver, JSON events to stdout from warning up, no falcoctl; - accepted events rendered from values.yaml's accepted list into a rules file of its own. - Event alerts: Alloy already ships the pods' logs to Loki, and system/loki/files/falco-rules.yaml alerts on them. - Health alerts: a PrometheusRule in system/falco alerts on Falco's health from its metrics. - Proof: Ginkgo specs on the sandbox and the testbed.

Tech Stack: Helm wrapper charts, Argo CD ApplicationSets, Loki ruler (LogQL), Prometheus rules, Go (testify, Ginkgo v2).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-runtime-detection-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Versions: the latest stable falcosecurity/falco chart and Falco image, pinned exactly. When this was written: chart 9.2.2, Falco 0.45.2. Check upstream when building (CLAUDE.md, Rules).
  • Detection only: no Falco Talon, no falcosidekick, no k8s-metacollector, no Tetragon.
  • No runtime downloads: falcoctl.artifact.install.enabled: false and falcoctl.artifact.follow.enabled: false. Rules come from the image's stable ruleset plus files vendored in system/falco/files/.
  • Driver and output: driver.kind: modern_ebpf, falco.json_output: true, falco.priority: warning.
  • Alert severities: critical, alert and emergency events alert with severity critical. error events alert with severity warning. warning events show only on the dashboard. Alerts are grouped by rule and namespace.
  • The sandbox keeps every event and alert, as production does. Only the clean-baseline check counts events that have a Kubernetes namespace. A noisy workstation process is accepted in values-dev.yaml, never in values.yaml.
  • Every accepted event has a non-empty reason.
  • Namespace falco: privileged under Pod Security Admission and in the mesh, with an allow for Prometheus on the metrics port. No new egress.
  • The testbed:
  • no PolicyException, ServiceMonitor or PrometheusRule there (their CRDs are missing);
  • Falco is listed as a layer in values-testbed.yaml.
  • If it breaks the testbed's bar, Falco goes to not_run, its proof becomes one recorded manual run, and the VM sizes stay.
  • Commits end with the session's Co-Authored-By and Claude-Session lines.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. Falco's own startup lines are not JSON. Every LogQL expression drops lines that fail | json (__error__=""), so a restart never fires or breaks an alert. Pinned in Task 2's TestFalcoLokiRules (the expressions carry __error__="").
  2. An accepted entry must narrow a rule without disabling it. The template renders a Falco exceptions: append on the named rule, never enabled: false. Pinned in Task 1's TestFalcoAccepted.
  3. Events from the workstation have no k8s.ns.name. The alert expressions group by namespace and still fire with an empty namespace. The baseline query filters namespace!="". Pinned in Task 2's test (the expression has no namespace filter).
  4. A node whose Falco pod is missing is caught by FalcoNotRunning (desired versus ready on the DaemonSet), not only by a failed scrape. Pinned in Task 2's TestFalcoPrometheusRules.
  5. The testbed's render has none of the kinds whose CRDs it lacks. Pinned in Task 1's TestFalcoRender (testbed case).

docs.title: Task 1: system/falco, the chart
docs.text:
Files: - Create: - system/falco/Chart.yaml: dependency falco from https://falcosecurity.github.io/charts, pinned; - system/falco/values.yaml; - system/falco/values-local.yaml; - system/falco/values-testbed.yaml; - system/falco/templates/accepted-rules.yaml; - system/falco/templates/policy-exception.yaml; - system/falco/templates/authorization-policy.yaml. - Create: system/falco/files/ holding the vendored incubating rules for 15g-2's list (reverse shell, crypto miner, container escape) where the image's stable ruleset lacks them. Each file has a header with the falcosecurity/rules version it came from. - Modify: - system/argocd/values.yaml: add falco to the templatePatch list next to kured and loki (privileged, in ambient); - test/e2e/policy_test.go:18: add falco to privilegedNamespaces; - system/argocd/values-dev.yaml: add system/falco to the root directories after system/trivy-operator; - system/argocd/values-testbed.yaml: add system/falco under a comment # Layer: runtime detection. - Test: test/offline/falco_test.go

Interfaces: - Produces: - renderFalco(t *testing.T, env, expr string) string: renders system/falco for "", dev or testbed with scripts/render-chart and runs a yq expression. Same shape as renderTrivyOperator. - The values key accepted: a list of {rule, name, fields, comps, values, reason}. - The ConfigMap falco-accepted-rules, mounted into Falco's rules.d. - The Service and ServiceMonitor named by the chart, scraped on Falco's metrics port.

  • Step 1: Write the failing test TestFalcoRender. It loops over envs "", dev and testbed and asserts, in the rendered falco ConfigMap or the DaemonSet args:
  • engine.kind is modern_ebpf;
  • json_output is true;
  • priority is warning;
  • rules_files contains /etc/falco/falco_rules.yaml and /etc/falco/rules.d;
  • the containerd socket list includes /run/k3s/containerd/containerd.sock;
  • no container is named falcoctl-artifact-install or falcoctl-artifact-follow;
  • no resource has kind Deployment (no sidekick or metacollector);
  • the Falco image tag equals the pinned app version;
  • the DaemonSet's pod template has a ConfigMap volume falco-accepted-rules;
  • that ConfigMap holds every file in system/falco/files/ (the vendored rules), as well as the accepted entries;
  • for "" and dev: one PolicyException, with a non-empty homelab/reason annotation and the SkipDryRunOnMissingResource=true sync option, plus one ServiceMonitor;
  • for testbed: no PolicyException, ServiceMonitor or PrometheusRule.
  • Step 2: Run it. go test -C test ./offline/ -run TestFalcoRender -count=1 → FAIL (system/falco does not exist).
  • Step 3: Write the chart.
  • values.yaml:
    • falco.driver.kind: modern_ebpf;
    • falco.falcoctl.artifact.install.enabled: false and follow.enabled: false;
    • falco.falco.json_output: true, priority: warning;
    • Falco's metrics on (metrics.enabled, Prometheus endpoint);
    • falco.serviceMonitor.create: true;
    • the accepted-rules volume through falco.mounts;
    • accepted: [] and policyExceptions: true.
  • accepted-rules.yaml: holds files/*.yaml as they are (.Files.Glob), then the accepted entries. Falco loads rules.d in lexicographic order, so the accepted entries' key sorts last (zz-accepted.yaml).
  • values-local.yaml: requests cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi; limits cpu: "1", memory: 512Mi. These are starting values: Task 4 measures and replaces them.
  • values-testbed.yaml: policyExceptions: false, falco.serviceMonitor.create: false, prometheusRules: false.
  • policy-exception.yaml: one exception for the DaemonSet's pods, listing the policies they break (privileged, host PID, host paths). Same form as system/loki/templates/policy-exception.yaml.
  • authorization-policy.yaml: allow with the same namespace, plus Prometheus on the metrics port. Same form as system/trivy-operator/templates/authorization-policy.yaml.
  • Kyverno: add docker.io/falcosecurity only if allowed-registries refuses it (it allows docker.io, so no change is expected).
  • Step 4: Run it. go test -C test ./offline/ -run TestFalcoRender -count=1 → PASS.
  • Step 5: Write the failing test TestFalcoAccepted.
  • Every entry of accepted in values.yaml, values-local.yaml and values-dev.yaml has a non-empty rule, name and reason.
  • For a fixture values file with one entry, the rendered falco-accepted-rules holds: - rule: <rule> / exceptions: [{name, fields, comps, values}] / override: {exceptions: append}.
  • The rendered file holds no enabled: false.
  • Step 6: Run it. go test -C test ./offline/ -run TestFalcoAccepted -count=1 → FAIL.
  • Step 7: Write templates/accepted-rules.yaml. One rules document per entry, appending the exception. The reason goes in as a YAML comment above the entry.
  • Step 8: Run the checks.
  • go test -C test ./offline/ -run 'TestFalco|TestPolicy' -count=1 → PASS.
  • scripts/ci-check policy, scripts/check-mesh-policies and scripts/check-backup-groups → no failures.
  • Step 9: Commit. feat(falco): system/falco detects at runtime, detection only, no runtime downloads.

docs.title: Task 2: Alerts and the dashboard
docs.text:
Files: - Create: - system/loki/files/falco-rules.yaml; - system/falco/templates/prometheus-rule.yaml, gated by .Values.prometheusRules, default true. - Modify: - system/loki/templates/audit-rules.yaml: add the key falco-rules.yaml from files/falco-rules.yaml; - system/monitoring-system/files/security-dashboard.json: add the panel "Falco events by priority, rule and namespace" (Loki, from warning up). - Test: test/offline/falco_test.go

Interfaces: - Consumes: renderFalco (Task 1). render.Loki and lokitool as in TestSecurityLogsRules. - Produces, Loki alerts (source: falco): - FalcoCriticalEvent, severity critical; - FalcoErrorEvent, severity warning. - Produces, Prometheus alerts: - FalcoNotRunning, severity critical; - FalcoStalled, severity critical; - FalcoEventsDropped, severity warning.

  • Step 1: Write the failing test TestFalcoLokiRules.
  • The rendered loki-audit-rules key falco-rules.yaml passes lokitool rules lint and lokitool rules check.
  • It has exactly the two Loki alerts above, with their severities and source: falco.
  • Each expression selects {job="pods", namespace="falco"}, runs | json, has __error__="" and groups by (rule, namespace).
  • FalcoCriticalEvent matches priority=~"Critical|Alert|Emergency"; FalcoErrorEvent matches priority="Error".
  • Neither expression filters on namespace (Review Focus 3).
  • Each has a summary and a description naming docs/how-to-guides/runtime-detection.md.
  • Step 2: Run it. go test -C test ./offline/ -run TestFalcoLokiRules -count=1 → FAIL.
  • Step 3: Write the Loki rules. Map output_fields["k8s.ns.name"] to the label namespace with | json extraction. Window [5m].
  • Step 4: Write the failing test TestFalcoPrometheusRules. In the PrometheusRule rendered for env "":
  • FalcoNotRunning compares kube_daemonset_status_number_ready with kube_daemonset_status_desired_number_scheduled for daemonset="falco", with for: 10m;
  • FalcoStalled fires on up == 0 for the Falco job, or when its syscall-event counter's increase is 0 over 10 minutes;
  • FalcoEventsDropped fires on an increase of Falco's drop counter.

Take the counters' names from Falco's /metrics, and note them in a comment. Candidates in 0.45: falcosecurity_scap_n_evts_total, falcosecurity_scap_n_drops_total. - [ ] Step 5: Run it. go test -C test ./offline/ -run TestFalcoPrometheusRules -count=1 → FAIL. - [ ] Step 6: Write prometheus-rule.yaml. Same form as system/trivy-operator/templates/prometheus-rule.yaml. - [ ] Step 7: Add the dashboard panel. A table or time series from sum by (priority, rule, namespace) (count_over_time({job="pods", namespace="falco"} | json | __error__="" [$__interval])). - [ ] Step 8: Run it. - go test -C test ./offline/ -run 'TestFalco|TestSecurityLogs|TestMonitoring' -count=1 → PASS. - scripts/render-chart system/monitoring-system succeeds. - [ ] Step 9: Commit. feat(falco): events alert through Loki, a stalled Falco through Prometheus, the Security dashboard shows them.

docs.text:
Files: - Create: test/e2e/falco_test.go - Modify: - test/scopes.yaml: - add label falco to labels:; - add falco to full; - add the group paths: [system/falco/**, system/loki/files/falco-rules.yaml, test/e2e/falco_test.go], tests: falco; - cli/internal/scope/repository_test.go:24: add falco to the expected full filter; - infra/testbed/release-paths.yaml: under not_run, add system/falco/templates/policy-exception.yaml and system/falco/templates/prometheus-rule.yaml.

Interfaces: - Consumes: lokiQuery (test/e2e/logs_test.go), kube.Kubectl, kube.CreateNamespace, kube.DeleteNamespace. - Consumes: the alert names from Task 2. Read the deployed expressions from the ConfigMap loki-audit-rules.

  • Step 1: Write Describe("Falco", Label("sandbox", "falco")), It "reports a read of /etc/shadow and a dropped binary", SpecTimeout(15*time.Minute).

  • Step 2: Write Describe("TestbedFalco", Label("testbed", "falco")), It "watches every node", SpecTimeout(15*time.Minute):

  • every Falco pod's log has the line that the modern eBPF probe is loaded;
  • the busybox drop-and-execute above, in a test namespace, appears in some Falco pod's log within 5 minutes, as JSON with that rule.
  • Step 3: Run the selection tests and see them fail. go test -C test ./offline/ -run 'TestE2E' -count=1 and go test -C cli ./internal/scope/ -count=1. They must fail on the new label or the missing full entry before the test/scopes.yaml edit.

docs.title: Task 4: The guide, the roadmap, and the proof on the clusters
docs.text:
Files: - Create: docs/how-to-guides/runtime-detection.md. It covers: - what Falco watches; - reading an event in Grafana (Explore, Loki: {namespace="falco"} | json); - each alert and what to do about it; - accepting an event in accepted with its reason, and where (values.yaml versus values-dev.yaml); - the measured resources; - 15g-2. - Modify: - mkdocs.yml: add the guide after how-to-guides/security-logs.md; - CLAUDE.md, roadmap: mark 15g done and name what it proved; - CLAUDE.md, Sandbox: one line on Falco; - CLAUDE.md, "Before the first production deploy": review Falco's events in the first days (accept with a reason or fix); the driver ran only on WSL's kernel and the testbed's VMs; record the testbed fallback here if it was taken; - system/falco/values-local.yaml: the measured limits; - system/falco/values*.yaml: accepted entries the baseline needs.

  • Step 1: Write the guide and the CLAUDE.md lines. Check them with mkdocs build --strict.
  • Step 2: Run scripts/ci-check all in the dev shell → rc=0.
  • Step 3: Commit, then run just dev from /home/nixos/homelab. Expected: the falco group's specs pass, and so does Falco.
  • Step 4: Run just dev-fresh, with the testbed stopped. Expected: the whole suite passes.
  • During the run, record Falco's peak memory and CPU: max_over_time(container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace="falco",container="falco"}[3h]) and the CPU rate.
  • Set values-local.yaml's limits to about twice the peak, and requests to about the median.
  • If Falco's CPU peak is above half a core, set falco.base_syscalls to the rules' set (base_syscalls.repair: true) and measure again.

Over the run's window, the Loki query sum by (rule, namespace) (count_over_time({job="pods", namespace="falco"} | json | __error__="" | priority=~"Error|Critical|Alert|Emergency" | output_fields_k8s_ns_name!="" [3h])) holds nothing but the falco-test-* namespaces.

docs.title: Buildah seccomp profile Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Turn on the kubelet's seccomp-default everywhere. Woodpecker's Buildah steps keep building under a Localhost profile (homelab/buildah.json) that nothing else may use.

Architecture: - The profile: a JSON file, containerd's RuntimeDefault plus measured additions. It ships to the nodes the way audit-policy.yaml does: NixOS tmpfiles on the nodes, a k3d --volume in the sandbox. - The mutation: a native MutatingAdmissionPolicy puts the profile on Woodpecker's Buildah step pods. - The guard: a native ValidatingAdmissionPolicy refuses that profile, and any other Localhost one, in namespace woodpecker for pods that are not all Buildah. - Both policies are in-tree (admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1, served by k3s 1.37.1): no webhook, no Kyverno dependency.

Tech Stack: k3s 1.37.1 (containerd embedded), NixOS flake infra/_modules/metal, OpenTofu module infra/_modules/k3d, Helm wrapper chart platform/woodpecker, Go tests (test/offline with testify, test/e2e with Ginkgo).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-buildah-seccomp-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• The flag is exactly --kubelet-arg=seccomp-default=true, in infra/_modules/k3d/k3d.yaml (nodeFilters: [server:*]) and infra/_modules/metal/flake/profiles/k3s-server.nix.
  • The profile's path is <kubelet seccomp root>/homelab/buildah.json, which is /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/homelab/buildah.json. Pods reference localhostProfile: homelab/buildah.json.
  • The source file is infra/_modules/metal/flake/seccomp/buildah.json, one file for the nodes and k3d.
  • The profile's base is the RuntimeDefault of the containerd embedded in k3s v1.37.1. The file records the k3s and containerd versions it came from.
  • No syscall is added unless Buildah was seen to need it. Each addition is listed with what needed it.
  • Image match: repository quay.io/buildah/stable, any tag or digest.
  • A failure never widens access. A missed mutation leaves RuntimeDefault, so the build fails.
  • Pipelines need no backend_options line.
  • Commits end with the session's Co-Authored-By and Claude-Session lines. Never commit to dev or master.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. The guard must not refuse what the mutation produces. Woodpecker's real Buildah step pod may carry more than the step's container: an init container, or a clone step's image. Task 4's sandbox spec runs the real pipeline, not a hand-made pod.
  2. A pod that sets its own profile.
  3. A step whose author sets RuntimeDefault keeps it: the mutation does not override it (offline fixture in Task 3, sandbox in Task 4).
  4. A container-level Localhost profile on a non-Buildah pod is refused, not only a pod-level one (Task 3 fixture, Task 4 spec).
  5. Image references with a digest or a registry port, such as quay.io/buildah/stable@sha256:… or quay.io/buildah/stable:v1.43.5, match. quay.io/buildah/stable-evil and evil.io/quay.io/buildah/stable do not. Task 3 covers each in its CEL tests.
  6. Pods outside woodpecker, and its server and agent pods, are untouched by both policies (Task 3 fixtures, Task 5's full suite).
  7. A newer kernel taking other syscall paths (clone3, the new mount API) on NixOS's kernel 7.0+. Task 6 builds on the testbed.

docs.title: Task 1: The profile, measured
docs.text:
Files: - Create: infra/_modules/metal/flake/seccomp/buildah.json - Create: infra/_modules/metal/flake/seccomp/README.md: where the base came from, the additions with what needed each, and how to regenerate it. - Test: test/offline/seccomp_test.go

Interfaces: - Produces: the file path above, and the profile name homelab/buildah.json. Tasks 2, 3, 4 and 6 use both.

  • Step 1: Find the base.
  • Read containerd's version from k3s v1.37.1's go.mod, tag v1.37.1+k3s1.
  • Generate the JSON of contrib/seccomp.DefaultProfile for a spec with containerd's default capability set (no CAP_SYS_ADMIN). Use a throwaway go run in the scratchpad against that containerd module version.

  • Check that nixpkgs' k3s_1_37 (the nodes' flake lock) is the same k3s patch. If not, ledger a ruling naming the version used.

  • Step 2: Measure the additions in the sandbox.

  • Copy the base with defaultAction: SCMP_ACT_LOG into the running k3d node, by hand at /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/homelab/measure.json.
  • Run a throwaway pod in namespace woodpecker:
    • image quay.io/buildah/stable:v1.43.5;
    • hostUsers: false, as Woodpecker's step pods have;
    • localhostProfile: homelab/measure.json;
    • command: TestWoodpecker's build (buildah --storage-driver vfs build --isolation chroot of a two-line Containerfile).
  • Collect the logged syscalls: dmesg/kmsg type=1326 lines with the pod's processes. If WSL's kernel does not log them, fall back to trial: base profile with SCMP_ACT_ERRNO, add each syscall the build fails on.
  • The additions are the logged syscalls that the base does not allow unconditionally.

  • Expected: a short list such as unshare, mount, umount2, pivot_root, setns, clone with namespace flags, possibly clone3. Delete the throwaway pod and file.

  • Step 3: Write the failing test TestBuildahSeccompProfile in test/offline/seccomp_test.go. It parses the file and asserts:

  • defaultAction is SCMP_ACT_ERRNO;
  • every addition from the README's list is allowed (SCMP_ACT_ALLOW, with no includes.caps condition);
  • a fixed sample of the base stays refused: bpf, kexec_load, init_module, ptrace, perf_event_open, keyctl, add_key, open_by_handle_at;
  • README.md names the k3s and containerd versions.

Run go test ./test/offline -run TestBuildahSeccompProfile. Expected: FAIL (file missing).

  • Step 4: Write buildah.json: the base, with the additions as their own syscalls entries (provenance goes in the README: seccomp JSON has no comments).

  • Prove it works. Copy it to the node as homelab/buildah.json, run the Step 2 pod with it: the build passes. Run the same pod with RuntimeDefault: it fails on unshare.

  • Step 5: Run the test. Expected: PASS. Commit feat(seccomp): Buildah's Localhost profile, RuntimeDefault plus what its chroot isolation needs.

docs.title: Task 2: The flag and the file on k3d and the nodes
docs.text:

docs.title: Task 3: The mutation and the guard
docs.text:
Files: - Create: platform/woodpecker/templates/seccomp-policy.yaml. It holds: - MutatingAdmissionPolicy woodpecker-buildah-seccomp with its binding; - ValidatingAdmissionPolicy woodpecker-localhost-seccomp with its binding (validationActions: [Deny]); - failurePolicy: Fail on both; - binding matchResources.namespaceSelector on kubernetes.io/metadata.name: {{ .Release.Namespace }}; - policy matchConstraints on pods CREATE. - Test: test/offline/woodpecker_seccomp_test.go

Interfaces: - Produces: policy names woodpecker-buildah-seccomp and woodpecker-localhost-seccomp. Task 4 reads them in failure messages.

The rules, which the CEL must implement: - Buildah pod: - every container and init container image, after stripping a @digest and then a :tag after the last /, equals quay.io/buildah/stable; - the pod has label woodpecker-ci.org/step or whatever the step-pod label the Kubernetes backend sets. Read it off a live step pod (TestWoodpecker's pipeline) and ledger it. - Mutation: on a Buildah pod with no pod-level seccompProfile and no container-level one, set spec.securityContext.seccompProfile to {type: Localhost, localhostProfile: homelab/buildah.json} (patchType: ApplyConfiguration, reinvocationPolicy: Never). - Guard: refuse a pod where the pod or any container (init included) has seccompProfile.type == 'Localhost', unless it is a Buildah pod and every such profile is homelab/buildah.json. - Message: "only Woodpecker's Buildah steps may use a Localhost seccomp profile (homelab/buildah.json)". - Annotate both policies with why they are native, not Kyverno: in-tree, they hold while Kyverno is down. They need no SkipDryRunOnMissingResource, since the kinds are built in.

  • Step 1: Write the failing test TestWoodpeckerSeccompPolicies.
  • It renders platform/woodpecker for both environments (render.Yq) and asserts both policies, both bindings, failurePolicy: Fail, [Deny] and the namespace selector.
  • It evaluates the two CEL rules over fixtures with k8s.io/apiserver's CEL libraries or github.com/google/cel-go with the Kubernetes CEL environment. If neither is practical in test/go.mod, assert the expressions' presence here and leave behavior to Task 4. Ledger the ruling.
  • Fixtures:
    • (a) Buildah step pod, no profile → mutated, admitted;
    • (b) alpine step pod → unchanged, admitted;
    • (c) Buildah pod with RuntimeDefault → unchanged;
    • (d) alpine with pod-level Localhost homelab/buildah.json → denied;
    • (e) alpine with a container-level one → denied;
    • (f) Buildah with Localhost other.json → denied;
    • (g) a Buildah container plus an alpine init container → not mutated, and denied if it asks;
    • (h) image refs quay.io/buildah/stable@sha256:…, quay.io/buildah/stable:v1.43.5 match; quay.io/buildah/stable-evil, evil.io/quay.io/buildah/stable do not.

Run it. Expected: FAIL. - [ ] Step 2: Write the template. Run the test, scripts/ci-check render, scripts/ci-check policy and scripts/ci-check mesh. Expected: PASS. - [ ] Step 3: Commit feat(woodpecker): native admission policies give Buildah steps their seccomp profile, and only them.

docs.title: Production's Nodes (12b-1) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: NixOS and one k3s cluster of three servers on the three HP mini PCs, installed from the network, and the hardware proofs: DNS, fio, kube-bench, the VIP moving with Wake-on-LAN, a power cut.

Architecture: - The node flake reads two new config.json fields, disk and network.dns. - infra/production/metal mirrors infra/testbed/metal, but nixie writes its record into the committed hosts.json (upstream's way). - The testbed's node specs also run on production. Two new specs, which stop nodes, carry a label hardware-proof that a routine production run never selects. - The install and the proofs are run by hand with the person, who provides the SSH key, the Hyper-V firewall rules, Cloudflare's login and the power strip.

Tech Stack: - Nix (the node flake) and Terragrunt/OpenTofu (the metal unit); - nixie and nixos-anywhere, lab cluster; - Ginkgo (test/e2e), testify (test/offline), just.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-production-nodes-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Nodes:
Node IP MAC homelab-1 (init_host) 192.168.0.11 38:22:e2:2c:dc:35 homelab-2 192.168.0.12 10:62:e5:16:d2:ca homelab-3 192.168.0.13 10:e7:c6:0f:63:a0

The API's VIP is 192.168.0.10. - Disk: /dev/nvme0n1 for every production node, from config.json's disk. Never in hosts.json: nixie drops unknown fields. - DNS: - production's config.json gets "network": {..., "dns": ["192.168.0.1"]}; - without network.dns, the nodes keep 8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1, so the testbed is unchanged; - budget: an NXDOMAIN and an AAAA-less name answer in under 1 s from a node and from a pod. - Install record: nixie writes machine_id_hash into infra/production/metal/hosts.json, and it is committed. The testbed keeps .state/testbed/ unchanged. - Host keys: trusted on first contact for hosts.json's addresses only (scripts/testbed-trust, reused). - Spec label: hardware-proof marks specs that power off nodes. just test e2e --env production with no --labels runs production && !hardware-proof && !scan. - fio: etcd's pattern --rw=write --ioengine=sync --fdatasync=1 --bs=2300 --size=22m, with a p99 fdatasync budget of 10 ms. - Never: - install a MAC not in hosts.json; - leave the Hyper-V rules after the install; - run just dev beside the testbed or with less than 30 GB free on C:; - commit to dev or master. - Commits end with the session's Co-Authored-By and Claude-Session lines.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A routine just test e2e --env production never powers off a node.
  2. Expect the default filter to exclude hardware-proof and scan, and --labels to still allow running them on purpose.
  3. Task 3 pins it with a dry-run (ginkgo --dry-run).
  4. A recorded host is never reinstalled.
  5. Expect nixie to get the repository's hosts.json itself, never a copy.
  6. Expect the record committed after the install.
  7. Task 2 pins it with an offline test on the unit's hook arguments.
  8. A node's own disk still wins over config.json's, and the testbed's VMs stay on /dev/sda. Task 1's fixture covers both.
  9. Wake-on-LAN from WSL over Wi-Fi may not reach a wired node.
  10. Expect the VIP spec to fail and name Wake-on-LAN.
  11. Expect a woken node with no nixie running to fall back to its NVMe.
  12. Task 5 runs it on the hardware.
  13. The power cut proves the nodes, not data. Expect the docs not to claim acknowledged writes survive (12b-2 does); Task 6 words it.

docs.text:

docs.title: Task 2: The unit infra/production/metal
docs.text:
Files: - Create: infra/production/metal/terragrunt.hcl, modelled on infra/testbed/metal/terragrunt.hcl. The differences: - no vms dependency; - the nixie hook runs scripts/metal-nixie with ${get_terragrunt_dir()}/hosts.json itself; - --address is the workstation's LAN address, from HOMELAB_PXE_ADDRESS (required; the hook fails with a message when it is unset); - trust reuses scripts/testbed-trust, its comment updated to cover production's install; - the enroll, kubeconfig and upgrade hooks use --environment production and infra/production/kubeconfig.yaml. - Create: infra/production/metal/hosts.json with the three hosts of Global Constraints (mac_address, ip). - Create: scripts/metal-nixie <hosts.json> <nixie args…>: sudo -v, then sudo "$(command -v nixie)" --hosts <hosts.json> "$@". No copy, no Wake-on-LAN listener: nixie's own Wake-on-LAN wakes real machines. - Modify: infra/production/argocd/terragrunt.hcl: dependencies { paths = ["../metal"] }, as the testbed's argocd. - Modify: infra/production/metal/authorized_keys: the person's new production public key (Task 4's step 1; until then the task leaves the placeholder). - Test: test/offline/metal_test.go.
