docs.title: Task 3: The specs run on production, and stop nodes only when asked
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: test/e2e/testbed_test.go. - testbedHosts() becomes metalHosts(), which reads infra/<metalEnv()>/metal/hosts.json. - metalEnv() returns testbed when ENV=testbed, and production when ENV is empty (just test e2e --env production). - Callers are renamed. - Modify: Describe("TestbedNodes"), Describe("TestbedSecretsEncrypted") and Describe("TestbedSeccomp") take the label production too. - Modify: test/e2e/scan_test.go: ScanBench takes production. - Create: test/e2e/production_test.go: - Describe("NodesResolveQuickly", Label("production")) (production only: the testbed's VMs also query 8.8.8.8 through NAT and may meet the same interception, a deferred minor, not this step's). On every node over SSH, and from a busybox pod in a scratch namespace, it times nslookup of nx-<random>.example.com (NXDOMAIN) and of ipv4only.arpa's AAAA. Each answers in under 1 s. The time is measured inside the node or pod (date +%s%N before and after), not around SSH. - Describe("ProductionVIPMoves", Label("production", "hardware-proof"), Serial). - It finds the VIP's holder (lease plndr-cp-lock) and records its bootID. - It runs systemctl poweroff over SSH and waits up to 2 minutes for /readyz through the VIP, and for the holder to change. - It then sends Wake-on-LAN to the stopped node's MAC with wakeOnLAN(mac string) error: a magic packet to UDP 255.255.255.255:9. - It waits up to 10 minutes for a new bootID and Ready. - On a timeout the message names Wake-on-LAN and asks the person to press the button. - Describe("ProductionPowerCut", Label("production", "hardware-proof"), Serial). - It records every node's bootID and prints "switch the power strip off, wait 30 s, switch it on". - It then waits up to 30 minutes for every node to report a new bootID and Ready, and for /readyz through the VIP. - It prints the duration from the first API failure to all Ready. - Modify: test/justfile e2e: for production with no --labels, the filter is production && !hardware-proof && !scan. - Modify: test/scopes.yaml: add label hardware-proof to labels:. - Test: the dry runs below, and TestE2EKeepsSelection.

  • TestProductionDefaultFilter (in test/offline, beside the e2e selection tests) runs just test e2e-filter production "" and just test e2e-filter production hardware-proof. It asserts the first prints production && !hardware-proof && !scan and the second (hardware-proof) && production.
  • It then lists each filter's specs with go tool ginkgo --dry-run -v --label-filter=<filter> ./e2e:
    • ProductionVIPMoves and ProductionPowerCut appear only in the second;
    • TestbedNodes and NodesResolveQuickly appear in the first.
  • Step 2: Run it. Expected: FAIL.
  • Step 3: Implement the files above. go vet ./e2e.
  • Step 4: Run TestProductionDefaultFilter and TestE2EKeepsSelection, then just cli check. Expected: PASS.
  • Step 5: Commit test(12b-1): the node specs run on production; specs that stop nodes only on purpose.

docs.text:

Commit hosts.json (the record) and authorized_keys: feat(12b-1): production's nodes installed. - [ ] Step 5: GREEN. The same command as step 2. A new kube-bench FAIL is triaged into .cluster-scan-accepted.yaml or fixed. - [ ] Step 6: Rerun terragrunt apply. Expected: nixie sees every host recorded and does not start; upgrade finds every node up to date.

docs.title: Matrix on tuwunel Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Replace the Dendrite and Element chart with one app-template file: tuwunel and FluffyChat, LAN only, signed in through Kanidm, proven in the sandbox.

Architecture: apps/matrix.yaml, like apps/actualbudget.yaml: - two controllers (server, client), routes on the LAN Gateway; - a KanidmOAuth2Client matrix whose secret tuwunel reads from a file, and an AuthorizationPolicy; - a daily volume.

Tech Stack: app-template (the version the apps ApplicationSet pins), tuwunel, FluffyChat, kaniop, Ginkgo.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-matrix-tuwunel-design.md

docs.title: Production's Platform (12b-2) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Production's platform (system/*, platform/*, no app) on the hardware through a stage switch, Ceph healthy, an etcd disk alert, and a power cut with data, before any app.

Architecture: - A label homelab/stage on Argo CD's cluster Secret gates whatever deploys an app: the apps ApplicationSet, root's apps/* directories (Matrix) and system/public-scan. - The bootstrap resolves the stage: unset keeps the cluster's label, a new cluster gets all, and it never moves back from all to platform. - The first production deploy runs from a master release with the stage set to platform.

Tech Stack: Argo CD ApplicationSets (Helm values), OpenTofu/Terragrunt (infra/_modules/argocd), POSIX sh, Prometheus rules, Ginkgo, testify, just.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-production-platform-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• The label: homelab/stage, values platform or all.
  • The variable is HOMELAB_PRODUCTION_STAGE (production only).
  • The sandbox and the testbed are always all.
  • Resolving the stage: requested platform or all wins, except platform on a cluster labelled all fails. Unset keeps the current label. Unset with no label gives all.
  • Selectors: every selector that gates apps matches homelab/bootstrap: "true" and homelab/stage: all. Selectors for anything else are unchanged.
  • Restated generators: the generators restated in values-dev.yaml, values-testbed.yaml and values-seed.yaml change with values.yaml's (Helm replaces lists; scripts/check-env-config checks them).
  • etcd alerts (warning):
  • EtcdSlowDisk: histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(etcd_disk_wal_fsync_duration_seconds_bucket{job="kube-etcd"}[10m])) > 0.010 for 1h, per instance;
  • EtcdLeaderChanges: increase(etcd_server_leader_changes_seen_total{job="kube-etcd"}[1h]) > 3.
  • Production:
  • no test accounts or clients;
  • Renovate's key withheld until 12b-3;
  • kured removed (spec decision 7);
  • the cut before lab backup enable.
  • Never:
  • just dev beside the testbed, or with C: under 30 GB;
  • commit to dev or master;
  • lower a cluster's stage.
  • Commits end with the session's Co-Authored-By and Claude-Session lines.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. An existing cluster with apps (the sandbox) loses no Application when the selectors gain homelab/stage.
  2. Expect the bootstrap to apply the labelled Secret before the ApplicationSets.
  3. Task 1 proves the order offline; Task 4's just dev proves it on the sandbox.
  4. A deploy with the variable unset never changes the stage. Expect platform to stay platform across repeated just infra deploy production. Task 1 pins it.
  5. Matrix and public-scan stay out under platform, and come with all. Expect it in every environment's restated generators. Task 1 renders each.
  6. The cut's scratch data is gone afterwards, even when the spec fails midway. Expect deferred cleanup. Task 3's spec owns it.
  7. Nothing reboots a node but lab cluster upgrade. kured is removed (spec decision 7); TestNoRebootDaemon pins it.

docs.title: Step 10f: Argo Workflows and Argo Events replace Woodpecker — Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Forgejo org ci's repositories build, sign and attest their images through Argo Events and Argo Workflows' golden path; Woodpecker is gone.

Architecture: Three wrapper charts: platform/argo-workflows (controller and SSO server), platform/argo-events (controller), platform/ci (EventBus, Forgejo EventSource and Sensor, the WorkflowTemplates, secrets, seccomp policies). lab infra forgejo sync keeps org ci's webhook and bot user; OpenBao signs through transit; Kyverno audits the signatures.

Tech Stack: Helm wrapper charts synced by Argo CD, argo-workflows 2.0.18 (v4.1.6), argo-events 2.4.28 (v1.9.11), Buildah, cosign (hashivault://), Syft or Trivy for SPDX, OpenBao transit, Kyverno, Go (cli/, test/).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-13-argo-ci-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Latest stable releases, pinned exactly; every image by tag or digest (Kyverno's pinned-images policy).
  • Hosts as <host>.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }}; no domain or IP in a chart (scripts/check-env-config).
  • Every workload: RuntimeDefault seccomp, no privilege escalation, non-root where the image allows, or a PolicyException with homelab/reason.
  • Every meshed namespace has an allow; webhooks' pods carry istio.io/dataplane-mode: none; scripts/check-mesh-policies passes.
  • Every PVC carries homelab/backup (scripts/check-backup-groups); every secret has a catalog entry (lab secrets check).
  • Secrets via ExternalSecrets from SecretStore openbao, keys under the reading namespace; generated ones under <namespace>/generated/.
  • New components get test/scopes.yaml entries in the same change.
  • just dev only from /home/nixos/homelab (never this worktree); never beside the testbed.
  • Commits end with the Co-Authored-By and Claude-Session lines.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A Forgejo push whose payload lacks fields the Sensor reads (a tag push, a branch deletion with an all-zero after): no Workflow, or one that ends error with a status, never a crash loop of the Sensor.
  2. A .ci.yaml that is not YAML or names image with a path outside the repository's name (../other): the run fails with a failure status, nothing pushed.
  3. The signing step on a pull request or a non-default branch: never signs (only default-branch pushes reach zot).
  4. A Workflow submitted through the UI by an editor with an inline template: refused by templateReferencing: Strict.
  5. Two pushes in a row to the same repository: both run; the second's status lands on its own commit.

Task 4 pins 1–3 and 5 in its offline template tests where a render can show them and in the CI e2e spec otherwise; Task 1 pins 4 (render) and Task 8 (e2e).

docs.title: OpenTelemetry Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: The OpenTelemetry Operator's Collectors replace Alloy for every log stream into Loki (OTLP, OTel labels), and traces from the Istio Gateways and the platform tools reach Tempo, linked to their logs in Grafana.

Architecture: system/opentelemetry holds the Operator and two OpenTelemetryCollectors: the agent (DaemonSet: files on the node → Loki directly, persistent queue) and the gateway (Deployment: OTLP traces → Tempo, Kubernetes events → Loki). system/tempo stores traces; system/loki loses Alloy and gains OTLP ingestion. Istio's Telemetry API makes the Gateways send spans and JSON access logs carrying trace_id.

Tech Stack: opentelemetry-operator chart 0.129.0 (Operator 0.162.0), otel/opentelemetry-collector-k8s 0.165.0, grafana-community tempo chart 3.2.1 (Tempo 3.1.1), Loki chart 18.17.0, Istio 1.32 Telemetry API, Go tests (testify offline, Ginkgo e2e).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-14-opentelemetry-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• (user) No parallel run: Alloy is removed in this branch; the sandbox shows what breaks.
  • (user) Loki labels follow OpenTelemetry's conventions; nothing keeps namespace, pod, container, app, job. The mapping every rewrite uses:
Before (Alloy) After (OTLP into Loki) namespace k8s_namespace_name pod k8s_pod_name container k8s_container_name app service_name node k8s_node_name (structured metadata unless a query needs it indexed) job="pods" dropped: any pod stream is selected by its k8s_* labels job="audit/k3s" service_name="k3s-audit" job="audit/openbao" service_name="openbao-audit" Kubernetes events' job service_name="kubernetes-events"
  • Versions pinned exactly as in Tech Stack; if the Operator refuses Collector 0.165.0, pin the newest pair that works and say why next to the pin.
  • Every PVC carries homelab/backup: none (Tempo, like Loki).
  • OTLP is never routed: no HTTPRoute to a Collector or Tempo; the gateway Collector's AuthorizationPolicy names its senders.
  • The Operator's pod webhook: failurePolicy: Ignore; its pods carry istio.io/dataplane-mode: none.
  • Audit streams keep 60 days unless Task 10's measurement says otherwise, then CLAUDE.md's rule (45, then 30 days; never a bigger volume).
  • The sandbox's new components get small requests in values-dev.yaml; the node stays under 85% of its memory during the suite (79% today).

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. A Collector restart while Loki is down: lines read meanwhile arrive later (LogsSurviveLokiOutage, Task 8; the agent's queue in file_storage, Task 2).
  2. The Operator down or not yet synced: pods anywhere in the cluster are still created (offline assertion on the webhook's failurePolicy, Task 1).
  3. OTLP sent by a namespace with no reason to send: refused (OTLPRefusedFromOthers, Task 8).
  4. The API server rotating audit.log: the agent keeps following it by name, no line read twice (offline assertion on the receiver's include and start_at, Task 2).
  5. OpenBao lines that are not audit JSON (its startup, its errors): stay ordinary pod logs, not openbao-audit (offline assertion on the routing condition, Task 2; SecurityLogsOpenBao, Task 8).

docs.title: Backstage-1 Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Backstage runs on the LAN behind Kanidm, with the homelab's catalog, TechDocs, a template creating repositories in Forgejo org ci, and the Kubernetes, Argo CD and alert views; homepage and the catalog are generated from one description per app.

Architecture: The app's source lives in backstage/ (made by @backstage/create-app), built like lab's image: from the checkout in the sandbox, by GitHub Actions (signed keyless, SBOM attested, checked by Kyverno) for production. platform/backstage wraps the upstream backstage chart with a CloudNativePG database, a Kanidm client, ESO secrets and read-only RBAC; in the sandbox it is an optional component. lab catalog generates the catalog and homepage's list from descriptions kept in each app's and component's own files.

Tech Stack: Backstage (latest stable, 1.55 or later), Node (the version create-app pins), the backstage Helm chart (backstage/charts), CloudNativePG, kaniop, ESO, Go (cli/), Ginkgo (test/e2e).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-16-backstage-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Latest stable release of every package, chart and image, pinned exactly (CLAUDE.md Rules); no latest tags.
  • Host backstage.<domain> on istio-system/gateway only; never on Gateway public.
  • Sign-in only for homelab-admins and homelab-editors (Kanidm scopeMap and the sign-in resolver).
  • Templates executable only by homelab-admins; editors may refresh entities, never register, unregister or execute.
  • Kubernetes reader: one read-only ClusterRole, no Secrets, no pods/log, no pods/exec.
  • Scaffolder actions installed: fetch:*, publish:gitea, catalog:register, debug:log only.
  • Every secret has an entry in cli/internal/rotate/catalog.yaml; every PVC its homelab/backup label (backstage-db: none).
  • In the sandbox Backstage syncs only with the cluster Secret label homelab/app-backstage.
  • Kanidm client: confidential, PKCE (sent by default), tokenSignedResponseAlg: ES256.
  • The threat model, CLAUDE.md and docs/superpowers/deferred-minors.md are updated in the same PR.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• A Kanidm user only in homelab-users reaches backstage.<domain>: Kanidm refuses at its consent step, and if a token were obtained the resolver refuses (no catalog User). Pinned in Task 6's spec.
  • An editor calls the scaffolder or catalog API directly (not through the UI): the permission policy refuses scaffolder.task.create and catalog.location.create/delete server-side. Pinned in Task 2's policy tests and Task 6's spec.
  • A description added to an app file but the generated files not regenerated: lab catalog check fails the basic checks. Pinned in Task 1.
  • An app file with several routes (apps/jellyfin.yaml: Jellyfin, Transmission, Prowlarr, Radarr, Sonarr, Jellyseerr): each route keeps its own homepage entry and catalog component. Pinned in Task 1's tests.
  • Backstage restarted with the database gone (sandbox fresh, or backstage-db recreated): the catalog rebuilds from its locations and LDAP without manual steps. Pinned in Task 6's spec (fresh install).

docs.title: Task 1: One description per app; lab catalog generates the catalog and homepage's list
docs.text:
Files: - Create: cli/internal/catalog/catalog.go, cli/internal/catalog/catalog_test.go, cli/cmd/lab/catalog.go (follow how existing commands register in cli/cmd/lab) - Create: catalog/ (generated: catalog/all.yaml, a Location listing one file per system; catalog/systems.yaml; catalog/components/*.yaml) - Modify: every apps/*.yaml (a top-level homelab: key; app-template's schema allows unknown keys), every system/*/Chart.yaml and platform/*/Chart.yaml (annotations:), apps/homepage.yaml (its services.yaml generated; external links under its own homelab.links) - Modify: scripts/ci-check (a check catalog running lab catalog check), test/scopes.yaml (catalog/** skipped: read only by Backstage, which Task 6's specs cover through platform/backstage/**)

Interfaces: - Produces: lab catalog generate (writes catalog/ and the services.yaml block of apps/homepage.yaml), lab catalog check (exit 1 and a diff when either differs). Entity names: an app's route <file>-<route> collapsed to <file> when a file has one route; components <dir>; owner group:default/homelab-admins; systems homelab-apps, homelab-platform, homelab-system under domain-less system homelab. - Description schema, in an app file (one item per route; route names the app-template route key):

homelab:
  - route: main
    name: Jellyfin
    description: Films and series for the family
    group: Popular          # homepage's group
    icon: jellyfin.svg      # homepage's icon
    lifecycle: production

and in a Chart.yaml: annotations: {homelab/name, homelab/description, homelab/group, homelab/icon, homelab/host (optional)}. A component without a host gets a catalog entity and no homepage entry.

  • Step 1: Write the failing tests in catalog_test.go: TestGenerateFromApps (a fixture app with two routes yields two components and two homepage entries with hosts <host>.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }} taken from the route's hostnames), TestGenerateFromCharts (a fixture Chart.yaml without homelab/host yields a component and no homepage entry), TestCheckReportsDrift (a changed description makes Check return an error naming the file), TestHomepageKeepsLinks (entries under apps/homepage.yaml's homelab.links are copied after the generated groups, unchanged).
  • Step 2: Run just cli test — Expected: FAIL (package catalog does not exist).
  • Step 3: Implement Generate(root string) (map[string][]byte, error) (path → content) and Check(root string) error in catalog.go; the command writes or compares. Output sorted and stable (the check diffs it).
  • Step 4: Run just cli test — Expected: PASS.
  • Step 5: Describe every app and component: move every entry of homepage's hand-written list into its app's homelab: key (same name, description, group, icon), external links into homelab.links; annotate every system/* and platform/* Chart.yaml. Run go run ./cmd/lab catalog generate from cli/.
  • Step 6: Verify homepage lost nothing: an offline test TestHomepageServicesKept in test/offline asserting the rendered services.yaml holds every href the list held before this task (the list frozen in the test).

docs.text:

Frontend: Kubernetes, Argo CD (community), TechDocs, home page; Alertmanager alerts through Roadie's backstage-plugin-prometheus if it builds against this Backstage, otherwise left out and noted in deferred-minors.md for Backstage-2. - Config read from the environment (names fixed for Task 5): BACKSTAGE_BASE_URL, KANIDM_ISSUER, AUTH_OIDC_CLIENT_ID, AUTH_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET, AUTH_SESSION_SECRET, BACKEND_SECRET, POSTGRES_HOST, POSTGRES_PORT, POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, CATALOG_REPOSITORY (the repository URL Argo CD reads), CATALOG_REVISION, FORGEJO_HOST, FORGEJO_TOKEN, ARGOCD_URL, ARGOCD_USERNAME, ARGOCD_PASSWORD, LDAP_URL, LDAP_BIND_DN, LDAP_BIND_SECRET, ALERTMANAGER_URL, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT. - Sign-in resolver: emailLocalPartMatchingUserEntityName or the Kanidm preferred_username matched to a User entity name; no dangerouslyAllowSignInWithoutUserInCatalog.

  • Step 1: Generate the app with create-app into backstage/ (name homelab); commit the untouched scaffold first (chore(backstage): the app as create-app makes it), so later diffs show only our changes.
  • Step 2: Write the failing policy tests in policy.test.ts: admins may execute templates (scaffolder.task.create → ALLOW for a user whose ownership refs include group:default/homelab-admins); editors may not execute templates (→ DENY for group:default/homelab-editors); editors may refresh, not register or unregister (catalog.entity.refresh ALLOW, catalog.location.create and catalog.location.delete DENY); everyone signed in reads the catalog (catalog.entity.read ALLOW for an editor).

  • Step 6: Wire the modules and config (Interfaces), the home page (starred entities, recently visited docs, links to https://argocd.${domain} and https://grafana.${domain} from config), TechDocs builder: local, publisher: local, catalog locations: ${CATALOG_REPOSITORY} at ${CATALOG_REVISION} path catalog/all.yaml, LDAP: groups homelab-admins and homelab-editors and their members only.

docs.title: Task 3: The image, built like lab's
docs.text:
Files: - Create: backstage/Dockerfile (multi-stage: build with yarn; runtime on the slim Node image create-app's docs use, Python with mkdocs-techdocs-core and every MkDocs plugin and extension mkdocs.yml uses, numeric non-root user), scripts/build-backstage-image (builds homelab-backstage:dev and k3d image imports it, like scripts/build-lab-image), .github/workflows/backstage-image.yaml (from lab-image.yaml: on master when backstage/** changes, ghcr.io/<owner>/homelab-backstage:<sha>, keyless signature, SPDX SBOM attested), system/kyverno/templates/backstage-image-policy.yaml (from lab-image-policy.yaml: production only, subject the new workflow) - Modify: justfile (just dev runs scripts/build-backstage-image when Backstage is among the sandbox's optional apps), test/offline (a TestBackstageImagePolicy beside TestLabImagePolicy), test/scopes.yaml

docs.title: Task 4: Kanidm, Forgejo and Argo CD give Backstage its identities
docs.text:
Files: - Create: platform/backstage/templates/kanidm-client.yaml (as platform/forgejo/templates/kanidm-client.yaml, scopeMap only homelab-admins and homelab-editors, redirect https://backstage.<domain>/api/auth/oidc/handler/frame) - Modify: platform/kanidm (LDAPS enabled through kaniop's Kanidm resource, reachable only from namespace backstage: its allow policy; a service account backstage-ldap able to read the two groups and their members) — if kaniop cannot enable LDAP, a backend module of our own reading Kanidm's REST API with that service account's API token replaces the LDAP module (record the choice in the plan's notes and the spec's design) - Modify: platform/kanidm/values.yaml (oauth2ClientNamespaces gains backstage), cli/internal/forgejo/sync.go (a user backstage in a team templates of org ci with "create repositories" only, and read access to org ops; its token written to OpenBao backstage/forgejo-token), system/argocd/values.yaml (a local account backstage with login, RBAC role:readonly; its password generated in OpenBao and bcrypted into argocd-secret by an ExternalSecret template) - Modify: cli/internal/rotate/catalog.yaml (entries kanidm-client.backstage, forgejo.backstage-token (workstation, like forgejo.ci-bot-token), argocd.backstage-password, kanidm.backstage-ldap, backstage.session-secret, backstage.backend-secret), platform/generated-secrets/values.yaml - Test: cli/internal/forgejo (TestSyncCreatesBackstageUser, beside ci-bot's tests), lab secrets check

docs.title: Sub-project 1a: kind + Cilium sandbox (foundation)
docs.text: Status: approved 2026-10-12, implemented on branch dev.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: A local sandbox, built with one command, that is the place to test changes on the dev branch before they are merged into master. 1a builds the foundation: cluster, networking, ingress, certificates, GitOps, and metrics. Platform services (users/authZ, Grafana, registry) come in 1b.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• The fork (duongle-steven/homelab) diverges from upstream. The apps/<name>/{Chart.yaml,values.yaml} layout stays so upstream changes can still be cherry-picked.
  • Roadmap: 0 workstation (done) → 1a sandbox foundation → 1b sandbox platform → 2 Gateway API migration → 3 production kubeadm + Ubuntu LTS. Each step changes one thing, so a failure points to that change.
  • master has no working sandbox flow. metal/k3d-dev.yaml exists but nothing calls it; upstream keeps that flow on its stale dev branch. upstream/dev edits values.yaml directly, deploys everything, and depends on in-cluster Gitea. This design does not reuse it.
  • Workstation: NixOS-WSL with Docker CE and 12 GB RAM. Pages are opened from a Windows browser via WSL localhost forwarding.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Cluster kind (kubeadm-based, matches the future production cluster), replaces k3d CNI Cilium with kube-proxy replacement, LB IPAM + L2 announcements (same as prod) Ingress ingress-nginx, kept for now (Gateway API is sub-project 2) Branching dev is the integration branch; sandbox config lives on every branch and is selected with env=dev Env overrides optional values-dev.yaml next to values.yaml, loaded only in dev GitOps source in dev github.com/duongle-steven/homelab, branch dev (no Gitea) Versions every tool and chart touched is moved to its current stable release (verified while planning, then pinned exactly)

docs.title: 1. Cluster layer (metal/)
docs.text:
• metal/kind-dev.yaml (new; delete metal/k3d-dev.yaml):
  • cluster name homelab-dev, one control-plane node, node image that ships with the current stable kind
  • networking.disableDefaultCNI: true, networking.kubeProxyMode: none
  • kubeadmConfigPatches binding etcd, kube-scheduler and kube-controller-manager metrics to 0.0.0.0, so Prometheus can scrape them (production kubeadm will need the same)
  • Fixed Docker network. Before the cluster is created, the kind Docker network is created with subnet 172.30.0.0/16 (skipped if it exists), so LB IPs stay the same across rebuilds.
  • make -C metal env=dev (default target depends on env; prod keeps boot cluster):
  • create the network, then kind create cluster --config kind-dev.yaml (skipped if the cluster exists), and write metal/kubeconfig.yaml
  • ansible-playbook -i inventories/dev.yml cluster.yml. The metal group in dev.yml is empty, so only the localhost Cilium play runs.
  • start container homelab-dev-proxy (alpine/socat, --network host, --restart unless-stopped) forwarding 127.0.0.1:80 and :443 to 172.30.255.200 (skipped if it is already running)
  • make -C metal env=dev clean: delete the cluster, the proxy container and the kind network.
  • Cilium role:
  • k8sServiceHost/k8sServicePort become inventory variables (prod.yml: 127.0.0.1/6444; dev.yml: homelab-dev-control-plane/6443)
  • bump to current stable Cilium and fix any changed CRD fields (e.g. CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool.spec.blocks vs cidrs, API version of the L2 policy)
  • dev.yml sets load_balancer_ip_pool: [172.30.255.200/29]
  • Flake: move nixpkgs to nixos-26.05, replace kube3d with kind, and add cilium-cli.

docs.title: 2. GitOps layer (system/, apps/)
docs.text:
• Bootstrap. system/bootstrap.yml takes env. In dev it renders ArgoCD with values.yaml + values-dev.yaml and skips the seed/Gitea switch. All dev settings for ArgoCD live in values-dev.yaml, not in values-seed.yaml: after bootstrap, ArgoCD manages itself through the ApplicationSet, which only loads values.yaml + values-dev.yaml.
  • system/argocd/values-dev.yaml:
  • git generator: repo https://github.com/duongle-steven/homelab, revision dev, an allowlist of exact paths: system/argocd, system/ingress-nginx, system/cert-manager, system/monitoring-system, apps/excalidraw
  • template source: same repo and revision, plus helm.valueFiles: [values.yaml, values-dev.yaml] and helm.ignoreMissingValueFiles: true
  • global.domain: argocd.127-0-0-1.nip.io
  • Helm replaces lists instead of merging them, and YAML anchors do not cross files, so the dev file restates generator and source in full.
  • Prod values.yaml is unchanged.
  • system/ingress-nginx/values-dev.yaml: Service annotation lbipam.cilium.io/ips: 172.30.255.200.
  • system/cert-manager:
  • templates/clusterissuer.yaml branches on a new value issuer.dev (default false)
  • when true, it renders a self-signed bootstrap issuer, a CA Certificate homelab-dev-ca (in the cert-manager namespace), and a ClusterIssuer named letsencrypt-prod of type ca backed by that certificate. Apps keep their cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-prod annotation unchanged.
  • The same CA is what 1b mounts into dex and Grafana. It can be imported into Windows to get rid of browser warnings (documented, optional).
  • system/monitoring-system/values-dev.yaml:
  • alertmanager.enabled: false. Disabling it removes the ntfy relay, which would otherwise send real notifications, and its manually created webhook-transformer secret.
  • kubeProxy.enabled: false (Cilium replaces kube-proxy)
  • drop the Loki datasource (no Loki in the sandbox)
  • apps/excalidraw/values-dev.yaml: host draw.127-0-0-1.nip.io, and the external-dns/Cloudflare annotations set to null.
  • Chart versions: the charts of the allowlisted components (argo-cd, argocd-apps, ingress-nginx, cert-manager, kube-prometheus-stack, app-template) are bumped to their current stable versions, one commit per chart. Breaking value changes are fixed in values.yaml, because they affect prod too.

docs.title: 3. Workflow, testing, docs
docs.text:
• Root Makefile:
  • make dev runs metal system smoke-test with env=dev. It skips external (Terraform/Cloudflare), post-install and the PXE clean.
  • make dev-clean runs make -C metal env=dev clean.
  • Plain make is unchanged.
  • Change flow: commit to dev, git push origin dev, and ArgoCD in the sandbox syncs. After it is verified, merge dev into master.
  • Smoke test (test/smoke_test.go): the app list depends on ENV (dev: argocd-server, excalidraw; prod: unchanged). make dev sets ENV=dev and INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY=1. Requests go to https://<host>.127-0-0-1.nip.io, so they use the real path: localhost → socat → LB IP (L2) → ingress-nginx → app.
  • Docs:
  • new repo CLAUDE.md with the architecture decisions, roadmap, stable-version rule, branch model and values-dev.yaml convention
  • rewrite docs/installation/sandbox.md for kind: 12 GB, make dev, push to origin dev, optional CA import, make dev-clean

docs.title: Acceptance criteria (on branch dev)
docs.text:
1. make dev succeeds from scratch, and succeeds again when run a second time.
  2. cilium status is OK; the ingress-nginx Service has external IP 172.30.255.200.
  3. All ArgoCD Applications in the allowlist are Synced and Healthy.
  4. Prometheus has no down targets for kubelet, apiserver, etcd, scheduler, controller-manager and ingress-nginx.
  5. The smoke test passes.
  6. https://draw.127-0-0-1.nip.io and https://argocd.127-0-0-1.nip.io open in the Windows browser.
  7. make dev-clean leaves no cluster, proxy container or kind network.
  8. Plain make (prod) targets and prod values are unchanged in behaviour, apart from chart and Cilium version bumps.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• WSL localhost forwarding for ports below 1024 bound by a container on the host network is assumed to work. It is verified early in the plan; if it fails, the fallback is binding the socat proxy to 0.0.0.0.
  • Cilium L2 announcements inside kind need the right devices/interface settings. These are verified with an ARP check from the WSL host.
  • Chart bumps may need value migrations (especially kube-prometheus-stack and argo-cd). One commit per chart keeps failures easy to locate.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• 1b: external-secrets, global-secrets, kanidm, dex, Grafana, zot, CoreDNS rewrite of *.127-0-0-1.nip.io, scripts/hacks changes
  • Gitea, Woodpecker, Renovate and Loki in the sandbox
  • Gateway API (sub-project 2), kubeadm and Ubuntu for production (sub-project 3)

docs.title: Sub-project 1b: sandbox identity (secrets, Kanidm, Dex)
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-12, written spec awaiting review. Branch: dev.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: The sandbox gets a working identity layer, declared in git and tested automatically: generated secrets, Kanidm with groups and test accounts, and Dex in front of Kanidm. Applications that log in through Dex (Grafana, ArgoCD, zot) are sub-project 1c.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Builds on 1a (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-kind-cilium-sandbox-design.md): kind + Cilium, ingress-nginx at 172.30.255.200, cert-manager issuing from the dev CA under the name letsencrypt-prod, ArgoCD syncing an allowlist from origin dev, and values-dev.yaml overlays.
  • Upstream setup today:
  • global-secrets is a Job that runs golang:1.19-alpine, downloads modules at runtime and creates random secrets that do not exist yet. It never regenerates them.
  • external-secrets 0.10 copies them to app namespaces with the v1beta1 API.
  • scripts/hacks uses pexpect to log in to the Kanidm CLI as idm_admin and creates the editor group and the dex OAuth2 client. It then writes kanidm.dex for Dex and configures Gitea.
  • scripts/onboard-user creates people and adds them to editor.
  • Kanidm runs as an app-template StatefulSet with a self-signed home.arpa cert. Dex talks to it with PKCE disabled.
  • Smoke tests only check that ingresses return 200; nothing tests SSO.
  • No production cluster exists yet. Production values still carry upstream's settings (khuedoan.com, …) until make configure runs in sub-project 3.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Identity provisioning Groups and OAuth2 clients in git through the kaniop operator; real people created by scripts/onboard-user (the repo is public) Kanidm deployment Managed by kaniop (Kanidm CR), replacing the app-template StatefulSet Groups homelab-admins, homelab-editors, homelab-users; anyone in none of them is refused Generated secrets ESO Password generators replace the Go Job; created once (refreshInterval: 0); manual rotation, documented Test accounts dev-admin, dev-editor, dev-viewer (one group each) and dev-outsider (no group), dev only Test tooling Go + chromedp in test/, driving chromium from nixpkgs Versions Current stable, verified 2026-10-12: external-secrets chart 2.12.0, kaniop 0.18.0, Kanidm 1.11.2, Dex chart 0.26.0 (Dex 2.46.0); re-check and pin exactly while planning

docs.title: 1. Secrets chain
docs.text:
• platform/external-secrets: bump the chart 0.10.2 → 2.12.0.
  • API migration: move every ExternalSecret and ClusterSecretStore in the repo to external-secrets.io/v1. This covers 10 files, including production-only apps:
  • apps/paperless, apps/tailscale, apps/wireguard
  • platform/dex, platform/gitea, platform/global-secrets, platform/grafana, platform/renovate, platform/woodpecker, platform/zot
  • platform/global-secrets:
  • Delete files/secret-generator/ and templates/secret-generator/.
  • A template iterates over a list in values.yaml, with the same entries as the old config.yaml: names, keys, lengths and special characters. Each entry renders:
    • a Password generator
    • an ExternalSecret with refreshInterval: 0 that writes the Secret into namespace global-secrets
  • ClusterSecretStore global-secrets is unchanged in behaviour (API version only).
  • values-dev.yaml adds dex.smoke (key client_secret).
  • Rotation: a new docs page describes manual rotation:
  • Delete the target Secret; ESO regenerates it.
  • Restart its consumers.
  • For admin passwords stored in an app database, also change the password in the app.

docs.title: 2. Kanidm managed by kaniop (platform/kanidm)
docs.text:
• Chart: the dependency changes from app-template to the kaniop chart (operator and CRDs). Delete templates/issuer.yaml and templates/certificate.yaml.
  • New templates:
  • Certificate for Kanidm from issuer letsencrypt-prod (the dev CA in the sandbox).
  • Kanidm CR:
    • Kanidm 1.11.2, one replica, 1Gi storage, that TLS secret
    • domain/origin from values: production uses values.yaml (still upstream's domain until make configure); dev uses auth.127-0-0-1.nip.io
    • ingress for the UI with backend-protocol: HTTPS
    • cross-namespace kanidmRef allowed for namespace dex
  • KanidmGroup × 3: homelab-admins, homelab-editors, homelab-users.
  • Dev only (testAccounts: true in values-dev.yaml): KanidmPersonAccount for each test account, and memberships dev-admin → admins, dev-editor → editors, dev-viewer → users. dev-outsider has no group.
  • Admin credentials: the admin/idm_admin passwords live in the Secret that kaniop manages; nothing uses recover-account any more.
  • Scripts and Makefile:
  • scripts/onboard-user <username> <fullname> <mail> <admins|editors|users>: reads the idm_admin password from the kaniop Secret, creates the person, adds them to homelab-<group> and prints a credential reset link.
  • Delete scripts/kanidm-reset-password and scripts/hacks.
  • Remove post-install from the root Makefile.

docs.title: 3. Dex and in-cluster SSO plumbing
docs.text:
• platform/dex/templates/kanidm-client.yaml:
  • a KanidmOAuth2Client named dex with kanidmRef to the Kanidm in namespace kanidm
  • redirect https://<dex domain>/callback
  • scopeMap granting openid profile email groups to the three homelab-* groups
  • kaniop writes dex-kanidm-oauth2-credentials into namespace dex
  • platform/dex:
  • bump the chart 0.16.0 → 0.26.0
  • OIDC connector to https://<auth domain>/oauth2/openid/dex, with pkceChallenge: S256, insecureEnableGroups: true and getUserInfo: true; client ID and secret come from the kaniop Secret
  • drop the gitea static client and GITEA_CLIENT_SECRET; keep grafana-sso for 1c
  • platform/dex/values-dev.yaml:
  • domain dex.127-0-0-1.nip.io
  • static client smoke with redirect https://smoke.127-0-0-1.nip.io/callback and secret from dex.smoke
  • the connector's rootCAs points at ca.crt, mounted from Dex's own dex-tls-certificate Secret. CA-issued certificates carry ca.crt, so no trust-manager is needed.
  • CoreDNS rewrite (dev only, metal/):
  • an Ansible task that runs only for env=dev adds this rule to the kind Corefile and restarts CoreDNS: rewrite name regex (.*)\.127-0-0-1\.nip\.io ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx.svc.cluster.local answer auto
  • Without it, pods resolve *.127-0-0-1.nip.io to their own loopback. Production does not need this.
  • Allowlist: system/argocd/values-dev.yaml adds platform/external-secrets, platform/global-secrets, platform/kanidm and platform/dex.

docs.title: 4. Tests, workflow, docs
docs.text:
• Tooling: add chromium to the flake and github.com/chromedp/chromedp to test/go.mod.
  • Account setup helper:
  • read the idm_admin password
  • create a credential reset token per test account
  • chromedp opens the reset link and sets a random password kept only in memory for the run
  • if Kanidm's account policy requires MFA, it also enrols TOTP and the test computes the codes
  • TestIdentityLogin, for each of dev-admin, dev-editor and dev-viewer:
  • open Dex /auth?client_id=smoke…
  • log in at Kanidm, and consent on first use
  • capture the redirect to smoke…/callback?code=…
  • exchange the code at Dex with the smoke secret
  • decode the id_token and assert email and that groups contains the account's group
  • TestIdentityDenied: dev-outsider logs in at Kanidm and no code comes back.
  • Smoke tests: in dev, TestSmoke also checks the kanidm and dex ingresses. make dev runs the smoke test with filter=Smoke|Identity.
  • RAM: after a build, query Prometheus for container_memory_working_set_bytes summed by namespace and record the table in docs/installation/sandbox.md.
  • Docs:
  • docs/installation/sandbox.md: test accounts, logging in, onboard-user with groups, and the RAM table.
  • New page: manual secret rotation.
  • CLAUDE.md: drop the "kanidm CLI 1.11" checklist line, and add notes on kaniop, the CoreDNS rewrite, the smoke client, and identity config in git vs people by script.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria (on branch dev)
docs.text:
1. make dev succeeds from scratch, including the identity tests, and succeeds again when run a second time.
  2. All 9 allowlisted Applications are Synced and Healthy (1a's five plus external-secrets, global-secrets, kanidm and dex).
  3. No external-secrets.io/v1beta1 remains in the repo. Production and dev renders pass for every changed chart.
  4. dev-admin, dev-editor and dev-viewer log in through Dex with the right groups; dev-outsider is refused.
  5. Prometheus has no down targets.
  6. The RAM table per namespace is in the docs.
  7. scripts/hacks, scripts/kanidm-reset-password and the post-install target are gone, and scripts/onboard-user works against the new Kanidm.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• kaniop is 0.x and has had a breaking CRD migration (v0.11). Pin it exactly and read the upgrade guide on every bump.
  • The Kanidm groups claim format may be the SPN (homelab-admins@<domain>) rather than the short name. The tests record the actual value, and 1c's role mapping uses it.
  • Kanidm account policy may require MFA for persons. The setup helper handles TOTP; if Kanidm insists on passkeys, the test needs a virtual WebAuthn authenticator (chromedp supports it), and this is verified first in the plan.
  • First sync ordering: CRDs (ESO, kaniop) and webhooks arrive after their users, as in 1a. ArgoCD retries are expected to converge, and the build time is measured.
  • Upstream drift: platform/kanidm no longer matches upstream, so upstream changes there will not cherry-pick.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• 1c: Grafana, ArgoCD and zot SSO (OIDC, API keys, role mapping), and their tests
  • Automatic secret rotation (and Reloader)
  • make configure and a real domain (sub-project 3)
  • Gitea, Woodpecker and Renovate in the sandbox

docs.title: Sub-project 2: Gateway API with Cilium Gateway
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-13, written spec awaiting review. Branch: feat/gateway-api (PR into dev).

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Every component is reached through Gateway API Gateways served by Cilium: homelab for the LAN and homelab-public for the apps published through the Cloudflare Tunnel, sharing one wildcard certificate. ingress-nginx (retired, no security fixes since 2026-03) and every Ingress object are removed. The sandbox proves the result, now with five more apps, including gitea and its SSH over TCPRoute.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Builds on sub-project 1 (kind + Cilium sandbox, identity, SSO). Specs: 2026-10-12-kind-cilium-sandbox-design.md, 2026-10-12-sandbox-identity-design.md, 2026-10-13-sandbox-sso-design.md.
  • Cilium is installed by Ansible (metal/roles/cilium, 1.20.2) for both the sandbox and production, with LB IPAM and L2 announcements. Gateway API is not enabled. Cilium 1.20 implements Gateway API v1.6.1, including HTTPRoute, TCPRoute and BackendTLSPolicy.
  • ingress-nginx (system/ingress-nginx, chart 4.15.1) holds the sandbox LB IP 172.30.255.200 (values-dev.yaml) and forwards TCP 22 to gitea SSH.
  • Ingress objects exist in 17 components. Six run in the sandbox (argocd, excalidraw, kanidm, dex, grafana, zot); the rest run only in production.
  • nginx-specific settings: zot proxy-body-size: "0", kanidm backend-protocol: HTTPS (Kanidm serves TLS itself and reuses the ingress certificate secret).
  • Certificates: every Ingress carries cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-prod. Production issues through ACME DNS-01 on Cloudflare; the sandbox issues from the local CA under the same issuer name.
  • Around the ingress:
  • the sandbox socat proxy forwards 127.0.0.1:80/443 to 172.30.255.200
  • the sandbox CoreDNS rewrite (metal/inventories/dev.yml, coredns_rewrite_rule) points *.127-0-0-1.nip.io at ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx; the role only adds the rule when that exact text is missing
  • cloudflared (production) forwards *.khuedoan.com to https://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx with noTLSVerify
  • external-dns (production, chart 1.14.3) uses the default sources (service, ingress)
  • three apps are public today (excalidraw, blog, matrix): their Ingress annotation external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/target: homelab-tunnel.khuedoan.com makes external-dns point their DNS at the tunnel; every other host points at the LAN ingress IP
  • external-dns reads target only from a Gateway, never from a route (gateway sources docs), and since v0.22 uses the annotation prefix external-dns.kubernetes.io/ (the alpha prefix is legacy)
  • Tests: TestSmoke and integration_test.go read hosts from Ingress objects (k8s.GetIngress).
  • Charts and route support (latest versions checked 2026-10-13):
Component Chart now → latest Native Gateway API support argocd argo-cd 10.10.3 (latest) server.httproute dex dex 0.26.0 (latest) httpRoute grafana grafana 13.5.0 → 13.5.1 route zot zot 0.1.128 (latest) httproute kanidm kaniop 0.18.0 → 0.19.0 Kanidm CR gateway, with backendTlsPolicy excalidraw app-template 5.3.0 (latest) route actualbudget, blog, homepage, jellyfin, ollama, pairdrop, paperless, speedtest app-template 2.2–2.6 → 5.3.0 route gitea gitea 10.1.3 → 12.7.0 gatewayAPI.core.httpRoute, tcpRoute, backendTLSPolicy woodpecker woodpecker 1.5.1 → 3.7.5 none matrix elementweb 0.0.6 (latest), dendrite 0.13.5 none
  • Sandbox memory: about 6 GiB used of the 12 GiB WSL VM.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Scope Migrate every component, including the ones that run only in production; delete system/ingress-nginx Topology Two Gateways in namespace gateway: homelab (LAN, DNS → its LB IP) and homelab-public (DNS → Cloudflare Tunnel, cloudflared → its Service); one shared wildcard certificate; apps attach HTTPRoutes to one of them Public apps excalidraw, blog and matrix attach to homelab-public; every other app to homelab. In the sandbox, excalidraw attaches to homelab (no tunnel) external-dns Chart 1.23.0, source gateway-httproute, annotation prefix external-dns.kubernetes.io/ everywhere (including the exclude filter) Delivery Gateway API CRDs and the Cilium gatewayAPI setting in metal/ (Ansible, before Cilium); the Gateway in a new ArgoCD component system/gateway; routes in each app's own values Chart versions Upgrade every touched chart to its latest stable and use its native route support; write templates/httproute.yaml only where a chart has none (woodpecker, matrix) Major upgrades app-template 2/3 → 5, gitea 10 → 12, woodpecker 1 → 3; each listed in the CLAUDE.md production checklist Sandbox apps Add pairdrop, speedtest, actualbudget, homepage and gitea (SQLite, in-memory cache, no Dex login) Kanidm backend TLS HTTPRoute plus BackendTLSPolicy from the kaniop Kanidm CR; Kanidm gets its own Certificate (tlsSecretName: kanidm-tls). Production validates with wellKnownCACertificates: System, the sandbox with the dev CA ConfigMap (Cilium 1.20.2 accepts only one ConfigMap with key ca.crt, no Secret) Dev CA distribution trust-manager v0.25.0, sandbox only (conditional dependency of system/cert-manager), copies homelab-dev-ca into a ConfigMap homelab-dev-ca (key ca.crt) in every namespace. Used by Kanidm's BackendTLSPolicy and by the dev CA mounts of dex, grafana, zot and argocd, which today read ca.crt from their own ingress certificate secrets gitea SSH TCPRoute on the Gateway listener ssh (port 22) Versions Re-check and pin exactly while planning (Gateway API CRDs, Cilium, every chart)

docs.title: 1. Gateway infrastructure
docs.text:
• metal/ (sandbox and production):
  • Install the Gateway API CRDs, standard channel, at the version the chosen Cilium release supports (v1.6.1 for 1.20), before Cilium. Cilium's operator enables its Gateway controller only when the CRDs exist at start; on an existing cluster, restart the operator once after installing the CRDs.
  • metal/roles/cilium adds gatewayAPI.enabled: true.
  • system/gateway (new ArgoCD component, wrapper chart with templates only):
  • Gateway homelab-public, gatewayClassName: cilium, annotation external-dns.kubernetes.io/target: homelab-tunnel.<domain>, one listener https (port 443, hostname *.<domain>, same wildcard secret, routes from all namespaces). No HTTP or SSH listener: Cloudflare and cloudflared only speak HTTPS to it. Its address comes from the LB pool, also in the sandbox.
  • Gateway homelab, gatewayClassName: cilium, listeners:
    • http, port 80, routes from namespace gateway only
    • https, port 443, hostname *.<domain>, TLS terminate with secret homelab-wildcard-tls, routes from all namespaces
    • ssh, port 22, TCP, routes from namespace gitea only
  • HTTPRoute https-redirect on listener http: RequestRedirect to https with status 301 for every host.
  • Certificate homelab-wildcard for *.<domain>, issuer letsencrypt-prod, secret homelab-wildcard-tls. No cert-manager gateway-shim.
  • values.yaml holds the domain (khuedoan.com until make configure in sub-project 3); values-dev.yaml sets 127-0-0-1.nip.io and pins the address 172.30.255.200 (LB IPAM, the address ingress-nginx holds today).
  • Remove system/ingress-nginx in the same change: the Gateway takes over its IP.
  • Sandbox allowlist (system/argocd/values-dev.yaml): drop system/ingress-nginx, add system/gateway.

docs.title: 2. Routes per app
docs.text:
• Common pattern: remove the ingress block, its cert-manager annotation and its tls block; add one HTTPRoute with parentRefs to gateway/homelab, sectionName: https, and one hostname <app>.<domain>. Sandbox hostnames stay in values-dev.yaml (<app>.127-0-0-1.nip.io). Apps no longer declare certificates.
  • Native chart support: argocd (server.httproute; server.insecure: true stays), dex (httpRoute), grafana (route), zot (httproute), gitea (gatewayAPI.core.httpRoute and tcpRoute), the app-template 5 apps (route).
  • kanidm: kaniop 0.19 Kanidm CR gateway with parentRefs, hostname and backendTlsPolicy (validation hostname auth.<domain>; CA: system trust in production, the sandbox CA in the sandbox). A Certificate for auth.<domain> replaces the ingress certificate Kanidm serves today.
  • Dev CA trust (sandbox): dex, grafana, zot and argocd mount the ConfigMap homelab-dev-ca instead of their former ingress certificate secrets; paths and SSL_CERT_DIR stay the same.
  • Own templates: woodpecker and matrix (elementweb, dendrite) add templates/httproute.yaml to their wrapper charts.
  • zot: large blob pushes must not be cut by a gateway timeout; set the route's timeouts so pushes are not limited, and verify with a 200 MB layer.
  • gitea: TCPRoute to the SSH service on listener ssh. Sandbox values-dev.yaml uses SQLite and an in-memory cache, disables postgresql-ha and valkey-cluster, and configures no Dex login. Its config job (upstream repositories migrated from GitHub) gets a configJob.enabled flag, off in the sandbox. The chart's own tcpRoute is still v1alpha2, so the wrapper chart has its own TCPRoute.
  • Public apps (excalidraw, blog, matrix): parentRefs to gateway/homelab-public; the route keeps only external-dns.kubernetes.io/cloudflare-proxied: "true" (the target comes from the Gateway). excalidraw's values-dev.yaml points parentRefs at gateway/homelab and clears the annotation.
  • ArgoCD CLI: document argocd --grpc-web; plain gRPC through the Gateway is not tested.
  • Sandbox additions: apps/pairdrop, apps/speedtest, apps/actualbudget, apps/homepage, platform/gitea join the allowlist.

docs.title: 3. Around the Gateway
docs.text:
Component Change Tested in the sandbox socat proxy none: the Gateway holds 172.30.255.200 yes CoreDNS rewrite target cilium-gateway-homelab.gateway.svc.cluster.local; the role replaces an existing *.127-0-0-1.nip.io rewrite rule instead of only adding when missing yes, through the identity and SSO tests cloudflared service https://cilium-gateway-homelab-public.gateway with matchSNItoHost: true (the wildcard listener needs a matching SNI); only public apps are reachable through the tunnel no external-dns chart 1.23.0, source gateway-httproute, policy: upsert-only set explicitly (the old chart default; now required), --annotation-filter=external-dns.kubernetes.io/exclude notin (true) no cert-manager wildcard and Kanidm certificates only; trust-manager and a Bundle homelab-dev-ca in the sandbox yes

The two untested rows are checked against upstream documentation while planning and listed in the CLAUDE.md production checklist.

docs.title: 4. Tests, rollout, docs
docs.text:
• Changed tests:
  • TestSmoke and integration_test.go read hosts from HTTPRoutes and wait for the parent conditions Accepted and ResolvedRefs. The route name per chart is found while planning and recorded in smokeApps.
  • The sandbox smoke list adds pairdrop, speedtest, actualbudget, homepage and gitea.
  • Identity and SSO tests are unchanged; they now cover the CoreDNS rewrite and Kanidm's BackendTLSPolicy.
  • New sandbox tests (run by make dev):
  • http:// requests get a 301 to https://
  • Gateway/homelab is Programmed with address 172.30.255.200; Gateway/homelab-public is Programmed
  • no Ingress objects and no ingress-nginx namespace remain
  • TCP to 172.30.255.200:22 returns gitea's SSH banner
  • a 200 MB layer pushes to zot through the Gateway
  • Rollout:
  • One PR from feat/gateway-api into dev; removing ingress-nginx and adding the Gateway must land together.
  • Basic checks on the branch: scripts/render-chart (prod and dev) for every changed chart, the offline Go tests, mkdocs build --strict.
  • After the merge: make dev on the running sandbox (upgrade path), then make dev-clean && make dev (fresh install, about 25 minutes).
  • Measure sandbox memory; report to the user before going on if it exceeds about 8 GiB.
  • Docs:
  • docs/installation/sandbox.md: app list, --grpc-web, Gateway instead of ingress-nginx.
  • Other pages under docs/ that mention ingress-nginx or Ingress.
  • CLAUDE.md Sandbox section: Gateway instead of ingress-nginx.
  • CLAUDE.md production checklist: the major chart upgrades; the public path (homelab-public, cloudflared matchSNItoHost, external-dns 1.23 with gateway-httproute and the new annotation prefix) is untested; install the Gateway API CRDs before Cilium.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria (on branch dev)
docs.text:
1. No system/ingress-nginx, no Ingress in any rendered chart (prod and dev).
  2. make dev passes on the upgraded sandbox and on a fresh one: Smoke (11 apps), Identity, SSO and the new Gateway tests.
  3. https://<app>.127-0-0-1.nip.io opens from the Windows browser for every sandbox app.
  4. Every changed chart renders for prod and dev with scripts/render-chart.
  5. CLAUDE.md and docs describe the Gateway setup and the new production caveats.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Major chart upgrades without sandbox coverage: blog, jellyfin, ollama, paperless, matrix, woodpecker only render. Production is installed from scratch in sub-project 3, so no in-place upgrade happens.
  • Envoy defaults differ from nginx: timeouts, body size and header limits; the zot push test covers the largest known case.
  • Cilium Gateway on an existing cluster needs an operator restart after the CRDs are installed; the fresh-install run covers the normal order.
  • gitea 12 in the sandbox differs from production in its database (SQLite).
  • Memory: five more apps; gitea is the largest unknown.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• apps/tailscale and apps/wireguard: no ingress, not touched.
  • Dex login for gitea, woodpecker and renovate tokens (production checklist, sub-project 3).
  • make configure and the real domain (sub-project 3).
  • gRPC routes, ListenerSets, per-app certificates.
  • The localhost socat stall (sub-project 1 finding).

docs.title: Sub-project 1c: SSO for Grafana, ArgoCD and zot
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-13, written spec awaiting review. Branch: dev.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: People log in to Grafana, ArgoCD and zot through Dex → Kanidm, and their Kanidm group decides what they may do. Each app keeps a local break-glass account. The sandbox proves every role with automated browser and API tests.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Builds on 1a (kind sandbox, values-dev.yaml overlays, dev CA) and 1b (ESO generators, Kanidm via kaniop, Dex with PKCE, identity tests in test/).
  • Specs: 2026-10-12-kind-cilium-sandbox-design.md, 2026-10-12-sandbox-identity-design.md.
  • Groups. homelab-admins, homelab-editors and homelab-users exist in Kanidm. Today the groups claim from Dex carries SPNs such as homelab-admins@auth.127-0-0-1.nip.io, plus UUIDs and Kanidm's built-in idm_* groups.
  • Kanidm login. It asks for the TOTP code before the password.
  • Grafana (platform/grafana):
  • not in the sandbox allowlist
  • generic_oauth already points at Dex but maps no roles
  • its chart moved to grafana-community (13.5.0); the old repo stops at 10.5.15
  • ArgoCD: no SSO (dex.enabled: false, no oidc.config).
  • zot: no auth (# TODO enable auth); chart 0.1.52, latest 0.1.128 (zot v2.1.22).
  • Test plumbing. The identity tests dial the ingress LB IP directly because the localhost socat proxy stalls about 1% of connects. Credentials and tokens are kept out of test logs.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Group format Normalised in Kanidm: the Dex client's claimMap emits homelab_groups with short names; the Dex connector maps it to groups. Same values in sandbox and production Grafana roles admins → Admin + Grafana server admin, editors → Editor, users → Viewer; no group → refused (role_attribute_strict) Grafana local admin Kept, password from global-secrets grafana.admin; login form stays next to "Sign in with Dex" ArgoCD roles admins → role:admin; editors → role:editor (get everything, sync, actions, logs, exec; no create/update/delete); users → role:readonly; others → nothing ArgoCD local admin Kept zot auth OIDC for the UI, per-person API keys for docker/crane, htpasswd machine account ci zot permissions admins read/create/update/delete, editors read/create/update, users read, ci read/create/update, anonymous none Dev CA trust in Go apps Mount the app's own ingress certificate ca.crt into /etc/homelab-dev-ca and set SSL_CERT_DIR=/etc/ssl/certs:/etc/homelab-dev-ca (dev only) Versions Grafana chart 13.5.0 from https://grafana-community.github.io/helm-charts, zot chart 0.1.128; re-check and pin exactly while planning

docs.title: 1. Shared groundwork
docs.text:
• Normalised groups:
  • platform/dex/templates/kanidm-client.yaml adds a claimMap named homelab_groups. Each of the three groups maps to its own short name, with joinStrategy: array.
  • The Dex Kanidm connector (both values files) adds claimMapping.groups: homelab_groups and overrideClaimMapping: true.
  • The groups claim every app receives becomes exactly ["homelab-<x>"].
  • TestIdentityLogin asserts equality with that list instead of a prefix match.
  • Generated secrets: platform/global-secrets/values.yaml adds:
  • dex.argocd and dex.zot (client_secret)
  • grafana.admin (password)
  • registry.ci (password)
  • Dex static clients: add argocd (redirect https://<argocd host>/auth/callback) and zot (redirect https://<registry host>/zot/auth/callback/oidc) next to grafana-sso, in both values files (lists are replaced). dex-secrets gains ARGOCD_CLIENT_SECRET and ZOT_CLIENT_SECRET.
  • Dev CA trust: each Go app mounts the ca.crt of its own ingress certificate and sets SSL_CERT_DIR in its values-dev.yaml only.
  • Allowlist: system/argocd/values-dev.yaml adds platform/grafana and platform/zot.
  • Test helper. browserAuthorize generalises to an app login helper:
  • open the app's login page and click its SSO button
  • follow Dex → Kanidm (TOTP, then password)
  • return to the app and hand back the browser's cookies for API calls

It reuses the stored credentials, totpClock, the direct-to-LB dialling and the quiet logging from 1b.

docs.title: 2. Grafana (platform/grafana)
docs.text:
• Chart: dependency grafana 13.5.0 from the grafana-community repo.
  • grafana.ini → auth.generic_oauth:
  • keep the Dex client grafana-sso with scopes: openid profile email groups
  • role_attribute_path: contains(groups[*], 'homelab-admins') && 'Admin' || contains(groups[*], 'homelab-editors') && 'Editor' || contains(groups[*], 'homelab-users') && 'Viewer'
  • role_attribute_strict: true
  • allow_assign_grafana_admin: true (admins also get Grafana server admin)
  • Local admin:
  • admin.existingSecret points at a Secret built by ExternalSecret from grafana.admin
  • the login form stays enabled
  • Data: datasources and dashboards are unchanged; sidecars read namespace monitoring-system.
  • values-dev.yaml:
  • host grafana.127-0-0-1.nip.io, with root_url, auth_url, token_url and api_url on the sandbox domains
  • dev CA mount and SSL_CERT_DIR

docs.title: 3. ArgoCD (system/argocd)
docs.text:
• configs.cm:
  • oidc.config with issuer Dex, clientID: argocd, clientSecret: $argocd-oidc:clientSecret and requestedScopes: [openid, profile, email, groups]
  • exec.enabled: "true", needed for the editor role. This also takes effect in production (admins can exec too).
  • Secret argocd-oidc: an ExternalSecret in namespace argocd from dex.argocd, with label app.kubernetes.io/part-of: argocd so ArgoCD reads it.
  • configs.rbac:
  • policy.default: ''
  • scopes: '[groups]'
  • policy.csv:
p, role:editor, applications, get, */*, allow
p, role:editor, applications, sync, */*, allow
p, role:editor, applications, action/*, */*, allow
p, role:editor, logs, get, */*, allow
p, role:editor, exec, create, */*, allow
p, role:editor, projects, get, *, allow
p, role:editor, clusters, get, *, allow
p, role:editor, repositories, get, *, allow
g, homelab-admins, role:admin
g, homelab-editors, role:editor
g, homelab-users, role:readonly
  • values-dev.yaml:
  • restate oidc.config with the sandbox Dex issuer (it is one string)
  • dev CA mount and SSL_CERT_DIR on argocd-server
  • Unchanged: the local admin account, and dex.enabled: false (the platform Dex is used).

docs.title: 4. zot (platform/zot)
docs.text:
• Chart: 0.1.128 (zot v2.1.22), with the search and ui extensions enabled.
  • http config:
  • externalUrl set to the registry host
  • auth.openid.providers.oidc:
    • issuer Dex, client zot
    • scopes openid profile email groups
    • claimMapping.username: preferred_username; groups come from groups
    • the client credentials file is mounted from an ExternalSecret built from dex.zot
  • auth.apikey: true
  • auth.htpasswd: user ci; the file is rendered by an ExternalSecret template using htpasswd (bcrypt) from registry.ci
  • registry-admin-secret stays as it is
  • accessControl:
  • repositories ** with the group and user policies in the table above
  • defaultPolicy: [] and no anonymous policy
  • values-dev.yaml: host registry.127-0-0-1.nip.io, sandbox Dex issuer, dev CA mount and SSL_CERT_DIR.

docs.title: 5. Tests, workflow, docs
docs.text:
• make dev runs the smoke test with filter Smoke|Identity|SSO. Each TestSSO* calls waitForIdentityStack and waits for its app's ingress before logging in.
  • TestSSOGrafana:
  • for dev-admin, dev-editor and dev-viewer, log in through "Sign in with Dex"
  • /api/user must return orgRole Admin, Editor and Viewer respectively, and isGrafanaAdmin must be true only for dev-admin
  • the local admin password logs in through /api/user basic auth
  • TestSSOArgoCD:
  • log in via Dex and use the argocd.token cookie with /api/v1/account/can-i
  • admin: sync, delete and exec are yes
  • editor: sync and exec yes, delete no
  • viewer: all three no
  • the local admin still gets a session from /api/v1/session
  • TestSSOZot:
  • log in to the UI via OIDC and create an API key through /zot/auth/apikey
  • with basic auth <user>:<key>, POST /v2/sso-test/blobs/uploads/ returns 202 for admin and editor and 403 for viewer; GET /v2/_catalog returns 200 for all
  • ci with its htpasswd password gets 202
  • a request without credentials gets 401
  • Smoke tests: in dev, TestSmoke adds the grafana and zot ingresses.
  • Docs:
  • docs/installation/sandbox.md: Grafana and zot links, the group → permission table per app, how to create a zot API key and docker login, and an updated RAM table
  • docs/getting-started/user-onboarding.md: what each group gets in each app
  • CLAUDE.md:
    • the homelab_groups convention and the SSL_CERT_DIR dev-CA pattern
    • roadmap: 1c done
    • production checklist: ArgoCD exec.enabled is on, and the Grafana chart moved repos

docs.title: Acceptance criteria (on branch dev)
docs.text:
1. make dev succeeds from scratch, including the smoke, identity and all SSO tests, and succeeds again when run a second time.
  2. All 11 allowlisted Applications are Synced and Healthy.
  3. The groups claim is exactly ["homelab-<x>"] for each test account.
  4. Grafana roles match the groups, and the local admin logs in.
  5. ArgoCD permissions match the table in section 5, and the local admin logs in.
  6. zot: admin and editor push, viewer pulls only, ci pushes, and anonymous requests get 401.
  7. Production and dev renders pass for every changed chart, and Prometheus has no down targets.
  8. The sandbox RAM table includes Grafana and zot.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• zot identity and chart layout. The username zot uses after claim mapping (needed for API-key basic auth), and how the 0.1.128 chart mounts config.json, htpasswd and the credentials file, are verified first while planning.
  • Grafana 13 and chart 13.5.0 may rename grafana.ini keys or chart values. Render prod and dev, and fix any differences in values.yaml.
  • Kanidm claimMap join strategy. The claim must arrive as a JSON array for Dex's claimMapping; the identity test asserts the exact list.
  • Exec in production becomes possible for admins and editors; noted in the production checklist.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• SSO for Gitea, Woodpecker, Renovate and the apps in apps/
  • A CI pipeline using ci
  • Automatic secret rotation
  • The socat proxy stall from 1a

docs.title: Step 4: compact apps/*.yaml layout
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-14, written spec awaiting review. Branch: feat/apps-layout (PR into dev).

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Every app-template app becomes one values file apps/<name>.yaml, deployed by an ApplicationSet that pins app-template once and injects the environment (domain, public Gateway). The rendered resources stay the same, so nothing else in the cluster notices the move. This follows upstream's nixos rewrite (PR #197).

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Roadmap step 4 in CLAUDE.md. Steps 0–3 are done (sandbox, Gateway API, latest images).
  • apps/ has 12 apps, each a wrapper chart (Chart.yaml, values.yaml):
  • 11 use app-template 5.3.0 only. Five have a values-dev.yaml for sandbox hosts (excalidraw also switches to the LAN Gateway, homepage sets HOMEPAGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS).
  • paperless has templates/secret.yaml (ExternalSecret); tailscale has templates/ with an ExternalSecret, Role, RoleBinding and ServiceAccount.
  • matrix uses the elementweb and dendrite charts with its own templates/httproute.yaml.
  • ArgoCD: the ApplicationSet root (chart argocd-apps in system/argocd) generates one Application per directory under system/*, platform/*, apps/*; the sandbox restates it with an allowlist in system/argocd/values-dev.yaml. values-seed.yaml is the first-install variant.
  • Upstream nixos: ApplicationSet apps with a git files generator over apps/*.yaml, multi-source (app-template chart + $values ref), Helm parameter global.domain; app files template hosts as '<host>.{{ .Values.global.domain }}'. Upstream removed matrix ("will add more later").
  • app-template 5.3.0 renders Helm templates in route hostnames, parentRefs, annotations and env values (checked with a render), and in configMaps data when renderFileContent: true. It has native externalSecrets, roles, roleBindings, serviceAccount and rawResources.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Layout apps/<name>.yaml = app-template values (no wrapper chart, no app-template: level) matrix Stays a directory, apps/matrix/, synced by root; it may be removed or rewritten later Environment differences Only Helm parameters from the ApplicationSet: global.domain and global.publicGateway; no per-app dev files. Add an overlay mechanism only when an app needs one app-template version Pinned once in the ApplicationSet apps Extra resources app-template's native externalSecrets, serviceAccount, roles, roleBindings (else rawResources), keeping object names opencloud Not in this step: it moves to step 5 (Kanidm OIDC directly, in the sandbox)

docs.title: 1. ApplicationSet apps
docs.text:
• In system/argocd/values.yaml (and values-seed.yaml), under argocd-apps.applicationsets:
  • generator: git files apps/*.yaml from the same repository and revision as root
  • Application name, Helm release and namespace: the file name without .yaml
  • sources: chart app-template 5.3.0 from https://bjw-s-labs.github.io/helm-charts with valueFiles: [$values/apps/<name>.yaml] and parameters global.domain (khuedoan.com) and global.publicGateway (homelab-public); the git repository as ref: values
  • syncPolicy like root: automated prune and self-heal, retries, CreateNamespace=true, ApplyOutOfSyncOnly=true
  • root keeps scanning apps/* directories, which now only matches apps/matrix/.
  • Sandbox (system/argocd/values-dev.yaml): restate apps in full (Helm replaces lists) with:
  • the GitHub repository and branch dev, like root
  • a files generator limited to apps/{actualbudget,excalidraw,homepage,pairdrop,speedtest}.yaml
  • parameters global.domain: 127-0-0-1.nip.io, global.publicGateway: homelab
  • the five apps/... entries removed from root's allowlist

docs.title: 2. App files
docs.text:
• apps/<name>/values.yaml → apps/<name>.yaml without the app-template: level; delete the directory (Chart.yaml, values-dev.yaml, templates/).
  • Hosts and other domain strings use {{ .Values.global.domain }}: route hostnames, env values (e.g. HOMEPAGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS, PAPERLESS_URL), homepage's services.yaml links (with renderFileContent: true).
  • Public apps (excalidraw, blog): parentRefs[].name: '{{ .Values.global.publicGateway }}'.
  • paperless and tailscale: extra objects through app-template's native keys, same names as today.
  • Kept from earlier steps: suffix: data PVC names, forceRename: ollama, homepage identifier: config, the Seerr note.
  • Template references to .Release.Name/.Release.Namespace in the old templates/ become the literal app name (release name = namespace = file name).

docs.title: 3. Rendering and tests
docs.text:
• scripts/render-chart also accepts a file apps/<name>.yaml: it renders app-template 5.3.0 with that file and the global.* parameters read from system/argocd/values.yaml or values-dev.yaml (the same source ArgoCD uses).
  • Equivalence check: for every converted app and both environments, the new render matches the render of the old wrapper chart, except chart labels (helm.sh/chart and similar). Any other difference is a bug.
  • Go tests: smokeApps is unchanged (route names stay).

docs.title: 4. Docs and rollout
docs.text:
• Docs: docs/installation/sandbox.md (how to add an app to the sandbox, how to render), the how-to pages that show app values, CLAUDE.md Sandbox section (layout, global.* parameters, the matrix exception).
  • Running sandbox: on merge, root drops the five apps and deletes their resources; apps creates them again (it may report "already exists" until root finishes; ArgoCD retries). Sandbox data of those apps is lost, which is acceptable. Then make dev, then one fresh install.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria (on branch dev)
docs.text:
1. apps/ contains only *.yaml files plus apps/matrix/.
  2. For every app and environment, the new render equals the old one except chart labels.
  3. make dev passes on the upgraded sandbox and on a fresh one (50 tests).
  4. The app-template version appears in exactly one place.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Templating coverage: a field app-template does not template would keep a literal {{ .Values.global.domain }}. The equivalence check catches it.
  • ApplicationSet handover on the running sandbox: both ApplicationSets briefly claim the same Application names. Fresh installs are unaffected.
  • Production-only apps (blog, jellyfin, ollama, paperless, tailscale, wireguard) are only checked by render equivalence.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• opencloud (step 5), Dex removal and Forgejo (step 5).
  • Moving the ApplicationSet into OpenTofu (step 7).
  • Rewriting or removing matrix.

docs.title: Step 5b: Forgejo replaces Gitea
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-14, written spec awaiting review. Branch: feat/forgejo (PR into dev).

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Forgejo replaces Gitea and is the source of truth for the GitOps repo: the first install seeds it from GitHub, then production Argo CD syncs from Forgejo. People log in with Kanidm through a per-app client (the step 5a pattern); homelab-admins are Forgejo site admins. Production stores Forgejo's data in a PostgreSQL cluster run by CloudNativePG; the sandbox uses SQLite and proves login, admin mapping, SSH and the seed.

Nothing called Gitea is kept: every name this repo controls becomes forgejo. The deployment starts from scratch; there is no data migration.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• platform/gitea: Gitea chart 12.7.0 with Bitnami postgresql-ha and valkey-cluster in production (one Gitea pod), SQLite in the sandbox; a TCPRoute for SSH; a config job (unfinished Go program that runs go get at every start) that migrates upstream's repositories. The config job is disabled in the sandbox, so the sandbox Gitea is empty and the seed-then-switch path has only ever been rendered.
  • Production Argo CD syncs http://gitea-http.gitea:3000/ops/homelab; values-seed.yaml syncs GitHub on the first install; system/bootstrap.yml picks between them by looking for a running Gitea pod.
  • Forgejo chart 17.3.0 (oci://code.forgejo.org/forgejo-helm/forgejo) defaults to Forgejo 15.0.10 (LTS); the latest stable Forgejo is 16.0.6. The chart bundles no database or cache.
  • The chart and image keep Gitea's names for their own interface; they cannot change without forking the chart or the image (Helm's dependency alias only renames the outer key forgejo:):
  • chart: the values key gitea: (forgejo.gitea.config, forgejo.gitea.oauth, forgejo.gitea.admin in the wrapper), the init container configure-gitea, the template names gitea.*, the env variables GITEA_* the init scripts use, /data/gitea/conf/app.ini (app.ini settings from env variables use FORGEJO__<section>__<key>)
  • image: /var/lib/gitea, /etc/gitea
  • The chart's gitea.oauth[] entries become flags of forgejo admin auth add-oauth/update-oauth, run by configure-gitea at every pod start; existingSecret must have the keys key and secret, and deployment.env reaches the init container too.
  • Forgejo 16.0.6 sends PKCE (S256) to openidConnect login sources (routers/web/auth/oauth.go, generateCodeChallenge). If discovery fails when the provider is registered, the next login hits "no provider", calls ResetOAuth2 and registers it again.
  • Upstream nixos runs Forgejo with SQLite, a confidential Kanidm client, no SSH, and seeds repositories with its toolbox (which reads secrets from OpenBao, not available until step 8).
  • Bitnami no longer publishes free images, so postgresql-ha is not an option.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Packaging Wrapper chart platform/forgejo (like platform/zot), namespace forgejo, fullnameOverride: forgejo Versions Forgejo chart 17.3.0, image code.forgejo.org/forgejo/forgejo:16.0.6 (overrides the chart's LTS default); CloudNativePG chart 0.29.1 (operator 1.30.1); PostgreSQL ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:18.6-standard-trixie Database Production: CloudNativePG Cluster forgejo-db, 3 instances, in namespace forgejo. Sandbox: SQLite High availability Database only: Forgejo stays one pod (Recreate), cache and session in memory Login Kanidm, confidential client forgejo with PKCE; the three role groups may log in; homelab-admins become site admins Local admin forgejo_admin from global-secrets forgejo.admin, kept as break-glass access SSH Kept: Service forgejo-ssh, TCPRoute on the ssh listener of gateway/homelab Source of truth Forgejo from step 5b: a seed Job copies the GitHub repo once into ops/homelab; production Argo CD syncs from Forgejo Naming Every name in this repo becomes forgejo; only chart-imposed names and history (past specs and plans, changelog, decision records) keep gitea Left for step 9 Push mirror to GitHub, Woodpecker and Renovate actually running, Forgejo credentials in OpenBao Left for step 10 Backups of the CloudNativePG cluster and the Forgejo volume

docs.title: platform/cloudnative-pg (production only)
docs.text:
• Wrapper chart depending on cloudnative-pg 0.29.1 from https://cloudnative-pg.github.io/charts, namespace cloudnative-pg (the root ApplicationSet names namespaces after the directory), CRDs installed by the chart (Argo CD already applies server side, so their size is fine), monitoring with the Prometheus Operator (PodMonitor).
  • Not in the sandbox allowlist: the sandbox runs no PostgreSQL. Production picks it up through the platform/* generator.

docs.title: platform/forgejo
docs.text:
Chart.yaml depends on forgejo 17.3.0. Templates:

  • admin-secret.yaml: ExternalSecret forgejo-admin (username: forgejo_admin, password from forgejo.admin); the chart uses it with passwordMode: keepUpdated.
  • kanidm-client.yaml: KanidmOAuth2Client forgejo:
  • origin: https://git.<domain>, redirectUrl: https://git.<domain>/user/oauth2/Kanidm/callback, strictRedirectUrl, preferShortUsername, disableConsentPrompt (confidential client)
  • scopeMap for homelab-admins, homelab-editors, homelab-users with openid profile email groups
  • claimMap homelab_groups with short names, as zot
  • tcproute.yaml: TCPRoute forgejo-ssh (gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1, like the Gitea one) to Service forgejo-ssh port 22, parent gateway/homelab section ssh.
