docs.title: Per component
docs.text:
Component Change istio-system Templates use global.baseDomain (Gateway listeners, Certificate, public target, CoreDNS rewrite); domain keys removed from values argocd argo-cd.global.domain: 'argocd.{{ .Values.global.baseDomain }}' (templated by the chart); oidc.config and the other argocd-cm keys rendered by a wrapper template with the chart's configs.cm.create: false; the chart's HTTPRoute disabled and a wrapper HTTPRoute instead; the apps ApplicationSet's global.domain parameter replaced by valuesObject baseDomain grafana grafana.ini and route use {{ .Values.global.baseDomain }}; host: grafana label for the Kanidm client forgejo route via tpl; the [server] section and the OAuth discovery URL from a wrapper Secret given to the chart's gitea.additionalConfigSources (or its documented equivalent found while implementing); seed Job reads global.seedRepository zot its config.json rendered by a wrapper ConfigMap mounted in place of the chart's (chart's mountConfig off) kanidm the Kanidm resource's domain from global.baseDomain kured timeZone from global.timezone (through tpl if the chart supports it, else a wrapper override found while implementing) cloudflared, woodpecker, renovate, matrix (production only) same rules; only rendered apps global.domain → global.baseDomain; blog's image registry and homepage's links use it; upstream's personal links (the docs site homelab.khuedoan.com) become the repository link

Every values-dev.yaml loses its domain overrides; a file left empty is deleted.

docs.title: Guard
docs.text:
scripts/check-network-config becomes scripts/check-env-config (one script for the environment's settings) and also fails when:

  • a chart or app file (system/, platform/, apps/) contains khuedoan.com or 127-0-0-1.nip.io (comments excepted);
  • a production render contains the sandbox's domain or a sandbox render the production one;
  • a key we pass under global (addresses, baseDomain, timezone, seedRepository) is also a key of a subchart's default global values.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
• A missing key in config.json: scripts/env-values fails (6d-1), and the ApplicationSet's missingkey=error generates nothing.
  • A subchart that later stops templating a value: the guard's render check sees the literal {{ or the wrong domain.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Offline: scripts/check-env-config RED before (the literals) and GREEN after; renders of every changed component in production and the sandbox; the existing checks.
  • make dev-clean; make dev: every test passes (they use the sandbox host names, so a wrong domain anywhere in Argo CD, Grafana, Forgejo, zot or Kanidm fails them).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text:
• CLAUDE.md: roadmap 7b done; rules: domain, time zone and seed repository live only in infra/<env>/cluster/config.json (global.baseDomain, global.timezone, global.seedRepository); the production checklist drops "Run make configure" for "set infra/production/cluster/config.json".
  • docs/installation/production/configuration.md: edit config.json instead of running make configure.
  • scripts/configure removed; the Terraform Cloud workspace of external/ stays until 7c (noted).

docs.title: Step 7a: infra/ with OpenTofu and Terragrunt, bootstrap
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-16, written spec awaiting review. Branch: feat/infra (PR into dev).

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: The sandbox is built, bootstrapped and removed by Terragrunt units under infra/, in upstream nixos's layout, and production's Argo CD bootstrap moves there too. make dev and make dev-clean keep working and run every sandbox test. Step 7 continues with 7b (environment settings such as the domain in infra/<env>/) and 7c (a cloudflare unit replacing external/).

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Today: metal/Makefile creates the k3d sandbox (Gateway API CRDs, k3d cluster create, kubeconfig, a socat proxy recreated on every run because the node address can change) and production nodes with Ansible (boot.yml, cluster.yml, kubeconfig written to metal/kubeconfig.yaml). system/bootstrap.yml (Ansible, system/Makefile) renders the system/argocd chart (values-dev.yaml in the sandbox; in production values-seed.yaml while Forgejo is not running, else values.yaml) and applies it server-side with field manager argocd-controller. Argo CD then manages itself (system/argocd is in the root ApplicationSet).
  • external/ (Terraform, state on upstream's Terraform Cloud workspace) stays until 7c.
  • Upstream nixos: infra/root.hcl, infra/_modules/<module>, infra/<env>/<unit>/terragrunt.hcl, kubeconfig at infra/<env>/kubeconfig.yaml; its argocd module uses helm_release and Argo CD does not manage itself.
  • Decided 2026-10-16: keep the ApplicationSet + wrapper chart model (OpenTofu bootstraps, Argo CD pulls everything in the cluster from git); state stays local until step 8 (R2, encryption); production nodes stay on Ansible until step 11.
  • Tools: the dev shell has OpenTofu 1.11.14 (latest 1.13.1, in nixpkgs-unstable) and no Terragrunt (latest 1.1.6; nixpkgs-unstable has a 1.1.x).

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Layout infra/root.hcl, infra/_modules/{k3d,argocd}, infra/sandbox/{cluster,argocd}, infra/production/argocd State Local, .state/<env>/<unit>/terraform.tfstate (git-ignored) Kubeconfig infra/<env>/kubeconfig.yaml (git-ignored), replacing metal/kubeconfig.yaml Sandbox cluster Module k3d: terraform_data + local-exec (no stable k3d provider) Production cluster Unchanged: make -C metal (Ansible) until step 11, writing infra/production/kubeconfig.yaml Argo CD bootstrap Module argocd: render the chart and apply it server-side once (re-applied only when the chart or values change); no helm_release Production safety prevent_destroy on production's bootstrap Tools OpenTofu and Terragrunt latest from nixpkgs-unstable in the dev shell

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
infra/
  root.hcl                     # local state, env/unit locals, kubeconfig path
  Makefile                     # check: terragrunt hcl validate, tofu fmt -check
  _modules/
    k3d/                       # sandbox cluster, Gateway API CRDs, proxy; k3d config (from metal/k3d-dev.yaml)
    argocd/                    # bootstrap Argo CD from system/argocd
  sandbox/
    cluster/config.json        # (6d-1)
    cluster/terragrunt.hcl     # module k3d
    argocd/terragrunt.hcl      # module argocd, depends on ../cluster, values-dev.yaml
  production/
    cluster/config.json        # (6d-1)
    argocd/terragrunt.hcl      # module argocd, seed/values selection, prevent_destroy

cluster/ keeps its config.json (read by Argo CD's ApplicationSets and later by OpenTofu); in the sandbox it also holds the unit that creates the cluster.

docs.title: Module k3d
docs.text:
Inputs: cluster name, k3d config path, Gateway API version, kubeconfig path, proxy bind address. Resources:

  • terraform_data.cluster: create runs what metal/Makefile's k3d target runs (download the Gateway API manifest, k3d cluster create --config, mount it into k3s's auto-deploy manifests, write the kubeconfig); destroy deletes the cluster and the kubeconfig. Replaced when the k3d config or the Gateway API version changes.
  • data.external.node: the node's address (docker inspect).
  • terraform_data.proxy: the socat proxy for 127.0.0.1:80/443/22, replaced when the node address changes (so an unchanged sandbox applies with no changes); it keeps the existing port guard and its error message. Destroy removes it.

docs.title: Module argocd
docs.text:
Inputs: kubeconfig, values files (relative to system/argocd), and for production a seed rule. One terraform_data whose create runs a script that:

  1. creates namespace argocd;
  2. in production, chooses values-seed.yaml when no Forgejo pod is running (as system/bootstrap.yml does), else values.yaml;
  3. renders system/argocd (helm dependency build, helm template --include-crds) and applies it with kubectl apply --server-side --field-manager argocd-controller --force-conflicts.

triggers_replace hashes the chart directory's files and the chosen values files, plus the sandbox cluster's id (a recreated cluster is bootstrapped again), so later applies do nothing unless they change; production ignores trigger changes and bootstraps once (a re-run would be a replacement, which prevent_destroy refuses); Argo CD's own sync applies every later change from git. Destroy does nothing in the sandbox (the cluster is deleted) and is refused in production (prevent_destroy).

docs.title: Make
docs.text:
• Root Makefile: KUBECONFIG = infra/$(env)/kubeconfig.yaml (env sandbox for make dev, production otherwise); dev = sandbox-push → terragrunt run --all apply in infra/sandbox (non-interactive) → sandbox-refresh → smoke-test; dev-clean = terragrunt run --all destroy in infra/sandbox; the default target = make -C metal → terragrunt run --all apply in infra/production → external → tests.
  • metal/Makefile loses its dev, k3d, proxy and clean targets; metal/k3d-dev.yaml moves into the module; the k3s role writes infra/production/kubeconfig.yaml.
  • system/bootstrap.yml and system/Makefile are removed.

docs.title: Dev shell
docs.text: flake.nix: unstable.opentofu and unstable.terragrunt (pinned by flake.lock; update nixpkgs-unstable if its Terragrunt is older than the latest release and a newer one is available there).

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
• Ports 80/443/22 taken, or the k3d node missing: the proxy step fails with today's messages.
  • A failed bootstrap leaves the unit's resource tainted; the next apply retries it.
  • Docker's 172.28.0.0/16 taken: k3d cluster create fails (CLAUDE.md already says how to find the culprit).

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Offline (make -C infra check, added to the basic checks): terragrunt hcl validate, tofu fmt -check -recursive, and tofu validate of each module.
  • make dev-clean; make dev: a fresh sandbox built entirely by Terragrunt passes every test (98).
  • A second make dev on the running sandbox: terragrunt run --all plan reports no changes before the apply.
  • make dev-clean leaves no k3d cluster, proxy container, kubeconfig or Docker network k3d-homelab-dev.
  • Production: terragrunt run --all plan in infra/production against a throwaway kubeconfig pointing at the sandbox shows the bootstrap it would apply (no production cluster exists).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text:
• docs/installation/sandbox.md, docs/installation/post-installation.md: kubeconfig path, make dev/dev-clean via Terragrunt.
  • CLAUDE.md: roadmap 7 split into 7a (done), 7b, 7c; the sandbox section names infra/sandbox instead of metal/Makefile/metal/k3d-dev.yaml; basic checks gain make -C infra check; the production checklist notes that production's bootstrap through Terragrunt was only planned.

docs.title: Step 8b: OpenTofu's secrets reach OpenBao through External Secrets; ntfy runs in the cluster; external/ removed
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-17, written spec awaiting review. Branch: feat/infra-secrets (PR into dev).

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Every secret the cluster needs comes from OpenBao. The ones OpenTofu creates (Cloudflare's tokens and Tunnel credentials, WireGuard's private key) reach OpenBao the way generated secrets do: as Kubernetes Secrets that a PushSecret writes into OpenBao, through a writer that can never touch generated/. Alerts go to a self-hosted ntfy (like upstream nixos), published through the Cloudflare Tunnel. external/ (Terraform Cloud state, ntfy, extra secrets) and the k8up-era scripts/backup are removed.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• After 8a: generated secrets go Password generator → Secret in global-secrets → PushSecret (store openbao-writer, role writer, secret/<namespace>/generated/* only) → OpenBao. OpenTofu writes only OpenBao's unseal key, as Secret openbao/openbao-unseal (unit infra/<env>/openbao, server-side apply, value on stdin).
  • infra/production/cloudflare (7c) outputs secrets (sensitive): cert-manager/cloudflare (api_token), external-dns/cloudflare (api_token, zone_id), cloudflared/cloudflare (credentials.json). The token that created them (~/.config/homelab/cloudflare.env) never leaves the workstation and is not in state (checked). The charts expect Secrets cloudflare-api-token (cert-manager key api-token, external-dns key value) and cloudflared-credentials (credentials.json); nothing creates them yet.
  • apps/wireguard.yaml and apps/tailscale.yaml (production only) read wireguard/private-key (private-key) and tailscale/auth-key (auth-key), which nothing writes yet.
  • external/ (upstream's Terraform Cloud workspace) keeps ntfy (Secret monitoring-system/webhook-transformer: ntfy.sh URL and a secret topic, read by Alertmanager's relay container) and extra-secrets (Secret global-secrets/external, read by nothing since 8a; scripts/backup still points at it and is broken).
  • Upstream nixos has no external/: ntfy (binwiederhier/ntfy) runs in the cluster with deny-all, users and tokens declared in its environment from OpenBao, NTFY_UPSTREAM_BASE_URL=https://ntfy.sh (iOS push), a route on the LAN Gateway only; Alertmanager posts to it with ?template=alertmanager and a token file, and its Watchdog receiver posts a message delayed 15 minutes with sequence_id: watchdog, so a stopped heartbeat lets the last one fire (a dead man's switch inside ntfy). Upstream has no VPN apps; the home network here sits behind CGNAT, so a LAN-only ntfy would be unreachable outside home until step 12.
  • Decided 2026-10-17: OpenTofu generates what it can (WireGuard key); Tailscale's auth key waits for step 12, where Headscale issues pre-auth keys itself (no third-party credential; apps/tailscale.yaml runs only in production, not deployed yet), so no secrets file is added; OpenTofu's values go through Kubernetes Secrets and PushSecret (not kubectl exec into OpenBao: ESO re-pushes within an hour if OpenBao loses its data, which has no backup until step 10, and it is the same pattern as global-secrets); ntfy self-hosted and published through the Tunnel, with iOS push through ntfy.sh (iPhone and Android), in this step.
  • Versions (2026-10-17): ntfy v2.31.1, OJFord/wireguard 0.4.1+2, hashicorp/random 3.9.1.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Delivery OpenTofu unit infra/<env>/secrets writes Secrets into namespace infra-secrets; platform/infra-secrets pushes each to OpenBao Writer SecretStore openbao-infra (service account openbao-infra, role infra, audience openbao) in infra-secrets Policy infra create, read, update on secret/data/* and secret/metadata/*; deny on secret/data/+/generated/* and secret/metadata/+/generated/* Push policy updatePolicy: Replace (OpenTofu is the source: a rotated Cloudflare token reaches OpenBao), deletionPolicy: None, hourly Cloudflare Production: the cloudflare unit's output secrets, as a Terragrunt dependency WireGuard wireguard_asymmetric_key in the unit; output wireguard_public_key (for peers); a prevent_destroy guard in production, as infra/<env>/openbao Tailscale Not in this step: tailscale/auth-key comes from Headscale in step 12 (upstream master pasted a 90-day auth key into external/terraform.tfvars) Secret names One Secret per OpenBao path, <namespace>.<name> (cert-manager.cloudflare, …), keys = properties ntfy apps/ntfy.yaml (namespace ntfy), one route on global.publicGateway (as excalidraw: a LAN route on the same host would compete for the DNS record), deny-all, signup and attachments off, NTFY_UPSTREAM_BASE_URL=https://ntfy.sh in production only ntfy users alerts (write-only on topic alerts, Alertmanager) and phone (read-only, people's apps); passwords and tokens from platform/global-secrets Alertmanager Posts to http://ntfy.ntfy/alerts?template=alertmanager with the alerts token; Watchdog as upstream (delayed message, sequence_id); relay container webhook-transformer removed; enabled in the sandbox too Removed external/, scripts/backup, the root Makefile's external, backup, restore targets, system/monitoring-system/files/webhook-transformer, egress 443 for monitoring-system

docs.title: OpenTofu unit secrets
docs.text:
infra/_modules/secrets takes kubeconfig, secrets (map path → map property → value, sensitive, default {}), and protect. It adds wireguard/private-key (private-key, from wireguard_asymmetric_key). It waits for namespace infra-secrets (as infra/_modules/openbao's wait-namespace.sh: its own step, so the timeout message shows) and applies every Secret server-side, the values on stdin (one JSON document, never an argument or a file), on every run. Secrets it no longer renders are left alone (removal is by hand: deleting an OpenBao value is an admin decision).

infra/production/secrets: depends on ../openbao and ../cloudflare (output secrets), protect = true. infra/sandbox/secrets: depends on ../openbao, no Cloudflare. Units run in both make infra env=production and make dev.

docs.title: platform/infra-secrets
docs.text:
A chart in namespace infra-secrets: service account openbao-infra, SecretStore openbao-infra, and a PushSecret per entry of secrets in its values (<namespace>/<name> with its properties):

Entry Properties Environments cert-manager/cloudflare api_token production external-dns/cloudflare api_token, zone_id production cloudflared/cloudflare credentials.json production wireguard/private-key private-key production, sandbox

values-dev.yaml lists only the sandbox's entries, so no PushSecret waits for a Secret its environment never writes. The namespace needs no mesh allow beyond the baseline (nothing calls it; External Secrets' controller makes the calls).

docs.title: OpenBao
docs.text: platform/openbao/values.yaml gains policy infra and role infra (openbao-infra in infra-secrets, audience openbao, 10m). Production has not initialised yet, so its first start loads them; the sandbox is rebuilt.

docs.title: Consumers
docs.text:
• system/cert-manager: ExternalSecret cloudflare-api-token (api-token ← cert-manager/cloudflare#api_token), production only (the sandbox issues from its CA).
  • system/external-dns: ExternalSecret cloudflare-api-token (value ← external-dns/cloudflare#api_token).
  • system/cloudflared: ExternalSecret cloudflared-credentials (credentials.json).
  • system/monitoring-system: ExternalSecret ntfy (token ← monitoring-system/generated/ntfy#token), mounted through alertmanagerSpec.secrets.

docs.title: ntfy
docs.text:
apps/ntfy.yaml (app-template): image docker.io/binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.31.1, serve, NTFY_BASE_URL https://ntfy.<baseDomain>, NTFY_BEHIND_PROXY, cache and auth files on a 1Gi PVC, NTFY_AUTH_DEFAULT_ACCESS=deny-all, NTFY_ENABLE_SIGNUP=false, no attachment cache dir (attachments off), NTFY_AUTH_ACCESS alerts:alerts:wo and phone:alerts:ro, NTFY_AUTH_USERS and NTFY_AUTH_TOKENS from an ExternalSecret (the bcrypt hashes come from ESO's htpasswd template function, as zot's). global-secrets entries generate each user's password and token (ntfy tokens are tk_ plus 29 characters) and push them to ntfy/generated/…; the alerts token also to monitoring-system/generated/ntfy. Route: global.publicGateway only (public in production: the Tunnel; external-dns publishes the record; at home too, phones go through Cloudflare). allow: that Gateway on its port, Alertmanager's service account. Egress: ntfy 443 (ntfy.sh, production). NTFY_UPSTREAM_BASE_URL stays empty in the sandbox, so it sends nothing out.

People subscribe in the ntfy app (Android, iOS) to server https://ntfy.<domain>, topic alerts, user phone (password from OpenBao or global-secrets, documented).

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
• A Secret not written yet (OpenTofu not applied): its PushSecret is not ready ("secret not found"); the consumer's ExternalSecret is not ready; nothing else is affected.
  • OpenBao loses its data: infra-secrets and global-secrets push everything again within an hour.
  • Namespace infra-secrets never appears: the unit fails after 30 minutes with a visible message.
  • A token outside generated/ collides with a generated path: refused by the infra policy; scripts/check-secret-stores refuses it before merge.
  • ntfy down or the Tunnel down: alerts do not reach phones; the Watchdog's delayed message cannot fire either. An external dead man's switch is an idea, not in this step.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Offline: renders; scripts/check-secret-stores extended (only platform/global-secrets pushes generated/ through openbao-writer, only platform/infra-secrets pushes elsewhere through openbao-infra; each push has a reader); scripts/check-mesh-policies (ntfy's allow, Alertmanager → ntfy in EXTRA); scripts/check-env-config (egress); make -C infra check.
  • Sandbox (test/): the secrets unit's wireguard/private-key reaches OpenBao and equals the Secret in infra-secrets; after its OpenBao value is deleted it comes back (forced sync); role infra writes outside generated/ but neither reads nor writes generated/; ntfy refuses requests without credentials, refuses a publish by phone, and an alert posted to Alertmanager reaches topic alerts (read as phone); the Watchdog's scheduled message exists; ntfy answers through the Gateway.
  • Production: terragrunt plan of infra/production/secrets reads the Cloudflare output (no apply before the cluster exists).
  • make dev-clean; make dev: every test passes.

docs.title: Docs
docs.text:
• docs/concepts/secrets-management.md: secrets from OpenTofu (infra-secrets), the two writers; the extra-secrets section replaced.
  • New docs/how-to-guides/alerts.md: subscribing to ntfy.
  • docs/installation/production/external-resources.md and other pages naming external/ or make external; VPN page: keys come from OpenBao / OpenTofu.
  • CLAUDE.md: roadmap 8b done; rules (two writers); production checklist (Cloudflare secrets reach the cluster; Tailscale's key in step 12; ntfy's public route untested; WireGuard's public key from the unit's output); Ideas: an external dead man's switch for the Watchdog.

docs.title: Step 9: Logs with Loki 3 and Grafana Alloy, in production and the sandbox
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-17, written spec awaiting review. Branch: feat/logs (PR into dev, after step 8b's PR #35 merges).

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Every pod's logs and the cluster's Kubernetes events land in Loki and stay queryable in Grafana for 30 days, in production and in the sandbox, where tests prove the path. The deprecated loki-stack chart (Loki 2.x, Promtail) is replaced by the maintained loki chart (single binary) and Grafana Alloy. The roadmap gains this step as 9; Git and CI, Backups, Nodes and Remote access become 10 to 13.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• system/loki wraps loki-stack 2.10.1 (Grafana's repository): Loki 2.9 with Promtail, ServiceMonitor on. It runs only in production (the root ApplicationSet takes system/*; the sandbox's list omits it and system/monitoring-system/values-dev.yaml drops Grafana's Loki data source). Its allow admits Grafana and Prometheus on 3100; scripts/check-mesh-policies has Grafana → Loki in EXTRA.
  • Upstream master and nixos use the same chart: Promtail as a DaemonSet reading /var/log/pods (and /var/lib/docker/containers) through hostPath; neither collects Kubernetes events.
  • Found 2026-10-17: Grafana's repository marks loki-stack deprecated (last 2.10.3, Loki 2.9.3); loki-distributed and lgtm-distributed are deprecated too; no maintained all-in-one chart exists. Promtail reached end of life on 2026-03-02; Grafana Alloy replaces it. The loki chart moved to https://grafana-community.github.io/helm-charts (Grafana's own copy stopped at 7.3.0); simple scalable mode is deprecated before Loki 4.0. k8s-monitoring (Alloy with ready-made pipelines) overlaps kube-prometheus-stack.
  • k3s runs containerd: the kubelet writes every container's log under /var/log/pods; /var/lib/docker/containers is empty there.
  • loki.source.kubernetes_events supports Alloy's clustering: watching every namespace, only one clustered instance collects; positions live in Alloy's storage path.
  • Decided 2026-10-17: separate charts (loki, plain alloy), Alloy as a DaemonSet reading files like upstream's Promtail, events kept 30 days, the step numbered 9.
  • Versions (2026-10-17): chart loki 18.17.0 (Loki 3.7.8), chart alloy 1.13.1 (Alloy v1.20.1).

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Component system/loki (namespace loki) wraps both charts, as upstream wraps loki-stack Loki deploymentMode: SingleBinary, 1 replica, filesystem storage on a 10Gi PVC, schema tsdb v13, auth_enabled: false, retention 30 days (compactor) Loki extras off gateway, canary, chunks and results caches, minio, helm test, self-monitoring dashboards that need the operator Collector Alloy DaemonSet; discovery.kubernetes (pods on its node) → loki.source.file on /var/log/pods (hostPath, read-only) → loki.process (stage.cri) → loki.write to http://loki:3100 Labels namespace, pod, container, app (the pod's app.kubernetes.io/name, else app), node; stream from the CRI line Positions Alloy's storage path on a hostPath (/var/lib/alloy), so a restarted pod resumes where it stopped Events loki.source.kubernetes_events, all namespaces, clustering on (one instance collects), labels namespace, job RBAC Alloy's chart ClusterRole: pods and nodes (discovery), events (get, list, watch) Mesh Alloy stays in the ambient mesh; same-namespace calls are allowed; Prometheus scrapes Alloy (12345) and Loki (3100) Grafana Data source http://loki.loki:3100 in production and the sandbox Sandbox system/loki joins the sandbox's root list; smaller PVC and retention (values-dev.yaml) Roadmap Step 9 Logs; old 9 to 12 become 10 to 13 everywhere they are named Backup Not in this step: step 11 decides whether Loki's PVC is backed up (default: not)

docs.title: system/loki
docs.text:
Chart.yaml depends on loki 18.17.0 (grafana-community) and alloy 1.13.1 (grafana). values.yaml:

  • loki: single binary as above; loki.limits_config.retention_period: 720h, compactor with retention enabled and its delete-request store on the filesystem; singleBinary.persistence.size: 10Gi; ServiceMonitor on (the chart's monitoring block), everything that needs Grafana Agent operator or Loki's own canary off.
  • alloy: controller.type: daemonset; alloy.clustering.enabled: true; mounts /var/log/pods read-only and /var/lib/alloy (hostPath, DirectoryOrCreate) as storage; runs as root (the log files are root's, read-only mount); config in alloy.configMap.content (River) with the pipeline above and the events source; ServiceMonitor on.
  • templates/authorization-policy.yaml: unchanged rules (same namespace, Grafana and Prometheus on 3100) plus Prometheus on Alloy's 12345.

values-dev.yaml: PVC 2Gi, retention 7 days.

docs.title: Wiring
docs.text:
• system/argocd/values-dev.yaml: system/loki in the root directories.
  • system/monitoring-system/values-dev.yaml: drop the override that removes Grafana's Loki data source.
  • scripts/check-mesh-policies: Grafana → Loki stays; the ServiceMonitor checks see the new ports.
  • Egress: nothing new (the API server is in the baseline).

docs.title: Roadmap renumbering
docs.text: CLAUDE.md's roadmap inserts "9. Logs: Loki 3 (single binary) and Grafana Alloy (pod logs and Kubernetes events), in the sandbox too (done)" and renumbers 9–12 to 10–13; every "step 9/10/11/12" in docs, comments, CLAUDE.md and docs/superpowers/deferred-minors.md follows (about 15 places, plus those 8b added).

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
• Loki down or its PVC full: Alloy keeps the lines in its write-ahead log (loki.write's wal, experimental in Alloy v1.20, on the host's /var/lib/alloy, segments kept 24 hours) and sends them once Loki is back; older segments are dropped; kube-prometheus-stack's pod alerts (crash loops, PVC filling up) reach ntfy.
  • A pod deleted before Alloy read its last lines: they are lost (the kubelet removes its log directory).
  • The events instance moves to another Alloy pod (node drain): a few events may be delivered twice.
  • Losing Loki's PVC loses past logs only. Whether step 11 (backups) declares Loki's PVC is decided there; until then logs have no backup.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Offline: renders (prod, dev), scripts/check-mesh-policies, scripts/check-env-config, scripts/check-secret-stores.
  • Sandbox (test/logs_test.go, through the API server's service proxy as prometheusQuery does):
  • a temporary pod prints a marker; a LogQL query {namespace="<ns>", pod="<pod>"} |= "<marker>" returns it within a few minutes, with the labels above;
  • a Kubernetes event of that namespace (for example the pod's Scheduled or Pulled) is in Loki;
  • after the Alloy pod on the node restarts, a second marker arrives and the first is not delivered again;
  • Grafana's Loki data source health check succeeds (Grafana API, admin user);
  • Prometheus has Loki's and Alloy's targets up.
  • make dev-clean; make dev: every test passes; the make dev filter gains Logs.

docs.title: Docs
docs.text:
• docs/reference/architecture/overview.md: the logs path.
  • A short how-to: querying logs and events in Grafana (Explore → Loki, label examples).
  • CLAUDE.md: roadmap (step 9 done, renumbered; step 11 gains "decide whether Loki's PVC is backed up"), Sandbox (Loki and Alloy run there), production checklist (Loki and Alloy ran only in the sandbox: rook-ceph PVC, retention sizing, /var/log/pods on NixOS k3s nodes).

docs.title: Step 8a: OpenBao holds the cluster's secrets, read per namespace through External Secrets
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-16, written spec awaiting review. Branch: feat/openbao (PR into dev).

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: OpenBao, in the cluster, is where the homelab's secrets live. Each namespace reads only its own branch (secret/<namespace>/*) through a SecretStore and External Secrets (ESO); generated secrets are pushed into it once and never overwritten. OpenBao unseals itself with a key OpenTofu creates and keeps outside the cluster, and configures itself from git on first start. Step 8 continues with 8b (OpenTofu's secrets, such as Cloudflare's, into OpenBao; external/ removed) and 8c (OpenTofu state on Cloudflare R2 with state encryption).

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Today platform/global-secrets generates random secrets with ESO Password generators into Kubernetes Secrets in namespace global-secrets, and a ClusterSecretStore global-secrets (Kubernetes provider) lets every namespace's ExternalSecret read any of them. Consumers: Forgejo and Argo CD (forgejo.admin), Grafana (grafana.admin), paperless (paperless.admin, paperless.secret-key), zot (registry.ci), woodpecker (woodpecker.agent). Read but created elsewhere: external (wireguard-private-key, tailscale-auth-key; external/, production only), forgejo.woodpecker, forgejo.renovate (nobody yet; step 9). kaniop creates Kanidm's OAuth2 client secrets in each app's namespace, outside this.
  • Upstream nixos runs OpenBao through bank-vaults (vault-operator, which initialises it and keeps its unseal keys and root token in a Kubernetes Secret, and secrets-webhook, which replaces bao: references in Secrets). Its policy apps lets a namespace's default service account read secret/<namespace>/*. It has no OpenBao backup yet (a TODO).
  • Decided 2026-10-16: keep ESO (OpenBao behind it); no bank-vaults; the unseal key comes from OpenTofu (kept in state, outside the cluster); per-namespace access like upstream; a shared chart renders each namespace's SecretStore.
  • Spike (2026-10-16, sandbox, OpenBao 2.7.1): seal "static" with a 32-byte key from a mounted Secret auto-unseals; self-initialisation (initialize stanzas) enables KV v2, Kubernetes auth, policies and roles on first start (no root token is returned, no recovery keys exist); a policy templated on the Kubernetes auth accessor (taken from an earlier self-init response) lets namespace A read secret/A/* and refuses B; after a restart OpenBao unseals itself, keeps its data and does not self-initialise again.
  • Found while planning (ESO 2.12 source, providers/v1/vault/client_push.go): a PushSecret reads the path before it writes (403 is an error, only 404 means "absent"), writes custom_metadata to secret/metadata/<path> first, and the data write that follows is then an update for OpenBao (KV v2's existence check looks at the metadata). So writer needs create, read and update on secret/data/* and secret/metadata/*: the spike's create-only policy cannot push through ESO. "Never overwritten" therefore comes from updatePolicy: IfNotExists, not from the policy; the writer's only holder is namespace global-secrets, which already holds every generated value in plain Secrets.
  • Amended after the PR's first review (2026-10-17): the writer reached every branch, which 8b's OpenTofu secrets would share; it is now limited to generated/ paths. Audiences, the key guard, the namespace wait as a separate step (OpenTofu hides a provisioner's output when its environment is sensitive) and the rotation order came from the same review's minors.
  • Versions (2026-10-16): OpenBao 2.7.1, chart openbao 0.30.4 (https://openbao.github.io/openbao-helm).

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Server platform/openbao: the official chart, standalone, 1 replica, raft storage on a PVC, no injector, no UI route Unseal seal "static", key from Secret openbao/openbao-unseal (file mount), key id homelab-1 Unseal key OpenTofu unit infra/<env>/openbao (random_bytes 32, kept in state), writes the Secret once the namespace exists Configuration Self-initialisation in the chart's config (git): KV v2 secret/, Kubernetes auth, policies apps, writer, admin, roles apps, writer, admin Emergency access Role admin bound to service account openbao-admin (namespace openbao): kubectl create token then log in; no root token exists Reading Every Application renders system/secret-store (extra source, like system/egress): SecretStore openbao in its namespace, Kubernetes auth role apps with the namespace's default service account Key layout secret/<namespace>/<name>, properties as today (password, …); generated secrets under secret/<namespace>/generated/<name> Generating platform/global-secrets keeps the Password generators; a PushSecret per entry writes it to each destination (updatePolicy: IfNotExists, checked hourly so a lost destination is pushed again) through a SecretStore with role writer Writer policy create, read, update on secret/data/+/generated/* and secret/metadata/+/generated/* (what ESO's push needs); no delete; it never reaches what OpenTofu writes (8b) Audience Every role requires audience openbao; the SecretStores request it (serviceAccountRef.audiences) Key protection One random_bytes; production's protect adds a prevent_destroy guard whose trigger is the key, so a plan that would replace or destroy it fails, and flipping protect never changes the key (turning it off needs the guard removed from state first) Shared secrets One generated value pushed to several branches (Forgejo's admin password to secret/forgejo/generated/admin and secret/argocd/generated/forgejo-admin) Old store ClusterSecretStore global-secrets removed; every ExternalSecret moves to SecretStore openbao

docs.title: OpenTofu unit openbao
docs.text: infra/_modules/openbao: random_bytes (32) and a terraform_data that waits for namespace openbao (created by Argo CD when it syncs platform/openbao) and applies Secret openbao-unseal (key key, the raw bytes) server-side. The key never changes unless the resource is replaced (rotation is a later concern: OpenBao's previous_key). infra/sandbox/openbao depends on ../argocd; infra/production/openbao likewise, with prevent_destroy. Its state now holds the unseal key: .state stays user-only (7c's hook), and 8c moves state to R2 with encryption.

docs.title: platform/openbao
docs.text:
Wrapper chart over openbao 0.30.4: server.standalone with the HCL config (listener without TLS inside the mesh; ztunnel's mTLS carries it), raft storage on a PVC (the chart's data-openbao-0, never pruned: a StatefulSet's PVCs are not Argo CD's), the unseal Secret mounted read-only, injector.enabled: false, ui: false. The config's initialize stanzas, in order:

  1. mounts: sys/mounts/secret (kv v2), sys/auth/kubernetes, auth/kubernetes/config, a read of sys/auth/kubernetes (its accessor);
  2. policies: apps (templated with the accessor: read on secret/data/{{identity.entity.aliases.<accessor>.metadata.service_account_namespace}}/*), writer (see Decisions), admin (everything);
  3. roles: apps (service account default in any namespace), writer (default in global-secrets), admin (openbao-admin in openbao).

Also: the openbao-admin ServiceAccount; system:auth-delegator for the server's service account (TokenReview); the namespace's allow AuthorizationPolicy (External Secrets' controller on 8200; same namespace); egress needs nothing new (the API server is in the baseline).

docs.title: system/secret-store
docs.text:
A chart every Application renders as an extra source (like system/egress, same exclude), producing in the Application's namespace:

apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: SecretStore
metadata:
  name: openbao
spec:
  provider:
    vault:
      server: http://openbao.openbao.svc.cluster.local:8200
      path: secret
      version: v2
      auth:
        kubernetes:
          mountPath: kubernetes
          role: apps
          serviceAccountRef:
            name: default

It renders only once ESO's CRDs exist (capability gate, like the Argo CD templates of 7b; scripts/render-chart passes the API).

docs.title: platform/global-secrets
docs.text:
Each entry gains destinations (namespace/name paths); the generator and its Kubernetes Secret stay; a PushSecret (refreshInterval 1h, updatePolicy: IfNotExists, deletionPolicy: None: an existing value is never replaced, a missing one, such as after OpenBao lost its data, is pushed again) pushes the Secret to each destination through SecretStore openbao-writer (role writer, rendered by the chart itself). The ClusterSecretStore and its RBAC are removed.

Entry Destinations forgejo.admin forgejo/generated/admin, argocd/generated/forgejo-admin grafana.admin grafana/generated/admin paperless.admin, paperless.secret-key paperless/generated/admin, paperless/generated/secret-key registry.ci zot/generated/ci woodpecker.agent woodpecker/generated/agent

docs.title: Consumers
docs.text: Every ExternalSecret that read ClusterSecretStore global-secrets reads SecretStore openbao with the new key (key: admin, property: password, …): platform/forgejo, system/argocd (forgejo-repository), platform/grafana, platform/zot, apps/paperless.yaml, platform/woodpecker, platform/renovate, apps/wireguard.yaml, apps/tailscale.yaml. The keys nobody creates yet keep their new paths (woodpecker/forgejo, renovate/forgejo, wireguard/private-key, tailscale/auth-key): 8b and step 9 write them.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
• The unseal Secret missing: the OpenBao pod waits (mount not optional); the OpenTofu unit times out with a message if namespace openbao never appears.
  • A self-initialisation request failing: OpenBao logs it and stops initialising; nothing reads secrets; the sandbox tests fail at once. Fix the config and recreate OpenBao's storage (the sandbox: make dev-clean).
  • A namespace reading another's branch: OpenBao refuses; ESO marks the ExternalSecret not ready.
  • Losing the cluster: the unseal key survives in OpenTofu's state; backups of OpenBao's data (raft snapshots) come in step 10, which must restore before self-initialisation runs on a new install.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Offline: renders of every changed component; scripts/check-mesh-policies (namespace openbao's allow), scripts/check-secret-stores (every ExternalSecret reads SecretStore openbao with keys under its namespace, generators aside; only platform/global-secrets pushes, through openbao-writer; no ClusterSecretStore), make -C infra check.
  • test/secrets_test.go (sandbox): OpenBao is initialised and unsealed; after its pod is deleted it comes back unsealed with the same data; a temporary pod in one namespace logs in with role apps and reads its own branch but not another namespace's, and cannot write even its own; the admin role (service account openbao-admin) lists the policies; Grafana's admin Secret (synced from OpenBao) equals the generated one in global-secrets.
  • make dev-clean; make dev: every existing test passes (SSO, Forgejo seed, zot CI login read secrets through OpenBao now).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text:
• docs/concepts/secrets-management.md: OpenBao, per-namespace branches, generating, the unseal key, emergency access.
  • CLAUDE.md: roadmap 8 split into 8a (done), 8b, 8c; rules: a component reads SecretStore openbao with keys under its namespace; a shared secret is pushed to each reader's branch; the production checklist: OpenBao's data has no backup until step 10, and its unseal key lives in .state until 8c.

docs.title: The ambient mesh recovers after a node restart
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-18; this written spec is waiting for review. Branch: fix/mesh-node-restart (PR into dev), on top of the branch's two spike commits.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: After a node restarts, whether it rebooted, crashed or lost power, the pods on it rejoin the ambient mesh and serve again without anyone stepping in. A sandbox test that restarts the node proves this on every make dev.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
On 2026-10-17, after PR #36 merged, make dev on dev failed. etcd's slow fdatasync made k3s lose leader election and exit, and the k3d node container restarted. After the restart, every meshed pod on the node stayed Pending, and ztunnel never became Ready. The mesh never recovered: one run was stuck for 92 minutes before it was stopped. A pod that is deleted, and so gets a new UID, starts normally.

ztunnel's log repeats this line for each stuck pod:

error inpod::workloadmanager failed to start proxy: Bind([::1]:15053, Os { code: 99, kind: AddrNotAvailable, ... })

istio-cni's log shows cmdAdd timing out:

istio-cni cmdAdd failed to contact node Istio CNI agent: failed to send event request: Post "http://unix/cmdadd":
context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)

Upstream knows the symptom, but nobody has explained it. istio/istio#52858 and #55794 ("after restarting the node") and istio/ztunnel#1707 report it on AKS, kubeadm and k3s, from 1.24 to 1.28.

  • A maintainer fixed a related race (istio/istio#56738, a deleted pod) but said the node-restart case is a different problem.
  • They guessed that "the pod's netns changes without the UID changing", but have "never been able to reproduce it".

docs.title: 55794 was closed by the stale bot. Istio 1.31.2 (2026-10-15) does not change this behaviour.
Investigation (2026-10-17/18, sandbox, Istio 1.31.1, k3s v1.37.1+k3s1, containerd 2.3.4)
docs.text:
Each run did docker restart k3d-homelab-dev-server-0 on a healthy sandbox. A throwaway sampler inside the node recorded, every second:

  • every netns's loopback addresses;
  • the pod sandboxes and their netns;
  • the netns file descriptors ztunnel held.

It also collected the pod logs from /var/log/pods and the kubelet log.

docs.title: Timeline (Istio defaults: istio-cni patches 10-flannel.conflist, IPv6 rules on)
docs.text: After the node is up What happened +7s k3s's API server is up +14s ztunnel and istio-cni start. They are DaemonSet pods, so they restart in place, in parallel and in no fixed order: in another run istio-cni started at +15s and ztunnel at +42s +14s → +70s ztunnel waits for istiod's XDS. First DNS fails (CoreDNS is not up), then TCP fails (istiod is not up), and its backoff grows to 10.24s. ztunnel connects to istio-cni's socket only once XDS is established: "Stream established" and "new ztunnel connected" are 1 ms apart +27s CoreDNS and istiod are Deployment pods, so they are replaced by new pods (new names and UIDs), which are scheduled again. Their sandboxes are ready at +45s; CoreDNS is ready at +52s and istiod at +60s +34s → +40s The kubelet recreates the sandboxes of all 28 meshed pods. istio-cni's agent has no ztunnel connection, so it marks each pod ambient.istio.io/redirection: pending and returns an error. The plugin had already timed out after 5s. containerd tears each sandbox down, and the loopback plugin's DEL sets lo down: 127.0.0.1 stays on lo, but ::1 is removed +70s ztunnel connects. The agent sends its snapshot, which still holds the netns of the sandboxes that were torn down after that ztunnel starts a proxy in each dead netns. Binding [::1]:15053 fails because the address is gone, so the entry stays pending and ztunnel stays not Ready. New sandboxes (same UID, new netns) keep timing out, so the loop never ends

docs.title: Why it never ends: the agent cannot answer within 5 seconds
docs.text:
The plugin waits 5s for the agent (cni/pkg/plugin/cnieventclient.go:49, Timeout: 5 * time.Second, hardcoded). The agent processes the pod adds that the kubelet keeps retrying one after another, and most of its time goes to iptables-nft-restore, at about 0.36s per call on WSL. With IPv6 rules on, each pod needs an IPv4 and an IPv6 restore.

The agent's time per add, from "adding pod to the mesh" to its answer:

istio-cni setting Median per minute Fastest Adds under 5s defaults (IPv6 rules on) 12.3–13.2s 9.6s 0 in 5 minutes, so it never recovers cni.ambient.ipv6: false 5.1–5.4s 4.6s 2 per minute, rising to 31, so it recovers in 5–13 minutes

No add ever succeeds while the agent's latency stays above 5s, so the backlog never shrinks. When a few adds do succeed, the backlog shrinks, more adds fit under 5s, and the loop unwinds. It is a contest between how much work is queued and how fast the agent works through it. Memory plays no part.

ztunnel itself handles a pod that comes back with the same UID and a new netns. src/inpod/statemanager.rs (1.31.1):

  • If an add arrives with a different netns inode, ztunnel replaces the old proxy (lines 262–271).
  • If that add succeeds, ztunnel drops the old pending entry (lines 243–244). Its test workload_added_while_pending is the regression test for #52858.
  • ztunnel is Ready once it has the snapshot and no pending entries (lines 346–349).

So a few stuck pods can heal once a fresh add gets through. Many stuck pods keep the agent and ztunnel too busy for that. Maintainers already note in istio/istio#53371 that the design, where the snapshot and the "PartialAdd" retries act as a queue, has no reconciliation.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Configuration Restarts Outcome Defaults 5 Never recovered (10, 12, 20+ and 92 minutes observed) istioOwnedCNIConfig only 1 Not recovered after 10 minutes istioOwnedCNIConfig + cni.ambient.ipv6: false 4 Recovered after 5.5, 6.5, 6.5 and 13.4 minutes Defaults, stuck for 92 minutes, then the istio-cni pod deleted 1 Recovered 3.7 minutes later

After that last recovery:

  • ztunnel served all 29 meshed workloads over HBONE, and every pod carried redirection: enabled.
  • The apps answered as before the restart: draw, home, speedtest and budget 200, pairdrop 404, grafana 302, git 303.
  • Restarting ztunnel alone does not help (tried on 2026-10-17), because the agent sends it the same snapshot again.
  • Restarting istio-cni does help, because its agent rebuilds the snapshot.

docs.title: Other findings
docs.text:
• On every start k3s rewrites 10-flannel.conflist, and the istio-cni plugin entry disappears from it: the entry was there before a restart and counted 0 after. Pods that the kubelet starts before the agent patches the file again never pass through istio-cni and run outside the mesh (istio/istio#55968, #60882).
  • With cni.istioOwnedCNIConfig: true, Istio writes its own 02-istio-cni.conflist, which k3s does not touch. It is the setting the maintainers point to for that race (istio/istio PR #56156; #60882: "This is solved by the ISTIO_OWNED_CNI setting"). It does not fix the deadlock.
  • ztunnel's own IPV6_ENABLED=false would stop ztunnel from binding [::1]. In a dead netns ztunnel would then "succeed", turn Ready, and leave the real pod outside the mesh. It is rejected.
  • istiod (HPA min 1) and k3s's CoreDNS run one replica each, as upstream nixos also does (infra/_modules/platform/istio.tf).
  • The official registry.k8s.io/kubectl image has no shell. alpine/kubectl 1.37.1 has sh and BusyBox date.

docs.title: How likely this is in production
docs.text:
The deadlock needs pods to start while their node's ztunnel is not connected, and enough of them at once to keep the agent above 5s.

  • kured reboot (drain first, one node at a time): pods move away before the reboot and come back after the node is Ready, by which time ztunnel is usually connected. Rare.
  • One node crashes (no drain), istiod and CoreDNS on other nodes: ztunnel gets XDS within seconds of starting. A container that starts late (+42s in one run) can still lose the race, but only about a third of the pods live on each node, and real CPUs run iptables faster than WSL. Unlikely, and a stuck node probably heals by itself.
  • The node running the only istiod or CoreDNS crashes: Kubernetes waits about 5 minutes (the default NotReady toleration) before rescheduling them. Without CoreDNS, the whole cluster loses DNS in that window.
  • Power loss (every node restarts): this is the sandbox's situation. It is unmeasured on real hardware.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Spike commits Keep them in the history (they record what was tried); later commits drop ipv6: false and fix the comment cni.ambient.ipv6: false Kept (revised during implementation, 2026-10-18). The watchdog alone failed: after it cleared the snapshot ztunnel turned Ready, but the agent stayed at ~11 s per pod, so new adds kept timing out, made new dead netns and ztunnel relapsed; the GREEN run needed 26 minutes. Pods only get IPv4 (cluster CIDR 10.42.0.0/16, upstream's IPv6-only hetzner-1 included), so the setting only matters for a dual-stack cluster: its comment says to remove it then. global.nativeNftables was tried instead and crash-loops istio-cni on k3s (kubelet or kubelite process not found, istio/istio#61078) cni.istioOwnedCNIConfig: true Kept. Its comment names the k3s rewrite of 10-flannel.conflist and istio/istio#55968 Watchdog A CronJob istio-cni-watchdog in istio-system, in production and in the sandbox Watchdog rule For each node: if the ztunnel container has been running for more than 180s and is not Ready, and the istio-cni container on that node has been running for more than 180s, delete that node's istio-cni pod. A healthy ztunnel is Ready within seconds, and the 180s istio-cni age stops repeated restarts Watchdog schedule Every minute; concurrencyPolicy: Forbid; startingDeadlineSeconds: 50; the Job's activeDeadlineSeconds: 50 and ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 300; history limits 1 Watchdog image alpine/kubectl:1.37.1, pinned by digest (it needs a shell; the official image has none). runAsNonRoot (UID 65534), read-only root filesystem, every capability dropped, small requests Watchdog RBAC ServiceAccount, Role and RoleBinding in istio-system: pods get, list, delete. The rule now looks only at ztunnel and istio-cni pods, so no cluster-wide read is needed Watchdog network istio-system is outside the mesh and outside system/egress, so the pod reaches the API server. The pod is excluded by namespace, so it starts while ztunnel is stuck. scripts/check-mesh-policies decides whether it needs a NetworkPolicy: it has no ports to open istiod in production pilot.autoscaleMin: 2 and a topologySpreadConstraints entry on kubernetes.io/hostname (maxSkew: 1, ScheduleAnyway) in values.yaml. values-dev.yaml sets autoscaleMin: 1 (one node) CoreDNS in production k3s manages it, and kube-system is outside Argo CD. Two replicas spread over nodes go into the production checklist for step 12 (NixOS k3s config) Istio Bump every Istio chart from 1.31.1 to 1.31.2, the latest stable, as the version rule requires when touching a component. Its notes are security fixes and do not touch this Upstream report A separate issue on istio/istio linking #55794, with the timeline and the latency table. It is public, so it is the user's call after this PR. Not part of this work

docs.title: Test
docs.text:
TestNodeRestart in test/node_restart_test.go. The name avoids every word in make dev's main filter (Mesh would match TestMeshSurvivesNodeRestart, because go test -run is not anchored).

  1. Record each app's status code through the Gateway, as probe.sh did (draw, home, speedtest, pairdrop, budget, grafana, git), and check the cluster is healthy first.
  2. Run docker restart on the node container (the name comes from the test environment).
  3. Within 20 minutes (revised from 12: recoveries measured 5.5 to 13.4 minutes), all of these hold:
  4. the API server answers;
  5. every ztunnel pod is Ready;
  6. no pod is outside Running or Succeeded, ignoring completed Jobs;
  7. every pod in a meshed namespace carries ambient.istio.io/redirection: enabled;
  8. every app returns the code recorded in step 1.
  9. On failure, the test logs ztunnel's not-ready state and the pods that are not running.

make dev runs it on its own after the main parallel run: a second smoke-test call with smoke_filter='NodeRestart', because it takes the whole cluster down. That adds about 6 to 15 minutes.

  • RED: before the watchdog exists, with ipv6: false dropped, the test fails at its 12-minute limit. This is already shown 5/5 times; the run is repeated on the branch.
  • GREEN: with the watchdog, it passes. Revised during implementation: the watchdog alone did not (26 minutes, see the cni.ambient.ipv6 decision); with ipv6: false and the watchdog the test passed in 662s.

The existing checks (render-chart, check-mesh-policies, check-env-config, check-secret-stores, go vet and the offline tests, mkdocs build --strict, make -C infra check) pass. make dev-clean && make dev passes from scratch (Istio's bump changes the CNI config on a running sandbox).

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• CLAUDE.md, Sandbox: the watchdog, why it exists, and that make dev ends with TestNodeRestart.
  • CLAUDE.md, the production list (each item marked "only in the sandbox"):
  • the watchdog and node-restart recovery ran only on the one-node sandbox;
  • istiod's two replicas and their spread were only rendered;
  • CoreDNS needs two replicas spread over nodes in step 12;
  • power loss is unmeasured.
  • docs/concepts/ (networking or mesh page, whichever describes ambient): a short section on node restarts. It covers the deadlock in two sentences, the watchdog, istioOwnedCNIConfig, and where to look (kubectl -n istio-system get pods, the watchdog's Job logs).
  • docs/superpowers/deferred-minors.md: this PR adds whatever minors its review defers.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• Patching Istio (raising the 5s timeouts, dropping dead netns from the snapshot). That is upstream's fix.
  • Measuring power loss on real hardware, which is step 12.
  • CoreDNS replicas, which are step 12.

docs.title: Step 8c: OpenTofu state on Cloudflare R2, encrypted
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-18, written spec awaiting review. Branch: feat/state-r2 (PR into dev).

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Production's OpenTofu state leaves the workstation for a Cloudflare R2 bucket, so losing the workstation no longer loses it. Every environment's state is encrypted at rest with OpenTofu's state encryption. Cloudflare credentials for OpenTofu come from the cf CLI's OAuth login, as upstream nixos does, instead of a long-lived API token kept in ~/.config/homelab/cloudflare.env.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• infra/root.hcl gives every unit a local backend under .state/<env>/<unit>/terraform.tfstate, readable by the user only (an after_hook runs chmod -R go-rwx .state). Its comment says "Local state until step 8".
  • Production state today: only infra/production/cloudflare has a non-empty state. It holds the tunnel secret (random_password), the tunnel, its DNS record and two cloudflare_account_tokens. argocd, openbao and secrets are empty, because production has not been built yet.
  • infra/production/openbao will hold the OpenBao unseal key, and secrets the WireGuard private key. These are the states that must never be lost.
  • The sandbox's units (cluster, openbao, secrets, argocd) are rebuilt by make dev-clean && make dev, so their state is disposable.
  • .envrc loads ~/.config/homelab/cloudflare.env (CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN), which docs/installation/production/external-resources.md tells the user to create. CLAUDE.md, docs/concepts/secrets-management.md and docs/installation/post-installation.md mention it.
  • Upstream nixos infra/root.hcl:
  • Credentials: cf --quiet auth whoami (with CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, _API_KEY and _EMAIL unset) returns JSON with authSource ("OAuth token from ") and accounts. The OAuth token is read from that file (.oauth_token).
  • Backend: http, address https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<account>/r2/buckets/homelab-<env>-tfstate/objects/<unit>/tfstate.json, update_method = "PUT", header Authorization: Bearer <token>. No lock.
  • The same token becomes CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN for plan, apply, import and refresh. Its Cloudflare module creates cloudflare_account_tokens with it, so the OAuth scopes cover ours.
  • init runs -reconfigure, and a before_hook (lab infra state ensure) creates the bucket. destroy is refused.
  • No state encryption.
  • flake.nix in upstream nixos builds cf (cloudflare/cf, pnpm workspace cf) with stdenv.mkDerivation until nixpkgs packages it (NixOS/nixpkgs#569193). It pins 1.0.0-beta.13; the latest release is cf@1.0.0-beta.18, and every release so far is a beta.
  • OpenTofu 1.11 (this flake's unstable.opentofu) supports state and plan encryption: key_provider "pbkdf2" with a passphrase of at least 16 characters, method "aes_gcm", an optional fallback for migrating from unencrypted state, and enforced = true. The encryption block may reference variables.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Which state goes to R2 Production only. The sandbox stays local in .state/sandbox/ (disposable, and make dev must not need a Cloudflare login) Bucket homelab-production-tfstate, one object per unit: <unit>/tfstate.json (upstream's layout) Backend http with upstream's address, update_method = "PUT" and a Bearer header with the OAuth token. No lock: one operator, and R2's object API has no lock endpoint Credentials cf --quiet auth whoami, read once per Terragrunt run (run_cmd --terragrunt-global-cache --terragrunt-quiet), with Cloudflare's env variables unset and CF_SEND_TELEMETRY=false. Account: CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID if set, else the first account. Production only: sandbox units never call cf Provider token The OAuth token becomes CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN for plan, apply, import, refresh and destroy of production units. ~/.config/homelab/cloudflare.env and its .envrc line are removed Bucket creation scripts/ensure-state-bucket <account> <bucket>: a POSIX script that uses curl with the OAuth token. It creates the bucket when GET says it is missing, and does nothing otherwise. It runs as a before_hook on production's init cf CLI Built in flake.nix from upstream's derivation, pinned to cf@1.0.0-beta.18 (no stable release exists; the comment says so) with its source and pnpm hashes Encryption Every environment. key_provider "pbkdf2" with passphrase = var.state_passphrase (the generated file also declares that variable, sensitive), method "aes_gcm", applied to state and plan, enforced = true. Terragrunt generates it as encryption.tf Passphrase HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE in ~/.config/homelab/state.env (mode 600, loaded by .envrc), plus a copy in the user's password manager. Terragrunt passes it as TF_VAR_state_passphrase from the environment, so it never lands in a generated file. A missing variable fails before any OpenTofu command. The user creates it; it is never printed, logged or committed Migration, sandbox make dev-clean, then make dev with encryption (fresh state, no fallback needed) Migration, production Only infra/production/cloudflare has state (applied 2026-10-16: the tunnel, its secret and DNS record, two account tokens); the other production units are empty. One time, with the user: ! cf auth login, the user confirms, then a temporary fallback { method = method.unencrypted.plain } in encryption.tf. Per unit, terragrunt init -migrate-state moves the local state to R2, encrypted. terragrunt plan must then show no changes for cloudflare, and the empty units must stay empty. Afterwards the fallback is removed, and the local .state/production/ files are kept until the user deletes them Passphrase rotation scripts/rotate-state-passphrase <env>. The user puts the new passphrase in HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE and the old one in HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE_PREVIOUS. While _PREVIOUS is set, the generated encryption.tf adds a second pbkdf2 key provider and method as fallback, and is otherwise unchanged. For every unit of the environment that has state, the script pulls the state (decrypted with the fallback) into a mode-600 temporary file, removed on exit, and pushes it back (encrypted with the new key). It then pulls each state again with _PREVIOUS unset, to prove the new key alone reads it. It refuses when either variable is missing, when they are equal, or when the new one is shorter than 16 characters. It never prints either passphrase, and it ends by telling the user to update the password manager and state.env and to drop _PREVIOUS destroy Production prevent_destroy guards stay as they are. Sandbox destroy keeps working (make dev-clean) .state/ permissions hook Kept for the sandbox; production writes nothing under .state/ any more

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text:
• cf not logged in: run_cmd fails, and Terragrunt prints cf's error. The docs say to run cf auth login.
  • No HOMELAB_STATE_PASSPHRASE: get_env without a default fails at parse time with the variable's name.
  • Wrong passphrase: OpenTofu refuses to decrypt and changes nothing.
  • An expired OAuth token: cf auth whoami refreshes it, as upstream relies on.
  • R2 unreachable: init, plan or apply fail. Nothing is written locally.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
The flow needs a Cloudflare login and the production account, so no test runs it unattended. Checks:

  • make -C infra check (HCL validity and formatting, with the new generate blocks).
  • Offline: scripts/ensure-state-bucket against a fake curl on PATH, written as a Go test in test/ like TestIstioCNIWatchdog:
  • the bucket is missing, so it is created;
  • the bucket exists, so nothing is created;
  • the API answers an error, so the script exits non-zero with the message.
  • Offline: scripts/rotate-state-passphrase against a throwaway Terragrunt tree in a temporary directory: a copy of infra/root.hcl and one sandbox unit with a terraform_data resource (no provider, local state). It runs the real terragrunt and tofu from the dev shell, as a Go test:
  • after apply with passphrase A, the state file holds no clear text;
  • after rotating to B, the state reads with B alone and not with A;
  • a missing or equal passphrase is refused, and nothing changes.
  • Sandbox: make dev-clean && make dev passes with encrypted local state. A check that .state/sandbox/*/terraform.tfstate is encrypted (the JSON has encrypted_data, and no resource attributes in clear text) is part of the plan's verification.
  • Production, with the user: after the migration, terragrunt plan in infra/production/cloudflare shows no changes; the R2 object exists and is encrypted (read back through the API, it shows encrypted_data).

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• docs/installation/production/external-resources.md:
  • replaces the API-token steps with cf auth login;
  • adds creating the passphrase (openssl rand -base64 32 into ~/.config/homelab/state.env with chmod 600, and the password manager copy);
  • explains rotation with scripts/rotate-state-passphrase;
  • says what losing the passphrase means: the state cannot be read, and the unseal key and WireGuard key inside it are lost.
  • CLAUDE.md:
  • Sandbox bullet: "State is local in .state/ until step 8" becomes "sandbox state is local in .state/sandbox/, production's is on R2; both encrypted".
  • Production checklist: the cloudflare.env sentence becomes the cf login, and the OpenBao bullet's "its unseal key lives in .state/production/openbao until 8c" becomes R2.
  • Roadmap: 8c done.
  • docs/concepts/secrets-management.md and docs/installation/post-installation.md: the cloudflare.env mentions become the cf login and state.env.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• A state lock (one operator).
  • Backups of the R2 bucket, which are step 11.

docs.title: Step 8d: production state through R2's S3 API, with a lock
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-18, written spec awaiting review. Branch: feat/state-s3-lock, stacked on feat/test-scopes (PR #39); its PR targets dev once #39 is merged.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Production's OpenTofu state moves from the http backend (R2's REST object API, Bearer OAuth token in backend.tf, no lock) to OpenTofu's s3 backend on R2's S3 endpoint with a lock file, as upstream nixos does. Expiring R2 credentials come from lab infra state credentials, ported from upstream, so no token is written into backend.tf. The infra/production/cloudflare unit works through cf's OAuth login, and the docs say how to get the scope it needs.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Step 8c shipped the http backend. Two problems are now known:
  • infra/production/cloudflare returned 403 on account API tokens. The spike on 2026-10-18 found the cause: on the cf auth login consent page, Account API Tokens is an option the user must enable; it is off by default. With it enabled, cf auth whoami lists account_api_tokens:create (476 scopes instead of 475), the token API answers (listing account tokens and permission groups: 200; creating and deleting a 10-minute R2 token: 200), and terragrunt plan in infra/production/cloudflare reports no changes.
  • The OAuth token is part of the generated backend.tf. After a new login (or a refresh), plan fails with "Backend initialization required: please run tofu init" until someone runs terragrunt init. The 8c reviewer reported this; the fake-R2 test did not reproduce it, the production unit did on 2026-10-18.
  • Upstream nixos (infra/root.hcl, cli/internal/cli/{cloudflare,infra_state}.go, cli/internal/state/r2.go):
  • remote_state with backend s3: bucket homelab-<env>-tfstate, key <unit>/tfstate.json, region auto, endpoint https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com, use_lockfile = true, profile r2-state from a generated r2-state.config whose credential_process is lab infra state credentials --account-id … --bucket …, and the skip_* settings R2 needs;
  • lab infra state credentials: reads the cf OAuth login, finds the permission group "Workers R2 Storage Bucket Item Write", deletes this credential's expired tokens, creates an account token for that bucket only that expires in one hour, waits until R2 accepts it (signed HEAD on the bucket), and prints AWS credential-process JSON (access key = token id, secret = SHA-256 of the token value);
  • lab infra state ensure: creates the bucket when it is missing (cloudflare-go GetR2Bucket/CreateR2Bucket);
  • dependencies: github.com/cloudflare/cloudflare-go v0.115.0, github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2 (SigV4 signer).
  • This fork's cli/ (step 14a) has the cobra root and lab test scope; the Makefile runs it with go run.
  • The R2 object written by the http backend, homelab-production-tfstate/cloudflare/tfstate.json, is the key the s3 backend uses for the same unit, so the migration moves no data.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Backend Production: s3 on https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com (upstream's settings, plus use_path_style = true so a fake endpoint works in tests; R2 accepts it), key <unit>/tfstate.json, use_lockfile = true. The sandbox stays local Credentials A generated r2-state.config with credential_process running lab infra state credentials --account-id <account> --bucket <bucket>; nothing secret lands in a generated file Running lab go -C <repo>/cli run ./cmd/lab … (as in 14a: no Nix package yet). HOMELAB_LAB overrides the command (tests) Port Upstream's cli/internal/state (r2.go and its tests) and cli/internal/cli/{cloudflare,infra_state}.go with tests, imports rewritten to github.com/duongle-steven/homelab/cli; infra and infra state commands join the root. Behaviour unchanged except: --account-id is always passed by root.hcl (the account scripts/cloudflare-credentials picks), so upstream's "exactly one account" rule only applies without it Bucket creation lab infra state ensure replaces scripts/ensure-state-bucket (and TestStateBucket) in the init hook Provider token Unchanged: scripts/cloudflare-credentials gives the OAuth token to the Cloudflare provider through CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN for plan, apply, import, refresh, destroy init Production keeps -reconfigure (the backend changes from http to s3 once; afterwards the config is stable) Migration One time, with the user: terragrunt init in each production unit switches to s3; the existing object is read as is (already encrypted); state list shows 8 resources in cloudflare and plan shows no changes; argocd, openbao, secrets stay empty. No HOMELAB_STATE_MIGRATE needed Docs for the login cf auth login: on the consent page, enable Account API Tokens (off by default); cf auth whoami must list account_api_tokens:create, otherwise cf auth login --force and enable it 8c's warning The "infra/production/cloudflare cannot plan until 8d" warning and its --filter '!cloudflare' workaround leave CLAUDE.md and the docs lab auth login Not added: cf auth login is enough once the option is enabled

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text:
• cf not logged in, or the login lacks account_api_tokens:create: credential_process fails, OpenTofu reports the credential error, and lab says to run cf auth login (upstream's messages, plus the consent-page hint).
  • R2 slow to accept a new token: lab retries the signed HEAD for up to 40 seconds (upstream).
  • A stale lock (an interrupted apply): terragrunt force-unlock <id> (OpenTofu's message names it); the docs say so.
  • Token pile-up: every credential_process call creates a one-hour token; the next call deletes this credential's expired ones (upstream's pruning).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Ported upstream unit tests for state (r2_test.go, credentials_test.go, r2_activation_test.go) and cli/cloudflare_test.go, adjusted to the import path; make -C cli test.
  • Offline OpenTofu tests (test/state_*): a small fake S3 server in Go (object GET/PUT/HEAD/DELETE, conditional PUT for the lock file, ListObjectsV2) replaces the fake R2 http server; HOMELAB_LAB points credential_process at a stub printing static credentials and HOMELAB_STATE_ENDPOINT at the fake. They prove:
  • production state lands encrypted in the fake bucket, and a lock file appears while a command runs;
  • a changed OAuth token leaves backend.tf unchanged and plan needs no init (the 8c bug);
  • rotation still skips units without an object and re-encrypts the others;
  • ensure runs on init.
  • Production, with the user: after the migration, state list (8) and plan (no changes) in cloudflare; the R2 bucket holds cloudflare/tfstate.json (encrypted) and no stray lock after the commands finish.
  • test/scopes.yaml: the new cli/internal/state and cli/internal/cli files are under cli/** (skipped: offline tests cover them); infra/root.hcl selects the whole suite.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• docs/installation/production/external-resources.md: the consent-page option, the whoami check, the warning and workaround removed, the lock (and force-unlock), where state lives (s3 backend on R2, one object per unit plus a lock file during commands).
  • CLAUDE.md: roadmap 8d (done); the Sandbox bullet's state sentence names the s3 backend and its lock; the production checklist's Cloudflare sentence loses "cannot plan or apply until step 8d"; the OpenBao bullet's --filter '!cloudflare' note goes; the Ideas entry for the Go CLI lists infra state ensure|credentials as ported.
  • docs/superpowers/deferred-minors.md: the 8b line about losing .state/production/secrets is reworded for state on R2 (losing the R2 object, or the passphrase).

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• The rest of upstream's lab (cluster, sso, user, secrets) and its Nix package (the CLI step).
  • Backups of the R2 bucket (step 11).

docs.title: Test scopes: sandbox tests chosen from the change
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-18, written spec awaiting review. Branch: feat/test-scopes (PR into dev). Roadmap: done before steps 8d–14, because every later step pays for full sandbox runs.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: make dev runs the sandbox tests that the branch's changes can affect, instead of the whole suite every time (about 13 minutes for the main set plus 6 to 9 for TestNodeRestart; step 8c ran it five times). The full suite still runs where it catches what a scoped run misses: after a merge into dev, and from scratch before master and releases. The selector is the first command of a Go CLI lab, laid out like upstream nixos's cli/, so the later CLI step adds commands to it instead of rewriting it, and Woodpecker (step 10) calls the same command.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• make dev (root Makefile): pushes HEAD to branch sandbox, applies infra/sandbox, runs smoke_filter='Smoke|Identity|SSO|Gateway|Forgejo|Mesh|Monitoring|Egress|Secrets|Ntfy|Logs', then smoke_filter='NodeRestart' alone (it restarts the node). test/Makefile runs gotestsum -- -timeout 60m -run "${filter}".
  • Tests are named by area: TestSmoke*, TestIdentity*, TestSSO<App>, TestGateway*, TestForgejo*, TestMesh*, TestMonitoring*, TestEgress*, TestSecrets*, TestNtfy*, TestLogs*, TestNodeRestart*; offline ones (TestState*, TestIstioCNIWatchdog, TestNodeRestart(Blockers|WatchdogJobs), …) run in the basic checks.
  • A change often affects areas outside its own component (Istio touches every route, OpenBao every app with a secret), so groups are named by test, not by component.
  • How others do it:
  • Prow (Kubernetes, Istio): presubmits with run_if_changed, postsubmits after merge, periodics without filters.
  • Cilium (.github/ariane-config.yaml): a smoke set on every PR, the full e2e set on /test, nightly runs; heavy workflows carry paths-ignore-regex (docs and the like), so they run unless the change is plainly harmless.
  • Upstream nixos: Woodpecker runs unit tests on when.path; e2e runs by hand with make -C tests e2e filter=….
  • Build-graph tools (Bazel target-determinator, Nx affected) need a build graph this GitOps repository lacks.
  • Upstream's CLI: Go module github.com/khuedoan/homelab/cli, cli/cmd/lab/main.go, cli/internal/cli (cobra root, SilenceUsage, Execute), packages under cli/internal/<area>, cli/Makefile (go vet, go test -race), packaged in its flake with buildGoModule.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Selection Automatic from git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD, through a map; plainly harmless changes run nothing; a file the map does not know runs everything Map test/scopes.yaml, next to the tests (format below) Groups Regexes of test names (Identity\|SSO), not components Tool lab test scope in Go, cli/ module github.com/duongle-steven/homelab/cli (this fork's path; files ported from upstream get their imports rewritten), cobra, upstream's layout (cmd/lab, internal/cli, internal/scope) Running lab go run ./cmd/lab from cli/ in the Makefile: no Nix packaging or vendor hash until the CLI step New components lab test scope --check (a basic check) fails when a component is in no group and not skipped, and when a group's regex matches no test Tests that run alone alone: [NodeRestart]: selected alone tests run after the others, as today Base origin/dev by default (make dev fetches it first); base=<ref> overrides Overrides make dev scope=full, make dev tests='<regex>' From scratch make dev-fresh = make dev-clean then make dev scope=full test/'s module path git.khuedoan.com/ops/homelab (upstream's 2022 Gitea path, a name nothing imports) becomes github.com/duongle-steven/homelab/test, as upstream nixos names its modules after GitHub (github.com/khuedoan/homelab/tests)

docs.title: test/scopes.yaml
docs.text:
# Paths are git globs (** spans directories), matched against the files a branch changes
skip: [...]          # changes that run no sandbox test
always: Smoke        # added to every non-empty selection
alone: [NodeRestart] # run after the others, one at a time (they disturb the cluster)
full: Smoke|Identity|SSO|Gateway|Forgejo|Mesh|Monitoring|Egress|Secrets|Ntfy|Logs|NodeRestart
groups:
  - paths: [...]
    tests: <regex> | full   # full: the whole suite
components:          # what --check expects the map to cover
  - system/*
  - platform/*
  - apps/*.yaml
  - apps/*/
  - infra/_modules/*
  - infra/*/*/

A file that matches several groups gets their union. A changed test/<name>_test.go (other than helpers) selects the tests it defines (func Test…, read with go/parser) and the tests of every other test file that uses one of its top-level names (its helpers), so editing a test or a helper runs what depends on it. make dev tests=<regex> refuses a term that matches no test, and a non-alone term that matches an alone test.

Initial groups:

Paths Tests docs/**, **/*.md, mkdocs.yml, LICENSE.md, renovate.json5, .github/** skip Makefile, test/Makefile, test/scopes.yaml, flake.nix, flake.lock, nix/**, .envrc, system/argocd/**, infra/_modules/argocd/**, infra/sandbox/argocd/**, test/*helpers*_test.go, test/go.mod, test/go.sum; inputs of the whole cluster: infra/_modules/k3d/**, infra/sandbox/cluster/** (config.json), infra/root.hcl, scripts/env-values; system/egress/** (rendered into every namespace) full system/istio-system/** Mesh\|Gateway\|Egress\|Identity\|NodeRestart system/cert-manager/** Gateway\|Identity\|SSO system/loki/** Logs system/monitoring-system/** Monitoring\|Mesh\|Ntfy\|Logs system/secret-store/**, platform/openbao/**, platform/external-secrets/**, platform/global-secrets/**, platform/infra-secrets/**, infra/_modules/openbao/**, infra/_modules/secrets/**, infra/sandbox/openbao/**, infra/sandbox/secrets/** Secrets\|Identity\|SSO\|Ntfy\|Forgejo\|Logs\|Gateway\|Monitoring (every reader of a secret) platform/kanidm/**, scripts/onboard-user Identity\|SSO\|ForgejoSeed\|GatewayZotLargePush (Forgejo and zot need Kanidm at start) platform/grafana/** SSOGrafana\|Logs\|Monitoring platform/forgejo/** Forgejo\|SSOForgejo\|GatewayForgejoSSH platform/zot/** SSOZot\|GatewayZotLargePush apps/actualbudget.yaml, apps/paperless.yaml, apps/opencloud.yaml, apps/ntfy.yaml SSOActualBudget, SSOPaperless, SSOOpenCloud, Ntfy (one group each) The other apps; production-only components (platform/cloudnative-pg, platform/renovate, platform/woodpecker, system/cloudflared, system/external-dns, system/kured, system/rook-ceph, system/volsync-system, infra/production/**, infra/_modules/cloudflare/**, metal/**); scripts/check-*, scripts/render-chart, scripts/env-values, cli/**, infra/Makefile "" (Smoke only: the sandbox does not run them, or offline checks cover them)

Everything else (other scripts/, new top-level files) is unknown: full.

docs.title: lab test scope
docs.text:
• lab test scope [--base origin/dev] [--alone], run from anywhere in the repository:
  • reads test/scopes.yaml and the changed files of <base>...HEAD;
  • prints one line to stdout: a regex for go test -run, full's regex, or nothing when every change is skipped;
