  • without --alone the alone tests are left out; with --alone it prints only the selected alone tests (as a regex, or nothing);
  • the output is sorted and deduplicated, so the same change prints the same line.
  • lab test scope --check: every path matching a components glob matches a group or skip; every group's regex (and always, full, alone) matches at least one Test… function in test/. Exits non-zero with the offenders.
  • Errors: an unreadable or invalid scopes.yaml, a failing git diff, or a base that does not exist exit non-zero with the reason (for the base: git fetch origin dev, or scope=full). make dev stops; it never guesses.

docs.title: make dev
docs.text:
scope ?= auto
base ?= origin/dev
tests ?=
  • scope=auto: git fetch -q origin dev; main set = lab test scope --base $(base), alone set = the same with --alone. Both empty: print "nothing to test in the sandbox" and stop before pushing.
  • scope=full: main set = full without the alone tests, alone set = alone.
  • tests=<regex> replaces both sets with that regex, run as the main set (TestNodeRestart in it still runs alone after the rest).
  • Then as today: push, apply infra/sandbox, refresh, the main set, then each alone test.
  • make dev-fresh: make dev-clean then make dev scope=full.

docs.title: Rules (CLAUDE.md)
docs.text:
When What A feature-branch commit that changes code Basic checks (now with lab test scope --check and make -C cli test), then make dev (scoped) A commit that only touches skipped paths Nothing more: make dev prints that there is nothing to test Before the PR The last scoped make dev already covered the whole branch (dev...HEAD) After merging into dev make dev scope=full on dev, unless every change was skipped dev → master PR, a release make dev-fresh A new component Add it to test/scopes.yaml in the same PR (--check fails otherwise; until then it runs everything)

The "comment-only commits skip tests" convention becomes the skip list plus judgement for comments in code files.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• cli/internal/scope unit tests, with throwaway git repositories and a small scopes.yaml:
  • only skipped files → empty;
  • files in two groups → their union plus always;
  • an unknown file → full;
  • a full group → full;
  • a changed test file → the tests it defines; a changed helper → full;
  • --alone → only the selected alone tests; the main output never contains them;
  • a missing base, an invalid scopes.yaml → errors;
  • --check: an uncovered component fails, a regex matching no test fails, the clean case passes.
  • make -C cli test (go vet, go test -race) joins the basic checks, and so does lab test scope --check on this repository.
  • This branch's own make dev runs scoped: it changes Makefile and test/scopes.yaml, which select full, so the first run is the full suite; a throwaway commit on top that touches only system/loki must select Smoke|Logs (checked with lab test scope, not pushed).

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• CLAUDE.md: the basic-checks rule and the make dev rule become the table above; the Sandbox section names test/scopes.yaml, lab test scope and make dev-fresh; the roadmap records this step (done) and moves go-task to 14b; the Ideas entry for the Go CLI notes that cli/ exists with lab test scope.
  • docs/: a short page under how-to guides on running sandbox tests (scoped, full, from scratch, a single group).

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• Upstream's tests/ layout (e2e/ behind E2E=1, benchmarks/, internal/ helpers, offline tests under go test -short), which would shorten the offline list and the map: a later step, with test/ → tests/.
  • Woodpecker pipelines (step 10); the rest of the lab commands and its Nix package (the CLI step).
  • Parallel tests or faster individual tests.
  • Remembering the last tested commit to narrow the base.

docs.title: Step 10a: GitHub Actions basic checks and protected branches
docs.text: Status: approved 2026-10-19. Branch: feat/ci-checks from dev (the trimmed dev shell of PR #41 is merged).

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Every pull request into dev or master runs the basic checks on GitHub Actions, in the same Nix dev shell as the workstation, and reports one status, checks. A repository ruleset makes dev and master accept changes only through pull requests whose checks passed. The user also learns GitHub Actions on the real thing (workflows, matrix jobs, caching, concurrency, pinned actions, least-privilege tokens, rulesets).

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Until production exists (step 12), work stays on GitHub: branches, pull requests, gh. Forgejo, Woodpecker and Renovate come in steps 10c–10e; 10b runs the sandbox on GitHub Actions.
  • The repository is public: GitHub-hosted runners are free and have 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of memory.
  • The basic checks (CLAUDE.md): scripts/render-chart <dir> and <dir> dev for every changed chart or app file, go vet and the offline tests in test/ (the TestState* tests run terragrunt and tofu), mkdocs build --strict, scripts/check-mesh-policies, scripts/check-env-config, scripts/check-secret-stores, make -C infra check, make -C cli test check. Locally check-env-config takes about ten minutes.
  • The dev shell lost pre-commit in the cleanup before this step; its useful hooks were yamllint, shellcheck and tofu fmt (make -C infra check already runs tofu fmt -check). Today yamllint -s . reports two warnings (.woodpecker/) and shellcheck three notes (infra/_modules/argocd/bootstrap.sh, system/istio-system/files/cni-watchdog.sh).
  • Latest releases on 2026-10-19: actions/checkout v7.0.1, cachix/install-nix-action v31.11.2, nix-community/cache-nix-action v7.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Workflow .github/workflows/checks.yaml, on pull_request (into dev, master) and push (to dev, master) Token permissions: contents: read at the workflow level; no job asks for more Concurrency Group by workflow and ref, cancel-in-progress for pull requests only (a push to dev always finishes) Actions Pinned by full commit SHA with the version in a comment (uses: actions/checkout@<sha> # v7.0.1); Renovate bumps them in 10d Tools cachix/install-nix-action installs Nix; nix-community/cache-nix-action keeps the store in the Actions cache (key: flake.lock and flake.nix); every check runs nix develop --command … in the default dev shell. No versions are pinned twice. If a cold run takes more than five minutes to enter the shell, a devShells.ci built from the same package list is the follow-up (measured, not assumed) Jobs A matrix, one job per check: render, go, cli, infra, docs, mesh, env-config, secret-stores, lint; fail-fast: false so every failure shows One status Job checks needs the matrix, runs if: always() and fails unless every matrix job succeeded. It is the only required check, so adding or removing jobs never touches the ruleset Changed charts New lab test charts --base <ref> in cli/ (reuses scope.Changed): prints each chart directory (nearest Chart.yaml under system/, platform/, apps/) and apps/<name>.yaml the diff touches, existing ones only; a change to scripts/render-chart, scripts/env-values, infra/*/cluster/config.json or system/argocd/values*.yaml prints all of them. render renders each, with and without dev. Locally it tells which charts the basic checks must render Base ref Pull requests: github.event.pull_request.base.sha; pushes: github.event.before (all charts when it is the zero SHA, a new branch); actions/checkout with fetch-depth: 0 Offline tests go runs go vet ./... and the CLAUDE.md offline list in test/; the state tests make their own passphrases, nothing secret is needed Lint New scripts/lint: yamllint -s ., shellcheck on every tracked file whose first line is a sh/bash shebang, actionlint (added to the dev shell). The existing findings are fixed in this step. It joins the basic checks Ruleset .github/rulesets/protect-dev-master.json: branches dev and master; pull request required (0 approvals); required status check checks (integration GitHub Actions); no force-push, no deletion; bypass: repository admins (for a GitHub Actions outage). Branch sandbox stays unprotected (make dev force-pushes it) Applying it Only after the workflow has passed once on this step's pull request (GitHub offers a check as required only once it has seen it). The gh api commands to create, update, show and delete it are in docs/how-to-guides/ci.md; running them changes GitHub settings, so the user approves each run Test scopes .github/** and scripts/lint join test/scopes.yaml's skip (no sandbox effect) Local checks CLAUDE.md: the basic checks still run before each commit (CI is the second line, not a replacement); scripts/lint is added to them; lab test charts --base origin/dev names the charts to render

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text:
• A failing check fails its matrix job and then checks; the pull request shows which job failed. fail-fast: false lets every job finish.
  • A cancelled job (a newer push) leaves checks failed for that run only; the newer run reports.
  • Cache miss: the run is slower (the shell downloads from cache.nixos.org), never wrong.
  • A GitHub Actions outage: admins bypass the ruleset; the docs say to run the basic checks locally first.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• cli/internal/scope (or a new package) unit tests for lab test charts: a chart file, a values-dev.yaml, an app file, a file outside any chart, a deleted chart, a global trigger (scripts/render-chart), the zero base.
  • scripts/lint passes on the repository; actionlint passes on the workflow.
  • The real proof is this step's pull request: the workflow runs, every job passes, checks reports. Timing is recorded (cold and warm cache) in the PR.
  • After the ruleset is applied: a throwaway draft pull request with a deliberately failing check shows mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED (gh pr view --json mergeStateStatus), then is closed and its branch deleted.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• docs/how-to-guides/ci.md (in the mkdocs nav): what runs and when, how to read a failure, the ruleset and its gh api commands, the bypass, how to add a check (a matrix entry plus its local command).
  • CLAUDE.md: the Rules bullet for branches and checks mentions CI and the ruleset; scripts/lint and lab test charts join the basic checks.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• The sandbox on GitHub Actions (10b).
  • Woodpecker, Renovate, Forgejo as the source of truth (10c–10e). .woodpecker/ stays until 10c.

docs.title: Step 10b: the sandbox on GitHub Actions
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-19, written spec awaiting review. Branch: feat/ci-sandbox from dev.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: GitHub Actions builds a fresh sandbox and runs the suite on every push to dev (full unless every change is skipped), on pull requests labelled sandbox (scoped like make dev), and on demand. Contributors' pull requests are then tested in the sandbox after their merge, or before it when a maintainer labels them, without anyone running make dev by hand.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• The sandbox's Argo CD syncs branch sandbox, which make dev force-pushes; the revision is written in system/argocd/values-dev.yaml (YAML anchor &revision sandbox, used by both ApplicationSets).
  • Argo CD manages itself: system/argocd is a directory of the root ApplicationSet, so it syncs its own chart from git and would undo any revision set from outside.
  • Upstream nixos does not: OpenTofu installs Argo CD (helm_release, chart argo-cd) and creates the platform's Applications, and the apps ApplicationSet's revision is the variable var.repository.revision.
  • system/argocd holds two templates rendered only once their CRDs exist: kanidm-client.yaml (kaniop) and forgejo-repository.yaml (ESO's ExternalSecret argocd-repo-forgejo, read by test/forgejo_test.go). Today they reach the cluster through Argo CD's own sync, because the bootstrap (infra/_modules/argocd/bootstrap.sh) runs before those CRDs exist.
  • Production's first install syncs from the seed repository on GitHub (values-seed.yaml, chosen by bootstrap.sh while Forgejo is not running); Argo CD's own sync then switches it to values.yaml (ops/homelab on Forgejo). infra/production/argocd bootstraps once (prevent_destroy, ignore_changes).
  • Step 10a: checks.yaml runs the basic checks in nix develop with cache-nix-action; the ruleset requires checks. The repository is public (GitHub-hosted runners: 4 vCPUs, 16 GB, free).
  • The sandbox needs no secret from outside: the state passphrase is generated, OpenTofu and the cluster generate the rest, the repository is public.
  • Measured locally: a fresh sandbox syncs in about 20 minutes, the main run takes about 13, TestNodeRestart 5 to 10.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Argo CD No longer manages itself (upstream nixos's model): system/argocd leaves the root generator; only infra/_modules/argocd applies it Core chart system/argocd keeps Argo CD, allow-hbone, the HTTPRoute, the OIDC Secret and both ApplicationSets CRD-gated templates Move to a new component system/argocd-config (in the root generator, synced by Argo CD like every other): the KanidmOAuth2Client and the ExternalSecret argocd-repo-forgejo, names unchanged Re-apply The bootstrap re-applies whenever the chart's files, the chosen values or the revision change, in every environment, as upstream's helm_release updates in place. Production drops "once": a guard against an accidental destroy stays (the unit's resource has no destroy-time action; the plan checks how prevent_destroy can stay without ignore_changes) Revision Module variable revision; bootstrap.sh rewrites every revision/targetRevision of a source or generator whose repoURL is the homelab repository in the rendered manifests (yq), so other repositories (app-template, the seed placeholder's replacement) are untouched. The sandbox unit takes it from HOMELAB_SANDBOX_REVISION (default sandbox); production keeps the values file's Seed switch Production switches from the seed to Forgejo at the first make infra env=production after Forgejo runs (bootstrap.sh already detects it). Documented in the installation docs and CLAUDE.md's production checklist make dev New parameter revision=<sha>: no push to branch sandbox; passes HOMELAB_SANDBOX_REVISION; everything else (scope selection, nothing-to-test exit, the alone run) unchanged Workflow .github/workflows/sandbox.yaml: push to dev → make dev scope=full revision=<sha>, skipped when lab test scope --base <before> selects nothing; pull_request labeled with sandbox → make dev base=<base sha> revision=<head sha>; workflow_dispatch (inputs scope, tests) on any branch Concurrency Pushes: one group per commit (none cancelled). Labelled pull requests: one group per pull request, a newer run cancels the older. Dispatch: one group per run Runner ubuntu-24.04, timeout-minutes: 90; frees disk (removes preinstalled dotnet, android, ghc); raises fs.inotify.max_user_instances and max_user_watches; Nix and its cache as in checks.yaml (saved on pushes only); a random state passphrase; permissions: contents: read Failure output On failure, an artifact with the test output, kubectl get pods -A, the Applications' sync and health, and the logs of pods that are not Ready Forks The pull_request event gives forks a read-only token, which is all the job needs. Only users with write access can label. New commits do not rerun it: remove and re-add the label. Whether Argo CD fetches a fork's head SHA (reachable through refs/pull/<n>/head) is checked early in the plan; if not, the label path covers same-repository pull requests and the docs say so Docker Hub First runs pull anonymously and are measured; if rate limits hit, the CI sandbox gets a k3s registries.yaml mirroring docker.io through mirror.gcr.io (no credential), CI only Status The workflow's job is a check on the commit or pull request; it is not required by the ruleset (it runs after the merge, or on request) Rules CLAUDE.md: after a merge, CI runs the full suite on dev (no manual make dev scope=full; check that run); before a dev → master PR the latest sandbox run on dev must be green (it is a fresh sandbox, as make dev-fresh), rerun with workflow_dispatch; make dev stays the test before a pull request Test scopes system/argocd-config/** joins the groups that cover Argo CD (the Forgejo and SSO tests); .github/** is already skipped

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text:
• A failing test fails the job; the artifact holds the cluster's state.
  • Nothing to test (every change skipped): the job succeeds in about a minute without building the sandbox.
  • Docker Hub rate limit: pods stay in ImagePullBackOff, visible in the artifact; the mirror is the fix.
  • A cancelled labelled run (newer label): its check shows cancelled; the newer run reports.
  • A broken dev after a merge: the push run fails and GitHub notifies the author; fix it with a new pull request.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Offline (in the go check): render system/argocd with the revision abc123 through the bootstrap's rewrite; every revision/targetRevision of the homelab repository becomes abc123, app-template's chart version and the seed repository do not; without a revision the output equals today's.
  • The sandbox suite after the restructure: make dev (the whole suite) proves Argo CD, its Kanidm client and argocd-repo-forgejo still come up with system/argocd-config.
  • On GitHub: this step's pull request labelled sandbox passes the suite; after the merge the push run on dev is green; a fork's labelled pull request is tried (or the limit documented).

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• docs/how-to-guides/ci.md: the sandbox workflow, its triggers, the label, the artifact, forks, dispatch.
  • docs/how-to-guides/sandbox-tests.md: make dev revision=.
  • Installation docs: Argo CD's changes need make infra env=production; the seed switch.
  • CLAUDE.md: Argo CD no longer manages itself (Sandbox bullets, the bootstrap, the production checklist's seed sentence), the new rules above, roadmap 10b done.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• Porting system/ and platform/ to OpenTofu-managed Applications as upstream does.
  • Woodpecker, Renovate, Forgejo as the source of truth (10c–10e).

docs.title: Step 10c: production deploys by an explicit push
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-20, written spec awaiting review. Branch: feat/forgejo-deploy from dev.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Production receives only the commits someone deliberately deploys. GitHub stays where work happens (pull requests, checks, the sandbox); production's Argo CD syncs ops/homelab on Forgejo, which changes only through lab infra forgejo push, run from the workstation, and only for a commit on origin/master whose checks passed. make infra env=production does the whole deploy in one command, the first install included, as upstream nixos's make infra does.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Upstream nixos has lab infra forgejo sync (with forgejo_admin: org ops, an empty ops/homelab, a team developers with write, the Woodpecker OAuth client into OpenBao) and lab infra forgejo push (HEAD to ops/homelab master as forgejo_admin, through GIT_ASKPASS; no guard). Its make infra runs terragrunt run --all apply, then sync, then push. It reads OpenBao with the root token through the API server's service proxy, and OpenTofu installs Forgejo and OpenBao from their charts, so Argo CD reads Forgejo from the start.
  • Here, Argo CD installs Forgejo and OpenBao from the GitOps repository, so production's first install reads the seed (values-seed.yaml, global.seedRepository on GitHub) until Forgejo serves ops/homelab. A Job forgejo-seed (platform/forgejo/templates/seed-job.yaml) copies the seed into ops/homelab once, as forgejo_admin. infra/_modules/argocd/choose-values.sh switches the bootstrap to values.yaml once a Forgejo pod runs, and never back.
  • Argo CD reads ops/homelab with forgejo_admin's password (system/argocd-config/templates/forgejo-repository.yaml, OpenBao argocd/generated/forgejo-admin, a second destination of forgejo.admin in platform/global-secrets).
  • OpenBao has no root token: admins log in with the role admin as service account openbao/openbao-admin (audience openbao; docs/concepts/secrets-management.md).
  • cli/ (lab) has test scope and infra state ensure|credentials (cobra); make infra env=production refuses anything but origin/master without changes (production-checkout, force=1 overrides).
  • Forgejo users come from Kanidm (auto-registration; homelab-admins become Forgejo admins at each login). Nothing declares Forgejo's orgs, teams or repositories.
  • Production does not exist yet: its nodes come in step 12. Before then the push can only reach the sandbox's Forgejo, which the sandbox's Argo CD does not read (it reads GitHub branch sandbox).

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
1. Port upstream's commands into cli/ (Go: forgejo-sdk, OpenBao's API client, client-go), with unit tests against fakes and sandbox tests against the real Forgejo and OpenBao. Rejected: a Job doing the sync (shell, hard to test, unlike upstream) and shell scripts (tokens in logs, against the plan to grow lab).
  2. lab infra forgejo sync|push|verify [--env production|sandbox], production by default. The domain comes from infra/<env>/cluster/config.json, the kubeconfig is infra/<env>/kubeconfig.yaml, the checkout is the repository lab runs in (no --source, no --domain, no --kubeconfig). The guards apply to production only; sandbox exists for the tests.
  3. No seed Job. sync creates an empty ops/homelab; the first push is the first deploy and passes the same guards. choose-values.sh switches only once Argo CD's own credential reads ops/homelab's master.
  4. sync owns org ops and nothing else in Forgejo (idempotent: what is right is kept, what is wrong is fixed, what is missing is created):
  5. org ops; repository ops/homelab, private, default branch master, content never touched;
  6. local users deploy and argocd, restricted (they see only repositories they collaborate on), created through the admin API with a random one-time password that is used to create their token and never stored;
  7. collaborators on ops/homelab: deploy write, argocd read; no team has write (unlike upstream);
  8. master's branch protection: push allowlist with only deploy, force-push disabled for everyone (a protected branch cannot be deleted);
  9. tokens: deploy's lab (write:repository), argocd's argocd (read:repository). A token stored in OpenBao that still authenticates (GET /api/v1/user) is kept; otherwise the token of that name is deleted and a new one created. They are written to OpenBao at secret/forgejo/deploy and secret/argocd/forgejo (property token); after a change sync force-syncs the ExternalSecret argocd/argocd-repo-forgejo and waits until its Secret holds the new token, so the terragrunt apply that follows (decision 9) can already switch to Forgejo.
  10. lab reads forgejo_admin's password from the Secret forgejo/forgejo-admin and logs in to OpenBao as openbao/openbao-admin (a TokenRequest with audience openbao, role admin) through the API server's service proxy; it revokes its OpenBao token when done. No token or password reaches an argument, the output or a log.
  11. sync waits for Forgejo and OpenBao to be ready (a first install takes about 20 minutes) and fails after 30 minutes.
  12. Guards (verify; push runs them first), in order, stopping at the first failure:
  13. no uncommitted change to tracked files;
  14. git fetch origin master, HEAD equals origin/master;
  15. GitHub's API, without a token (the repository is seed_repository from infra/production/cluster/config.json): the latest check run checks on HEAD succeeded, and a pull request merged into master whose merge_commit_sha is HEAD has a latest check run sandbox on its head that succeeded. No such pull request (a direct push) fails. A check still running fails with "wait for it and run again"; an API error fails, never passes.
  16. push: guards (production), then git -c credential.helper= push https://git.<domain>/ops/homelab.git HEAD:refs/heads/master with deploy's token through GIT_ASKPASS and an environment variable, as upstream does. Never forced: a rollback is a revert through a pull request on GitHub, and Forgejo refuses a non-fast-forward push. If Forgejo's master already is HEAD, it says so and pushes nothing. In the sandbox, lab dials the node (docker inspect, http.curloptResolve for git, a dialer for the API) and trusts homelab-dev-ca, so it works on GitHub Actions without the localhost proxy. push serves only ops/homelab: other repositories (blog) reach Forgejo by mirror or by hand, decided in step 10e. No --wait; the history of ops/homelab is the deploy log.
  17. Argo CD's credential argocd-repo-forgejo: username argocd, password from argocd/forgejo token. forgejo.admin loses its destination argocd/generated/forgejo-admin: the admin password stays in namespace forgejo.
  18. choose-values.sh switches from the seed when the Secret argocd/argocd-repo-forgejo exists and its token reads /api/v1/repos/ops/homelab/branches/master from inside the Forgejo pod (kubectl exec, the token on stdin, curl to localhost:3000). Forgejo down, no token yet, nothing pushed yet or a wrong credential keep the seed. Once the root ApplicationSet reads Forgejo it never goes back (as today). A kubectl failure other than "not found" fails the script, as today.
  19. make infra env=production runs, stopping at the first failure:
  20. lab infra forgejo verify (skipped with force=1, which replaces today's production-checkout);
  21. terragrunt run --all apply in infra/production;
  22. lab infra forgejo sync;
  23. lab infra forgejo push;
  24. terragrunt apply in infra/production/argocd (the switch to Forgejo on the first install; afterwards a change to system/argocd, or nothing).

The first install and every later deploy are the same command. lab infra forgejo push alone deploys without touching the infrastructure. The sandbox's make dev does not change. 10. Out of this step, moved in the roadmap: the staging guard goes to step 12 with make staging (nothing can mark a commit before then, and production does not exist before then either); the Woodpecker OAuth client goes to step 10e with Woodpecker.

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text:
• A guard fails: nothing is pushed or applied; the message names the guard and, for a check, its state and link.
  • sync fails halfway: running it again finishes the job (every step checks before it changes).
  • A token in OpenBao that no longer authenticates (deleted in Forgejo, Forgejo's data lost): sync replaces it, and ESO refreshes argocd-repo-forgejo within its refresh interval (or force-sync it).
  • forgejo_admin and Kanidm admins are Forgejo site admins. If a site admin can still push to the protected master (the sandbox test records which), the docs say so: like a GitHub admin, it is a deliberate bypass, not a guard.
  • Forgejo down during a deploy: sync waits up to 30 minutes, then fails; production keeps syncing what it has.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• cli/, unit tests (in make -C cli test, part of the basic checks):
  • guards against a fake GitHub API: both checks succeeded passes; a running check, a failed check, no pull request, an API error, HEAD not origin/master and an uncommitted change each fail;
  • sync against a fake Forgejo: a first run creates everything, a second run writes nothing, a valid token is kept, an invalid one is replaced, the branch protection matches decision 4;
  • push: the token is in neither git's arguments nor its output.
  • test/ against the sandbox (replacing TestForgejoSeed and TestForgejoSeedIsIdempotent):
  • sync --env sandbox twice: the second run changes nothing and keeps the tokens in OpenBao;
  • push --env sandbox: Forgejo's master is HEAD;
  • the protection: argocd's token cannot push; deploy can neither force-push nor delete master; forgejo_admin's push is recorded either way;
  • argocd-repo-forgejo reads master with the read-only token.
  • Offline: TestArgoCDChooseValues gains Forgejo running without master (seed), master readable (switch) and a wrong credential (seed); a Makefile test shows make infra env=production runs verify before applying and skips it with force=1. test/scopes.yaml gets the new tests.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• docs/installation/production/deployment.md: the first install and later deploys (one command), rollback by revert, what force=1 skips.
  • Forgejo's docs: sync owns org ops (users deploy and argocd, the protection, the tokens); nothing declares other orgs or repositories.
  • CLAUDE.md: 10c done; the staging guard in step 12; the Woodpecker OAuth client in 10e; the production checklist without the seed Job and with Argo CD's read-only token.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• Running any of it against production (step 12), the staging guard (step 12), Woodpecker and its OAuth client (10e).
  • Declaring Forgejo orgs, teams or repositories other than ops (for example groupTeamMap).
  • Pushing repositories other than ops/homelab.

docs.title: Step 10d: Renovate on GitHub through our own GitHub App
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-20; decision 2 revised in chat 2026-10-21 (the token is minted in Renovate's pod, not by ESO's generator, so ESO needs no internet). Branch: feat/renovate from dev.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Renovate runs in the production cluster and opens pull requests into dev on GitHub, authenticated as a GitHub App of our own installed only on chosen repositories, so its pull requests run checks (and, labelled sandbox, the sandbox) like anyone's. No long-lived token: the App's private key stays in OpenBao and Renovate gets installation tokens that live one hour.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• platform/renovate exists but targets Forgejo: chart 31.97.3, platform: forgejo, a token renovate/forgejo that nothing writes; renovate.json5 extends the old config:base. Egress allows ports 80 and 443 for renovate.
  • Upstream master ran Renovate in the cluster against Gitea with a token scripts/hacks minted through Gitea's admin API; upstream nixos has only renovate.json5 and no bot pull requests on GitHub.
  • Upstream nixos's secrets are all created by OpenTofu (provider resources, random_password) or lab, never typed in. A GitHub App's private key cannot be created through an API (only in GitHub's UI, or the manifest flow, which also needs a browser): it is the first secret a person brings in, next to the state passphrase (the only secret that must be kept). It can be regenerated on GitHub at any time.
  • External Secrets 2.12 has the generator GithubAccessToken, but it runs in ESO's controller, which reads every Secret: with default-deny egress (step 6d-2) it would need the internet, so it is not used (decision 2).
  • GitHub mints an installation token for a JWT signed with the App's key (POST /app/installations/<id>/access_tokens, optional permissions), and a token revokes itself (DELETE /installation/token). The Renovate chart has cronjob.initContainers, cronjob.preCommand (before renovate, in one bash -c with set -e), extraVolumes and extraVolumeMounts.
  • Production does not exist before step 12; the sandbox takes no secret from outside.
  • Today every push to dev runs the whole sandbox suite and none cancels another, and the maintainer labels every own pull request sandbox although make dev already ran the same scope locally.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
1. Key path (B'): infra/_modules/secrets takes the App's private key once, from the file HOMELAB_GITHUB_APP_KEY names (read by infra/production/secrets), and keeps it in its encrypted state on R2 (a terraform_data whose stored value later runs keep when the variable is empty; a new key replaces it with -replace). It joins the secrets map as renovate/github-app (property private-key), so it reaches OpenBao like the WireGuard key (infra-secrets → platform/infra-secrets). The file can be deleted after the first apply.
  2. Token, minted per run in Renovate's pod: an ExternalSecret in namespace renovate copies renovate/github-app into the Secret renovate-github-app (ESO reads OpenBao as usual and needs no internet). The CronJob's initContainer github-token (Renovate's own image: node signs the JWT, no other image to pin; the script in a ConfigMap) mounts only that Secret, signs a JWT that lives 9 minutes, mints an installation token with only contents, pull_requests, workflows, issues (write) and checks, statuses (read) for every repository the App is installed on, and writes it to an emptyDir in memory. The Renovate container never mounts the key: its preCommand reads the token into RENOVATE_TOKEN and traps EXIT to revoke it (DELETE /installation/token), so the token ends with the run, failed or not (a killed pod's token expires within the hour). The pod has automountServiceAccountToken: false. App ID and installation ID live in platform/renovate/values.yaml (neither is secret). NetworkPolicies apply to the whole pod: renovate keeps 443 (Renovate reaches many registries), external-secrets gets no internet.
  3. The App (created by hand, documented): duongle-lab-renovate, permissions Contents, Pull requests, Workflows, Issues (the Dependency Dashboard) read and write, Commit statuses and Checks read, Metadata read; no webhook; installed on "Only select repositories": homelab. Renovate's autodiscover lists exactly the installation's repositories; autodiscoverFilter: ["duongle-steven/*"] guards against an installation elsewhere. Adding a repository is a change on GitHub only.
  4. Renovate: chart 46.372.0 (the latest), CronJob daily at 05:00 in global.timezone (timeZone), so its pull requests and their sandbox runs are done before the working day, production only (not among the sandbox's components). Global config in values.yaml: platform: github, autodiscover, autodiscoverFilter, onboarding: false, requireConfig: required, gitAuthor the App's bot (<slug>[bot] <<bot user id>+<slug>[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>, the id from gh api /users/<slug>[bot]).
  5. Repository config (renovate.json5): config:recommended, baseBranches: ["dev"], minor and patch grouped as today, majors separate, lockFileMaintenance weekly (flake.lock), labels: ["sandbox"], no automerge. The default managers cover Helm charts and values, Go modules, OpenTofu providers and SHA-pinned actions.
  6. Sandbox runs: a push to dev cancels the sandbox run of an older push still in progress (only the newest dev is tested in full; an older commit can be tested on demand with revision): sandbox.yaml's concurrency group is the workflow and branch for a push, and the run for a workflow_dispatch, so a manual run and a dev run never cancel each other. The other workflows' groups already start with the workflow's name and the pull request (sandbox-label: the pull request and the label; sandbox-release, sandbox-retarget: the pull request), so a label run on one pull request (ours or Renovate's) cancels only an older label run on the same pull request, never another pull request's run, a dev run or a release. Own pull requests are labelled sandbox only when they change what the local sandbox cannot prove (the first install, CI); Renovate's always are, since nobody runs make dev for them. Labelling needs Triage or more on the repository (today only the owner); the App labels through its Issues and Pull requests write permissions, and a label added by an App, unlike one added with GITHUB_TOKEN, triggers workflows.
  7. Egress: renovate keeps port 443 only.

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text:
• A wrong App ID, installation ID, key or permission: the initContainer fails with GitHub's status and message (never the key, the JWT or a token), the Job fails and Renovate does not start. The proof below catches this before production. The key not yet given: the pod waits for its Secret.
  • A run longer than an hour fails part-way; the next day's run continues (Renovate is idempotent).
  • OpenBao loses its data (no backup before step 11): the next make infra env=production writes the key again from the state. A lost or leaked key: generate a new one on GitHub, delete the old, apply with -replace.

docs.title: Proof (once, not a permanent test)
docs.text: On the sandbox, with the key written to its OpenBao by the admin role: apply platform/renovate rendered for production into namespace renovate and run its CronJob once (kubectl create job --from=cronjob/...) with RENOVATE_DRY_RUN=lookup: the initContainer mints a token (our IDs, key and permissions match the App), Renovate logs in and reads homelab with our config, and once the Job ends the token is revoked (a GitHub API call with it returns 401; the token is read from the pod's log of a hash only, never printed). The real run that opens a pull request into dev labelled sandbox waits for the next dev → master release: Renovate reads renovate.json5 from the default branch. Then delete the namespace and the key from the sandbox.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Offline (basic checks): platform/renovate rendered for production mounts the key only in the initContainer, the token's emptyDir in memory, automountServiceAccountToken: false, no GithubAccessToken, the CronJob's 05:00 and timeZone; the mint script against a fake GitHub API signs a valid RS256 JWT for the App ID, asks for exactly the six permissions, writes the token, prints neither the token nor the key, and fails on an API error; and no Forgejo leftovers; the sandbox does not deploy it; renovate-config-validator (nixpkgs renovate, in the dev shell and scripts/lint) accepts renovate.json5 and the global config.
  • State test: infra/_modules/secrets keeps the stored key when a later apply passes none, and -replace takes a new one.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• A how-to for Renovate: create and install the App, the first make infra with HOMELAB_GITHUB_APP_KEY, rotating the key, adding a repository.
  • CLAUDE.md: 10d done with the App's real permissions; the production checklist (Renovate only rendered and proven once on the sandbox; App and installation IDs in values.yaml; the key's path); the sandbox label rule; dev runs cancel older ones. The egress table without port 80 for renovate.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• Renovate on Forgejo repositories (blog and others: step 10e), automerge, Mend's hosted Renovate.
  • Reusing a dev result for the dev → master check.

docs.title: Step 8e: generated secrets straight to OpenBao
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-21, written spec awaiting review. Branch: feat/generated-secrets from dev.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: A generated secret has one value, the one in OpenBao, and nothing else holds a copy that can differ from it. Tests, docs and people read generated values where the apps read them.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• platform/global-secrets (namespace global-secrets, from upstream master, where other namespaces read its Secrets): for each entry of values.yaml, a Password generator, an ExternalSecret (refreshPolicy: CreatedOnce) writing it into a Secret <name>, and a PushSecret (updatePolicy: IfNotExists, refreshInterval: 1h, deletionPolicy: None, SecretStore openbao-writer, role writer) copying that Secret to each destination secret/<namespace>/generated/<name>. Apps read only OpenBao, through their namespace's SecretStore openbao.
  • ESO 2.12's CreatedOnce (shouldRefresh) generates again when the ExternalSecret's status has no SyncedResourceVersion or the Secret looks invalid (missing from the cache, or a wrong label or data hash). A reconcile that reads a stale ExternalSecret right after the first sync regenerates the Secret. The PushSecret then keeps OpenBao's first value (IfNotExists), so the Secret in global-secrets differs from what every app reads. This failed sandbox-label on PR #49 (ntfy.phone-token: TestNtfyUsers and three alert tests got 401) and, before PR #47, zot's registry.ci.
  • What reads the copies in global-secrets: the tests (ntfyToken, registry.ci in gateway_test.go and sso_test.go, grafana.admin in secrets_test.go, test/global_secrets_test.go), and the docs that tell people to read a password there (alerts.md: ntfy's phone; post-installation.md, sandbox.md: paperless, Grafana, zot's ci). No app reads them. On a restore (step 11) they would be regenerated and differ from OpenBao too.
  • ESO 2.12's PushSecret takes spec.selector.generatorRef: each reconcile calls the generator once and, with IfNotExists, writes only the destinations that do not exist (SecretExists), all from that one value.
  • OpenBao's role writer is bound to namespace global-secrets (platform/openbao/values.yaml, an initialize stanza: applied only on an empty storage).
  • One entry has two destinations: ntfy.alerts-token (ntfy/generated/alerts-token, read by ntfy; monitoring-system/generated/ntfy, read by Alertmanager). OpenBao's policy apps lets a namespace read only its own branch.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
1. Rename platform/global-secrets to platform/generated-secrets, namespace generated-secrets: it holds only Password generators, PushSecrets and the SecretStore openbao-writer (role writer, the namespace's default service account). OpenBao's role writer is bound to generated-secrets. Production does not exist yet; the sandbox is rebuilt (below).
  2. No intermediate Secret: each entry is a Password generator and a PushSecret with selector.generatorRef (that generator), updatePolicy: IfNotExists, deletionPolicy: None, refreshInterval: 1h, one data item per destination (secretKey: password, remoteRef.property: <key>). No ExternalSecret, no Secret in the namespace. A missing destination (an OpenBao that lost its data, a rotation) is written within the hour or at a force-sync; an existing one never changes.
  3. One value per entry, copied per namespace in one push: an entry's destinations are written by the same reconcile, so they hold the same value. A destination added to an existing entry later would get a new value: the docs say to copy the existing value there with the admin role first (the push then leaves it). No cross-namespace read in OpenBao's policy.
  4. OpenBao is the only source: the tests read generated values from OpenBao (role writer reads */generated/*, as it must before writing) or from the app's own Secret; the docs tell people the same (bao kv get with the admin role, or the Secret the app's own ExternalSecret writes in its namespace).
  5. Rotation (docs/concepts/secrets-management.md) becomes: with the admin role, delete every destination of the entry (bao kv metadata delete), force-sync its PushSecret, force-sync the readers' ExternalSecrets, restart the apps, and change admin passwords inside the app. Roadmap 11b automates it.
  6. Values stay in values.yaml as today (name, key, length, special, destinations, extraSecrets).

docs.title: Migration
docs.text:
• Sandbox: make dev-fresh once (CI always builds fresh). On an existing sandbox the old namespace keeps its resources (preserveResourcesOnDeletion) and OpenBao's role writer still names global-secrets; the docs say so.
  • Production: nothing to migrate (step 12).

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text:
• A generator or OpenBao error: the PushSecret reports it (Errored) and retries; an existing destination is never touched, so no app sees a new value.
  • OpenBao loses its data without a backup: every generated secret is generated again at the next push (as today); step 11 backs OpenBao up.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Offline (basic checks, replacing test/global_secrets_test.go): platform/generated-secrets rendered has, for every entry, a Password generator and a PushSecret with generatorRef to it, IfNotExists, deletionPolicy: None, one data item per destination with secretKey: password and the entry's key as property, and no ExternalSecret or Secret; scripts/check-secret-stores knows the new name.
  • Sandbox (Secrets group): namespace generated-secrets has no Secret; every destination exists in OpenBao; two force-syncs of a PushSecret leave OpenBao's value unchanged (hashes compared, never printed); both destinations of ntfy.alerts-token are equal. The tests that read generated values (ntfy, zot's ci, Grafana's admin) read them from OpenBao.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: • docs/concepts/secrets-management.md (the generated secrets section, rotation, adding a destination), alerts.md, post-installation.md, sandbox.md; CLAUDE.md: 8e done, the sandbox paragraph and the production checklist where they name global-secrets.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: • Rotation commands and schedules (11b), backups (11a), cross-namespace reads in OpenBao.

docs.title: Step 10e: Woodpecker for other repositories on Forgejo
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-21. Branch: feat/woodpecker from dev.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Repositories on Forgejo other than ops/homelab get CI in the cluster: a push runs the repository's .woodpecker.yaml and can build an image into zot. Only the people allowed to run code in the cluster can sign in. The sandbox proves it end to end with a test repository; the blog's own repository comes later.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• platform/woodpecker (chart 3.7.5, app 3.19.0, production only): two agents on the Kubernetes backend, WOODPECKER_OPEN: true, WOODPECKER_ADMIN: forgejo_admin, an HTTPRoute ci.<domain>, an AuthorizationPolicy (Gateway and Forgejo's webhooks on 8000), egress 80/443. Its ExternalSecret woodpecker-secret reads woodpecker/forgejo (client_id, client_secret), which nothing writes, and woodpecker/generated/agent. The server does not read that Secret (CLAUDE.md's production checklist), and the agents never get the agent secret. WOODPECKER_WEBHOOK_HOST is Woodpecker 2's name; Woodpecker 3 reads WOODPECKER_EXPERT_WEBHOOK_HOST.
  • Upstream nixos (infra/_modules/platform/woodpecker.tf, cli/internal/forgejo): lab infra forgejo sync creates a confidential Forgejo OAuth2 application woodpecker (redirect https://ci.<domain>/authorize) and writes client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri to woodpecker/forgejo; Forgejo maps a Kanidm group to an org team (groupTeamMap, groupTeamMapRemoval: true); server and agents read the agent secret from one Secret (createAgentSecret: false, mapAgentSecret: false, extraSecretNamesForEnvFrom).
  • Our lab infra forgejo sync owns org ops and refuses any team grant on ops/homelab, so the CI org must be another org.
  • Forgejo's accounts come only from Kanidm; its login source sets homelab-admins as Forgejo admins.
  • zot lets user ci (htpasswd, zot/generated/ci) read, create and update every repository.
  • The sandbox today: the k3d node uses 7.3 GiB of the workstation's 11.7 GiB, its pods 5.3 GiB, about 4 GiB is free. Woodpecker adds an estimated 100 to 150 MiB at rest (server and one agent) and up to 0.5 GiB while a build runs.
  • .woodpecker/ in this repository (from upstream master) runs removed checks; this repository's CI is GitHub Actions, and production's Forgejo holds it only to deploy (deferred minor "dev shell cleanup").
  • Deferred minor #31: a change to Woodpecker's or zot's settings does not restart their pods.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
1. Sign-in only for members of Forgejo org ci: WOODPECKER_OPEN: true with WOODPECKER_ORGS: ci (a user outside the org cannot register). lab infra forgejo sync creates the private org ci and its team developers (write on code and pull requests, may create org repositories, not all repositories); Forgejo's login source maps homelab-admins to ci/Owners (Woodpecker lets only org admins set org secrets) and homelab-editors to ci/developers (groupTeamMap, groupTeamMapRemoval: true, so leaving the group in Kanidm drops the membership at the next login). homelab-users and outsiders cannot sign in. WOODPECKER_ADMIN: forgejo_admin stays.
  2. The OAuth client from lab infra forgejo sync, ported from upstream: the Forgejo OAuth2 application woodpecker (confidential, redirect https://ci.<domain>/authorize), its credentials written to woodpecker/forgejo (client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri) with the admin role, kept while they match and replaced otherwise; two applications named woodpecker fail the sync. make infra env=production already runs sync.
  3. Server and agents wired: the server reads woodpecker-secret (Forgejo client and agent secret) and woodpecker-environment; the agents read only the agent secret (a second ExternalSecret woodpecker-agent), as upstream. WOODPECKER_EXPERT_WEBHOOK_HOST replaces WOODPECKER_WEBHOOK_HOST. No checksum annotation: the chart passes podAnnotations without tpl, so the wrapper cannot hash woodpecker-environment into them; settings in server.env/agent.env already roll the pods, and Secrets ESO writes from OpenBao never would. #31 stays deferred; 11b chooses between a controller that watches Secrets (Stakater Reloader) and explicit restarts.
  4. Step pods unprivileged: no privileged plugins (WOODPECKER_PLUGINS_PRIVILEGED empty), every *_ALLOW_FROM_STEP option off (service account, node selector, labels, annotations, runtime class), steps in user namespaces (WOODPECKER_BACKEND_K8S_USER_NAMESPACES) so a step's root is not the node's root. The step pods' service account has no API access. The plan's first task proves it on the k3d node (Kubernetes 1.37, kernel 6.18); if user namespaces do not work there, steps run without them, still unprivileged, and the spec's review decides.
  5. Images built with Buildah (quay.io/buildah/stable, pinned): --isolation chroot, --storage-driver vfs, no privilege, pushed to registry.<domain>/<repository> as zot's ci. Kaniko is archived; BuildKit rootless needs seccomp and AppArmor unconfined.
  6. zot's credentials for pipelines: an org secret registry_password in Woodpecker's org ci (with registry_username: ci), set with the admin role by a documented command (the value read from OpenBao, never printed) by a member of homelab-admins. Pipelines use from_secret. Rotation (11b) changes it there too.
  7. The sandbox runs Woodpecker (system/argocd/values-dev.yaml, values-dev.yaml: one agent, the dev CA for the server; Forgejo's clone and zot's push skip TLS verification only in the sandbox's test pipeline, since step pods cannot mount the CA). Its woodpecker/forgejo appears when lab infra forgejo sync --env sandbox runs; until then the server waits for its Secret.
  8. .woodpecker/ removed from this repository (fixes the "dev shell cleanup" minor).
  9. Versions: the latest chart and server, agent and Buildah images, pinned.
  10. Break-glass when GitHub or the internet is down (asked in chat): production keeps running (Argo CD reads Forgejo), but verify needs GitHub. lab infra forgejo push --break-glass=<reason> (production only) skips verify's GitHub checks and nothing else: no uncommitted changes, HEAD must fast-forward what Forgejo's master holds (never forced), the reason is printed and required (non-empty). make infra env=production break_glass=<reason> runs verify --break-glass (the same checks against Forgejo, before anything is applied) and passes it to push. Afterwards the same commit reaches GitHub's master through a branch, a PR into dev and the release PR (merge commits keep it an ancestor, so the next normal push fast-forwards). docs/how-to-guides/deploy-to-forgejo.md gets a break-glass section: what works without GitHub (Forgejo, Argo CD for charts and images already cached; OpenTofu needs R2, so with no internet only push works, never make infra), that charts on *.github.io and images on ghcr.io also depend on GitHub, and the last resort without any push (pause an Application's auto-sync in Argo CD, kubectl, then resume after the fix lands in git).

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text:
• woodpecker/forgejo missing (sync not run yet): the ExternalSecret errors and the server waits; nothing else depends on Woodpecker.
  • A Forgejo OAuth application changed by hand: the next sync restores it and writes the new credentials; ESO refreshes woodpecker-secret within its refresh interval, then the server is restarted by hand (kubectl rollout restart statefulset/woodpecker-server -n woodpecker, documented).
  • A build that needs privilege fails; it is never granted per repository.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Offline: lab unit tests for the org, team and OAuth client (fake Forgejo, as sync_test.go): created, kept when right, fixed when wrong, refused when duplicated; no secret in errors. Renders: server and agent env, no privileged plugins, the ExternalSecrets; scripts/check-* pass.
  • Sandbox (new group Woodpecker, test/scopes.yaml): lab infra forgejo sync --env sandbox, then dev-editor signs in to Woodpecker through Forgejo and Kanidm, dev-viewer is refused (not in ci); as dev-editor, a test repository in org ci (a Dockerfile and a .woodpecker.yaml that builds with Buildah and pushes to zot as ci), activated through Woodpecker's API, pushed; the pipeline succeeds within 10 minutes and zot serves the tag; the step pods ran without privilege and in a user namespace; cleanup removes the repository, the Woodpecker repository and the image.
  • TestForgejoDeploy also checks the OAuth client in OpenBao and that a second sync keeps it.
  • lab unit tests for --break-glass: refused for the sandbox and with an empty reason; with a reason, no GitHub call is made and a HEAD that does not fast-forward Forgejo's master is still refused; make infra's offline test (TestMakeInfraProduction) passes break_glass and skips verify.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• docs/how-to-guides/woodpecker.md: signing in (groups), activating a repository, the org secret command, a .woodpecker.yaml example with Buildah, mirroring a repository into Forgejo.
  • docs/concepts/secrets-management.md: woodpecker/forgejo written by sync; docs/how-to-guides/deploy-to-forgejo.md: what sync creates; networking.md if a rule changes.
  • CLAUDE.md: 10e done; the production checklist's Woodpecker lines (server not reading its Secret, woodpecker/forgejo unwritten) replaced by what production still does not prove.
  • deferred-minors.md: "dev shell cleanup" removed; #31 kept, its step changed to 11b (Reloader or explicit restarts).

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• The blog's repository and its deployment (after 10e, when its source exists), pull credentials for apps/blog.
  • Forgejo Actions, Woodpecker for ops/homelab, a Nix cache, per-org namespaces.

docs.title: Step 11a: backups
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-22, amended while planning (decisions 5, 8 and 9; approved in chat). Branch: feat/backups from dev.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
A cluster that is switched off, loses power or loses one disk or node comes back with its data. The step itself does nothing for that case: Ceph's replicas already cover it. What 11a adds:

  • Mistakes: a person deletes something or an app corrupts its data, and the volume can go back an hour.
  • Loss of every node, or new hardware: the state that is not in git can be restored from off-site, by a command someone chooses to run.

Git rebuilds everything else. Argo CD recreates every resource from the repository, and OpenTofu's state (with OpenBao's unseal key) is already on R2. Backups therefore hold volume data only, never Kubernetes resources.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Storage:
  • Production: rook-ceph (system/rook-ceph, chart 1.13.5), pools with 2 replicas, default VolumeSnapshotClasses and a snapshot-controller already installed.
  • Sandbox: k3d's local-path provisioner, with no CSI snapshots.
  • VolSync: system/volsync-system (chart 0.9.1) is installed but used by nothing. Namespaces get the label volsync.backube/privileged-movers (system/argocd/values.yaml). docs/how-to-guides/backup-and-restore.md still describes upstream master's removed make backup.
  • Upstream nixos (commit 481903b7, 2026-10-22) replaced VolSync with Velero (docs/reference/architecture/decision-records.md there):
  • infra/_modules/backup creates the R2 bucket <prefix>-backup, an account token that can write only that bucket, and a random_password for the repository, all with prevent_destroy.
  • Velero (chart 12.2.1, plugin velero-plugin-for-aws v1.14.4) runs with deployNodeAgent, CSI snapshot data movement and an hourly schedule of the whole cluster.
  • Their restore is manual: backup_read_only makes the location ReadOnly and disables the schedule, then velero restore create.
  • Their open items: OpenBao's data ("TODO: Add tested backups for secrets storage"), and databases that "may still need backup hooks".
  • R2's free tier (account-wide, Standard class): 10 GB-month, 1 million Class A and 10 million Class B operations per month, egress free. The state bucket uses a few MB of it.
  • Deferred minors that point to step 11:
  • 8b: losing secrets/tfstate.json creates a new WireGuard key.

docs.title: 34: a partial restore makes two destinations of one generated secret drift.
1. Velero replaces VolSync
docs.text: This follows upstream nixos. system/volsync-system, its AuthorizationPolicy, its scopes.yaml entry and the privileged-movers label go away. Velero lives in system/velero, as Argo CD components do here (upstream installs it from OpenTofu). It uses the latest chart and plugin, pinned. If the chart's app version lags Velero's latest release, the image is pinned to the latest one.

docs.title: 2. Volumes only, never resources
docs.text: Backups include PersistentVolumeClaims and their data. They include no Deployment, Secret, ConfigMap or custom resource: Argo CD rebuilds those from git, and restoring them over Argo CD would fight it.

docs.title: 3. Three layers
docs.text:
Layer Where Covers Does not cover Ceph replicas (existing) the nodes' disks power loss, sudden shutdown, one disk or node lost deletion, corruption (copied to every replica) Local snapshots (new) Ceph, on the nodes deletion, corruption, a failed upgrade: back one hour losing several nodes or Ceph itself, new hardware Off-site copies (new) R2 bucket homelab-production-backup losing every node, new hardware losing R2 or the state passphrase
  • Local snapshots:
  • Ceph VolumeSnapshots of every volume in groups A and B below, every hour, keeping 48 hours.
  • Taking and restoring one must work without the internet. A layer whose metadata lives only on R2 does not qualify.
  • Off-site copies: Velero with Kopia (deduplicated, compressed, encrypted) to R2.

docs.title: 4. What goes off-site
docs.text:
Membership is declared next to each component: a label on its PVC or namespace. A new app gets no off-site copy unless it says so.

Group Volumes Off-site A: automatic OpenBao, Kanidm, Forgejo (forgejo-data and PostgreSQL forgejo-db), Woodpecker's server, ntfy, Matrix (Dendrite and its PostgreSQL), and every other app published on the internet that keeps data a daily schedule, kept 30 days B: on demand Actual Budget, paperless, OpenCloud only when someone runs the command (decision 7), kept 30 days C: never zot, Loki, ollama, jellyfin (one PVC holds its config, the *arr apps' config and the media; config without the media is worth nothing, and only losing Ceph loses it) nothing; they are rebuilt or downloaded again

Group C still gets local snapshots where that is cheap. That is the builder's call, given the disk space Ceph has.

docs.title: 5. Consistent copies
docs.text:
Each backup must be restorable, not just a file copy of a running database:

  • OpenBao goes off-site as a raft snapshot (bao operator raft snapshot save), not as a copy of its data directory. The snapshot restores with the same unseal key, which survives in OpenTofu's state on R2.
  • PostgreSQL (forgejo-db, Matrix): its volume goes the same way as every other volume. A crash-consistent snapshot is enough, because PostgreSQL replays its WAL (the log it writes before changing data) at start.
  • Forgejo's two volumes (forgejo-data: repositories, attachments; forgejo-db: users, issues, pull requests, branches) are restored from the same backup run and snapshotted one right after the other. A few seconds between the two can leave them slightly apart; forgejo doctor repairs that.
  • No point-in-time recovery (CloudNativePG's barman-cloud backups), and none planned: it restores a database to any second, but Forgejo's repositories live on forgejo-data, which only has the backup moments, and the two must match. So Forgejo could only go back to those moments anyway; point-in-time would buy an exact match instead of a forgejo doctor run, at the price of a second restore path. CloudNativePG stays as the database operator.
  • SQLite apps (Kanidm, Woodpecker, ntfy): a crash-consistent snapshot, which SQLite recovers from. kaniop 0.19's own Kanidm backups (KanidmBackupSchedule) need an S3 repository of their own, a second restore path, so Kanidm goes through Velero like the rest, unless the planning spike shows kaniop cannot take a restored volume.
  • Restoring OpenBao and the apps: they come from the same backup run. Their passwords have to match, which also settles deferred minor #34 for a full restore.

docs.title: 6. Credentials outside the cluster
docs.text:
• The R2 bucket and its credentials: a new OpenTofu unit infra/production/backup (upstream's infra/_modules/backup, with prevent_destroy) creates the bucket and a token that can write only that bucket.
  • The Kopia repository password: the same unit generates it as a random_password. It must survive the loss of the cluster, so it cannot exist only in OpenBao, which is itself in the backup.
  • Into the cluster: both reach Velero through infra/production/secrets → infra-secrets → OpenBao, as OpenTofu's other secrets do.
  • Network: Velero's namespace gets egress 443 in production (system/egress).

docs.title: 7. Commands (in lab)
docs.text:
• lab backup push <app>: an on-demand off-site copy of one app (group B, or any group A app before a risky change).
  • Before uploading, it prints the volume's used size and the bucket's current size against R2's 10 GB free tier.
  • It asks for confirmation, then creates the Velero Backup and waits for it.
  • lab backup restore: a whole-cluster restore after a fresh install, on a cluster Argo CD has already built from git.
  • The person picks the backup run. Its default is the newest one that completed before this cluster was created, never a backup the new cluster made of its own empty volumes.
  • Order: OpenBao first, from its raft snapshot. Then each group A volume, with that app's workloads stopped and its empty volume replaced. Then the apps start.
  • Group B apps are restored too when that run contains them.
  • lab backup restore <app> [--from local|offsite] [--at <time>]: one app, from a local snapshot or an off-site copy.
  • Visibility: a status listing of backups and snapshots is the builder's call. So are the flag names.

docs.title: 8. Restore never destroys the backups
docs.text:
• Read-only by default: git declares Velero's location ReadOnly and every schedule paused, and Argo CD ignores those two fields. Every new cluster therefore starts unable to write or delete backups, with no flag to remember: Argo CD installs Velero as soon as the cluster exists, before anyone could pass one (upstream's backup_read_only is a flag, and make infra restore=1 was this spec's first idea).
  • lab backup enable switches the location to ReadWrite and the schedules on: once on a brand-new homelab, or after a restore was checked (the docs say how). lab backup disable switches back. The switch lives in the cluster and survives later syncs.
  • A cluster never enabled is noticed: an alert fires when no backup succeeded for 26 hours.
  • Anti-goal: expiry must not eat the last good backups. Retention is by count, not by age: Velero's own expiry is set far out, and a prune job keeps the newest 30 completed backups of each schedule and of each app, and runs only while the location is writable. A cluster dead for months loses nothing.

docs.title: 9. The sandbox proves the path
docs.text:
The sandbox has no R2 and no Ceph.

  • S3: versitygw in the sandbox, sandbox only, pinned. MinIO's community edition is no longer maintained.
  • CSI snapshots: csi-driver-host-path and snapshot-controller, the sandbox's default StorageClass. The local snapshots and Velero's CSI data mover then run in the sandbox as in production; only Ceph's specifics stay on the production checklist.
  • Forgejo on PostgreSQL: the sandbox runs Forgejo on CloudNativePG as production does (instead of SQLite), so the test restores both of Forgejo's volumes. This removes "CloudNativePG and Forgejo on PostgreSQL were only rendered" from the production checklist. Measured 2026-10-22: about 4.7 GiB of the workstation's memory is free; CloudNativePG, one PostgreSQL instance, Velero, its node agent and the S3 server are estimated at 400 to 600 MiB at rest.
  • TestBackup:
  • It writes a marker into Forgejo (a repository with a commit, and an issue) and a key into OpenBao.
  • It takes a backup, then deletes the app's volume and the key.
  • lab backup restore brings back the repository, its commit, the issue and the key, and Forgejo works.
  • It shows that a fresh cluster is read-only and deletes nothing.
  • It shows that lab backup push prints the size and asks before uploading.
  • Isolation: the test must not disturb the other tests. A raft snapshot restore rolls back all of OpenBao, so it either runs alone, as TestNodeRestart does, or restores only what it wrote since the snapshot. The builder decides.
  • Wiring: a test/scopes.yaml entry, the Argo CD lists for system/velero, and resource limits sized to the sandbox's free memory, measured before and after.
  • Production checklist (CLAUDE.md), for what the sandbox cannot run: Ceph's snapshots and their space, the data mover on Ceph, R2 and its token, the first lab backup enable.

docs.title: 10. Docs
docs.text:
• docs/how-to-guides/backup-and-restore.md is rewritten:
  • the three layers and which failure each one covers;
  • groups A, B and C, and how to add an app to A or B;
  • checking R2 usage;
  • restoring one app;
  • restoring the whole cluster on new hardware, end to end: OpenTofu state, passphrase, the cluster read-only, lab backup restore, checking, leaving read-only.
  • Other docs: a decision record (Velero, volumes only), the roadmap line 11a in CLAUDE.md, the production checklist, and secrets-management.md (where the repository password lives).

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Backing up Kubernetes resources, Argo CD's state or cert-manager's certificates.
  • Automatic restore on a fresh install. Restore is always a command someone runs.
  • Backing up group C, media, or OpenTofu's state (already on R2, encrypted).
  • A second off-site provider. Upstream's "TODO migrate to Backblaze B2" stays an idea.
  • Rotation of the backup credentials (step 11b) and node hardware: UPS and shutdown order (step 12).

docs.title: Anti-goals: a failure even if it works
docs.text:
• A restore, a schedule or an expiry that deletes the only good backup.
  • A backup that cannot be restored without the cluster it came from, for example a key that exists only in OpenBao.
  • OpenBao restored from one point in time and the apps from another.
  • Uploading group B data to R2 without the person seeing its size first.

docs.title: Left to the builder
docs.text:
• Velero's exact settings, the local-snapshot mechanism (Velero without data movement, a snapshot scheduler or a CronJob) and how group membership is declared, all within decisions 3 and 4.
  • The flags and output of the lab backup commands, and where the read-only state is kept.
  • The sandbox's S3 server, and whether TestBackup runs alone.
  • Velero's mesh policies (AuthorizationPolicy, the node agent's and data-mover pods' needs), its egress and its metrics.

docs.title: Step 11b: secrets rotation
docs.text: Status: design approved in chat 2026-10-24. Branch: feat/secrets-rotation from dev.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
A secret must be easy to replace in two situations:

  • On a schedule: this is the best practice that limits the damage of a leak nobody has noticed.
  • In an emergency: a secret is known to have leaked, or might have, and is perhaps being used. You can replace just the one you suspect, or every secret at once ("assume everything leaked").

Treat the homelab as production from the start, so this step never has to be rebuilt. Rotation should cause no downtime, ideally by letting the old and the new value work side by side for a while.

The user decided the following in chat (2026-10-23/24):

  • One command handles both cases: one secret by name, or all of them.
  • Rotation follows each secret's official way of changing it, when it has one.
  • Production will run several replicas wherever an app or tool needs them. That is not done in this step. The sandbox keeps one replica where resources require it, and a short outage there is fine.
  • Results reach people through ntfy, with Telegram as a second path.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Upstream nixos (fe353778, 2026-10-23) has nothing to reuse. Its roadmap lists "Secrets rotation" unchecked, and its docs/concepts/secrets-management.md only says to reapply and restart after a rotation. Follow its layout: commands in lab (cli/, cobra) and secrets in OpenBao.
  • Best practice (OWASP Secrets Management Cheat Sheet, NIST SP 800-57 and SP 800-63B, Vault/OpenBao guidance):
  • Short-lived credentials beat rotation. Three are already short-lived here: Renovate's token is minted for each run, R2's state credentials expire, and TLS certificates come from cert-manager.
  • Automate scheduled rotation per kind of secret.
  • Human passwords are not rotated on a schedule (NIST 800-63B), only when they may have leaked.
  • Every secret needs a ready emergency procedure: where it lives, who reads it, what to restart, and whether the old value is really revoked.
  • Rotate without an outage: where both sides must change, keep an overlap window or change both together.
  • Where secrets live today (docs/concepts/secrets-management.md):
  • generated secrets: platform/generated-secrets pushes each one once (IfNotExists) to secret/<namespace>/generated/<name>;
  • OpenTofu's secrets: infra/<env>/secrets → namespace infra-secrets → platform/infra-secrets (Replace);
  • Kanidm's OAuth2 client secrets and admin passwords: written by kaniop;
  • Forgejo's deploy and argocd tokens and Woodpecker's Forgejo OAuth client: written by lab infra forgejo sync;
  • OpenBao's unseal key: infra/<env>/openbao;
  • the state passphrase: the workstation (scripts/rotate-state-passphrase).
  • kaniop's KanidmOAuth2Client has spec.secretRotation (enabled, periodDays): the operator regenerates the client secret periodically. This is the official way for those secrets.
  • Step 11a gives backups and lab backup restore, so a failed rotation can be undone.

docs.title: 1. One command, one secret or all of them
docs.text:
• lab secrets rotate <name> replaces one secret.
  • lab secrets rotate --all replaces every secret in the catalog (decision 3). It prints the list and the expected effect of each item (what restarts, who must act) and asks for confirmation. It then rotates them one after another and reports each result. A failure stops the run and names what is done and what is left.
  • lab secrets list prints the catalog: each secret's method, class, schedule and last rotation.
  • Names are the catalog's, e.g. grafana.admin, ntfy.alerts-token, forgejo.deploy-token, kanidm-client.grafana, cloudflare.cert-manager.
  • --yes skips the confirmation, like lab backup. In an emergency the person runs the command from the workstation. The scheduled run uses the same code (decision 5).

docs.title: 2. How a secret is rotated: the official way first
docs.text:
For each secret, in this order:

  1. Official overlap. The other side supports two valid values at once, or a new credential beside the old one: several tokens per user, a new API token before the old one is deleted, several keys per GitHub App. Create the new value, move every reader to it, check that they work, then revoke the old one. This needs no further justification.
  2. No official overlap. Classify what a short failure would do:
  3. Class 1, nobody notices or it retries itself: change both sides close together and restart the readers. A failed request is retried automatically (Alertmanager re-sends, kubelet retries pulls, Argo CD refetches), or nothing reads the secret at runtime (admin passwords used only by people, occasionally).
  4. Class 2, a person can retry: a login fails or a CI pipeline fails and is restarted. Accept it, but make it unlikely: wait until the app is idle (no running Woodpecker pipeline) and run scheduled rotations at a quiet hour.
  5. Class 3, cannot be skipped: a failure loses data or leaves something stuck until a person repairs it. Only here does the builder design a workaround that creates an overlap (e.g. a second zot user or a second OAuth2 client, then switch and delete the first). The spike found no class 3 secret.
  6. The catalog records each secret's method and class, and the reason for that class.

docs.title: 3. The catalog
docs.text:
The catalog is a file in the repository, e.g. cli/internal/secrets/catalog.yaml or Go code. The builder chooses its form. Each entry gives:

  • the name, and where the secret lives (OpenBao path, OpenTofu resource, kaniop, Forgejo);
  • its readers (namespace, ExternalSecret or Secret, and the workloads to restart);
  • the method (decision 2) and the class with its reason;
  • whether it rotates on a schedule, and its period;
  • for secrets lab cannot change alone, the steps a person follows.

A check fails when a secret exists that the catalog does not know, like scripts/check-backup-groups does for PVCs. That check covers:

  • every generated secret in platform/generated-secrets/values.yaml;
  • every infra-secrets path;
  • every KanidmOAuth2Client;
  • the Forgejo tokens.

A new secret therefore cannot ship without a rotation entry. Entries that are never rotated stay in the catalog with the reason.

Starting catalog. Task 1's spike (decision 10) confirmed the methods it covered; the builder fills in the rest the same way:

Secret Readers Method Class if no overlap Schedule forgejo.admin, grafana.admin, paperless.admin people; Forgejo's init container and lab infra forgejo sync use Forgejo's change it in the app (its API or CLI), then in OpenBao 1 (Forgejo's: run while sync and the init container are not running) command only (human password) paperless.secret-key paperless (sessions, its Celery messages, the classifier file) no overlap: paperless has no SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS setting. Change it in OpenBao, refresh, restart paperless while no task is queued; the classifier file fails its check and is retrained by the hourly task 2 (every session ends, people log in again) command only woodpecker.agent Woodpecker agents: one per-agent token for each agent replica, at secret/woodpecker/agent-<n> (<n> the StatefulSet ordinal); the server's shared WOODPECKER_AGENT_SECRET is emptied overlap: Woodpecker 3's per-agent tokens. lab creates a new agent token (POST /api/agents, admin API, with woodpecker.admin-token), writes it to the replica's path, restarts that agent once no step pod runs (label woodpecker-ci.org/step), then deletes the old agent (DELETE /api/agents/<id>), which revokes its token. The shared secret is dropped because changing it never revokes the old value (amendment 3) n/a 90 days woodpecker.admin-token (secret/woodpecker/admin-token, new) lab only (Woodpecker's admin API, for woodpecker.agent and registry.ci's org secret) Woodpecker's token reset: DELETE /api/user/token with the current token signs a new one and invalidates every earlier token of that user (and its web sessions); lab writes the new one to OpenBao. The first token needs a person: Forgejo's site admin (WOODPECKER_ADMIN) signs in to Woodpecker once and writes it with the admin role, as docs/how-to-guides/woodpecker.md will say 1 (only lab reads it) 90 days registry.ci zot's htpasswd, Woodpecker's org secret registry_password (set by hand today, docs/how-to-guides/woodpecker.md) change in OpenBao and zot, then the org secret through Woodpecker's API 2 (wait for no running pipeline) 90 days ntfy.alerts-token ntfy (NTFY_AUTH_TOKENS), Alertmanager (credentials_file) overlap: ntfy accepts several tokens per user. Add the new one (ntfy restarts), switch OpenBao's value (Alertmanager reads the file at every notification, no restart), then drop the old (ntfy restarts and removes it from auth.db) n/a 90 days ntfy.alerts-password none at runtime (only ntfy's own NTFY_AUTH_USERS; confirmed) change it in OpenBao, refresh ntfy-auth, restart ntfy 1 90 days ntfy.phone-token, ntfy.phone-password people's phones overlap: list both tokens until people confirm, then drop the old n/a command only: people must re-enter them forgejo.deploy-token, forgejo.argocd-token lab infra forgejo push, Argo CD's argocd-repo-forgejo overlap: a new Forgejo access token, then delete the old n/a 90 days forgejo.woodpecker-oauth (secret/woodpecker/forgejo) Woodpecker Forgejo regenerates the OAuth2 app's secret (no overlap) 2 (a login fails) command only kanidm-client.<app> (every confidential KanidmOAuth2Client) the app's Secret <client>-kanidm-oauth2-credentials one-off regeneration: the annotation kaniop.rs/force-secret-rotation on the client (kaniop resets the secret in Kanidm, rewrites the Secret and removes the annotation), then restart the readers that read it at start (Grafana, Actual Budget, paperless, Forgejo); Argo CD picks it up live. Deleting the Secret does not regenerate it 2 (a login fails until the restart, open sessions stay) command only: kaniop's own period restarts no reader kanidm.admin-passwords (admin, idm_admin) lab, the tests, kaniop kaniop writes new ones when their Secret is deleted (confirmed on kaniop 0.19.0) 1 command only cloudflare.cert-manager, cloudflare.external-dns cert-manager, external-dns no overlap for the readers: -replace of the cloudflare_account_token destroys the old token in the same apply, before infra-secrets pushes the new one; cert-manager reads the token at each DNS01 solve and retries, external-dns restarts (env variable) and retries on its next sync (amendment 1; to confirm in production) 1 90 days, through make infra env=production (decision 5) cloudflare.tunnel cloudflared Cloudflare's token refresh: -replace=random_password.tunnel_secret updates the same Tunnel in place (PATCH .../cfd_tunnel/<id> with a new tunnel_secret; same id, same record); connected cloudflared keeps serving until it restarts with the new credentials.json (to confirm in production) 2 with one replica (the public routes drop for the restart); seamless with two command only backup.r2-token (velero/repository) Velero no overlap for the reader, like Cloudflare's: one apply replaces the token; a failed upload is retried by the next schedule; never at 02:00, the daily backup (to confirm in production) 1 90 days, like Cloudflare's backup.kopia-password (velero/encryption) Velero's repositories never: Velero uses one password for every repository and has no change-password, so a new value makes every existing repository unreadable; Kopia's own change-password only re-wraps the key, and the data keys stay the same, so it gains nothing against a leak.
